passages.name: 2018年6月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一个新罕布什尔州男子五十多年前扔进大海的漂流瓶，在一千五百英里外被人捡到，捡到的人亲手把它送还给了他的女儿，还拿到了瓶里信上许诺的奖金。第二篇新闻报道讲南卡罗来纳州为防治寨卡病毒从空中喷洒杀虫剂，结果数百万只蜜蜂死亡，当地官员为此道歉。第三篇新闻报道介绍世界上最大的飞行器“空中登陆者10号”首次试飞，以及它的来历和优点。第一段长对话里，两个人商量今晚出去看什么，最后决定明天去看西班牙舞蹈节。第二段长对话里，转学生凯瑟琳担心自己融不进新学校，李老师安慰她、鼓励她多参加课外活动。第一篇短文讲一项用老鼠做的研究：饥饿的驱动力胜过恐惧、口渴和社交需要。第二篇短文讲美国州际公路系统最初是为了国防修建的，以及它的修建过程。第三篇短文介绍一位年轻发明家设计的“智能方向盘”，用来防止司机边开车边发短信。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A message in a bottle sent out to sea by a New Hampshire man more than five decades ago was found 1,500 miles away and has been returned to his daughter.
paras.zh: 五十多年前，一位新罕布什尔州男子把一封信装进瓶子扔进大海，这个漂流瓶在一千五百英里外被人发现，现在已经送还给了他的女儿。

paras.en: The long-lost message was discovered by Clint Buffington of Utah while he was vacationing.
paras.zh: 这封失落多年的信是犹他州的克林特·巴芬顿度假时发现的。

w.m: adj. 失踪已久的；久违的

paras.en: Buffington says he found a soda bottle half buried in the sand that looked like it had been there since the beginning of time.
paras.zh: 巴芬顿说，他发现一个汽水瓶半埋在沙子里，看上去像是从远古时代起就在那儿了。

w.m: 自古以来；从远古时代起

paras.en: The note inside the bottle said Return to 419 Ocean Street and receive a reward of $150 from Richard and Tina Pierce, owners of the Beachcomber Motel.
paras.zh: 瓶子里的字条写着：送回海洋街419号，即可从海滨拾贝汽车旅馆的老板理查德·皮尔斯和蒂娜·皮尔斯那里领取一百五十美元的奖金。

paras.en: The motel was owned by the parents of Paula Pierce in 1960.
paras.zh: 一九六〇年，这家汽车旅馆归葆拉·皮尔斯的父母所有。

paras.en: Her father had written the note as a joke and had thrown it into the Atlantic Ocean.
paras.zh: 她父亲写这张字条是开个玩笑，然后把它扔进了大西洋。

paras.en: Buffington flew to New Hampshire to deliver the message to Paula Pierce.
paras.zh: 巴芬顿飞到新罕布什尔州，把这封信交给了葆拉·皮尔斯。

paras.en: She held up to her father’s promise, giving Buffington that reward.
paras.zh: 她兑现了父亲的承诺，把那笔奖金给了巴芬顿。

paras.en: But the biggest reward is the message in a bottle finding its way back home.
paras.zh: 不过，最大的回报是这个漂流瓶终于回了家。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What is the news report mainly about?
paras.zh: 第一题：这篇新闻报道主要讲了什么？

paras.en: Question two: Why did Paula Pierce give Clint Buffington the reward?
paras.zh: 第二题：葆拉·皮尔斯为什么给克林特·巴芬顿那笔奖金？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Millions of bees have died in South Carolina during aerial insect spraying operations that were carried out to combat the Zika virus.
paras.zh: 南卡罗来纳州为防治寨卡病毒从空中喷洒杀虫剂，导致数百万只蜜蜂死亡。

paras.en: The insect spraying over the weekend left more than two million bees dead on the spot in Dorchester County, South Carolina, where four travel-related cases of Zika disease have been confirmed in the area.
paras.zh: 周末的这次杀虫剂喷洒让南卡罗来纳州多切斯特县两百多万只蜜蜂当场死亡，该地区已确诊四例与旅行有关的寨卡病例。

paras.en: Most of the deaths came from Flower Town Bee Farm, a company in Somerville that sells bees and honey products.
paras.zh: 死掉的蜜蜂大多来自萨默维尔一家出售蜜蜂和蜂蜜产品的公司——花镇蜜蜂农场。

paras.en: Juanita Stanley, who owns the company, said the farm looks like it’s been destroyed.
paras.zh: 公司老板胡安妮塔·斯坦利说，农场看上去像是被毁了一样。

paras.en: The farm lost about 2.5 million bees.
paras.zh: 农场损失了大约两百五十万只蜜蜂。

paras.en: Dorchester County officials apologized for the accidental mass killing of bees.
paras.zh: 多切斯特县的官员为意外造成大批蜜蜂死亡道了歉。

paras.en: Dorchester County is aware that some beekeepers in the area that was sprayed on Sunday lost their bee colonies, County Manager Jason Ward said in a statement, I’m not pleased that so many bees were killed.
paras.zh: 县行政长官贾森·沃德在一份声明中说，多切斯特县知道，周日喷洒过的地区有一些养蜂人失去了蜂群，这么多蜜蜂被杀死，我很难过。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: Why were spraying operations carried out in Dorchester County?
paras.zh: 第三题：多切斯特县为什么要喷洒杀虫剂？

paras.en: Question four: What does the news report say about Flower Town Bee Farm?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于花镇蜜蜂农场，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The world’s largest aircraft has taken to the skies for the first time.
paras.zh: 世界上最大的飞行器首次飞上了天空。

paras.en: The Airlander 10 spent nearly two hours in the air, having taken off from Cardington Airfield in Bedfordshire.
paras.zh: “空中登陆者10号”从贝德福德郡的卡灵顿机场起飞，在空中飞行了将近两个小时。

paras.en: During its flight, it reached 3,000 feet and performed a series of gentle turns all over a safe area.
paras.zh: 飞行期间，它升到三千英尺的高度，在一片安全区域上空做了一系列平缓的转弯。

paras.en: The aircraft is massive, as long as a football field and as tall as six double-decker buses and capable of flying for up to five days.
paras.zh: 这架飞行器非常庞大，跟一个足球场一样长，跟六辆双层巴士摞起来一样高，最多能连续飞行五天。

paras.en: It was first developed for the US government as a long-range spy aircraft, but was abandoned following budget cutbacks.
paras.zh: 它最初是为美国政府研发的远程侦察机，但由于预算削减而被放弃。

paras.en: The aircraft cost 25 million pounds and can carry heavier loads than huge jet planes, while also producing less noise and emitting less pollution.
paras.zh: 这架飞行器造价两千五百万英镑，能比大型喷气式飞机运载更重的货物，同时噪音更小，排放的污染也更少。

paras.en: The makers believe it’s the future of aircraft, and one day we’ll be using them to go places.
paras.zh: 制造商相信它代表着飞行器的未来，总有一天我们会坐着它四处出行。

paras.en: But there’s still a long way to go.
paras.zh: 不过，要走的路还很长。

paras.en: The airlander will need to have two hundred hours flying time before being allowed to fly by the Aviation Administration.
paras.zh: “空中登陆者”要累计飞行两百个小时，才能获得航空管理局的飞行许可。

paras.en: If it passes, though, we can hope we’ll all get some extra leg room.
paras.zh: 不过，如果它通过了，我们就有望都得到更宽敞的腿部空间。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about the first flight of the Airlander ten?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于“空中登陆者10号”的首次飞行，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 6: What caused the US government to abandon the Airlander 10 as a spy aircraft?
paras.zh: 第六题：是什么原因让美国政府放弃把“空中登陆者10号”用作侦察机？

paras.en: Question seven: What is the advantage of the Airlander 10 over huge jet planes?
paras.zh: 第七题：和大型喷气式飞机相比，“空中登陆者10号”有什么优势？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Do you feel like going out tonight?
paras.zh: 你今晚想出去玩吗？

paras.en: Yeah, why not?
paras.zh: 好啊，为什么不呢？

paras.en: We haven’t been out for ages.
paras.zh: 我们好久没出去了。

paras.en: What’s on?
paras.zh: 有什么好看的？

paras.en: Well, there’s a film about climate change.
paras.zh: 嗯，有一部讲气候变化的电影。

paras.en: Does it sound good to you?
paras.zh: 你觉得这个怎么样？

paras.en: Oh, not really.
paras.zh: 哦，不怎么样。

paras.en: It doesn’t really appeal to me.
paras.zh: 我对它不太感兴趣。

paras.en: What’s it about?
paras.zh: 讲的是什么？

paras.en: Just climate change?
paras.zh: 就讲气候变化？

paras.en: I think it’s about how climate change affects everyday life.
paras.zh: 我想它讲的是气候变化怎样影响日常生活。

paras.en: I wonder how they make it entertaining.
paras.zh: 我真想知道他们怎么把它拍得好看。

w.m: adj. 有趣的；娱乐性强的

paras.en: Well, it sounds really awful.
paras.zh: 嗯，听起来真没意思。

paras.en: It’s an important subject, I agree.
paras.zh: 我承认，这个话题很重要。

paras.en: But I’m not in the mood for anything depressing.
paras.zh: 可我现在不想看让人心情沉重的东西。

w.m: adj. 令人沮丧的；压抑的

paras.en: What else is on?
paras.zh: 还有什么别的吗？

paras.en: There’s a Spanish dance festival.
paras.zh: 有一个西班牙舞蹈节。

paras.en: Oh, I love dance.
paras.zh: 哦，我喜欢跳舞。

paras.en: That sounds really interesting.
paras.zh: 这个听起来很有意思。

paras.en: Apparently it’s absolutely brilliant.
paras.zh: 听说特别精彩。

paras.en: Let’s see what it says in the paper.
paras.zh: 我们看看报上怎么说。

paras.en: Anna Gomez leads in an exciting production of the great Spanish love story Carmen.
paras.zh: 安娜·戈麦斯领衔主演一部激动人心的西班牙经典爱情剧《卡门》。

paras.en: Okay then, what time is it on?
paras.zh: 好吧，那几点开始？
七点半。

paras.en: Well, that’s no good.
paras.zh: 嗯，那不行。

paras.en: We haven’t got enough time to get there.
paras.zh: 我们来不及赶到那里了。

paras.en: Is there anything else?
paras.zh: 还有别的吗？

paras.en: There’s a comedy special on.
paras.zh: 有一场喜剧特别节目。

paras.en: Where’s it on?
paras.zh: 在哪儿演？

paras.en: It’s at the city theatre.
paras.zh: 在市剧院。

paras.en: It’s a charity comedy night with lots of different acts.
paras.zh: 是一场慈善喜剧之夜，有很多不同的节目。

paras.en: It looks pretty good.
paras.zh: 看上去挺不错的。

paras.en: The critic in the local paper says it’s the funniest thing he’s ever seen.
paras.zh: 当地报纸上的评论家说，这是他看过的最好笑的节目。

paras.en: It says here: Roger Whitehead is an amazing host to a night of fun performances.
paras.zh: 这上面写着：罗杰·怀特黑德主持了一个充满欢乐表演的夜晚，主持得非常棒。

w.m: adj. 了不起的；令人惊叹的

paras.en: Hm, I’m not keen on him.
paras.zh: 嗯，我不太喜欢他。

paras.en: He’s not very funny.
paras.zh: 他不怎么好笑。

paras.en: Are you sure you fancy going out tonight?
paras.zh: 你确定你今晚想出去吗？

paras.en: You’re not very enthusiastic.
paras.zh: 你好像兴致不高啊。

paras.en: Perhaps you’re right.
paras.zh: 也许你说得对。

paras.en: Okay, let’s go see the dance, but tomorrow, not tonight.
paras.zh: 好吧，我们去看舞蹈吧，不过明天去，今晚不去了。

paras.en: Great.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: I’ll book the tickets online.
paras.zh: 我在网上订票。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the woman think of climate change?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士怎么看气候变化？

paras.en: Question nine: Why do the speakers give up going to the Spanish Dance Festival tonight?
paras.zh: 第九题：两位说话人为什么不去看今晚的西班牙舞蹈节了？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the critic say about the comedy performed at the city theatre?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于在市剧院上演的喜剧，评论家是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman decide to do tomorrow?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士决定明天做什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Good morning, Mr. Lee.
paras.zh: 早上好，李老师。

paras.en: May I have a minute of your time?
paras.zh: 能耽误您一点时间吗？

paras.en: Sure, Catherine.
paras.zh: 当然可以，凯瑟琳。

paras.en: What can I do for you?
paras.zh: 有什么事吗？

paras.en: I’m quite anxious about transferring over to your college.
paras.zh: 转到你们学院来，我心里很不安。

paras.en: I’m afraid I won’t fit in.
paras.zh: 我怕自己融不进去。

paras.en: Don’t worry, Catherine.
paras.zh: 别担心，凯瑟琳。

paras.en: This happens to many transfer students.
paras.zh: 很多转学生都会这样。

paras.en: Yes, I know, but I’m younger than most of the students in my year, and that worries me a lot.
paras.zh: 是的，我知道，可我比同年级的大多数同学都小，这让我很担心。

paras.en: Well, you may be the only younger one in your year, but, you know, we have a lot of after-school activities you can join in, and so, this way, you’ll be able to meet new friends of different age groups.
paras.zh: 嗯，你可能是你们年级唯一年纪小一点的，不过你知道，我们有很多课外活动你可以参加，这样一来，你就能认识不同年龄段的新朋友了。

paras.en: That’s nice.
paras.zh: 那太好了。

paras.en: I love games and hobby groups.
paras.zh: 我喜欢游戏和兴趣小组。

paras.en: I’m sure you do.
paras.zh: 我相信你会喜欢的。

paras.en: So you’ll be just fine.
paras.zh: 所以你会适应得很好的。

paras.en: Don’t worry so much and try to make the most of what we have on offer here.
paras.zh: 别想太多，好好利用我们这里提供的条件。

paras.en: Also, remember that you can come to me any time of the day if you need help.
paras.zh: 还有，记住，如果你需要帮助，白天随时都可以来找我。

paras.en: Thanks so much.
paras.zh: 太感谢了。

paras.en: I definitely feel better now.
paras.zh: 我现在感觉好多了。

paras.en: As a matter of fact, I’ve already contacted one of the girls who’d be living in the same house as me, and she seemed really nice.
paras.zh: 其实，我已经联系了一个会跟我住同一栋房子的女孩，她看起来人很好。

paras.en: I guess, living on campus, I’ll have a chance to have a closer circle of friends, since we’ll be living together.
paras.zh: 我想，住在校园里，我们住在一起，我就有机会交到更亲近的朋友。

paras.en: All students are very friendly with new arrivals.
paras.zh: 所有学生对新来的人都很友好。

paras.en: Let me check who’d be living with you in your flat.
paras.zh: 我查一下谁会跟你住同一套公寓。

paras.en: Okay, there are Hannah, Kelly, and Bree.
paras.zh: 好，有汉娜、凯莉和布里。

paras.en: Bree is also a new student here, like you.
paras.zh: 布里也是新来的学生，和你一样。

paras.en: I’m sure you two will have more to share with each other.
paras.zh: 我相信你们俩会有更多可以聊的。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Why does Catherine feel anxious?
paras.zh: 第十二题：凯瑟琳为什么感到不安？

paras.en: Question 13: What does Mr. Lee encourage Catherine to do?
paras.zh: 第十三题：李老师鼓励凯瑟琳做什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does Mr. Lee promise to do for Catherine?
paras.zh: 第十四题：李老师答应为凯瑟琳做什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What do we learn about Catherine’s schoolmate, Bree?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于凯瑟琳的同学布里，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Have you ever felt like you would do just about anything to satisfy your hunger?
paras.zh: 你有没有过这样的感觉：为了填饱肚子，你几乎什么都愿意做？

paras.en: A new study in mice may help to explain why hunger can feel like such a powerful motivating force.
paras.zh: 一项用老鼠做的新研究或许能解释，为什么饥饿会让人感觉是一股如此强大的驱动力。

paras.en: In the study, researchers found that hunger outweighed other physical drives including fear, thirst, and social needs.
paras.zh: 研究人员在这项研究中发现，饥饿压倒了其他生理驱动力，包括恐惧、口渴和社交需要。

paras.en: To determine which feeling won out, the researchers did a series of experiments.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚哪种感觉占上风，研究人员做了一系列实验。

paras.en: In one experiment, the mice were both hungry and thirsty.
paras.zh: 在一个实验中，老鼠又饿又渴。

paras.en: When given the choice of either eating food or drinking water, the mice went for the food, the researchers found.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，让老鼠在吃东西和喝水之间二选一时，它们选了食物。

paras.en: However, when the mice were well fed but thirsty, they opted to drink, according to the study.
paras.zh: 不过，根据这项研究，当老鼠吃饱了但口渴时，它们会选择喝水。

paras.en: In the second experiment meant to pit the mice’s hunger against their fear, hungry mice were placed in a cage that had certain fox-scented areas and other places that smelled safer, in other words, not like an animal that could eat them, but also had food.
paras.zh: 第二个实验是想让老鼠的饥饿和恐惧较量一下：把饥饿的老鼠放进一个笼子，笼子里有些地方带着狐狸的气味，另一些地方闻起来更安全，也就是说，闻起来不像会吃掉它们的动物，但那里也有食物。

paras.en: It turned out that, when the mice were hungry, they ventured into the unsafe areas for food but when the mice were well fed, they stayed in areas of the cage that were considered safe.
paras.zh: 结果发现，老鼠饿的时候，会冒险进入不安全的区域找食物；而吃饱的时候，它们就待在笼子里被认为安全的区域。

paras.en: Hunger also outweighed the mice’s social needs, the researchers found.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，饥饿也压倒了老鼠的社交需要。

paras.en: Mice are usually social animals and prefer to be in the company of other mice, according to the study.
paras.zh: 根据这项研究，老鼠通常是群居动物，喜欢和别的老鼠待在一起。

paras.en: When the mice were hungry they opted to leave the company of other mice to go get food.
paras.zh: 老鼠饿的时候，会选择离开其他老鼠，去找吃的。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What is the researcher’s purpose in carrying out the series of experiments with mice?
paras.zh: 第十六题：研究人员用老鼠做这一系列实验的目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: In what circumstances do mice venture into unsafe areas?
paras.zh: 第十七题：老鼠在什么情况下会冒险进入不安全的区域？

paras.en: Question 18: What is said about mice at the end of the passage?
paras.zh: 第十八题：短文最后讲了老鼠的什么？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: The United States has one of the best highway systems in the world.
paras.zh: 美国拥有世界上最好的公路系统之一。

paras.en: Interstate highways connect just about every large and mid-sized city in the country.
paras.zh: 州际公路几乎连通了全国每一个大中型城市。

paras.en: Did you ever wonder why such a complete system of excellent roads exists?
paras.zh: 你有没有想过，为什么会有这样一套完备的优质公路系统？

paras.en: For an answer, you would have to go back to the early 1920s.
paras.zh: 要找答案，就得回到二十世纪二十年代初。

paras.en: In those years, just after World War I, the military wanted to build an American highway system for national defense.
paras.zh: 在那些年里，也就是第一次世界大战刚结束后，军方想修建一套美国公路系统，用于国防。

paras.en: Such a system could, if necessary, move troops quickly from one area to another.
paras.zh: 必要时，这样一套系统可以把部队从一个地区迅速调到另一个地区。

paras.en: It could also get people out of cities in danger of being bombed.
paras.zh: 它还能把人们从有轰炸危险的城市里撤出来。

paras.en: So-called roads of national importance were designated, but they were mostly small country roads.
paras.zh: 当时指定了一些所谓“具有国家重要性”的道路，但它们大多是乡间小路。

paras.en: In 1944, Congress passed a bill to upgrade the system, but did not fund the plan right away.
paras.zh: 一九四四年，国会通过了一项升级这一系统的法案，但没有马上给这个计划拨款。

paras.en: In the 1950s, the plan began to become a reality.
paras.zh: 到了二十世纪五十年代，这个计划开始变成现实。

paras.en: Over $25 billion was appropriated by Congress, and construction began on about 40,000 miles of new roads.
paras.zh: 国会拨款二百五十多亿美元，大约四万英里的新公路开工建设。

paras.en: The idea was to connect the new system to existing expressways and freeways.
paras.zh: 当时的设想是把新系统和现有的高速公路连接起来。

paras.en: And though the system was built mostly to make car travel easier, defense was not forgotten.
paras.zh: 虽然修建这套系统主要是为了让开车出行更方便，但国防也没有被忘记。

paras.en: For instance, highway overpasses had to be high enough to allow trailers carrying military missiles to pass under them.
paras.zh: 比如，公路立交桥必须足够高，好让运载军用导弹的拖车从下面通过。

paras.en: By 1974, the system was mostly completed.
paras.zh: 到一九七四年，这套系统基本完工。

paras.en: A few additional roads would come later.
paras.zh: 后来又修了一些新增的道路。

paras.en: Quick and easy travel between all parts of the country was now possible.
paras.zh: 现在，全国各地之间都能快速便捷地往来了。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about the American highway system?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于美国公路系统，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question twenty: What was the original purpose of building a highway system?
paras.zh: 第二十题：修建公路系统的最初目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 21: When was the interstate highway system mostly completed?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：州际公路系统是什么时候基本完工的？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Texting while driving was listed as a major cause of road deaths among young Americans back in 2013.
paras.zh: 早在二〇一三年，边开车边发短信就被列为美国年轻人交通事故死亡的一个主要原因。

paras.en: A recent study said that 40% of American teens claimed to have been in a car when the driver used a cell phone in a way that put people in danger.
paras.zh: 最近的一项研究称，百分之四十的美国青少年说，自己坐过司机以危险方式用手机的车。

paras.en: This sounds like a widespread disease, but it’s one that technology may now help to cure.
paras.zh: 这听起来像一种广泛流行的病，但现在科技或许能帮忙治好它。

paras.en: T.J. Evarts, a 20-year-old inventor, has come up with a novel solution that could easily put texting drivers on notice.
paras.zh: 二十岁的发明家T.J.埃瓦茨想出了一个新颖的办法，能轻松地给边开车边发短信的司机提个醒。

paras.en: It’s called Smart Wheel, and it’s designed to fit over the steering wheel of most standard vehicles to track whether or not the driver has two hands on the wheel at all times.
paras.zh: 它叫“智能方向盘”，可以套在大多数标准车辆的方向盘上，随时监测司机是不是两只手都握着方向盘。

paras.en: Evarts’ invention warns the drivers with a light and a sound when they hold the wheel with one hand only, but as soon as they place the other hand back on the wheel, the light turns back to green and the sound stops.
paras.zh: 埃瓦茨的这项发明会在司机单手握方向盘时用灯光和声音提醒他们，而他们一把另一只手放回方向盘上，灯就变回绿色，声音也停了。

paras.en: It also watches for what’s called close-by hands, where both hands are close together near the top of the wheel, so the driver can type with both thumbs and drive at the same time.
paras.zh: 它还会监测所谓的“双手靠拢”，就是两只手在方向盘顶部附近靠在一起，这样司机就能一边用两个大拇指打字，一边开车。

paras.en: All the data Smart Wheel collects is also sent to a connected app, so any parents who install Smart Wheel can keep track of the teens’ driving habits.
paras.zh: “智能方向盘”收集的所有数据也会发送到一个与之连接的应用程序上，这样，装了“智能方向盘”的家长都能随时掌握孩子的驾驶习惯。

paras.en: If they try to remove or damage the cover, that’s reported as well.
paras.zh: 如果他们想拆掉或者弄坏方向盘套，这个也会报告上去。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What is a major cause of road deaths among young Americans?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：美国年轻人交通事故死亡的一个主要原因是什么？

paras.en: Question twenty three: What is Smart Wheel?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：“智能方向盘”是什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What happens if the driver has one hand on the wheel?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：如果司机只用一只手握方向盘，会怎么样？

paras.en: Question 25: How do parents keep track of their teens’ driving habits?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：家长怎样随时掌握孩子的驾驶习惯？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2018年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2018年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲阿肯色州一名女子在高速公路上开车时，一条四英尺长的鼠蛇从座位底下爬出来，她受了惊吓，但还是安全停了车。第二篇新闻报道讲一项调查发现，麦当劳等快餐连锁店的得来速服务变慢了，原因是菜单选择更多、食品更复杂。第三篇新闻报道讲美国官员即将批准私营公司“月球快车”的探月任务，这将是第一次飞出地球轨道的私人任务。第一段长对话里，索菲娅在泰国度假，打电话给鲍勃讲她在海滩晒太阳、参观孤儿院的经历。第二段长对话里，女士约戴维去新开的健身房，两人聊到优惠活动和怎样锻炼。第一篇短文讲求职者怎样用表格、谷歌等工具管理求职申请，并强调重质不重量。第二篇短文讲作者认为孩子即使不必上学也不会流落街头，还建议让学生走出校舍，到社会上直接认识世界。第三篇短文讲美国人热爱跳舞，舞蹈老师们讲述了跳舞带给人们的快乐和意义。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Kelly Swisher, an Arkansas woman, escaped injury and managed to safely stop her car after a four-foot-long rat snake came out from under her car seat and slid across her feet as she was driving down the highway.
paras.zh: 阿肯色州女子凯莉·斯威舍在高速公路上开车时，一条四英尺长的鼠蛇从她的座位底下钻出来，从她脚上滑了过去，她没有受伤，还设法安全地停下了车。

paras.en: Rat snakes aren’t poisonous or a threat to people generally, but the woman says the snake she encountered Thursday terrified her out of her wits.
paras.zh: 鼠蛇没有毒，一般对人也没有威胁，但这名女子说，周四她碰到的那条蛇把她吓得魂都没了。

paras.en: It was rough with big scales, said Swisher, who was on her way to pick up her friend at the airport when it happened.
paras.zh: 斯威舍说，它摸上去很粗糙，鳞片很大。事情发生时，她正要去机场接朋友。

paras.en: I don’t know whether I had my hands on the steering wheel or not.
paras.zh: 我都不知道自己的手当时还在不在方向盘上。

paras.en: I am not the most flexible person in the world, but I can guarantee my knees were up next to my ears.
paras.zh: 我不是世界上身体最柔软的人，但我敢保证，我的膝盖当时都抬到耳朵边了。

paras.en: She said the snake first slid back under the seat and she hoped it would stay there until she was able to get off the highway and stop.
paras.zh: 她说，蛇先是滑回了座位底下，她希望它就待在那儿，等她下了高速公路把车停下来。

paras.en: That didn’t work out, she said.
paras.zh: 她说，可是事与愿违。

paras.en: Here he comes, and he wound up in my back seat before I could finally get off the road, stop and get out of the car.
paras.zh: 它又出来了，我还没来得及下公路、停车、下车，它就跑到我的后座上去了。

paras.en: She called for help and Washington County Animal Control Officers came and captured the snake.
paras.zh: 她打电话求助，华盛顿县动物管控部门的工作人员赶来抓住了那条蛇。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: How did Kelly Swisher feel when she first came across the rat snake?
paras.zh: 第一题：凯莉·斯威舍刚碰见那条鼠蛇时有什么感觉？

paras.en: Question two: What does the report say about the snake?
paras.zh: 第二题：报道里是怎么说这条蛇的？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Fast food, it turns out, isn’t quite as fast as it used to be.
paras.zh: 原来，快餐已经不像以前那么快了。

paras.en: A new study finds that McDonald’s posted its slowest drive-through times since this survey was first conducted 15 years ago.
paras.zh: 一项新研究发现，麦当劳的得来速服务时间创下了十五年前首次开展这项调查以来的最慢纪录。

w.m: adj. 免下车（服务）的；得来速的

paras.en: At McDonald’s, customers will spend on average 3 minutes and 9 seconds from the time they place their orders until they receive their food.
paras.zh: 在麦当劳，顾客从下单到拿到食物，平均要花三分钟零九秒。

paras.en: That’s about 10 seconds more than the industry average.
paras.zh: 这比行业平均水平多了大约十秒。

paras.en: And a lot slower than a decade ago, according to the study, which was commissioned by QSR, an industry trade publication.
paras.zh: 据这项研究，这也比十年前慢了很多。这项研究是行业杂志《快餐服务餐厅》委托开展的。

paras.en: And McDonald’s wasn’t alone in slowing down.
paras.zh: 而且变慢的不只麦当劳一家。

paras.en: Other chains also saw their drive-through performance slow down.
paras.zh: 其他连锁店的得来速服务也慢了下来。

w.m: adj. 免下车（服务）的；得来速的

paras.en: Among the reasons for the slower service, today there are more choices on the menu and the products themselves are more complex and take longer to prepare.
paras.zh: 服务变慢的原因有：如今菜单上的选择更多了，产品本身也更复杂，做起来更费时间。

paras.en: Speed, of course, is essential to the drive-through experience, and drive-throughs are hugely important to chains such as McDonald’s, Burger King, and Taco Bell.
paras.zh: 当然，速度是得来速服务的关键，而得来速对麦当劳、汉堡王和塔可钟这样的连锁店来说非常重要。

w.m: adj. 极其重要的；必不可少的
adj. 免下车（服务）的；得来速的
n. 免下车餐厅；得来速窗口

paras.en: Usually, the drive-through accounts for sixty to seventy percent of all business that goes through a fast food restaurant, notes Sam Oches, editor of QSR.
paras.zh: 《快餐服务餐厅》的编辑萨姆·奥克斯指出，通常得来速占一家快餐店全部生意的百分之六十到七十。

w.m: n. 免下车餐厅；得来速窗口

paras.en: Of course, consumers also want their orders prepared correctly, and on that score, Oches says, accuracy is still really high.
paras.zh: 当然，顾客也希望自己点的东西做得准确无误，奥克斯说，在这方面，准确率仍然很高。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What is the news report mainly about?
paras.zh: 第三题：这篇新闻报道主要讲了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What has slowed down McDonald’s drive-through service?
paras.zh: 第四题：是什么让麦当劳的得来速服务变慢了？

w.m: adj. 免下车（服务）的；得来速的

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The first private mission outside of Earth’s orbit is closer than many of us think.
paras.zh: 首次飞出地球轨道的私人任务，比我们很多人想的来得更快。

paras.en: U.S. government officials are set to approve a mission by privately held space company Moon Express to travel outside of Earth’s orbit in late 2017.
paras.zh: 美国政府官员即将批准私营航天公司“月球快车”在二〇一七年年底执行一项飞出地球轨道的任务。

paras.en: Moon Express’s mission involves plans to land a suitcase-sized package of scientific equipment on the Moon for ongoing exploration and commercial development.
paras.zh: “月球快车”的任务计划把一个手提箱大小的科学设备包送上月球，用于持续的探索和商业开发。

paras.en: The decision involved months of lobbying and coordinated conversations between a number of federal agencies.
paras.zh: 做出这个决定之前，好几个联邦机构之间进行了几个月的游说和协调沟通。

paras.en: Under international treaties, the U.S. is responsible for the cargo of both public and private spacecraft.
paras.zh: 根据国际条约，美国要对公共和私人航天器运载的货物负责。

paras.en: This makes commercial space travel a complex legal issue, not just domestically, but abroad.
paras.zh: 所以，商业太空旅行是一个复杂的法律问题，不光在国内是这样，在国外也是。

paras.en: A Moon Express representative declined to comment on this story, but noted that the company is very optimistic about its proposal.
paras.zh: “月球快车”的一位代表拒绝对这篇报道发表评论，但表示公司对自己的计划非常乐观。

paras.en: Moon Express is not the only company seeking for the rights to travel to outer space.
paras.zh: “月球快车”并不是唯一在争取进入外太空权利的公司。

paras.en: Elon Musk’s SpaceX aims to send an unmanned aircraft to Mars by 2018.
paras.zh: 埃隆·马斯克的太空探索技术公司（SpaceX）打算在二〇一八年之前把一架无人驾驶飞行器送上火星。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What is the news report mainly about?
paras.zh: 第五题：这篇新闻报道主要讲了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What is Moon Express planning to do?
paras.zh: 第六题：“月球快车”打算做什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does Moon Express think of its mission?
paras.zh: 第七题：“月球快车”怎么看自己的这项任务？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hey, Sophia, how are you doing?
paras.zh: 嘿，索菲娅，最近怎么样？

paras.en: Hi, Bob.
paras.zh: 嗨，鲍勃。

paras.en: I’m good, thanks.
paras.zh: 我挺好的，谢谢。

paras.en: Actually, I’m on holiday with my family in Thailand at the moment, although I wish it were with my friends instead.
paras.zh: 其实，我现在正和家人在泰国度假，不过我倒希望是跟朋友一起来。

w.m: v. 希望（用于虚拟语气）

paras.en: Really?
paras.zh: 真的吗？

paras.en: You never said you were going to Thailand.
paras.zh: 你从来没说过要去泰国啊。

paras.en: How I envy you.
paras.zh: 真羡慕你。

paras.en: I’ve only been here a week, but you know, Thailand’s an amazing place.
paras.zh: 我才来了一个星期，不过你知道吗，泰国真是个了不起的地方。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；了不起的

paras.en: I’m having a great time here.
paras.zh: 我在这儿玩得很开心。

paras.en: In fact, I’m now lying on the beach in Phuket.
paras.zh: 其实，我现在正躺在普吉岛的海滩上。

paras.en: I’ve been in the sun for around 15 minutes only, and I’m already getting sunburnt.
paras.zh: 我才晒了十五分钟左右，就已经快晒伤了。

paras.en: Have you been here before?
paras.zh: 你以前来过这儿吗？

paras.en: No, I wish I had.
paras.zh: 没有，真希望我来过。

w.m: v. 希望（用于虚拟语气）

paras.en: What else have you been doing in Thailand besides enjoying the sun?
paras.zh: 在泰国除了晒太阳，你还做了些什么？

paras.en: Well, I met a guy from Germany yesterday.
paras.zh: 嗯，我昨天认识了一个德国小伙子。

paras.en: He showed me around the orphanage he works at.
paras.zh: 他带我参观了他工作的那家孤儿院。

paras.en: There, I met many volunteer teachers who are mainly young people from Europe.
paras.zh: 在那儿，我认识了很多志愿者老师，大多是从欧洲来的年轻人。

paras.en: Ah, that’s interesting.
paras.zh: 啊，那挺有意思的。

paras.en: Yes, I also made a new little friend, Sarah.
paras.zh: 是啊，我还交了一个新的小朋友，叫萨拉。

paras.en: She was so cute.
paras.zh: 她太可爱了。

paras.en: I was so sad when I had to leave at the end of the day.
paras.zh: 那天结束要走的时候，我难过极了。

paras.en: If I ever come back to Thailand, I’d definitely visit this place again as a volunteer.
paras.zh: 要是我再来泰国，一定会再去那儿当志愿者。

w.m: adv. 曾经；（用于条件句）将来某时

paras.en: Well, you can tell me all about it when you get back.
paras.zh: 好啊，等你回来再跟我细说吧。

paras.en: My phone battery is almost dead now.
paras.zh: 我手机快没电了。

paras.en: Remember to get me something from the souvenir shops.
paras.zh: 记得在纪念品店给我买点东西。

paras.en: I like to collect bits and pieces from different parts of the world.
paras.zh: 我喜欢收集世界各地的小玩意儿。

paras.en: Bye now.
paras.zh: 那先这样，拜拜。

paras.en: Enjoy yourself, Sophia.
paras.zh: 玩得开心，索菲娅。

paras.en: Bye.
paras.zh: 拜拜。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the woman say she is doing now?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士说她现在在做什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What did the woman do yesterday?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士昨天做了什么？

paras.en: Question ten: Why does the man have to end the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士为什么不得不结束谈话？

paras.en: Question 11: Why does the man ask the woman to bring him something from Thailand?
paras.zh: 第十一题：男士为什么让女士从泰国给他带点东西？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi David, there’s a new gym opening in town today.
paras.zh: 嗨，戴维，今天城里有一家新健身房开业。

paras.en: Would you like to go with me this afternoon?
paras.zh: 今天下午你想跟我一起去吗？

paras.en: Yes, more than glad to.
paras.zh: 想啊，非常乐意。

paras.en: I haven’t been to a gym for ages.
paras.zh: 我好久没去健身房了。

paras.en: I need to do some exercise to tone up.
paras.zh: 我得锻炼锻炼，练出点肌肉来。

paras.en: Then this is a good chance.
paras.zh: 那这正是个好机会。

paras.en: They sent me an invitation with a note saying I could take a friend for free on the first day.
paras.zh: 他们给我寄了一份邀请函，上面附了一张字条，说开业第一天我可以免费带一个朋友去。

paras.en: Also, if we both sign up before Friday, we can get a discount on a six-month membership.
paras.zh: 还有，如果我们俩在周五之前报名，办六个月的会员卡可以打折。

paras.en: Great.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: Count me in.
paras.zh: 算我一个。

paras.en: I really want to lose some of this belly fat and turn it into muscle.
paras.zh: 我真想减掉一些肚子上的赘肉，把它变成肌肉。

paras.en: But I’m not sure which of the gym equipment would best help.
paras.zh: 可我不知道哪种健身器材最管用。

paras.en: Well, I’m no expert at that, but I think you can try lifting weights and do at least 200 sit-ups twice a day.
paras.zh: 嗯，这方面我不是什么专家，不过我觉得你可以试试举重，每天做两次仰卧起坐，每次至少两百个。

paras.en: I’ve never tried weight lifting before.
paras.zh: 我以前从来没试过举重。

paras.en: Is it dangerous?
paras.zh: 危险吗？

paras.en: No, not at all, if you know some of the basics.
paras.zh: 不危险，一点也不，只要你懂一些基本要领。

w.m: n. 基本要领；基础知识

paras.en: Don’t worry, I’ll show you the ropes.
paras.zh: 别担心，我来教你怎么做。

paras.en: I used to practice this at another gym before my membership ended.
paras.zh: 我以前在另一家健身房练过，后来会员到期了。

paras.en: I’ll be your personal trainer.
paras.zh: 我来当你的私人教练。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。

paras.en: What other equipment do they have?
paras.zh: 他们还有什么别的器材？

paras.en: Well, like all gyms they have all sorts of things to help build up muscles in different parts of the body, like upright bicycles, chest stretching machines and running machines.
paras.zh: 嗯，跟所有健身房一样，他们有各种各样的器械，帮你锻炼身体不同部位的肌肉，比如立式健身车、扩胸器和跑步机。

paras.en: You could use any of these to suit your purpose.
paras.zh: 你可以根据自己的需要用其中任何一种。

paras.en: Now, the gym opens at noon, so can we meet up in town at 1:30 p.m.?
paras.zh: 好，健身房中午开门，那我们下午一点半在城里碰头好吗？

paras.en: Perfect.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: See you there, coach.
paras.zh: 到时候见，教练。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What are the speakers talking about?
paras.zh: 第十二题：两位说话人在谈论什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the gym offer at its opening?
paras.zh: 第十三题：健身房开业时提供什么优惠？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What is the man concerned about?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士担心什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What do we learn about the woman from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：从对话中我们对女士有什么了解？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then, mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: In today’s job market, it’s not uncommon for job seekers to submit applications for many positions.
paras.zh: 在如今的就业市场上，求职者同时申请很多职位的情况并不少见。

paras.en: That involves lots of time and lots of work to organize.
paras.zh: 这要花很多时间，整理起来也很费事。

paras.en: Certainly, you don’t want to waste your precious hours on following the developments in a disorderly fashion and miss important deadlines, confuse interview times, or forget to follow up as a result.
paras.zh: 你肯定不想把宝贵的时间浪费在毫无头绪地跟进各种进展上，结果错过重要的截止日期、记混面试时间，或者忘了后续跟进。

paras.en: Accordingly, managing your job search properly is just as important as identifying job opportunities and submitting your applications.
paras.zh: 所以，管理好自己的求职过程，跟发现工作机会、提交申请一样重要。

paras.en: If you’re familiar with Microsoft Excel or a similar program, creating a table is a simple and effective way to keep track of your job applications.
paras.zh: 如果你熟悉微软的Excel或者类似的软件，做一张表格就是追踪求职申请简单又有效的办法。

paras.en: If Excel isn’t quite your cup of tea, don’t worry.
paras.zh: 如果你不太喜欢用Excel，也别担心。

paras.en: You can create a table in Microsoft Word or a similar word processor.
paras.zh: 你可以在微软Word或者类似的文字处理软件里做表格。

paras.en: Google is another tool to help you get organized effectively.
paras.zh: 谷歌是另一个能帮你有效整理的工具。

paras.en: If you have a Gmail account, you can create, save, and send tables in addition to written documents like your cover letter and resume.
paras.zh: 如果你有Gmail账号，除了求职信和简历这类书面文件，你还能创建、保存和发送表格。

paras.en: You can also link up with Google Calendar to make sure you stay on top of important dates.
paras.zh: 你还可以关联谷歌日历，确保随时掌握重要的日子。

paras.en: Clearly, there are plenty of ways to keep track of your job search, and making the effort to simplify your job search will pay off.
paras.zh: 显然，追踪求职进展的办法有很多，花点力气把求职过程简化一下，是会有回报的。

paras.en: Nevertheless, you should always focus on quality, not quantity.
paras.zh: 不过，你应该始终注重质量，而不是数量。

paras.en: Only apply for positions you are qualified for and make each application count, personalizing each cover letter and updating and editing your resume.
paras.zh: 只申请你能胜任的职位，并让每一份申请都有分量：每封求职信都要量身定制，简历也要更新、修改。

w.m: adj. 有资格的；能胜任的
v. 使个性化；量身定制

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about today’s job seekers?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于如今的求职者，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What can job applicants do with the help of Google?
paras.zh: 第十七题：借助谷歌，求职者可以做什么？

paras.en: Question eighteen: What does the speaker suggest job seekers do?
paras.zh: 第十八题：说话人建议求职者做什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Some people say, if kids didn’t have to go to school, they’d all be out in the streets.
paras.zh: 有人说，要是孩子们不用上学，他们就都会跑到街上去。

paras.en: My reply is, no, they wouldn’t.
paras.zh: 我的回答是：不，他们不会。

paras.en: First, even if schools stayed just the way they are, children would spend at least some time there because that’s where they’d be likely to find friends.
paras.zh: 首先，就算学校还是现在这个样子，孩子们也至少会在那里待一段时间，因为他们很可能在那里找到朋友。

paras.en: Second, schools wouldn’t stay the way they are.
paras.zh: 第二，学校不会一直是现在这个样子。

paras.en: They’d get better because we would have to start making them what they ought to be right now.
paras.zh: 学校会变得更好，因为我们就得从现在起着手把学校办成它们本该有的样子。

paras.en: Last, if we stirred up our brains and gave children a little help, those who did not want to go to school could find other things to do, things many children now do during their holidays.
paras.zh: 最后，如果我们开动脑筋，给孩子们一点帮助，那些不想上学的孩子就能找到别的事情做，也就是很多孩子现在放假时做的事情。

paras.en: There’s something easier we could do.
paras.zh: 还有一件更容易做到的事。

paras.en: We need to get kids out of the school buildings.
paras.zh: 我们得让孩子们走出教学楼。

paras.en: Give them a chance to learn about the world at first hand.
paras.zh: 给他们一个机会，亲身去了解这个世界。

paras.en: In Philadelphia and Portland, Oregon, plans are being drawn up for public schools that won’t have any school buildings at all.
paras.zh: 在费城和俄勒冈州的波特兰，有关部门正在为一些根本没有校舍的公立学校制定计划。

paras.en: That will take the students out into the city and help them to use it and its people as a resource.
paras.zh: 这些学校会把学生带到城市里，帮助他们把城市和城里的人当作一种资源来利用。

paras.en: In other words, students, perhaps in groups, perhaps independently, will go to libraries, museums, exhibitions, courtrooms, radio and TV stations, meetings, businesses and laboratories to learn about their world and society at first hand.
paras.zh: 也就是说，学生们会到图书馆、博物馆、展览会、法庭、广播电台和电视台、各种会议、企业和实验室去，也许是分组去，也许是单独去，亲身了解他们的世界和社会。

paras.en: A small private school in Washington is already doing this.
paras.zh: 华盛顿有一所小型私立学校已经在这么做了。

paras.en: It makes sense.
paras.zh: 这是有道理的。

paras.en: We need more of it.
paras.zh: 我们需要更多这样的做法。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What are some people worried about, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十九题：根据说话人的说法，有些人担心什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the speaker think we could do for kids who dislike school?
paras.zh: 第二十题：说话人认为，对于不喜欢上学的孩子，我们可以做些什么？

paras.en: Question twenty one: What does the speaker say is the easier thing we could do?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说，我们可以做的更容易的事是什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Before there was the written word, there was the language of dance.
paras.zh: 在有文字之前，就有了舞蹈这种语言。

paras.en: Dance expresses love and hate, joy and sorrow, life and death, and everything else in between.
paras.zh: 舞蹈能表达爱与恨、喜与悲、生与死，以及介于两者之间的一切。

paras.en: Dance in America is everywhere.
paras.zh: 在美国，舞蹈无处不在。

paras.en: We dance from Florida to Alaska, from horizon to horizon and coast to coast.
paras.zh: 从佛罗里达到阿拉斯加，从地平线这头到那头，从东海岸到西海岸，我们都在跳舞。

w.m: 从东海岸到西海岸；全国各地

paras.en: We dance at weddings, birthdays, office parties, or just to fill the time.
paras.zh: 我们在婚礼上、生日会上、公司聚会上跳舞，或者只是跳舞打发时间。

paras.en: I adore dancing, says Lester Bridges, the owner of a dance studio in a small town in Iowa.
paras.zh: 我特别喜欢跳舞，艾奥瓦州一个小镇上的舞蹈工作室老板莱斯特·布里奇斯说。

paras.en: I can’t imagine doing anything else with my life.
paras.zh: 我想象不出这辈子还能做别的什么。

paras.en: Bridges runs dance classes for all ages.
paras.zh: 布里奇斯开设了面向各个年龄段的舞蹈课。

paras.en: Teaching dance is wonderful.
paras.zh: 教跳舞是一件很美妙的事。

paras.en: My older students say it makes them feel young.
paras.zh: 我那些年纪大的学生说，跳舞让他们觉得自己年轻了。

paras.en: It’s marvelous to watch them.
paras.zh: 看着他们跳舞，真是太棒了。

paras.en: For many of them, it’s a way of meeting people and having a social life.
paras.zh: 对他们很多人来说，这是结识朋友、过上社交生活的一种方式。

paras.en: So why do we dance?
paras.zh: 那么，我们为什么跳舞？

paras.en: I can tell you about one young couple, says Bridges.
paras.zh: 我可以跟你讲讲一对年轻夫妻的事，布里奇斯说。

paras.en: They arrive at the class in a bad mood and they leave with a smile.
paras.zh: 他们来上课时心情很差，离开时却面带笑容。

paras.en: Dancing seems to change their mood completely.
paras.zh: 跳舞好像彻底改变了他们的心情。

paras.en: So, do we dance in order to make ourselves feel better, calmer, healthier?
paras.zh: 那么，我们跳舞是为了让自己感觉更好、更平静、更健康吗？

paras.en: Andrea Hillier, a dance teacher, says, Dance, like the rhythm of a beating heart, is life.
paras.zh: 舞蹈老师安德烈娅·希利尔说，舞蹈就像心跳的节奏，它就是生命。

paras.en: Even after all these years, I want to get better and better.
paras.zh: 即使过了这么多年，我还是想跳得越来越好。

paras.en: I keep practicing even when I’m exhausted.
paras.zh: 就算累得筋疲力尽，我也会一直练。

paras.en: I find it hard to stop.
paras.zh: 我觉得很难停下来。

paras.en: Dancing reminds me I’m alive.
paras.zh: 跳舞让我感到自己还活着。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the passage say about dance in America?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于美国的舞蹈，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question twenty-three: What do we know about Lester Bridges’ dance studio?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于莱斯特·布里奇斯的舞蹈工作室，我们知道什么？

paras.en: Question twenty four: What happened to the young couple after they attended Lester Bridges’s class?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：那对年轻夫妻上了莱斯特·布里奇斯的课以后，发生了什么变化？

paras.en: Question 25: What did Andrea Hillier say about dancing?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：安德烈娅·希利尔对跳舞是怎么说的？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲科学家计划在二〇一九年借一台不到一公斤的设备，把4G移动网络覆盖到月球，之所以不用5G，是因为5G还在测试阶段、不够稳定。第二篇新闻报道讲海沃德一家废弃商场夜里起火，消防员约四十五分钟控制住火势，无人受伤，起火原因还在调查。第三篇新闻报道讲日本因为土豆歉收，薯片卖到原价的六倍，而日本出于防病考虑，严格限制进口土豆。第一段长对话里，男士嫌布朗先生的课无聊，女士介绍了自己让笔一直动起来、随手画画和在家大声朗读的专注方法。第二段长对话里，女士翻看去印度度蜜月的照片，讲泰姬陵背后的爱情故事、印度城市的拥挤和美食。第一篇短文介绍皮尤研究中心的一项调查：多数美国人对当地公共图书馆评价很正面。第二篇短文介绍萨凡纳猫：个头大、像狗一样忠诚、跳得高、好奇心强，还不怕水。第三篇短文讲孩子刚上学时父母的心情，并强调家庭生活对孩子的学业成功起决定作用。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A device that weighs less than 1 kilogram is part of a mission that will allow scientists to deliver fourth generation or 4G mobile coverage to the moon in 2019.
paras.zh: 一台重量不到一公斤的设备是一项任务的一部分，这项任务将让科学家在二〇一九年把第四代移动通信，也就是4G信号覆盖到月球上。

paras.en: If successful, the tiny device will provide the moon with its first ever mobile phone network.
paras.zh: 如果成功，这台小小的设备将给月球带来有史以来第一个手机网络。

paras.en: The lunar network will support high-definition streaming of video and data between the moon and Earth.
paras.zh: 这个月球网络将支持月球和地球之间的高清视频和数据流传输。

w.m: n. 流传输；流媒体播放

paras.en: The network is part of Mission to the Moon.
paras.zh: 这个网络是“登月使命”项目的一部分。

paras.en: This is a project with the goal of landing the first privately paid for mission to the Moon.
paras.zh: 这个项目的目标是完成第一次私人出资的登月任务。

paras.en: The 4G mission is set to launch from Cape Canaveral in the United States on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in 2019.
paras.zh: 这次4G任务定于二〇一九年用太空探索技术公司的猎鹰9号火箭，从美国卡纳维拉尔角发射升空。

paras.en: Mission to the Moon intends to establish and test the first elements of a communications network on the Moon.
paras.zh: “登月使命”项目打算在月球上建立并测试第一批通信网络设施。

paras.en: The scientists working on the project opted to build a 4G rather than a fifth generation or 5G network.
paras.zh: 参与这个项目的科学家们选择建4G网络，而不是第五代移动通信，也就是5G网络。

paras.en: This is because fifth generation networks are still in testing and trial phases.
paras.zh: 这是因为第五代网络还处在测试和试用阶段。

paras.en: This means that a 5G network may not yet be stable enough to work on the moon’s surface.
paras.zh: 这就意味着5G网络可能还不够稳定，没法在月球表面工作。

paras.en: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What are scientists planning to do?
paras.zh: 第一题：科学家们正计划做什么？

paras.en: Question 2: Why did scientists choose to set up a 4G network in their mission?
paras.zh: 第二题：科学家们为什么选择在任务中建立4G网络？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Firefighters responded to a fire Wednesday night at an abandoned mall in Hayward.
paras.zh: 星期三晚上，海沃德一家废弃的商场起火，消防员赶到现场。

paras.en: The fire was reported at 9.26pm at an old shopping centre on Mission Avenue near St Mary’s Church.
paras.zh: 火情是晚上九点二十六分报告的，起火地点是圣玛丽教堂附近、使命大道上的一家旧购物中心。

paras.en: Six fire engines, two trucks and two chiefs responded to the scene.
paras.zh: 六辆消防车、两辆云梯车和两名消防队长赶到了现场。

paras.en: Crews had the fire under control in about 45 minutes and managed to contain the fire to its point of origin.
paras.zh: 消防队员大约四十五分钟就控制住了火势，并且把火控制在了起火点。

paras.en: There were some people inside the building when the fire broke out, but there were no reports of any injuries.
paras.zh: 起火时楼里有一些人，但没有人员受伤的报告。

paras.en: Fire investigators have responded to the scene but have not yet determined the cause of the fire.
paras.zh: 火灾调查员已经赶到现场，但还没有查明起火原因。

paras.en: Firefighters will remain on the scene until later this morning to ensure that the fire doesn’t start up again.
paras.zh: 消防员会在现场一直待到今天上午晚些时候，确保火不会再烧起来。

paras.en: The shopping mall had not been in use since 2002.
paras.zh: 这家购物中心从二〇〇二年起就没再用过。

paras.en: In 2014, City Hall developed a plan to knock down the building and replace it with affordable housing.
paras.zh: 二〇一四年，市政府制定了一项计划，打算拆掉这栋楼，改建成经济适用房。

paras.en: However, the plan was dropped due to lack of funds.
paras.zh: 但是，由于缺少资金，这项计划被放弃了。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What does the news item say about the fire?
paras.zh: 第三题：这则新闻是怎么说这场火灾的？

paras.en: Question four: What had City Hall planned to do?
paras.zh: 第四题：市政府原来打算做什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Potato chips in Japan are being sold for six times their normal price.
paras.zh: 在日本，薯片正以平时六倍的价格出售。

paras.en: This is after the country’s main manufacturer stopped sales due to a potato shortage.
paras.zh: 这是因为日本最大的薯片生产商由于土豆短缺停止了销售。

paras.en: Storms and floods in its main potato growing region last year caused the worst harvest in more than three decades.
paras.zh: 去年，日本主要的土豆产区遭遇暴风雨和洪水，造成了三十多年来最差的收成。

paras.en: Local media reports suggest Calbee and its main rival, Koike-Ya, are halting almost 50 products.
paras.zh: 据当地媒体报道，卡乐比和它的主要竞争对手湖池屋正在暂停近五十种产品的生产。

paras.en: We don’t know when we’ll be able to restart, a company spokesman said.
paras.zh: “我们不知道什么时候能恢复生产。”一位公司发言人说。

paras.en: Snack lovers are panic buying, and many supermarket shelves are bare.
paras.zh: 爱吃零食的人都在抢购，许多超市的货架都空了。

paras.en: Japanese laws limit the amount of imported potatoes that can be used in Japanese-made products.
paras.zh: 日本法律限制了日本国产食品中能使用的进口土豆的数量。

paras.en: Japan says fear of disease is its main reason to block fresh imports.
paras.zh: 日本说，担心疾病是它禁止进口新鲜土豆的主要原因。

paras.en: It still only allows potatoes from selected U.S. states.
paras.zh: 它仍然只允许进口美国部分州的土豆。

paras.en: This is only at certain times and on condition that they are processed at factories based near Japanese ports.
paras.zh: 而且只能在特定时间进口，条件是这些土豆必须在日本港口附近的工厂加工。

paras.en: But global warming has raised the possibility that domestic produce could be seriously affected by rare weather events more often.
paras.zh: 可是，全球变暖让国产农产品更有可能频繁受到罕见天气的严重影响。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What problem is Japan facing?
paras.zh: 第五题：日本面临什么问题？

paras.en: Question six: Why does Japan limit the import of potatoes?
paras.zh: 第六题：日本为什么限制土豆进口？

paras.en: Question seven: What might affect Japanese domestic produce?
paras.zh: 第七题：什么可能会影响日本国产农产品？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Mr. Brown’s lectures are so boring.
paras.zh: 布朗先生的课太无聊了。

paras.en: Yes, he is not a very exciting speaker, but the subject is interesting.
paras.zh: 是啊，他讲课不太吸引人，不过这门课本身挺有意思的。

w.m: adj. 令人兴奋的；精彩的

paras.en: During every one of his lectures, I try to listen.
paras.zh: 他的每一节课，我都努力认真听。

paras.en: I really try.
paras.zh: 我真的很努力。

paras.en: But after about ten minutes, my mind begins to wander and I lose concentration.
paras.zh: 可是大概十分钟以后，我就开始走神，注意力也集中不起来了。

paras.en: But I see that you seem to be okay.
paras.zh: 但我看你好像没什么问题。

paras.en: How do you stay focused through the entire hour?
paras.zh: 你是怎么一整节课都保持专注的？

paras.en: Well, what I do is keep my pen moving.
paras.zh: 嗯，我的办法是让笔一直动着。

paras.en: What do you mean?
paras.zh: 你这话什么意思？

paras.en: It’s a method of active concentration I read about.
paras.zh: 这是我在书上看到的一种主动集中注意力的方法。

paras.en: One of the most effective ways to concentrate is to write things down.
paras.zh: 集中注意力最有效的方法之一，就是把东西写下来。

paras.en: But it has to be done by hand, not typing on a keyboard.
paras.zh: 不过一定要手写，不能用键盘打字。

paras.en: You see, writing by hand forces you to actually engage with what you’re learning in a more physical way.
paras.zh: 你看，手写会逼着你用一种更身体力行的方式，真正投入到你学的内容里去。

paras.en: Do you review your notes afterwards then?
paras.zh: 那你课后会复习笔记吗？

paras.en: Sometimes, but that’s not important.
paras.zh: 有时候会，不过那不重要。

paras.en: My notes may or may not be useful, but the point is that by writing down what Mr. Brown says, I can follow his line of thinking more easily.
paras.zh: 我的笔记可能有用，也可能没用，关键是通过把布朗先生讲的东西写下来，我能更轻松地跟上他的思路。

paras.en: In fact, sometimes I draw a little too.
paras.zh: 其实，有时候我也会画一点画。

paras.en: You draw in class?
paras.zh: 你上课画画？

paras.en: And that helps you pay attention?
paras.zh: 那样还能帮你集中注意力？

paras.en: Yes, honestly, it works for me.
paras.zh: 是啊，说真的，这招对我很管用。

paras.en: I just draw little lines and nonsense, really.
paras.zh: 其实我就是随手画些小线条之类乱七八糟的东西。

w.m: n. 无意义的东西；胡乱的东西

paras.en: It was also in that article I read.
paras.zh: 这也是我看的那篇文章里讲的。

paras.en: It can keep the mind active, prevent getting bored and help to concentrate.
paras.zh: 它能让大脑保持活跃，防止觉得无聊，帮助集中注意力。

paras.en: Again, the point is to listen hard while keeping the pen moving.
paras.zh: 还是那句话，关键是一边让笔动着，一边用心听。

paras.en: If I’m at home and I need to study, what I do is read out loud.
paras.zh: 如果我在家要学习，我的办法是大声朗读。

paras.en: It has a similar effect to writing by hand.
paras.zh: 这和手写的效果差不多。

paras.en: It helps memorize information in a physical way.
paras.zh: 它能帮助你用一种身体参与的方式记住信息。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the man think of Mr. Brown’s lectures?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士觉得布朗先生的课怎么样？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman do during Mr. Brown’s lectures?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士在布朗先生的课上做什么？

paras.en: Question ten: Why does the woman draw in class?
paras.zh: 第十题：女士为什么在课上画画？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman say about reading out loud?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于大声朗读，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: And where’s this?
paras.zh: 这是哪儿？

paras.en: These photos are from the Taj Mahal in India.
paras.zh: 这些照片是在印度的泰姬陵拍的。

paras.en: We went there about ten years ago for our honeymoon.
paras.zh: 大约十年前我们去那里度的蜜月。

paras.en: Was it romantic?
paras.zh: 浪漫吗？

paras.en: Yeah, the Taj Mahal was a very romantic place.
paras.zh: 嗯，泰姬陵是个非常浪漫的地方。

paras.en: The guide told us there is a famous love story behind this building that all Indians learn in school.
paras.zh: 导游跟我们说，这座建筑背后有一个著名的爱情故事，所有印度人上学时都会学到。

paras.en: I think it was during the 1600s, and the princess at the time died while giving birth to her 14th child.
paras.zh: 我记得是在十七世纪，当时的王妃在生第十四个孩子时去世了。

paras.en: The emperor loved the princess so much and was so sad when she died that he ordered the palace to be built in her honour.
paras.zh: 皇帝非常爱这位王妃，她去世时他悲痛万分，于是下令建造这座宫殿来纪念她。

paras.en: Wow, that sounds very romantic.
paras.zh: 哇，听起来好浪漫。

paras.en: It looks amazing.
paras.zh: 看起来真漂亮。

paras.en: Yes, it’s gorgeous.
paras.zh: 是啊，美极了。

w.m: adj. 非常美丽的；极好的

paras.en: It’s also larger in real life than it looks in the photos.
paras.zh: 而且它实际上比照片里看起来还要大。

paras.en: The building is very tall, and there are gardens and a wall around it all.
paras.zh: 这座建筑很高，四周有花园，还有一圈围墙。

paras.en: It’s all built in this white stone, and some walls of the building are decorated with jewels.
paras.zh: 它全是用这种白色石头建的，有些墙上还镶着宝石。

paras.en: It must have been very crowded when you were there.
paras.zh: 你们去的时候肯定人很多吧。

paras.en: Yes, it’s a very famous tourist destination, so there are thousands of visitors every day.
paras.zh: 是啊，那是非常有名的旅游景点，每天都有成千上万的游客。

paras.en: Was the rest of India crowded?
paras.zh: 印度其他地方也很拥挤吗？

paras.en: Yes, very crowded in many cities.
paras.zh: 是啊，很多城市都非常拥挤。

paras.en: It was sometimes so crowded that it was difficult to walk along the streets, especially through busy markets.
paras.zh: 有时候挤得连在街上走路都很难，特别是穿过热闹的市场时。

paras.en: And there are so many cars.
paras.zh: 而且车特别多。

paras.en: Traffic was terrible.
paras.zh: 交通糟透了。

paras.en: But the people are friendly.
paras.zh: 不过那里的人很友好。

paras.en: The culture is amazing, and we had a great time.
paras.zh: 那里的文化很了不起，我们玩得很开心。

w.m: adj. 了不起的；令人惊叹的

paras.en: What about the food?
paras.zh: 吃的怎么样？

paras.en: Indian food is great.
paras.zh: 印度菜很棒。

paras.en: There are lots of different dishes to try, and every region has its own special food.
paras.zh: 有很多不同的菜可以尝，而且每个地区都有自己的特色美食。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: For what purpose did the woman go to India?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士去印度是为了什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: Why was the Taj Mahal built?
paras.zh: 第十三题：泰姬陵是为什么建造的？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the woman say about the Taj Mahal?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于泰姬陵，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What is the woman’s impression of Indian cities?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士对印度城市的印象怎么样？

paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
