paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: A Pew Research Centre survey of more than 1,000 Americans conducted in April 2016 finds that Americans continue to express largely positive views about the current state of their local public libraries.
paras.zh: 皮尤研究中心二〇一六年四月对一千多名美国人做了一项调查，发现美国人对当地公共图书馆的现状总体上仍然评价很正面。

paras.en: For instance, around three quarters say that public libraries provide them with the resources they need.
paras.zh: 比如，大约四分之三的人说，公共图书馆为他们提供了所需要的资源。

paras.en: And 66% say the closing of their local public library would have a major impact on their community, although notably, just 33% say this would have a major impact on them personally or on their family.
paras.zh: 百分之六十六的人说，当地公共图书馆要是关门，会对他们的社区产生重大影响；不过值得注意的是，只有百分之三十三的人说，这会对他们个人或家庭产生重大影响。

paras.en: A majority of Americans feel libraries are doing a good job of providing a safe place for people to hang out or spend time, as well as opening up educational opportunities for people of all ages.
paras.zh: 大多数美国人觉得，图书馆在为人们提供一个可以闲待、消磨时间的安全场所方面做得很好，也给各个年龄段的人带来了受教育的机会。

paras.en: And roughly half think their libraries contribute a lot to their communities in terms of helping spark creativity among young people and providing a trusted place for people to learn about new technologies.
paras.zh: 大约一半的人认为，图书馆对社区贡献很大，比如帮助激发年轻人的创造力，为人们提供一个学习新技术的可靠场所。

paras.en: As in past Pew Research Centre surveys of library use, the April 2016 survey also measured Americans’ usage of and engagement with libraries.
paras.zh: 和皮尤研究中心以往关于图书馆使用情况的调查一样，这次二〇一六年四月的调查也测量了美国人对图书馆的使用和参与程度。

paras.en: Overall, 53% of Americans ages 16 and older have had some interaction with a public library in the past year, either through an in-person visit or using a library website.
paras.zh: 总的来说，十六岁及以上的美国人中，百分之五十三在过去一年里和公共图书馆打过交道，要么亲自去过，要么用过图书馆的网站。

paras.en: Some 48% of adults specifically visited a library in the past 12 months, a modest increase from the 44% who said that in late 2015.
paras.zh: 大约百分之四十八的成年人在过去十二个月里专门去过图书馆，比二〇一五年底说去过的百分之四十四略有增加。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What do most Americans say about local public libraries?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于当地公共图书馆，大多数美国人是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 17: How can local public libraries benefit young people?
paras.zh: 第十七题：当地公共图书馆能怎样让年轻人受益？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the 2016 survey show about adult library users?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于成年图书馆使用者，二〇一六年的调查显示了什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: A savannah cat is a crossbreed between a domestic cat and a medium-sized wild African cat called the serval.
paras.zh: 萨凡纳猫是家猫和一种名叫薮猫的非洲中型野猫杂交出来的品种。

paras.en: The unusual cross became popular among breeders at the end of the 1990s, and in 2001, the International Cat Association accepted it as a new registered breed.
paras.zh: 这种不寻常的杂交猫在二十世纪九十年代末受到繁育者的欢迎，二〇〇一年，国际猫协会把它认定为一个新的注册品种。

paras.en: The savannahs are tall and slim and can weigh up to 9.1 kilograms, making them one of the largest breeds of cats that people can own.
paras.zh: 萨凡纳猫又高又瘦，体重可达九点一公斤，是人们能养的个头最大的猫之一。

paras.en: They have a spotted coat similar to that of many types of wild cats, and their ears are very large.
paras.zh: 它们身上有斑点，和很多野猫的皮毛很像，耳朵也很大。

paras.en: They are also commonly compared to dogs in their loyalty and can be trained to walk on a lead and to fetch.
paras.zh: 人们还常常拿它们的忠诚和狗相比，它们可以被训练得会拴着绳子遛弯，还会把东西叼回来。

paras.en: An often noted characteristic of the savannah is its jumping ability.
paras.zh: 萨凡纳猫一个常被人提到的特点是它的跳跃能力。

paras.en: They are known to jump on top of doors and high cabinets.
paras.zh: 大家都知道它们能跳到门顶和高高的柜子上。

paras.en: Some can leap about 2.5 meters high from a standing position.
paras.zh: 有些萨凡纳猫原地起跳能跳大约二点五米高。

paras.en: Cats are typically known for being very inquisitive, and so are the savannahs.
paras.zh: 猫通常以好奇心很强出名，萨凡纳猫也是这样。

paras.en: They often learn how to open doors and cupboards.
paras.zh: 它们经常学会开门、开柜子。

paras.en: Many savannah cats do not fear water and will play with or even dive into water.
paras.zh: 很多萨凡纳猫不怕水，会玩水，甚至会跳进水里。

paras.en: Some owners even shower with their savannah cats.
paras.zh: 有些主人甚至和自己的萨凡纳猫一起洗澡。

paras.en: Presenting a water bowl to a savannah may also prove a challenge, as some will promptly begin to bat all the water out of the bowl until it is empty using their front paws.
paras.zh: 给萨凡纳猫放一碗水也可能是件难事，因为有些猫会马上用前爪把碗里的水全拍出来，直到碗空了为止。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn about the savannah cat?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于萨凡纳猫，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty: What is characteristic of savannah cats?
paras.zh: 第二十题：萨凡纳猫有什么特点？

paras.en: Question 21: What do some people do with their savannah cats?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：有些人会和他们的萨凡纳猫一起做什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: When children start school for the very first time, parents often feel a sense of excitement, coupled with a touch of sadness at the end of an era.
paras.zh: 孩子第一次上学时，父母往往会感到兴奋，同时又因为一段时光的结束而有点难过。

paras.en: This is the start of a new adventure for children, playing and interacting with new friends, sharing, taking turns, and settling into a new routine.
paras.zh: 这是孩子一段新冒险的开始：和新朋友一起玩耍、交往，学会分享、轮流，慢慢适应新的日常作息。

paras.en: But of course, this is not the start of your child’s education, which in fact began at birth.
paras.zh: 当然，这并不是孩子教育的开始，孩子的教育其实从出生就开始了。

paras.en: Back then, you would have been your child’s most influential teachers.
paras.zh: 那时候，你可能就是孩子最有影响力的老师。

paras.en: During this time at home, your child would have learned more than at any other period in their life.
paras.zh: 在家里的这段时间，孩子学到的东西可能比人生中任何其他时期都多。

paras.en: During your child’s first year in school, much time will be spent in learning to read, and they need to know that this is fun and worthwhile.
paras.zh: 孩子上学的第一年，会花很多时间学阅读，他们需要知道阅读既有趣又值得。

paras.en: Your child will naturally copy you, so it is important that you are seen reading and enjoying books, newspapers, and magazines, rather than just absorbed in screens.
paras.zh: 孩子自然会模仿你，所以很重要的一点是，要让他们看到你在读书、看报、看杂志，而且乐在其中，而不是只顾着盯着屏幕。

w.m: adj. 专心的；全神贯注的

paras.en: Ultimately, an excellent education should be a close partnership between parents and teachers.
paras.zh: 说到底，良好的教育应该是父母和老师之间的紧密合作。

paras.en: A child’s year splits fairly neatly into thirds, a third at school, a third asleep, and a third awake at home or on holiday.
paras.zh: 孩子的一年大体上可以平分成三份：三分之一在学校，三分之一在睡觉，三分之一醒着待在家里或者在度假。

paras.en: Irrespective of the quality of a school, a child’s home life is of key importance.
paras.zh: 不管学校质量如何，孩子的家庭生活都至关重要。

paras.en: It is the determining factor of their academic success.
paras.zh: 它是决定孩子学业成功的因素。

paras.en: Your child may have started on a new journey, but your work is far from finished.
paras.zh: 你的孩子也许已经踏上了一段新的旅程，但你的工作还远没有结束。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: How do parents feel when their children start going to school?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：孩子开始上学时，父母有什么感受？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the passage say about children’s education?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于孩子的教育，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What should parents do for the success of their children’s education?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：为了孩子教育的成功，父母应该做什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the passage say is the key factor of children’s academic success?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：短文说孩子学业成功的关键因素是什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2018年12月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2018年12月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲布鲁克林一处建筑工地的空置老楼在拆除时局部坍塌，一名捡建材的男子被困近一个半小时后获救，伤情不危及生命。第二篇新闻报道讲英国新成立的组织“全国算术能力”，指出数百万人数学能力差，影响生活，要改变“我学不好数学”的心态。第三篇新闻报道讲荷兰国王威廉-亚历山大二十多年来兼任航空公司客座飞行员，他说飞行能让他放下王室职责、专心做别的事。第一段长对话里，罗马尼亚一家家具公司的负责人塞米诺讲公司的创办、只用本地木材，以及加入欧盟后的快速发展。第二段长对话里，男士邀请女士周末去新餐厅“珍珠”，并介绍《614》杂志和每年的“餐厅周”活动。第一篇短文讲一项研究：让孩子反复尝蔬菜、不给奖励，比用玩具或表扬更能让他们爱上蔬菜。第二篇短文讲人类在月球上留下的大量垃圾从哪里来，以及它们的研究价值。第三篇短文讲写电子邮件的几条规矩：收到邮件要回复，群发邮件不必回复，要用规范的英语。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News report one.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Rescue crews pulled a man to safety after a collapse at a construction site in Brooklyn on Tuesday.
paras.zh: 星期二，布鲁克林一处建筑工地发生坍塌，救援人员把一名男子救到了安全地带。

paras.en: The incident happened on the 400 block of Rutland Road just after 12.30 p.m. The Fire Department of New York says the vacant 100-year-old building being pulled down partially collapsed.
paras.zh: 事故发生在拉特兰路四百号街区，时间是中午十二点半刚过。纽约消防局说，这栋正在拆除的空置百年老楼发生了局部坍塌。

w.m: adj. 空着的；无人使用的

paras.en: A man described as a non-worker civilian was buried up to his waist in the basement.
paras.zh: 一名据称不是工人的平民被埋在地下室里，土一直埋到他的腰部。

paras.en: The man was collecting building materials when the first floor collapsed underneath him.
paras.zh: 这名男子当时正在收集建筑材料，结果脚下的一楼塌了下去。

paras.en: He was trapped under a beam about 10 feet below the surface for nearly an hour and a half.
paras.zh: 他被困在地面以下大约十英尺的一根房梁下，困了将近一个半小时。

paras.en: The man was then taken to hospital.
paras.zh: 随后，这名男子被送往医院。

paras.en: Officials said he is in stable condition with non-life-threatening injuries.
paras.zh: 官方说，他情况稳定，受的伤不危及生命。

paras.en: The building was reportedly purchased by a neighboring church in 2011.
paras.zh: 据报道，这栋楼二〇一一年被附近的一座教堂买了下来。

paras.en: It was the site of a 2006 fire and has remained vacant ever since.
paras.zh: 二〇〇六年这里发生过一场火灾，从那以后就一直空着。

w.m: adj. 空着的；无人使用的

paras.en: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What happened at a construction site in Brooklyn on Tuesday?
paras.zh: 第一题：星期二布鲁克林的一处建筑工地发生了什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What does the report say about the non-worker civilian?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于那名不是工人的平民，报道说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Millions of people are struggling to understand their paychecks or calculate money in shops, campaigners have said.
paras.zh: 社会活动人士说，有好几百万人连自己的工资单都看不明白，在商店里也算不清钱。

paras.en: Being bad at maths should no longer be seen as a badge of honour or down to genetics, according to National Numeracy, a new organisation which aims to challenge the nation’s negative view of the subject.
paras.zh: “全国算术能力”是一个新组织，目标是改变全国人对数学的负面看法。该组织表示，数学不好不应该再被看成一种光荣，也不该归结于遗传。

w.m: n. 计算能力；算术能力

paras.en: Chris Humphries, chairman of the group, said that poor maths skills can affect an individual’s life, leaving them at a higher risk of being excluded from school or out of work.
paras.zh: 这个组织的主席克里斯·汉弗莱斯说，数学能力差会影响一个人的生活，让他们更容易被学校开除或者失业。

paras.en: Figures from a government survey published last year show that 17 million adults in England have basic maths skills that are, at best, the same as an 11-year-old, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，去年公布的一项政府调查数据显示，英格兰有一千七百万成年人的基本数学能力，充其量只相当于一个十一岁孩子的水平。

paras.en: Speaking at the launch of National Numeracy, Mr Humphries said, That’s a scary figure because what it means is they often can’t calculate or give change.
paras.zh: 汉弗莱斯先生在“全国算术能力”的成立仪式上说：“这个数字很吓人，因为这意味着他们常常不会算账，也不会找零钱。”

w.m: n. 计算能力；算术能力

paras.en: Mike Ellicock, chief executive of National Numeracy, said, We want to challenge this I-can’t-do-maths attitude that is prevalent in the UK, adding that it was vital that all primary school teachers understand key maths concepts, as young children who fail to learn the basics will suffer later on.
paras.zh: “全国算术能力”的首席执行官迈克·埃利科克说：“我们要改变英国普遍存在的这种‘我学不好数学’的心态。”他还说，所有小学老师都要弄懂数学的关键概念，这一点非常重要，因为小孩子要是没学好基础知识，以后就会吃亏。

w.m: n. 计算能力；算术能力

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What does the organisation National Numeracy aim to do?
paras.zh: 第三题：“全国算术能力”这个组织的目标是什么？

w.m: n. 计算能力；算术能力

paras.en: Question 4: What is vital according to the chief executive of National Numeracy?
paras.zh: 第四题：据首席执行官说，什么是极其重要的？

w.m: n. 计算能力；算术能力

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The Dutch King has revealed that for more than two decades, he has held down a part-time second job alongside his royal duties.
paras.zh: 荷兰国王透露，二十多年来，他在履行王室职责之外，一直还兼着一份业余工作。

paras.en: King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands said that he recently ended his role as a regular guest pilot after 21 years with the national airline’s fleet of now outdated aircraft.
paras.zh: 荷兰国王威廉-亚历山大说，他在国家航空公司的机队里担任常驻客座飞行员二十一年，驾驶的是如今已经过时的飞机，最近他卸下了这个角色。

paras.en: As a guest flyer, the king worked about twice a month, always as co-pilot.
paras.zh: 作为客座飞行员，国王大约每月飞两次，一直担任副驾驶。

paras.en: He will now retrain to fly the bigger Boeing 737s as the old planes are being phased out of service.
paras.zh: 由于旧飞机正逐步退役，他现在要重新培训，去驾驶更大的波音737。

paras.en: The 50-year-old father of three and king to 17 million Dutch citizens calls flying a hobby.
paras.zh: 这位五十岁的国王有三个孩子，是一千七百万荷兰公民的国王，他把飞行称作一种爱好。

paras.en: It lets him leave his royal duties on the ground and fully focus on something else.
paras.zh: 飞行能让他把王室职责留在地面上，全身心投入到别的事情上。

paras.en: You have an aircraft, passengers, and crew.
paras.zh: 你有一架飞机，有乘客，有机组人员。

paras.en: You have responsibility for them, the king said.
paras.zh: 你要对他们负责，国王说。

paras.en: You can’t take your problems from the ground into the skies.
paras.zh: 你不能把地面上的烦恼带到天上去。

paras.en: You can completely change focus and concentrate on something else.
paras.zh: 你可以完全转移注意力，专心做别的事。

paras.en: That, for me, is the most relaxing part of flying.
paras.zh: 对我来说，这就是飞行最让人放松的地方。

paras.en: Willem-Alexander said he is rarely recognized by passengers.
paras.zh: 威廉-亚历山大说，乘客很少认出他来。

paras.en: Very few people pay attention to him as he walks through the airport in his airline uniform and cap.
paras.zh: 他穿着航空公司的制服、戴着帽子穿过机场时，很少有人注意到他。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What does the report say about the Dutch King?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于荷兰国王，报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question six: Why does the king say he likes flying?
paras.zh: 第六题：国王说他为什么喜欢飞行？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the king say about passengers at the airport?
paras.zh: 第七题：关于机场的乘客，国王说了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Morning, Miss Semino.
paras.zh: 早上好，塞米诺女士。

paras.en: Welcome to our studio.
paras.zh: 欢迎来到我们的演播室。

paras.en: Thanks.
paras.zh: 谢谢。

paras.en: My pleasure.
paras.zh: 不客气。

paras.en: Okay, then.
paras.zh: 好，那我们开始吧。

paras.en: Let me start by asking you how old your company is.
paras.zh: 我先问问您，您的公司创办多久了？

paras.en: My grandparents started the company in 1955.
paras.zh: 我祖父母在一九五五年创办了这家公司。

paras.en: Why did they decide to open a furniture plant in Bucharest?
paras.zh: 他们为什么决定在布加勒斯特开家具厂？

paras.en: At the time, there was a construction boom.
paras.zh: 当时正赶上建筑热潮。

paras.en: There was a great need for furniture and my grandparents saw a business opportunity.
paras.zh: 大家非常需要家具，我祖父母看到了商机。

paras.en: Their aim was to provide quality, yet affordable wooden furniture.
paras.zh: 他们的目标是提供质量好、价格又实惠的木制家具。

w.m: adj. 负担得起的；实惠的

paras.en: And this goal has never changed.
paras.zh: 这个目标从来没变过。

paras.en: Do you still only work with wood?
paras.zh: 你们现在还是只做木制品吗？

paras.en: That’s right.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: It’s what we know and what we do best.
paras.zh: 这是我们了解的，也是我们最擅长的。

paras.en: If we started trying different materials, our quality would probably suffer.
paras.zh: 如果我们开始尝试不同的材料，质量可能就会下降。

paras.en: And all the wood is local?
paras.zh: 木材全都是本地的吗？

paras.en: Correct.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: 100% of our raw material comes from Romania.
paras.zh: 我们的原材料百分之百来自罗马尼亚。

paras.en: Could you please outline how the company has grown over time?
paras.zh: 您能简单介绍一下公司这些年是怎么发展起来的吗？

paras.en: What have been the main challenges and opportunities that you have faced?
paras.zh: 你们遇到过的主要挑战和机遇有哪些？

paras.en: Well, back in the 50s and 60s, Romania was a lot poorer than it is today.
paras.zh: 嗯，在五六十年代，罗马尼亚比现在穷得多。

paras.en: My grandfather and father did not have much capital, and our customers didn’t have much money either.
paras.zh: 我祖父和父亲没多少资金，我们的顾客也没多少钱。

paras.en: So that limited growth.
paras.zh: 所以这就限制了公司的发展。

paras.en: The big change was in 2007, when Romania joined the European Union.
paras.zh: 大的转变出现在二〇〇七年，那年罗马尼亚加入了欧盟。

paras.en: Suddenly, our market exploded in size and we could now sell our products all across the continent.
paras.zh: 我们的市场一下子大大扩张，现在可以把产品卖到整个欧洲大陆。

paras.en: There was also more financial investment and, as a result, we went from having 20 employees to 200.
paras.zh: 金融投资也多了，结果，我们的员工从二十人增加到了两百人。

paras.en: Which countries are your biggest market?
paras.zh: 哪些国家是你们最大的市场？

paras.en: Besides Romania, our biggest market is Germany.
paras.zh: 除了罗马尼亚，我们最大的市场是德国。

paras.en: There is strong demand there for our traditional style of furniture.
paras.zh: 那里对我们这种传统风格的家具需求很大。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: Why did Semino’s grandparents start a furniture plant in Bucharest?
paras.zh: 第八题：塞米诺的祖父母为什么在布加勒斯特开办家具厂？

paras.en: Question nine: What was Semino’s grandfather trying to do?
paras.zh: 第九题：塞米诺的祖父当时想做什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does Semino say about her company’s raw materials?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于公司的原材料，塞米诺说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: Where does Semino’s company sell their products?
paras.zh: 第十一题：塞米诺的公司在哪里销售产品？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Have you heard about the new restaurant, The Pearl?
paras.zh: 你听说那家新开的餐厅“珍珠”了吗？

paras.en: Susan and I are going to try it out this weekend.
paras.zh: 我和苏珊这个周末要去尝尝。

paras.en: We have a reservation on Saturday at 7 o’clock.
paras.zh: 我们订了星期六七点的位子。

paras.en: I can call to add two more to the table if you’d like.
paras.zh: 你们要是愿意，我可以打电话再加两个人。

paras.en: That sounds great.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: We’d love to join you.
paras.zh: 我们很乐意跟你们一起去。

paras.en: You always seem to know the best places to go.
paras.zh: 你好像总能知道最好去的地方。

paras.en: Where do you hear about these things?
paras.zh: 这些消息你都是从哪儿听来的？

paras.en: I have a habit of reading 614 Magazine.
paras.zh: 我习惯看《614》杂志。

paras.en: It has all the information on local events within the 614 calling code area.
paras.zh: 上面有614电话区号范围内所有本地活动的信息。

paras.en: That’s a clever name for the magazine, then.
paras.zh: 那这杂志的名字起得真巧妙。

paras.en: Does it only focus on new restaurant openings?
paras.zh: 它只关注新开的餐厅吗？

paras.en: They have other information too, things like concerts, festivals, and small shops.
paras.zh: 它也有别的信息，比如音乐会、节日活动、小店之类的。

paras.en: I think the restaurant information and reviews are the most exciting, though.
paras.zh: 不过我觉得餐厅信息和点评是最精彩的。

w.m: adj. 令人兴奋的；精彩的

paras.en: Each year, they also sponsor a local event called Restaurant Week.
paras.zh: 他们每年还会赞助一个本地活动，叫“餐厅周”。

paras.en: Restaurant Week?
paras.zh: 餐厅周？

paras.en: What’s that?
paras.zh: 那是什么？

paras.en: Oh, it’s wonderful.
paras.zh: 哦，那可太棒了。

paras.en: All the stylish restaurants participate.
paras.zh: 所有时髦的餐厅都会参加。

paras.en: They have special set menus for the week, usually in spring, at a number of different price points.
paras.zh: 他们那一周会推出特价套餐，通常是在春天，有好几个不同的价位。

paras.en: Susan and I go to at least three different places during the event.
paras.zh: 活动期间我和苏珊至少会去三家不同的餐厅。

paras.en: It’s a great opportunity to try some of the more expensive restaurants at a discounted price and try something new.
paras.zh: 这是个好机会，可以用折扣价去尝尝一些比较贵的餐厅，换换口味。

paras.en: That’s how we found the Pearl, actually.
paras.zh: 其实，我们就是这么发现“珍珠”的。

paras.en: Wow, that’s an event I would be interested in.
paras.zh: 哇，这个活动我会感兴趣的。

paras.en: When will it be happening this year?
paras.zh: 今年什么时候举行？

paras.en: You’re in luck.
paras.zh: 你运气真好。

paras.en: Restaurant Week starts in just a few days, the first Sunday in May.
paras.zh: 餐厅周再过几天就开始了，就在五月的第一个星期天。

paras.en: Let’s make sure to set a double date during the event.
paras.zh: 活动期间咱们两对一定要约一次一起去吃饭。

paras.en: Just let me know what type of food you would like to try.
paras.zh: 你想尝什么样的菜，告诉我一声就行。

paras.en: Okay, I will.
paras.zh: 好的，我会的。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the man invite the woman to do this weekend?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士邀请女士这个周末做什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the man say about 614 Magazine?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于《614》杂志，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the man usually do with Susan during restaurant week?
paras.zh: 第十四题：餐厅周期间，男士通常和苏珊一起做什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: Why does the man say the woman is in luck?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士为什么说女士运气好？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: All parents know it is difficult to get children to eat their vegetables.
paras.zh: 所有父母都知道，让孩子吃蔬菜很难。

paras.en: Some of them offer rewards or treats for children finishing their share.
paras.zh: 有些父母会给吃完自己那份的孩子奖励或者好吃的。

paras.en: But researchers have discovered that youngsters who are not praised for trying vegetables are more likely to eat them eventually.
paras.zh: 但研究人员发现，尝了蔬菜却没受到表扬的孩子，最终反而更有可能吃蔬菜。

paras.en: The study found that the best way to get children to eat food they do not like is simply to give them repeated exposure to it.
paras.zh: 研究发现，让孩子吃他们不喜欢的食物，最好的办法就是让他们反复接触这种食物。

paras.en: Psychologists from Ghent University in Belgium studied 98 children.
paras.zh: 比利时根特大学的心理学家研究了九十八名儿童。

paras.en: They gave them five kinds of vegetables to eat: mushrooms, peas, eggplants, carrots and cabbages.
paras.zh: 他们给孩子们吃五种蔬菜：蘑菇、豌豆、茄子、胡萝卜和卷心菜。

paras.en: The taste tests revealed that carrots were the least liked vegetable among youngsters.
paras.zh: 品尝测试显示，胡萝卜是孩子们最不喜欢的蔬菜。

paras.en: The children were then given a bowl of boiled carrots and told to choose how much to eat.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员给孩子们一碗煮胡萝卜，让他们自己决定吃多少。

paras.en: After eight minutes they were asked to rate the dish as delicious, just okay or disgusting.
paras.zh: 八分钟后，研究人员请他们给这道菜打分：好吃、一般还是难吃。

w.m: adj. 令人恶心的；难吃的

paras.en: The trial went on twice a week for a month with a follow-up taste test after eight weeks.
paras.zh: 实验每周进行两次，持续了一个月，八周后又做了一次跟进品尝测试。

paras.en: Children were split into three groups, with one group asked to try the bowl of carrots repeatedly with no further encouragement.
paras.zh: 孩子们被分成三组，其中一组只是反复尝那碗胡萝卜，不给任何额外的鼓励。

paras.en: The other two groups were given rewards of a toy or verbal praise.
paras.zh: 另外两组分别得到玩具或者口头表扬作为奖励。

paras.en: After the trial, 81% of children who simply tried the carrots consistently liked them.
paras.zh: 实验结束后，只是尝胡萝卜的孩子中，有百分之八十一一直都喜欢胡萝卜。

paras.en: This is in contrast to 68% for the group given a toy and 75% for the group given verbal praise.
paras.zh: 相比之下，得到玩具的那组是百分之六十八，得到口头表扬的那组是百分之七十五。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What is the best way to get children to eat vegetables according to a recent study?
paras.zh: 第十六题：根据最近的一项研究，让孩子吃蔬菜最好的办法是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What did the researchers find about carrots?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于胡萝卜，研究人员发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the result of this research show?
paras.zh: 第十八题：这项研究的结果说明了什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: One thing about the moon many people don’t know is that it has a lot of garbage on its surface left over from human space exploration.
paras.zh: 关于月球，很多人不知道的一件事是，月球表面有很多人类太空探索留下的垃圾。

paras.en: But how much garbage exactly have humans left on the moon?
paras.zh: 那么，人类到底在月球上留下了多少垃圾呢？

paras.en: It’s hard to be accurate, but the trash likely weighs more than 181,000 kilograms on Earth.
paras.zh: 很难算准，不过这些垃圾在地球上称的话，很可能超过十八万一千公斤。

paras.en: Much of it was left by American astronauts who landed on the lunar surface between 1969 and 1972 during NASA’s Apollo missions.
paras.zh: 其中大部分是一九六九年到一九七二年间，美国宇航员在美国国家航空航天局的阿波罗登月任务中登上月球表面时留下的。

paras.en: The other rubbish comes from missions that did not have human crews.
paras.zh: 其余的垃圾来自没有载人的任务。

paras.en: These missions were conducted by various space exploring agencies, including those from the U.S., Russia, Japan, India, and Europe.
paras.zh: 这些任务是由各国的太空探索机构执行的，包括美国、俄罗斯、日本、印度和欧洲的机构。

paras.en: Many of the older pieces are equipment sent to learn about the moon.
paras.zh: 很多比较旧的东西是为了了解月球而送上去的设备。

paras.en: The equipment stayed there after its missions ended.
paras.zh: 任务结束后，这些设备就留在了那里。

paras.en: The moon is also home to lunar orbiters that mapped the moon before they crashed into its surface, adding to the garbage heap.
paras.zh: 月球上还有一些绕月探测器，它们先给月球绘制地图，然后撞上月球表面，也成了垃圾堆的一部分。

paras.en: The objects left by the Apollo astronauts included equipment that was no longer needed.
paras.zh: 阿波罗宇航员留下的东西包括已经不再需要的设备。

paras.en: Bringing back unneeded equipment would have used up precious resources such as fuel.
paras.zh: 把用不着的设备带回来，会耗掉燃料之类的宝贵资源。

paras.en: But as the saying goes, one person’s trash is another’s treasure.
paras.zh: 不过俗话说得好，一个人的垃圾是另一个人的宝贝。

paras.en: Researchers can study the garbage left on the moon to see how its materials weathered the radiation and vacuum of space over time.
paras.zh: 研究人员可以研究留在月球上的垃圾，看看这些材料长期经受太空的辐射和真空后变成了什么样。

w.m: v. 经受住；（受风吹日晒而）变化

paras.en: Moreover, some of the objects on the moon are still being used, including a laser range reflector left by the Apollo 11 crew.
paras.zh: 而且，月球上有些东西现在还在用，包括阿波罗11号机组留下的一台激光测距反射器。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the passage say may be unknown to many people?
paras.zh: 第十九题：短文说什么可能是很多人不知道的？

paras.en: Question 20: Why has a lot of equipment been left on the moon?
paras.zh: 第二十题：为什么很多设备被留在了月球上？

paras.en: Question 21: What can researchers do with the garbage on the moon?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：研究人员可以用月球上的垃圾做什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: In my line of work, I receive a lot of emails.
paras.zh: 干我这一行，我会收到很多电子邮件。

paras.en: I also send a lot of emails.
paras.zh: 我也会发很多邮件。

paras.en: Though social media and messaging apps have taken over some of the roles from email as a form of communication, email is likely to retain an important role for business communication in the future.
paras.zh: 虽然社交媒体和即时通信软件已经取代了电子邮件作为交流方式的部分作用，但在未来，电子邮件很可能在商务交流中仍然扮演重要角色。

paras.en: Surprisingly, though, a lot of companies and organisations lack formal guidelines for emailing.
paras.zh: 不过让人意外的是，很多公司和机构都没有正式的邮件规范。

paras.en: As most of you will soon be entering the workforce, I would like to share with you my own rules for emailing.
paras.zh: 你们大多数人很快就要参加工作了，所以我想和你们分享一下我自己写邮件的规矩。

paras.en: If someone sends you an email, reply to them acknowledging the email.
paras.zh: 如果有人给你发了邮件，要回复对方，表示收到了。

paras.en: A simple thank you lets the sender know that their email has arrived safely, that it has not been lost among what could be 50 other emails that have arrived in your email inbox that day.
paras.zh: 简单一句“谢谢”，就能让发件人知道邮件已经安全送达，没有淹没在你收件箱当天可能收到的五十封其他邮件里。

paras.en: It’s not necessary to reply to a mass email sent to numerous recipients.
paras.zh: 发给很多收件人的群发邮件就不必回复了。

paras.en: These emails are often informative rather than personalised correspondence requiring a response or action.
paras.zh: 这类邮件往往只是传达信息，而不是需要回复或采取行动的个人信件。

w.m: adj. 个人的；针对个人的

paras.en: But it’s common politeness to respond to a personal message, preferably within 24 hours of receiving it.
paras.zh: 但回复私人邮件是起码的礼貌，最好在收到后二十四小时内回复。

paras.en: It’s also important to use proper English.
paras.zh: 用规范的英语也很重要。

paras.en: Just because emails are a quick form of communication doesn’t mean emails, especially business emails, should be written using informal shortened forms of words.
paras.zh: 邮件是一种快捷的交流方式，但这并不意味着邮件，尤其是商务邮件，就可以用不正式的缩略词来写。

paras.en: Think of an email as a letter.
paras.zh: 要把邮件当成一封信来看待。

paras.en: Spelling, grammar and punctuation should not be overlooked and never use capitals to emphasise a word or words in an email.
paras.zh: 拼写、语法和标点都不能忽视，而且在邮件里千万不要用大写字母来强调一个或几个词。

paras.en: It’s the same as yelling.
paras.zh: 那就跟大喊大叫一样。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the passage say about email?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于电子邮件，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What should one do upon receiving a personalized email?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：收到私人邮件后应该怎么做？

w.m: adj. 个人的；针对个人的

paras.en: Question 24: What does the passage say about a mass email?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于群发邮件，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What should one do when writing a business email?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：写商务邮件时应该怎么做？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲加州一名九岁男孩从旧金山游到恶魔岛再游回来，成了完成这段游程最年轻的人，父亲用加倍的奖金给他打气。第二篇新闻报道讲中国取消晚婚假期奖励的新规定，一些年轻情侣赶着登记结婚，律师说新规还要地方政府落实，不必着急。第三篇新闻报道讲新西兰两名室友创办的聚会后清洁公司，生意火爆，国内外的请求纷至沓来。第一段长对话里，凯尔第二次才考过驾驶理论考试，正在上路考的驾驶课，课程不便宜。第二段长对话里，男士被利兹大学录取，和埃玛聊学费、奖学金，埃玛打算先在英国教书，再去海外的国际学校。第一篇短文讲蚂蚁怎样危害家庭，以及怎样防止蚂蚁进屋。第二篇短文里，一位研究人员介绍他对人体免疫系统随年龄变化的研究和“千名长者”志愿者。第三篇短文讲老师特德·科马达用国际象棋帮助低收入社区的学生学会三思而后行。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A nine-year-old Central California boy braved strong currents and cold water to swim from San Francisco to Alcatraz Island and back.
paras.zh: 加州中部一名九岁男孩顶着强劲的水流和冰冷的海水，从旧金山游到恶魔岛，又游了回来。

paras.en: A California television station in Fresno reported Tuesday that James Savage set a record as the youngest swimmer to make the journey to the former prison.
paras.zh: 弗雷斯诺的一家加州电视台周二报道说，詹姆斯·萨维奇创下了纪录，成为游到这座旧监狱岛最年轻的人。

paras.en: The TV station reported that by completing the swim, the fourth grade student from Los Banos broke a record previously held by a 10-year-old boy.
paras.zh: 电视台报道说，这名来自洛斯巴诺斯的四年级学生完成了这次游泳，打破了此前一名十岁男孩保持的纪录。

paras.en: James said that waves in the San Francisco Bay hitting him in the face 30 minutes into his swim made him want to give up.
paras.zh: 詹姆斯说，游了三十分钟后，旧金山湾的海浪一个劲儿地往他脸上打，让他想放弃。

paras.en: His father said he had offered his son $100 as a reward.
paras.zh: 他父亲说，自己之前答应给儿子一百美元作为奖励。

paras.en: To encourage his struggling son, he doubled it to $200.
paras.zh: 为了给苦苦支撑的儿子打气，他把奖金翻倍，加到了两百美元。

paras.en: James pushed forward, making it to Alcatraz Island and back in a little more than two hours.
paras.zh: 詹姆斯咬牙坚持，用了两个多小时游到恶魔岛，又游了回来。

paras.en: Alcatraz is over a mile from the mainland.
paras.zh: 恶魔岛离大陆有一英里多。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What did the boy from Central California do according to the report?
paras.zh: 第一题：根据这篇报道，来自加州中部的男孩做了什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What did the father do to encourage his son?
paras.zh: 第二题：父亲做了什么来鼓励儿子？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: On the 1st of January, new regulations will come into effect which eliminate an annual leave bonus for people who put off marrying until the age of 23 for women and 25 for men, the South China Morning Post reports.
paras.zh: 据《南华早报》报道，一月一日起，新规定将开始生效，取消对女性推迟到二十三岁、男性推迟到二十五岁才结婚的人给的年假奖励。

paras.en: The holiday bonus was designed to encourage young people to delay getting married in line with China’s one-child policy.
paras.zh: 这项假期奖励原本是为了配合中国的独生子女政策，鼓励年轻人晚婚。

paras.en: But with that policy now being abolished, this holiday incentive is no longer necessary, the government says.
paras.zh: 但政府说，既然这项政策已经废除，这项假期奖励也就没有必要了。

paras.en: In Shanghai, a young couple at a marriage registration office told the paper that they decided to register their marriage as soon as possible to take advantage of the existing policy because an extra holiday was a big deal for them.
paras.zh: 在上海，婚姻登记处的一对年轻情侣告诉该报，他们决定尽快登记结婚，赶上现行政策，因为多一段假期对他们来说可是件大事。

paras.en: In Beijing, one registration office had about 300 couples seeking to get married the day after the changes were announced, rather than the usual number of between seventy and eighty.
paras.zh: 在北京，变化宣布后的第二天，一家登记处有大约三百对情侣前来登记结婚，而平时只有七八十对。

paras.en: But one lawyer tells the paper that the changes still have to be adopted by local governments and these procedures take time, so people who are rushing to register for marriage can relax.
paras.zh: 但一位律师告诉该报，这些变化还要地方政府采纳，这些程序需要时间，所以急着登记结婚的人可以放松一下。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What was the purpose of the annual leave bonus in China?
paras.zh: 第三题：中国的年假奖励是为了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What do we learn about the new regulations?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于新规定，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Everyone loves a good house party, but the cleaning up the next morning isn’t as enjoyable.
paras.zh: 人人都喜欢一场好玩的家庭聚会，可第二天早上收拾残局就没那么开心了。

paras.en: Now, however, a New Zealand-based start-up company aims to bring messy homes and even splitting headaches back to normal.
paras.zh: 不过现在，一家总部在新西兰的初创公司打算把乱糟糟的家，甚至头痛欲裂的人，都恢复正常。

paras.en: The properly named Startup Morning After Maids was launched about a month ago in Auckland by roommates Rebecca Foley and Catherine Ashurst.
paras.zh: 这家名副其实、叫“第二天早上女佣”的初创公司，大约一个月前由室友丽贝卡·福利和凯瑟琳·阿什赫斯特在奥克兰创办。

paras.en: Aside from cleaning up, the two will also cook breakfast and even get coffee and painkillers for recovering merrymakers.
paras.zh: 除了打扫卫生，两人还会做早餐，甚至给宿醉未醒的狂欢者买咖啡和止痛药。

paras.en: Although they are both gainfully employed, they fit cleaning jobs into their nights and weekends, which is when their service is in most demand anyway.
paras.zh: 两人虽然都有正式工作，但她们把清洁活儿安排在晚上和周末，反正这正是她们的服务最抢手的时候。

paras.en: Besides being flooded with requests from across the country, Foley and Ashurst have also received requests from the US and Canada to provide services there.
paras.zh: 除了全国各地的请求像潮水一样涌来，福利和阿什赫斯特还收到了来自美国和加拿大的请求，希望她们去那里提供服务。

paras.en: They are reportedly meeting with lawyers to see how best to take the business forward.
paras.zh: 据报道，她们正在和律师见面，看看怎样把生意做得更好。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is the news report mainly about?
paras.zh: 第五题：这篇新闻报道主要讲什么？

paras.en: Question six: What is a common problem with a house party?
paras.zh: 第六题：家庭聚会常见的问题是什么？

paras.en: Question 7: What are Rebecca Foley and Catherine Ashurst planning to do?
paras.zh: 第七题：丽贝卡·福利和凯瑟琳·阿什赫斯特打算做什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation 1.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Kyle, how did your driver’s theory exam go?
paras.zh: 凯尔，你的驾驶理论考试考得怎么样？

paras.en: It was yesterday, right?
paras.zh: 是昨天考的，对吧？

paras.en: Yes, I prepared as much as I could, but I was so nervous since it was my second try.
paras.zh: 是啊，我尽了最大努力去准备，可还是特别紧张，因为这是我第二次考了。

paras.en: The people who worked at the test center were very kind, though.
paras.zh: 不过考试中心的工作人员都很和气。

paras.en: We had a little conversation, which calmed me down a bit, and that was just what I needed.
paras.zh: 我们聊了几句，让我平静了一点，这正是我需要的。

paras.en: Then, after the exam, they printed out my result, but I was afraid to open it until I was outside.
paras.zh: 考完以后，他们把成绩打印出来，可我一直不敢打开，到了外面才敢看。

paras.en: It was such a relief to pass.
paras.zh: 考过了，真是松了一口气。

paras.en: Congratulations.
paras.zh: 祝贺你。

paras.en: I knew you could do it.
paras.zh: 我就知道你能行。

paras.en: I guess you underestimated how difficult it would be the first time, didn’t you?
paras.zh: 我猜你第一次低估了考试的难度，是不是？

paras.en: I hear a lot of people make that mistake and go in underprepared.
paras.zh: 我听说很多人都犯这个错，没准备好就去考了。

paras.en: But good job in passing the second time.
paras.zh: 不过第二次考过了，真棒。

paras.en: I’m so proud of you.
paras.zh: 我真为你骄傲。

paras.en: Now, all you have to do next is your road test.
paras.zh: 现在你下一步只要考路考就行了。

paras.en: Have you had any lessons yet?
paras.zh: 你上过课了吗？

paras.en: Yes, thanks.
paras.zh: 上过了，谢谢。

paras.en: I’m so happy to be actually on the road now.
paras.zh: 现在真的上路开车了，我好开心。

paras.en: I’ve only had two driving lessons so far, and my instructor is very understanding.
paras.zh: 到目前为止我只上了两节驾驶课，我的教练很体谅人。

w.m: adj. 体谅人的；通情达理的

paras.en: So I’m really enjoying it, and I can’t wait for my next session, although the lessons are rather expensive.
paras.zh: 所以我真的很喜欢，等不及要上下一节课了，虽然课挺贵的。

paras.en: Twenty pounds an hour and the instructor says I’ll need about thirty to forty lessons in total.
paras.zh: 一小时二十英镑，教练说我总共要上三四十节课。

paras.en: That’s what, six to eight hundred pounds?
paras.zh: 那得多少，六到八百英镑？

paras.en: So, this time I’ll need to make a lot more effort and hopefully we’ll be successful the first time.
paras.zh: 所以这次我得更加努力，希望第一次就能考过。

paras.en: Well, good luck.
paras.zh: 好吧，祝你好运。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What did the man do yesterday?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士昨天做了什么？

paras.en: Question nine: Why did he fail the exam the first time?
paras.zh: 第九题：他第一次为什么没考过？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the man say about his driving lessons?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于驾驶课，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question eleven: What does the man hope to do next?
paras.zh: 第十一题：男士希望接下来做什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Emma, I got accepted to the University of Leeds.
paras.zh: 埃玛，我被利兹大学录取了。

paras.en: Since you’re going to university in England, do you know how much it is for international students to study there?
paras.zh: 你要去英国上大学，那你知道留学生在那里读书要花多少钱吗？

paras.en: Congratulations.
paras.zh: 恭喜啊。

paras.en: Yes, I believe for international students you’ll have to pay around thirteen thousand pounds a year.
paras.zh: 知道，我记得留学生一年大概要交一万三千英镑。

paras.en: It’s just a bit more than the local students.
paras.zh: 只比本地学生多一点。

paras.en: Okay, so that’s about $17,000 for the tuition and fees.
paras.zh: 好的，那学费和杂费加起来大约一万七千美元。

paras.en: Anyway, I’m only going to be there for a year, doing my master’s, so it’s pretty good.
paras.zh: 反正我只在那儿待一年，读硕士，所以挺划算的。

paras.en: If I stayed in the US, it’d take two years and cost at least $50,000 in tuition alone.
paras.zh: 要是我留在美国，得读两年，光学费就至少五万美元。

paras.en: Also, I’ve a good chance of winning a scholarship at Leeds, which would be pretty awesome.
paras.zh: 而且我很有希望拿到利兹的奖学金，那就太棒了。

paras.en: The benefits of being a music genius.
paras.zh: 这就是当音乐天才的好处。

paras.en: Yeah, I heard you’re a talented piano player.
paras.zh: 是啊，我听说你钢琴弹得很好。

paras.en: So you’re doing a postgraduate degree now?
paras.zh: 那你现在在读研究生吗？

paras.en: I’m still in my last year, graduating next June.
paras.zh: 我还在读大四，明年六月毕业。

paras.en: Finally, I’ll be done with my studies and could go on to earning loads of money.
paras.zh: 我终于要读完书了，可以去挣大钱了。

paras.en: Are you still planning on being a teacher?
paras.zh: 你还打算当老师吗？

paras.en: No money in that job, then.
paras.zh: 那这份工作可挣不了钱啊。

paras.en: You’d be surprised.
paras.zh: 那你就想错了。

paras.en: I’m still going to be a teacher, but the plan is to work at an international school overseas after I get a year or so of experience in England.
paras.zh: 我还是要当老师，不过打算先在英国积累一年左右的经验，再去海外的国际学校工作。

paras.en: It’s better pay and I get to travel.
paras.zh: 那里工资更高，我还能去旅行。

paras.en: Which reminds me, I’m late for my class, and I’ve got some documents I need to print out first.
paras.zh: 说到这个，我上课要迟到了，还有些文件得先打印出来。

paras.en: I’d better run.
paras.zh: 我得赶紧走了。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What does the man want to know?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士想知道什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What is the man going to do?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士打算做什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What might qualify the man for a scholarship at Leeds University?
paras.zh: 第十四题：什么可能让男士有资格拿到利兹大学的奖学金？

paras.en: Question 15: What is the woman planning to do after graduation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士毕业后打算做什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Scientists have identified thousands of known ant species around the world, and only a few of them bug humans.
paras.zh: 科学家已经认出了世界各地几千种已知的蚂蚁，其中只有少数几种会烦扰人类。

paras.en: Most ants live in the woods or out in nature.
paras.zh: 大多数蚂蚁生活在树林里或者野外。

paras.en: There, they keep other creatures in check, distribute seeds, and clean dead and decaying materials from the ground.
paras.zh: 在那里，它们能控制其他生物的数量、传播种子，还能清理地上死去和腐烂的东西。

paras.en: A very small percentage of ants do harm to humans, but those are incredibly challenging to control.
paras.zh: 只有很小一部分蚂蚁会危害人类，但这些蚂蚁极难控制。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: They are small enough to easily slip inside your house, live in colonies that number in the tens of thousands to the hundreds of thousands, and reproduce quickly.
paras.zh: 它们个头小，很容易溜进你家；它们群居，一群有几万到几十万只；而且繁殖得很快。

paras.en: That makes them good at getting in and hard to kick out.
paras.zh: 所以它们很容易钻进来，却很难赶出去。

paras.en: Once they settle in, these insects start affecting your home.
paras.zh: 它们一旦安顿下来，就开始影响你的家。

paras.en: In addition to biting ants, other species can cause different kinds of damage.
paras.zh: 除了会咬人的蚂蚁，其他种类也会造成各种损害。

paras.en: Some, like carpenter ants, can undermine a home’s structure, while others interfere with electrical units.
paras.zh: 有些蚂蚁，比如木匠蚁，会破坏房屋的结构，还有些会干扰电器设备。

paras.en: Unfortunately, our homes are very attractive to ants, because they provide everything the colony needs to survive, such as food, water and shelter.
paras.zh: 不幸的是，我们的家对蚂蚁很有吸引力，因为家里能提供蚁群生存所需的一切，比如食物、水和栖身之处。

paras.en: So how can we prevent ants from getting into our homes?
paras.zh: 那么我们怎样才能不让蚂蚁进家门呢？

paras.en: Most important of all, avoid giving ants any access to food, particularly sugary food, because ants have a sweet tooth.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，别让蚂蚁接触到任何食物，尤其是含糖的食物，因为蚂蚁爱吃甜食。

paras.en: We also need to clean up spills as soon as they occur and store food in airtight containers.
paras.zh: 我们还要把洒出来的东西一出现就清理干净，把食物放在密封的容器里。

paras.en: Even garbage attracts ants, so empty your trash as often as possible and store your outside garbage in a lidded can, well away from doors and windows.
paras.zh: 连垃圾都会招蚂蚁，所以要尽量勤倒垃圾，屋外的垃圾要放在带盖的垃圾桶里，离门窗远一点。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the passage say about ants?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于蚂蚁，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What do we learn from the passage about carpenter ants?
paras.zh: 第十七题：从短文中，我们对木匠蚁了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What can we do to prevent ants from getting into our homes?
paras.zh: 第十八题：我们怎样做才能不让蚂蚁进家门？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: My research focus is on what happens to our immune system as we age.
paras.zh: 我的研究重点是，随着年龄增长，我们的免疫系统会发生什么变化。

paras.en: So the job of the immune system is to fight infections.
paras.zh: 免疫系统的作用就是抵抗感染。

paras.en: It also protects us from viruses and from autoimmune diseases.
paras.zh: 它还保护我们不受病毒和自身免疫病的侵害。

paras.en: We know that as we get older, it’s easier for us to get infections.
paras.zh: 我们知道，人年纪越大，就越容易感染。

paras.en: So older adults have more chances of falling ill.
paras.zh: 所以老年人生病的可能性更大。

paras.en: This is evidence that our immune system really doesn’t function so well when we age.
paras.zh: 这说明，人老了以后，免疫系统确实没那么好用了。

paras.en: In most of our work, when we’re looking at older adults who’ve got an illness, we always have to have health controls.
paras.zh: 在我们的大部分工作中，研究患病的老年人时，总要有健康的对照组。

paras.en: So we work very closely with a great group of volunteers called the 1000 Elders.
paras.zh: 所以我们和一群很棒的志愿者合作得非常紧密，他们叫“千名长者”。

paras.en: These volunteers are all 65 or over, but in good health.
paras.zh: 这些志愿者都在六十五岁以上，但身体都很健康。

paras.en: They come to the university to provide us with blood samples, to be interviewed, and to help us carry out a whole range of research.
paras.zh: 他们来大学给我们提供血样、接受访谈，还帮我们开展各种各样的研究。

paras.en: The real impact of our research is going to be on health in old age.
paras.zh: 我们研究的真正影响将体现在老年人的健康上。

paras.en: At the moment, we’re living much longer.
paras.zh: 现在，我们的寿命长多了。

paras.en: Life expectancy is increasing at two years for every decade.
paras.zh: 人的预期寿命每十年增加两年。

paras.en: That means an extra five hours a day.
paras.zh: 也就是说每天多出五个小时。

paras.en: I want to make sure that older adults are still able to enjoy their old age and that they’re not spending time in hospital with infections, feeling unwell, and being generally weak.
paras.zh: 我希望确保老年人仍然能享受晚年，不会因为感染住在医院里，身体不舒服，整个人都很虚弱。

paras.en: We want people to be healthy, even when they are old.
paras.zh: 我们希望人们即使老了也很健康。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What is the focus of the speaker’s research?
paras.zh: 第十九题：说话人的研究重点是什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What are the volunteers asked to do in the research?
paras.zh: 第二十题：志愿者在研究中被要求做什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say will be the impact of his research?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说他的研究会有什么影响？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: When Ted Komada started teaching 14 years ago at Killip Elementary, he didn’t know how to manage a classroom and was struggling to connect with students.
paras.zh: 十四年前，特德·科马达刚到基利普小学教书时，不知道怎么管理课堂，也很难和学生打成一片。

w.m: adj. 初级的（这里指小学）

paras.en: He noticed a couple of days after school that a group of kids would get together to play chess.
paras.zh: 有几天放学后，他注意到有一群孩子会聚在一起下国际象棋。

paras.en: I know how to play chess.
paras.zh: 我会下国际象棋。

paras.en: Let me go and show these kids how to do it, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，我去教这些孩子怎么下。

paras.en: Now, Komada coaches the school’s chess team.
paras.zh: 现在，科马达是学校国际象棋队的教练。

paras.en: The whole program started as a safe place for kids to come after school.
paras.zh: 整个项目一开始是给孩子们放学后找个安全的去处。

paras.en: And this week, dozens of those students are getting ready to head out to Nashville, Tennessee to compete with about 5,000 other young people at the Super Nationals of Chess.
paras.zh: 这周，几十名学生正准备动身去田纳西州的纳什维尔，在国际象棋超级全国赛上和大约五千名年轻人一较高下。

paras.en: The competition only happens every four years.
paras.zh: 这项比赛每四年才举行一次。

paras.en: And the last time the team went, they won the third place in the nation.
paras.zh: 上一次这支队参赛时，拿了全国第三名。

paras.en: Komada says chess gives him and his students control.
paras.zh: 科马达说，国际象棋让他和他的学生都有了掌控感。

paras.en: The school has the highest number of kids from low-income families.
paras.zh: 这所学校来自低收入家庭的孩子最多。

paras.en: Police frequent the area day and night, as two months ago, a young man was shot just down the street.
paras.zh: 警察白天黑夜都在这一带巡逻，因为两个月前，就在街那头，一名年轻男子中枪了。

paras.en: Komada likes to teach his students that they should think about their move before they do it.
paras.zh: 科马达喜欢教学生，走一步棋之前先想一想。

paras.en: The lessons prove valuable outside the classroom as well.
paras.zh: 这些道理在课堂之外也很有用。

paras.en: Many parents see these lessons translate into the real world.
paras.zh: 很多家长看到，这些道理在现实生活中也用上了。

paras.en: Students are more likely to think about their actions and see whether they will lead to trouble.
paras.zh: 学生们更有可能先想想自己的行为，看看会不会惹麻烦。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What did Ted Komada notice one day after he started teaching at Killip Elementary?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：特德·科马达到基利普小学教书后，有一天注意到了什么？

w.m: adj. 初级的（这里指小学）

paras.en: Question 23: What are dozens of students from Komada’s school going to do this week?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：科马达学校的几十名学生这周要去做什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What do we learn about the students of Killip Elementary?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于基利普小学的学生，我们了解到什么？

w.m: adj. 初级的（这里指小学）

paras.en: Question twenty five: What have the students learned from Komada?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：学生们从科马达那里学到了什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2019年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2019年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲法国旅游业因安全担忧、罢工和洪水大幅下滑，今年可能损失十多亿美元的收入。第二篇新闻报道讲一架小飞机冒险飞到南极点科考站，接回两名生病的美国工作人员。第三篇新闻报道讲弗吉尼亚州一名直升机驾驶员用直升机给七岁的儿子拔掉了松动的牙齿。第一段长对话里，快递员保罗要给埃玛送一个大包裹，两人约在后天送货、签收。第二段长对话里，埃米莉两天后就要去意大利留学，心里有些难过，男士安慰她，并说周六尽量去机场送她。第一篇短文介绍意大利的埃特纳火山：喷发历史、山坡上的农业和洞穴，以及山上的动物。第二篇短文里，作家布伦丹·伦纳德说，与其只做自己热爱的事，不如热爱自己做的事，才华离不开努力。第三篇短文里，说话人讲她从小跳芭蕾，工作后中断，后来在亚洲重新爱上萨尔萨舞，用跳舞来减轻压力。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: France is facing potentially more than $1 billion in lost revenue this year due to huge declines in tourism.
paras.zh: 由于旅游业大幅下滑，法国今年可能损失十多亿美元的收入。

paras.en: Safety concerns have been one of the biggest reasons why the country has lost over half a billion in revenue already in the first six months of 2016.
paras.zh: 安全担忧是最主要的原因之一，二〇一六年头六个月，法国的收入已经减少了五亿多。

paras.en: The terror attacks in Paris last November were called Europe’s worst in the past decade.
paras.zh: 去年十一月的巴黎恐怖袭击被称为欧洲近十年来最严重的一次。

paras.en: Besides violence, workers’ strikes and heavy floods are said to have also been why international tourists have stayed away.
paras.zh: 据说除了暴力事件，工人罢工和严重的洪水也是外国游客不来的原因。

paras.en: So far in the Paris region, there’s been a 46% decline in Japanese visitors, 35% fewer Russians, and 27% fewer Italians.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，在巴黎地区，日本游客减少了百分之四十六，俄罗斯游客少了百分之三十五，意大利游客少了百分之二十七。

paras.en: American travelers seem the least affected.
paras.zh: 美国游客似乎受的影响最小。

paras.en: Their numbers have only dropped by roughly 5%.
paras.zh: 他们的人数只下降了大约百分之五。

paras.en: According to the French government, the country is the number one tourist destination in the world, and tourism is extremely important to the French economy.
paras.zh: 据法国政府说，法国是全世界头号旅游目的地，旅游业对法国经济极其重要。

paras.en: The sector represents roughly 9% of its GDP.
paras.zh: 旅游业大约占法国国内生产总值的百分之九。

paras.en: The head of Paris’s Tourism Board said, It’s time to realize that the tourism sector is going through an industrial disaster.
paras.zh: 巴黎旅游局局长说，现在该认识到，旅游业正在经历一场产业灾难。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What accounts most for the huge declines in tourism in France?
paras.zh: 第一题：法国旅游业大幅下滑，最主要的原因是什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What do we learn from the report about tourism in France?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于法国的旅游业，我们从报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A small plane with two sick US workers arrived safely in Chile late Wednesday after leaving Antarctica in a daring rescue mission from a remote South Pole research station.
paras.zh: 一架载着两名生病的美国工作人员的小飞机周三深夜安全抵达智利；此前，它从南极点一个偏远的科考站出发，完成了一次惊险的救援任务，飞离了南极洲。

paras.en: After making a stop for a few hours at a British station on the edge of Antarctica, the two workers were flown to the southernmost Chilean city of Punta Arenas.
paras.zh: 在南极洲边缘的一个英国科考站停了几个小时后，两名工作人员被送上飞机，飞到了智利最南端的城市蓬塔阿雷纳斯。

paras.en: In a chaotic two days of flying, the rescue team flew 3,000 miles round trip from the British station Rothera to pick up the workers at the US Amundsen-Scott station at the South Pole.
paras.zh: 在手忙脚乱的两天飞行里，救援队从英国的罗瑟拉站出发，往返飞了三千英里，去南极点的美国阿蒙森-斯科特站接这两名工作人员。

paras.en: The two patients aboard will be transported to a medical facility that can provide a level of care that is not available at Amundsen-Scott, says a spokesperson.
paras.zh: 一位发言人说，机上的两名病人将被送往一家医疗机构，那里能提供阿蒙森-斯科特站没有的医疗条件。

paras.en: Normally, planes don’t go to the polar post from February to October because of the dangers of flying in the pitch dark and cold.
paras.zh: 平时，二月到十月飞机不去这个极地站，因为在漆黑寒冷中飞行很危险。

paras.en: Antarctica creates a hostile environment, says the operations director for the British Antarctic Survey.
paras.zh: 英国南极调查局的运营主管说，南极洲的环境非常恶劣。

paras.en: If you are not careful, it’ll come round and bite you.
paras.zh: 稍不小心，它就会回过头来咬你一口。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What was the small plane’s mission to Antarctica?
paras.zh: 第三题：小飞机去南极洲执行的是什么任务？

paras.en: Question 4: What makes flying to Antarctica dangerous from February to October?
paras.zh: 第四题：二月到十月飞往南极洲为什么危险？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A pilot from Virginia removed his son’s loose tooth using a helicopter.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚州一名飞行员用直升机拔掉了儿子松动的牙齿。

paras.en: Rick Rahim from Virginia flies helicopters for a living, and when his seven-year-old son’s tooth became loose, he did not waste time by tying it to a door handle.
paras.zh: 弗吉尼亚州的里克·拉希姆以开直升机为生，他七岁的儿子牙齿松了，他没有浪费时间把牙拴在门把手上。

paras.en: Instead, Mr. Rahim tied one end of a string around his son’s tooth and the other end to his full-sized commercial helicopter.
paras.zh: 而是把一根绳子的一头拴在儿子的牙上，另一头拴在他那架正常大小的商用直升机上。

paras.en: The father of four posted a video clip of his playful venture on Facebook, advising parents to do fun and creative stuff with their kids.
paras.zh: 这位四个孩子的父亲在脸书上发了一段这次好玩尝试的视频，建议家长和孩子一起做些有趣、有创意的事。

paras.en: The video shows him launching the helicopter into the air and flying just far enough to successfully remove the loose tooth.
paras.zh: 视频里，他让直升机升空，飞出去一点距离，刚好把松动的牙齿成功拔了下来。

paras.en: At the end of the video, Mr. Rahim assures watchers that the circumstances were safe and that he has 13 years of helicopter flying experience behind him.
paras.zh: 视频最后，拉希姆先生向观众保证，当时的情况很安全，而且他有十三年驾驶直升机的经验。

paras.en: You’ve got to do everything safe in life, and that’s what I did today, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，人生中做什么都得安全，我今天就是这么做的。

paras.en: Mr. Rahim later said that although some parents have used remote control helicopters to pull teeth before, he might be the first to use a full-sized aircraft, as he can’t find evidence that it has been done before.
paras.zh: 拉希姆先生后来说，虽然以前有家长用过遥控直升机拔牙，但他可能是第一个用正常大小的飞机拔牙的人，因为他找不到以前有人这么做过的证据。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: How did Rick Rahim remove his son’s loose tooth?
paras.zh: 第五题：里克·拉希姆是怎么拔掉儿子松动的牙齿的？

paras.en: Question six: What does the news report say about Rick Rahim?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于里克·拉希姆，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question 7: What did Rick Rahim advise parents to do with their kids?
paras.zh: 第七题：里克·拉希姆建议家长和孩子一起做什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hi, Emma speaking.
paras.zh: 喂，我是埃玛。

paras.en: Who’s this?
paras.zh: 请问您是哪位？

paras.en: Hi, Emma.
paras.zh: 你好，埃玛。

paras.en: I’m Paul from Hermes Delivery Service.
paras.zh: 我是赫尔墨斯快递公司的保罗。

paras.en: Here’s a package for you.
paras.zh: 这儿有您一个包裹。

paras.en: Are you at home to collect it?
paras.zh: 您在家吗？可以来取一下吗？

paras.en: Oh, sorry, Paul.
paras.zh: 哦，不好意思，保罗。

paras.en: I’m out at the moment.
paras.zh: 我现在不在家。

paras.en: Can you put it in my mailbox?
paras.zh: 你能把它放进我的信箱吗？

paras.en: I’m afraid I can’t do that.
paras.zh: 恐怕不行。

paras.en: Sorry.
paras.zh: 不好意思。

paras.en: The package is too big and it needs a signature to confirm you have received it.
paras.zh: 包裹太大了，而且需要您签名，确认您已经收到。

paras.en: So I would need to deliver it at a time when you’re in.
paras.zh: 所以我得等您在家的时候再送。

paras.en: Okay, well, I’m out all day today, but I should be in tomorrow morning before I go out for lunch, and then I’ll be at home again later in the afternoon.
paras.zh: 好吧，我今天一整天都不在家，不过明天上午我出去吃午饭之前应该在家，下午晚些时候我也会回家。

paras.en: Will either of those times be convenient for you?
paras.zh: 这两个时间您有方便的吗？

paras.en: They’re not, unfortunately.
paras.zh: 不巧，都不方便。

paras.en: I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 不好意思。

paras.en: I won’t be in the area tomorrow, as I have some other deliveries to make on the other side of town.
paras.zh: 我明天不在这一带，因为我要去城的另一头送别的货。

paras.en: I could come the day after, if that suits you.
paras.zh: 后天我可以来，要是您方便的话。

paras.en: Okay, yes, that should be fine.
paras.zh: 好的，可以，那应该没问题。

paras.en: I have a friend coming round in the afternoon, but I’ll be at home, so the day after tomorrow will be great.
paras.zh: 我下午有个朋友要来，不过我会在家，所以后天正好。

paras.en: Do I need to pay for the package?
paras.zh: 这个包裹我需要付钱吗？

paras.en: No, you don’t.
paras.zh: 不用。

paras.en: It says here that you paid for it when you ordered it online.
paras.zh: 这上面写着，您网上下单的时候已经付过钱了。

paras.en: Oh, yes, I did.
paras.zh: 哦，对，我付过。

paras.en: I got mixed up.
paras.zh: 我搞混了。

paras.en: So you just need to sign the form to say you’ve received it.
paras.zh: 所以您只要签个单子，说明您已经收到就行了。

paras.en: Okay, great.
paras.zh: 好的，太好了。

paras.en: See you the day after tomorrow, then.
paras.zh: 那就后天见。

paras.en: Yes, see you then.
paras.zh: 好的，到时候见。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: Why is the man making the phone call?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士为什么打这个电话？

paras.en: Question nine: Why can’t the woman meet the man today?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士今天为什么不能和男士见面？

paras.en: Question 10: Why is the man unable to see the woman tomorrow?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士明天为什么见不了女士？

paras.en: Question 11: What should the woman do to receive her purchase?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士要做什么才能收到她买的东西？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi, Emily.
paras.zh: 嗨，埃米莉。

paras.en: I hear you’re leaving for Italy soon.
paras.zh: 听说你很快就要去意大利了。

paras.en: Do you plan to have a going-away party before you disappear?
paras.zh: 你走之前打算办个送别聚会吗？

paras.en: It’d be really nice for us to hang out together before you go.
paras.zh: 你走之前，我们能一起出去玩玩就太好了。

paras.en: I’m not sure.
paras.zh: 我不确定。

paras.en: I’m leaving in just two more days, and I’m going to miss all my friends here, and especially this place.
paras.zh: 我再过两天就走了，我会想念这里所有的朋友，尤其是这个地方。

paras.en: Why don’t you come over?
paras.zh: 你怎么不过来坐坐？

paras.en: I’m feeling rather sad, actually.
paras.zh: 其实我挺难过的。

paras.en: I’m currently sitting alone at a table outside the Black Cat Cafe, listening to the rain and watching people passing by.
paras.zh: 我现在一个人坐在黑猫咖啡馆外面的一张桌子旁，听着雨声，看着来来往往的行人。

paras.en: I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 不好意思。

paras.en: I can’t just now.
paras.zh: 我现在去不了。

paras.en: I need to get this assignment finished by Monday, and I’m way behind.
paras.zh: 我得在周一前把这份作业做完，我落下了一大截。

paras.en: Anyhow, cheer up.
paras.zh: 不管怎样，开心点。

paras.en: You’re not leaving for good, and you’ll absolutely love Italy.
paras.zh: 你又不是一去不回，而且你一定会非常喜欢意大利的。

paras.en: Yeah, you’re right.
paras.zh: 是啊，你说得对。

paras.en: But I just feel like I’m not quite ready to go, and studying in a foreign country seems a bit overwhelming.
paras.zh: 可我就是觉得自己还没完全准备好，去国外读书好像有点让人招架不住。

w.m: adj. 让人招架不住的；压倒性的

paras.en: Just think of your life in Milan.
paras.zh: 你就想想在米兰的生活吧。

paras.en: In the mornings, you can go down to a small local cafe, soaking up the sun’s rays and drinking coffee.
paras.zh: 早上，你可以去本地的一家小咖啡馆，晒着太阳，喝着咖啡。

paras.en: I envy you.
paras.zh: 我好羡慕你。

paras.en: You can buy lots of gorgeous Italian clothes.
paras.zh: 你可以买好多漂亮的意大利衣服。

paras.en: That does sound nice.
paras.zh: 听起来确实不错。

paras.en: And of course, I can keep in touch with everyone through Facebook.
paras.zh: 当然，我还可以通过脸书和大家保持联系。

paras.en: Maybe you can all come visit me.
paras.zh: 说不定你们都可以来看我。

paras.en: Of course we will.
paras.zh: 我们当然会去。

paras.en: When is your flight?
paras.zh: 你的航班是什么时候？

paras.en: On Saturday, after lunch, at 1:45.
paras.zh: 周六，吃完午饭，一点四十五分。

paras.en: Okay, I’ll try and come to the airport on Saturday to see you off.
paras.zh: 好，周六我尽量去机场送你。

paras.en: I’ll give you a call that morning, no matter what.
paras.zh: 不管怎样，那天上午我都会给你打个电话。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What is the woman going to do?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士打算做什么？

paras.en: Question 13: How does the woman feel at the moment?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士现在心情怎么样？

paras.en: Question fourteen: Why can’t the man meet the woman now?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士现在为什么不能和女士见面？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What will the man possibly do on Saturday?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士周六可能会做什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Mount Etna is one of the most active volcanoes on earth.
paras.zh: 埃特纳火山是地球上最活跃的火山之一。

paras.en: The mountain has been in a state of near-continuous eruption for half a million years.
paras.zh: 五十万年来，这座山几乎一直在不断喷发。

paras.en: Exploring the Etna geographical area reveals a history written in fire.
paras.zh: 探索埃特纳火山一带，你会看到一部用火写成的历史。

paras.en: Before the eruptions it was covered by forests of pine trees.
paras.zh: 在喷发之前，这里覆盖着一片片松树林。

paras.en: Located in southern Italy, Etna is the highest active volcano in Europe.
paras.zh: 埃特纳火山位于意大利南部，是欧洲最高的活火山。

paras.en: However, its height often changes when volcanic material accumulates during eruptions and subsequently collapses.
paras.zh: 不过，喷发时火山物质不断堆积，随后又会坍塌，所以它的高度经常变化。

paras.en: Few volcanoes in the world have an eruption history so thoroughly documented by historical records.
paras.zh: 世界上很少有火山的喷发史被史料记载得这么详细。

paras.en: Etna’s eruption history dates back as far as 1500 BC.
paras.zh: 埃特纳火山的喷发史可以追溯到公元前一五〇〇年。

paras.en: Some 200 eruptions have been recorded down through the centuries, but compared with other volcanoes, most of its eruptions have so far been fairly light in terms of death and destruction.
paras.zh: 几百年来，有记录的喷发大约有两百次，但和其他火山相比，到目前为止，它的大部分喷发造成的死亡和破坏都比较轻。

paras.en: Only about 100 deaths have been attributed to the volcano.
paras.zh: 只有大约一百人的死亡被认为是这座火山造成的。

paras.en: The mountain hasn’t been entirely harmless, however.
paras.zh: 不过，这座山也并不是完全无害。

paras.en: In 1928 it destroyed the town of Mascali.
paras.zh: 一九二八年，它毁掉了马斯卡利镇。

paras.en: Over the centuries, Etna’s lower slopes have been shaped by human hands to take advantage of rich soils for growing grapes, apples and nuts.
paras.zh: 几百年来，人们改造了埃特纳火山较低的山坡，利用肥沃的土壤种葡萄、苹果和坚果。

paras.en: Local people have also carved out over 200 caves in the soft rock and used them for everything from sacred burial places to food storage.
paras.zh: 当地人还在松软的岩石上凿出了两百多个洞穴，从神圣的墓地到储存食物，什么都用它们。

paras.en: Large mammals once wandered the volcano’s slopes, but today foxes, wild cats, rabbits and mice are more common.
paras.zh: 以前，大型哺乳动物曾在火山的山坡上游荡，但如今狐狸、野猫、兔子和老鼠更常见。

paras.en: Some of those small mammals help to sustain such big birds as golden eagles.
paras.zh: 其中一些小型哺乳动物养活了像金雕这样的大型鸟类。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What does the speaker say about Mount Etna?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于埃特纳火山，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What do we learn about the lower slopes of Mount Etna?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于埃特纳火山较低的山坡，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker say about big birds like golden eagles at Mount Etna?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于埃特纳火山上金雕这样的大型鸟类，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: My name is Brendan Leonard, and I’m an author, magazine writer, filmmaker, and public speaker.
paras.zh: 我叫布伦丹·伦纳德，是一名作家、杂志撰稿人、电影人，也是公众演讲者。

paras.en: I’m self-employed, which means I work for myself and I do what I love.
paras.zh: 我是自由职业者，也就是说，我给自己打工，做自己热爱的事。

w.m: adj. 自由职业的；自己经营的

paras.en: We have a popular saying in America, which goes, do what you love and you’ll never work a day in your life.
paras.zh: 在美国有句俗话说得好：做你热爱的事，你这辈子就一天也不用工作。

paras.en: But I’m here to tell you that instead of focusing on doing what we love, I think we should focus on loving what we do.
paras.zh: 但我在这里想告诉大家，与其把心思放在做自己热爱的事上，我觉得我们更应该热爱自己做的事。

paras.en: In my line of work, you hear a lot about talent, which is an idea we’ve mostly invented to give ourselves an excuse to be lazy.
paras.zh: 在我这一行，你会经常听人说起天赋，可这个概念基本上是我们自己编出来的，好给偷懒找借口。

paras.en: Here’s why.
paras.zh: 原因是这样的。

paras.en: If you see someone doing something really well, you would say it’s because they’re talented.
paras.zh: 要是你看到有人把一件事做得特别好，你会说那是因为他们有天赋。

paras.en: You think they’re somehow special.
paras.zh: 你觉得他们有点与众不同。

w.m: adv. 以某种方式；不知怎么地

paras.en: You discount the tremendous amount of work they’ve done to get to where they are.
paras.zh: 你忽视了他们为走到今天付出的大量努力。

paras.en: Research has shown that talent is nothing without hard work.
paras.zh: 研究表明，没有努力，天赋什么都不是。

paras.en: I choose to believe in hard work, but not so much in talent.
paras.zh: 我选择相信努力，不太相信天赋。

paras.en: There are no special people, just people who put in enough hard work until something special happens.
paras.zh: 没有什么特别的人，只有一直努力、直到好事发生的人。

paras.en: I can promise you one thing.
paras.zh: 有一件事我可以向你保证。

paras.en: Whatever you choose to do for a career, if you work hard at it, eventually special things will happen.
paras.zh: 不管你选择干哪一行，只要你努力去做，最终都会有好事发生。

paras.en: They may not happen as quickly as you’d like them to, and they may turn out to be completely different from the special things you imagined at the beginning, but they will happen.
paras.zh: 这些好事可能不会像你希望的那么快到来，也可能和你一开始想象的完全不同，但它们一定会发生。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn about the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于说话人，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What is the speaker’s advice to his audience?
paras.zh: 第二十题：说话人给听众的建议是什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say about talent?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于天赋，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: A question we often ask others and are also frequently asked by others is, what do you normally do after school or work?
paras.zh: 我们常问别人、也常被别人问的一个问题是：你放学或下班后一般做什么？

paras.en: Some commonplace answers are, well, I go to the gym.
paras.zh: 一些常见的回答是：嗯，我去健身房。

paras.en: Um I just go home and watch TV.
paras.zh: 嗯，我就回家看电视。

paras.en: I meet my friends for dinner.
paras.zh: 我约朋友吃晚饭。

paras.en: Or I just go to bed because it’s so late and I’m tired.
paras.zh: 或者我直接上床睡觉，因为太晚了，我很累。

paras.en: Unlike any of these typical responses, I’m proud to say that I love to dance salsa after a long and tiring day of work.
paras.zh: 和这些典型的回答都不一样，我可以自豪地说，工作了漫长又累人的一天之后，我喜欢跳萨尔萨舞。

paras.en: Salsa is a kind of dancing that evolved in the mid-1970s in New York.
paras.zh: 萨尔萨舞是七十年代中期在纽约发展起来的一种舞蹈。

paras.en: My dancing life began not because I wanted to do it, but because my mother was sick and tired of seeing me running around after school doing nothing.
paras.zh: 我开始跳舞，并不是因为我想跳，而是因为我妈妈实在看不惯我放学后到处乱跑、无所事事。

paras.en: So she enrolled me into a ballet course when I was six.
paras.zh: 所以在我六岁时，她给我报了一个芭蕾舞班。

paras.en: I fell in love with it instantly and continued with ballet dancing for about ten years.
paras.zh: 我立刻就爱上了芭蕾，一跳就是十年左右。

paras.en: Then, I left my native country of New Zealand to start my career as an English teacher, which eventually brought my dancing life to a halt.
paras.zh: 后来，我离开祖国新西兰，开始了英语老师的职业生涯，跳舞这件事也就因此停了下来。

paras.en: It wasn’t until I rediscovered salsa in a lovely studio while working in Asia that I renewed my passion for dancing.
paras.zh: 直到在亚洲工作时，我在一间可爱的舞蹈室里重新发现了萨尔萨舞，才重新燃起了对跳舞的热情。

paras.en: Since then, I have been trying to attend dancing classes twice a week after work.
paras.zh: 从那以后，我一直尽量每周下班后上两次舞蹈课。

paras.en: It’s a great way for me to relieve stress and pressure and dance my way towards feeling energetic and happy again.
paras.zh: 这是我缓解压力的好办法，跳着跳着，我又变得精力充沛、开开心心的。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What does the speaker say about the dance salsa?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于萨尔萨舞，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: Why did the speaker’s mother enroll her in a ballet course?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：说话人的妈妈为什么给她报了芭蕾舞班？

paras.en: Question 24: When did the speaker’s dancing life come to a halt?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：说话人的舞蹈生涯是什么时候停下来的？

paras.en: Question 25: In what way has salsa dancing benefited the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：跳萨尔萨舞给说话人带来了什么好处？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
