passages.name: 2019年12月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲纽约展望公园里一头走失的牛在街头和公园里闲逛，成了游客围观的对象，警察用麻醉箭把它放倒后交给了动物管理部门。第二篇新闻报道讲美国国家自然历史博物馆将翻修化石馆，翻修期间特别展区免费开放，本周展出澳大利亚古代壁画，下周举办年度野生动物摄影师大赛。第三篇新闻报道讲法国一座历史主题公园训练了六只秃鼻乌鸦捡垃圾，有些家长担心孩子会故意乱扔垃圾。第一段长对话里，女士介绍想制作的电视节目《科学国度》，并向对方申请两百万美元的资金支持。第二段长对话里，男士觉得自己一事无成，女士劝他正视错误、肯定每一点进步，只跟过去的自己比。第一篇短文讲单一性别教育对女生的好处。第二篇短文讲西雅图其实雨量不多，只是下雨的日子多、雨也小。第三篇短文讲运动后肌肉酸痛的原因、身体修复的过程和缓解的办法。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: New York City police captured a cow on the loose in Prospect Park on Tuesday after the animal became an attraction for tourists while walking along the streets and enjoying the park facilities.
paras.zh: 周二，纽约市警方在展望公园抓住了一头走失的牛。这头牛在街上溜达、在公园里四处游玩，成了吸引游客的一道风景。

w.m: n. 吸引人的事物；看点

paras.en: The confused creature and camera-holding humans stared at each other through a fence for several minutes.
paras.zh: 这头一脸茫然的牛和举着相机的人们隔着栅栏对视了好几分钟。

paras.en: At other times the cow wandered around the five hundred twenty six acre park and the artificial grass field normally used for human sporting events.
paras.zh: 其他时候，这头牛在占地五百二十六英亩的公园里四处游荡，还跑上了平时供人举办体育赛事的人造草坪场地。

paras.en: Officers used soccer goals to fence the animal in.
paras.zh: 警察用足球球门把这头牛围了起来。

paras.en: However, the cow then moved through one of the nets, knocking down a police officer in the process.
paras.zh: 然而，这头牛随后从一张球网中钻了出去，还顺带撞倒了一名警察。

paras.en: Police eventually trapped the cow between two vehicles parked on either side of a baseball field’s bench area.
paras.zh: 最后，警察把这头牛困在了停在棒球场替补席两侧的两辆车之间。

w.m: n. 长凳；（运动员的）替补席

paras.en: An officer then shot an arrow to put it to sleep.
paras.zh: 接着，一名警察射出一支麻醉箭让它睡着。

paras.en: Then officers waited for the drug to take effect.
paras.zh: 然后警察们等着药效发作。

paras.en: After it fell asleep, they loaded the cow into a horse trailer.
paras.zh: 牛睡着以后，他们把它装进了一辆运马拖车。

paras.en: It was not clear where the cow came from or how it got lost.
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚这头牛是从哪儿来的，又是怎么走丢的。

paras.en: Police turned it over to the animal control department after they caught it.
paras.zh: 抓到牛以后，警方把它移交给了动物管理部门。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What happened in New York’s Prospect Park on Tuesday?
paras.zh: 第一题：周二在纽约的展望公园发生了什么事？

paras.en: Question two: What do we learn about the cow from the end of the news report?
paras.zh: 第二题：从新闻报道的结尾，我们对这头牛了解到什么？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Starting April 28th of this year, the National Museum of Natural History will begin renovating its fossil hall.
paras.zh: 从今年四月二十八日起，美国国家自然历史博物馆将开始翻修化石馆。

paras.en: The fossil hall, which displays some of the world’s oldest and largest fossil specimens, receives more than two million visitors each year.
paras.zh: 化石馆展出的是一些世界上最古老、最大的化石标本，每年接待两百多万名游客。

paras.en: It’s one of the museum’s most famous attractions.
paras.zh: 它是这家博物馆最有名的看点之一。

w.m: n. 吸引人的事物；看点

paras.en: As a result, the museum plans to expand the hall as well as add to its ancient birds collection.
paras.zh: 因此，博物馆计划扩建这个展厅，同时充实古鸟类藏品。

paras.en: Bird lovers, both young and old, have already responded with excitement at the news.
paras.zh: 喜爱鸟类的人们，不管老少，都已经对这个消息表现得十分兴奋。

paras.en: The museum’s social media account has been flooded with messages of support.
paras.zh: 博物馆的社交媒体账号收到了潮水般的支持留言。

paras.en: In the meantime, the current collection will be closed.
paras.zh: 在此期间，现有的藏品将停止展出。

paras.en: However, visitors will be compensated during the closure.
paras.zh: 不过，闭馆期间游客会得到补偿。

paras.en: The museum’s special exhibition area will now be free of charge.
paras.zh: 博物馆的特别展区现在将免费开放。

paras.en: This week the Resident Exhibition is a display of ancient wall paintings on loan from Australia.
paras.zh: 本周常设展厅展出的是从澳大利亚借来的古代壁画。

paras.en: They celebrate the cultural heritage of the country and will be available to view until Sunday.
paras.zh: 这些壁画展现了这个国家的文化遗产，展期到周日为止。

w.m: adj. 可获得的；可看到的

paras.en: Next week the exhibition will be taken over by the Wildlife Photographer of the Year competition.
paras.zh: 下周，展厅将由年度野生动物摄影师大赛接手。

paras.en: The winner of this year’s competition will be awarded a preview of the new fossil hall as well as a cash prize.
paras.zh: 今年比赛的冠军将获得提前参观新化石馆的机会和一笔奖金。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What does the news report say about the fossil hall of the National Museum of Natural History?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于国家自然历史博物馆的化石馆，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question 4: What is on display this week in the museum’s resident exhibition hall?
paras.zh: 第四题：本周博物馆常设展厅展出的是什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Six birds have just been trained to pick up rubbish at a French historical theme park.
paras.zh: 法国一座历史主题公园刚刚训练了六只鸟来捡垃圾。

paras.en: According to the park’s manager, mister Villier, The goal is not just to clear up the park.
paras.zh: 公园经理维利耶先生说，这样做的目的不只是清理公园。

paras.en: He says visitors are already good at keeping things clean.
paras.zh: 他说游客们本来就很注意保持干净。

paras.en: Instead, he wants to show that nature itself can teach us to take care of the environment.
paras.zh: 他其实是想表明，大自然本身就能教会我们爱护环境。

paras.en: He says that rooks, the chosen birds, are considered to be particularly intelligent.
paras.zh: 他说，被选中的秃鼻乌鸦被认为特别聪明。

paras.en: In the right circumstances, they even like to communicate with humans and establish a relationship through play.
paras.zh: 在合适的条件下，它们甚至喜欢和人交流，通过玩耍建立关系。

paras.en: The birds will be encouraged to clean the park through the use of a small box that delivers a small amount of bird food each time the rook deposits a cigarette end or small piece of rubbish.
paras.zh: 公园会用一个小盒子鼓励这些鸟清理公园：每当秃鼻乌鸦放进一个烟头或一小片垃圾，盒子就会送出一点鸟食。

paras.en: So far, visitors to the theme park have been excited to see the birds in action.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，主题公园的游客看到这些鸟干活都很兴奋。

paras.en: However, some parents are concerned that it encourages their children to drop litter so they can watch the birds pick it up.
paras.zh: 不过，有些家长担心这会怂恿孩子们乱扔垃圾，好看这些鸟把它捡起来。

paras.en: Villier is not concerned about this criticism.
paras.zh: 维利耶对这种批评并不担心。

paras.en: He maintains most of the feedback he has received has been overwhelmingly positive.
paras.zh: 他坚持说，他收到的大部分反馈都非常正面。

w.m: adv. 压倒性地；绝大多数地

paras.en: He hopes now to train more birds.
paras.zh: 他现在希望训练更多的鸟。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What have six birds been trained to do at a French historical theme park?
paras.zh: 第五题：法国一座历史主题公园训练了六只鸟做什么？

paras.en: Question six: Why were rooks chosen by the park manager?
paras.zh: 第六题：公园经理为什么选中了秃鼻乌鸦？

paras.en: Question seven: What is the concern of some parents?
paras.zh: 第七题：有些家长担心什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you’ll hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation 1.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: The name of the TV show we wish to produce is Science Nation.
paras.zh: 我们想制作的电视节目叫《科学国度》。

paras.en: Please tell us more.
paras.zh: 请再给我们详细讲讲。

paras.en: What will Science Nation be about?
paras.zh: 《科学国度》会讲些什么？

paras.en: It’ll be about science, all sorts of science.
paras.zh: 讲的是科学，各种各样的科学。

paras.en: Each episode will focus on a different area of science.
paras.zh: 每一集聚焦科学的一个不同领域。

paras.en: And tell us what we know, how we know it, and what we still don’t know.
paras.zh: 告诉观众我们知道什么、是怎么知道的，还有哪些我们仍然不知道。

paras.en: The show will have one host only, and this will be Professor Susan Powell from Harvard University.
paras.zh: 节目只有一位主持人，就是哈佛大学的苏珊·鲍威尔教授。

paras.en: She’s a great public speaker.
paras.zh: 她非常擅长公开演讲。

w.m: 演讲者；擅长当众讲话的人

paras.en: So just to be clear, will the show’s format be like that of a documentary?
paras.zh: 那么我确认一下，这个节目的形式会像纪录片那样吗？

paras.en: Kind of.
paras.zh: 算是吧。

paras.en: It’ll be like a documentary in the sense that it’ll be non-fiction and fact-based.
paras.zh: 说它像纪录片，是因为它不是虚构的，而是以事实为基础。

paras.en: However, our idea is for it to be also fun and entertaining, something which traditional documentaries aren’t so much.
paras.zh: 不过，我们的想法是让它同时也有趣、好看，这一点是传统纪录片不太做得到的。

w.m: adj. 有趣的；娱乐性强的

paras.en: Please keep in mind this will be a new TV show like nothing ever done before.
paras.zh: 请记住，这将是一档前所未有的全新电视节目。

paras.en: Okay, so it’ll be both educational and entertaining.
paras.zh: 好的，那它既有教育意义，又有娱乐性。

w.m: adj. 有趣的；娱乐性强的

paras.en: And your audience will be anyone interested in science, right?
paras.zh: 你们的观众就是所有对科学感兴趣的人，对吧？

paras.en: That’s correct, yes.
paras.zh: 对，没错。

paras.en: Right, thank you.
paras.zh: 好的，谢谢。

paras.en: So I think we’re more or less clear on what the show will be like.
paras.zh: 那么，我想我们大致清楚这个节目会是什么样了。

paras.en: Could you please tell us now what exactly you want from us?
paras.zh: 现在能告诉我们，你们具体想从我们这里得到什么吗？

paras.en: Yes, of course.
paras.zh: 好，当然可以。

paras.en: Basically, what we need from you is financial support.
paras.zh: 简单来说，我们需要你们提供的是资金支持。

paras.en: In order to go ahead with this idea, we need two million dollars.
paras.zh: 要把这个想法付诸实施，我们需要两百万美元。

paras.en: This would cover the cost of making all twelve shows in the first season for the first year.
paras.zh: 这笔钱可以支付第一年第一季全部十二期节目的制作费用。

paras.en: If the show is a success, we can then look at making a second season for the following year.
paras.zh: 如果节目成功了，我们就可以考虑在下一年制作第二季。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What do we learn about the TV show Science Nation?
paras.zh: 第八题：关于电视节目《科学国度》，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question nine: In what way will the TV show Science Nation differ from traditional documentaries?
paras.zh: 第九题：电视节目《科学国度》和传统纪录片有什么不同？

paras.en: Question 10: Who will be the intended audience of the TV show Science Nation?
paras.zh: 第十题：电视节目《科学国度》的目标观众是谁？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman want the man to do for the TV show?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士想让男士为这个电视节目做什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: What’s up with you?
paras.zh: 你怎么了？

paras.en: You don’t look very happy.
paras.zh: 你看起来不太开心。

paras.en: I feel like I’m a failure.
paras.zh: 我觉得自己是个失败者。

paras.en: I can’t seem to do anything very well.
paras.zh: 我好像什么事都做不好。

paras.en: I wouldn’t say that.
paras.zh: 我可不这么认为。

paras.en: You do very well in a lot of things.
paras.zh: 你很多事都做得很好。

paras.en: That presentation you gave last week was excellent.
paras.zh: 你上周做的那个报告就很出色。

paras.en: Yes, but I have this urge to strive for perfection.
paras.zh: 是啊，可我总有一股追求完美的冲动。

paras.en: I really want to push harder and progress further.
paras.zh: 我真的很想更努力一点，再进一步。

paras.en: Well, that’s very admirable.
paras.zh: 嗯，这很值得钦佩。

paras.en: But be careful.
paras.zh: 不过要当心。

paras.en: Over-concern with being perfect can damage our confidence if we never achieve it.
paras.zh: 如果总也做不到完美，过分追求完美就会损害我们的自信。

w.m: n. 过分在意；过度关注

paras.en: Yes, I know.
paras.zh: 是啊，我知道。

paras.en: I feel awful whenever I make a mistake in whatever I’m trying to do.
paras.zh: 不管做什么，只要一出错，我就感觉糟透了。

paras.en: Well, think about it.
paras.zh: 嗯，你好好想想。

paras.en: You can’t make progress without making mistakes and learning from them.
paras.zh: 不犯错误、不从错误中学习，就不可能进步。

paras.en: Thomas Edison, the famous inventor, once said, I’ve not failed.
paras.zh: 大发明家托马斯·爱迪生说过：“我没有失败。

paras.en: I’ve just found ten thousand ways that won’t work.
paras.zh: 我只是找到了一万种行不通的方法。”

paras.en: You may well be right.
paras.zh: 你说得很可能有道理。

paras.en: I guess I should recognize my mistakes and learn the lesson they teach me and move forward.
paras.zh: 我想我应该正视自己的错误，吸取它们给我的教训，然后继续往前走。

paras.en: Also, remember a successful ending is not the only thing worthy of a celebration.
paras.zh: 另外，记住，成功的结局不是唯一值得庆祝的事。

paras.en: You need to recognize each step of progress you take towards achieving your goals and, no matter how tiny it is, it’s still good news.
paras.zh: 你要肯定自己朝目标迈出的每一步，不管多小，都是好消息。

paras.en: I always feel down when I see others accomplishing things, and I feel miserable about my own achievements.
paras.zh: 每次看到别人有所成就，我都很沮丧，对自己的成绩感到很难过。

paras.en: I’m always trying to be as good as others, but I never seem to get there.
paras.zh: 我总想做得跟别人一样好，可好像永远也做不到。

paras.en: Listen, if you always compare yourself with others, you’ll never feel good enough.
paras.zh: 听着，如果你总拿自己跟别人比，就永远不会觉得自己够好。

paras.en: You’re the only person you should be comparing yourself with.
paras.zh: 你唯一应该比较的人，就是你自己。

paras.en: When you compare your current status with the starting point, you’ll find you’ve made progress, right?
paras.zh: 拿你现在的状态跟起点比一比，你会发现自己进步了，对吧？

paras.en: That’s good enough.
paras.zh: 这就足够好了。

paras.en: That’s great advice.
paras.zh: 这个建议太好了。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。

paras.en: I’m feeling better already.
paras.zh: 我已经感觉好多了。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: How does the man feel about himself?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士对自己有什么感觉？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the woman think is the man’s problem?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士认为男士的问题是什么？

paras.en: Question 14: How does the man feel when he sees others accomplishing things?
paras.zh: 第十四题：看到别人有所成就时，男士有什么感觉？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the woman suggest the man do?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士建议男士怎么做？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Single-sex education can have enormous benefits for female students.
paras.zh: 单一性别教育能给女生带来巨大的好处。

paras.en: Numerous studies have shown that women who attend single-sex schools tend to have stronger self-confidence, better study habits and more ambitious career goals than women who attend coeducational schools.
paras.zh: 大量研究表明，和上男女同校学校的女生相比，上女校的女生往往更自信、学习习惯更好、职业目标更远大。

paras.en: Girls who graduate from single-sex schools are three times more likely to become engineers than those who attend coeducational schools.
paras.zh: 从女校毕业的女生成为工程师的可能性，是男女同校学校毕业生的三倍。

paras.en: The reason is that all girls’ schools encourage women to enter fields traditionally dominated by men, such as science, technology and engineering.
paras.zh: 原因是女校鼓励女生进入传统上由男性主导的领域，比如科学、技术和工程。

paras.en: In coeducational schools, girls are often expected to succeed only in the humanities or the arts.
paras.zh: 在男女同校的学校里，人们往往只指望女生在人文学科或艺术方面取得成功。

paras.en: Research has also shown that in co-educational settings, teachers are more likely to praise and give in-depth responses to a boy’s comments in class.
paras.zh: 研究还表明，在男女同校的环境里，老师更有可能表扬男生在课堂上的发言，并认真深入地回应。

paras.en: In contrast, they might only respond to a girl’s comments with a nod.
paras.zh: 相比之下，对女生的发言，他们可能只是点点头。

paras.en: They’re also more likely to encourage boys to work through problems on their own, while they tend to step in and help girls who struggle with a problem.
paras.zh: 他们还更有可能鼓励男生自己解决问题，而女生遇到难题时，他们往往会插手帮忙。

paras.en: In an all-girls setting, girls are more likely to speak up frequently and make significant contributions to class than in a coeducational setting.
paras.zh: 和男女同校的环境相比，在全是女生的环境里，女生更有可能经常主动发言，为课堂作出重要的贡献。

paras.en: Girls studying in a single-sex setting also earn higher scores on their college board and advanced placement exams than girls who study in coeducational settings.
paras.zh: 在单一性别环境里学习的女生，在美国大学理事会考试和大学先修课程考试中的分数，也比在男女同校环境里学习的女生高。

paras.en: All girls’ schools tend to be smaller than coeducational schools, which means teachers will be able to tailor the materials to girl students’ personal learning styles and interests.
paras.zh: 女校的规模往往比男女同校的学校小，这意味着老师能根据女生各自的学习方式和兴趣来调整教学材料。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What advantage does the speaker say girls from single-sex schools have over those from coeducational schools?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人说，和男女同校学校的女生相比，女校的女生有什么优势？

paras.en: Question 17: What do teachers tend to do in coeducational settings?
paras.zh: 第十七题：在男女同校的环境里，老师往往会怎么做？

paras.en: Question 18: What are teachers more likely to do in an all-girls school?
paras.zh: 第十八题：在女校里，老师更有可能怎么做？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Today I found out that Seattle doesn’t really get that much rain compared with most US cities.
paras.zh: 今天我才知道，和美国大多数城市相比，西雅图的雨其实并不算多。

paras.en: In fact, Seattle ranks forty-fourth among major US cities in average annual rainfall.
paras.zh: 事实上，在美国主要城市中，西雅图的年均降雨量只排第四十四位。

paras.en: Cities that get more rainfall than Seattle include Houston, Memphis, Nashville, and pretty much every major city on the eastern coast, such as New York, Boston, and Miami.
paras.zh: 比西雅图降雨多的城市有休斯敦、孟菲斯、纳什维尔，还有东海岸几乎每一个大城市，比如纽约、波士顿和迈阿密。

paras.en: So why does everyone think of Seattle as a rainy city?
paras.zh: 那么，为什么大家都觉得西雅图是座多雨的城市呢？

paras.en: The primary root of this misconception lies in that Seattle has a relatively large number of days per year with rainfall, compared with New York and Boston, which get an average of about sixteen per cent more rain per year than Seattle, but also average between them about thirty six fewer days a year of rainfall.
paras.zh: 这种误解的主要根源在于，西雅图一年中下雨的天数相对较多。纽约和波士顿每年的降雨量平均比西雅图多百分之十六左右，但两座城市平均每年下雨的天数却比西雅图少三十六天左右。

paras.en: So it rains a lot less in Seattle, and the rain is spread out over more days than those cities.
paras.zh: 所以西雅图的雨量要少得多，只是分散在比那些城市更多的天数里。

paras.en: This is why few locals in Seattle carry an umbrella generally.
paras.zh: 这就是为什么西雅图本地人一般很少带伞。

paras.en: When it does rain, it tends to be a very light rain that isn’t troublesome.
paras.zh: 就算下雨，往往也是不怎么烦人的小雨。

w.m: adj. 令人烦恼的；麻烦的

paras.en: It almost never really rains, as most people think.
paras.zh: 它几乎从来不像大多数人想的那样真正下大雨。

paras.en: On top of that, it never really storms in Seattle either.
paras.zh: 除此之外，西雅图也从来没有真正的暴风雨。

paras.en: Seattle gets an average of a mere seven days a year with thunder.
paras.zh: 西雅图平均每年只有七天打雷。

paras.en: So in short, if you like sunny but not too hot summers, mild winters but with lots of cloudy days, Seattle’s the place to be.
paras.zh: 所以简单来说，如果你喜欢晴朗但不太热的夏天、温和却多阴天的冬天，西雅图就是你该去的地方。

paras.en: Anyway, if you visit Seattle don’t bring an umbrella.
paras.zh: 不管怎样，如果你去西雅图，别带伞。

paras.en: People will look at you thinking you’re funny.
paras.zh: 不然大家会看着你，觉得你很好笑。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What did the speaker find out about Seattle?
paras.zh: 第十九题：说话人发现了西雅图的什么情况？

paras.en: Question 20: Why do local people in Seattle seldom carry an umbrella?
paras.zh: 第二十题：西雅图本地人为什么很少带伞？

paras.en: Question 21: Why does the speaker say Seattle is a good place to be?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人为什么说西雅图是个值得去的地方？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: After a tough workout or a day full of physical activity, it’s common to find your muscles aching.
paras.zh: 经过一场高强度的锻炼，或者一整天的体力活动之后，肌肉酸痛是很常见的。

paras.en: But where do these pains come from?
paras.zh: 可这些疼痛是从哪儿来的呢？

paras.en: According to a German professor, the soreness comes from straining your muscles in an uncommon way.
paras.zh: 一位德国教授说，酸痛是因为肌肉用了不常用的发力方式而拉伤。

paras.en: For example, jumping on a bicycle for a ride.
paras.zh: 比如，跳上自行车骑一圈。

paras.en: Because you haven’t ridden in a long time, soreness occurs since your leg muscles aren’t used to that movement.
paras.zh: 因为你很久没骑车了，腿部肌肉不习惯那个动作，所以会酸痛。

paras.en: When muscles perform an activity they aren’t regularly exposed to, the tiny fibres that are inside them are being torn apart.
paras.zh: 肌肉做平时不常做的活动时，里面细小的纤维就会被撕裂。

paras.en: As muscle soreness develops, the body has to work to repair the muscle tears.
paras.zh: 随着肌肉酸痛加重，身体就得着手修复肌肉的撕裂伤。

paras.en: But this doesn’t happen immediately.
paras.zh: 不过这不是马上就发生的。

paras.en: First, the body must realize the muscles are damaged.
paras.zh: 首先，身体必须意识到肌肉受损了。

paras.en: When the body realizes the muscles are hurt, the response is to increase blood flow to the area and increase body heat.
paras.zh: 身体意识到肌肉受了伤，就会这样应对：增加流向那个部位的血液，并提高体温。

paras.en: Damaged cells are then cleaned up and the body sends cells specially designed to break down the large muscle fibre fragments.
paras.zh: 然后受损的细胞会被清理掉，身体会派出专门的细胞来分解大块的肌肉纤维碎片。

paras.en: Healing can take place after this.
paras.zh: 在这之后，伤处才能开始愈合。

paras.en: It takes about a day until these cells make it to your aching muscles.
paras.zh: 这些细胞要花大约一天才能到达你酸痛的肌肉。

paras.en: That’s why there’s most often a delay associated with muscle soreness.
paras.zh: 这就是为什么肌肉酸痛通常会延迟出现。

paras.en: Repair of damaged cells takes about two days and afterwards the soreness disappears.
paras.zh: 受损细胞的修复大约需要两天，之后酸痛就会消失。

paras.en: Unfortunately, there’s little that can be done to relieve muscle soreness.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，能缓解肌肉酸痛的办法不多。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: Pain-relieving creams don’t work, but a hot shower or warm bath can provide some relief.
paras.zh: 止痛膏不管用，但洗个热水澡或泡个温水澡能缓解一些。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What does the German professor say about muscle soreness?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于肌肉酸痛，这位德国教授说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What happens when muscles are damaged according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：根据短文，肌肉受损时会发生什么？

paras.en: Question 24: How long does it take for damaged cells to heal?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：受损的细胞需要多长时间才能愈合？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker suggest one do to relieve muscle soreness?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人建议怎样缓解肌肉酸痛？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲英国男护士人数三年来持续减少，卫生大臣认为这是文化问题，呼吁更多男性考虑当护士。第二篇新闻报道讲一名利比亚男子在绍斯波特海滩睡着后被涨潮包围，救生员及时赶到把他救了下来。第三篇新闻报道讲一只浣熊爬上一座二十五层的摩天大楼，在网上走红，最后被动物管理人员用猫粮诱捕。第一段长对话里，女士第一次领到全职工作的月薪，男士建议她用这笔钱去健身房办卡，多和同事来往。第二段长对话里，男士拿不定主意是去伦敦读博士还是去纽约工作，家人、导师和女朋友的意见各不相同。第一篇短文讲分析能力的含义和提高的办法：开阔眼界、玩益智游戏、参加辩论社或读书会。第二篇短文讲狗和狗之间也能建立深厚长久的感情，大多数狗一生只认一个伴侣。第三篇短文讲美国新墨西哥州一个男孩被一块一百二十万年前的动物化石绊倒，大学研究人员把化石挖出来保存了起来。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The British Government has called for more men to consider a career in nursing.
paras.zh: 英国政府呼吁更多男性考虑从事护理工作。

paras.en: Figures show the number of male nurses has fallen in the last three years.
paras.zh: 数据显示，男护士的人数在过去三年里有所减少。

paras.en: Now the number of men working in the nursing sector has reached a seven-year low.
paras.zh: 现在，护理行业的男性从业人数已降到七年来的最低点。

paras.en: Numbers of male nurses increased between 2011 and 2014 and reached a peak of 7,168.
paras.zh: 男护士人数在二〇一一年到二〇一四年间有所增加，最多时达到七千一百六十八人。

paras.en: This figure has dropped to only 6,924 in 2017.
paras.zh: 到二〇一七年，这个数字降到了只有六千九百二十四人。

paras.en: The UK Health Secretary said, This is clearly a cultural problem, and probably one that exists in many parts of the world.
paras.zh: 英国卫生大臣说：“这显然是一个文化问题，很可能在世界上很多地方都存在。

paras.en: But we can make efforts to change that now.
paras.zh: 但我们现在就可以努力改变这种状况。

paras.en: We want to persuade males to think about career options of going into nursing.
paras.zh: 我们希望说服男性考虑去做护理这一职业选择。

paras.en: There is absolutely no reason why men can’t go into this profession.
paras.zh: 男性完全没有理由不能从事这一职业。”

paras.en: The Health Secretary said that the Government already has plans to attract a more varied workforce into nursing.
paras.zh: 卫生大臣说，政府已经计划吸引更多不同背景的人加入护理队伍。

w.m: adj. 各种各样的；多样的

paras.en: She stated, “We are leading the way on workforce planning.
paras.zh: 她说：“在人力规划上，我们走在前面。

paras.en: We will become the first nation in Europe to publish a national health and care workforce plan.
paras.zh: 我们将成为欧洲第一个公布全国卫生和护理人力规划的国家。”

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What problem is Britain facing?
paras.zh: 第一题：英国面临什么问题？

paras.en: Question 2: What is the cause of the problem according to the UK Health Secretary?
paras.zh: 第二题：英国卫生大臣认为，这个问题的原因是什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A man from Libya was enjoying a walk along the sands at Southport Beach.
paras.zh: 一名来自利比亚的男子正在绍斯波特海滩的沙滩上散步。

paras.en: When he was about half a mile out from the dock he felt a bit tired, so he lay down and fell asleep.
paras.zh: 走到离码头大约半英里远的地方时，他感到有点累，就躺下睡着了。

paras.en: But the tide swept in quickly at the beach, and the man was shocked to wake up and find the tide had come in and completely surrounded him, cutting him off from the shore.
paras.zh: 但海滩上的潮水涨得很快，这名男子醒来时大吃一惊，发现潮水已经涨上来，把他团团围住，切断了他回岸上的路。

paras.en: Fortunately for him, the Beach Life Guards were quickly on the scene to stop him from drowning.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，海滩救生员很快赶到现场，没让他被淹死。

paras.en: They acted professionally to ensure the man was comfortable until an ambulance arrived.
paras.zh: 他们的处理很专业，一直让这名男子保持舒适，直到救护车赶到。

paras.en: He was then taken to hospital.
paras.zh: 随后他被送往医院。

paras.en: He is now in a stable condition.
paras.zh: 他现在情况稳定。

paras.en: When interviewed, Keith Porter of the Southport Beach said, “Our beach is so flat that it’s very common for the tide to come around the back of people and cut them off from the beach.
paras.zh: 接受采访时，绍斯波特海滩的基思·波特说：“我们的海滩很平，潮水绕到人身后、把人跟海滩隔开是很常见的。

paras.en: Thankfully the emergency services have again worked well together to ensure a positive outcome and we wish the gentleman a speedy recovery.
paras.zh: 好在各个应急部门又一次配合得很好，确保了好的结果。我们祝这位先生早日康复。”

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What does the news report say about the Libyan man?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于这名利比亚男子，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What did Keith Porter say at an interview?
paras.zh: 第四题：基思·波特在采访中说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A raccoon, a small cat-like animal, climbed to the top of a 25-story skyscraper early on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 周三凌晨，一只浣熊爬上了一座二十五层的摩天大楼楼顶。浣熊是一种长得像猫的小动物。

paras.en: It was captured after becoming an online star across the world.
paras.zh: 它在全世界的网上走红之后被抓住了。

paras.en: At a little before 3 a.m., the animal made it to the roof of the building.
paras.zh: 凌晨快三点的时候，这只动物爬到了大楼的楼顶。

paras.en: After it took a long break on a 17th floor window edge, at the top of the building, animal control officers put cat food in traps and captured the raccoon.
paras.zh: 它在十七楼的窗沿上歇了很久，爬到楼顶以后，动物管理人员在捕捉笼里放了猫粮，把这只浣熊抓住了。

paras.en: A private wildlife management company will release the animal into the wild.
paras.zh: 一家私营野生动物管理公司将把它放归野外。

paras.en: The raccoon’s upward journey began on Monday.
paras.zh: 这只浣熊的“登高之旅”是从周一开始的。

paras.en: The brown animal was spotted stuck on a narrow window edge of the office tower.
paras.zh: 当时有人看到这只棕色的动物被困在这座办公大楼一处窄窄的窗沿上。

paras.en: On Tuesday, the raccoon slowly climbed the building.
paras.zh: 周二，这只浣熊慢慢地往楼上爬。

paras.en: It reached the 23rd floor and its legend continued to grow on social media with every floor it climbed.
paras.zh: 它爬到了二十三楼，每多爬一层，它在社交媒体上的传奇就又多一分热度。

paras.en: As it went up, people gathered on the sidewalk below to take photos and cheer for its safety.
paras.zh: 它往上爬的时候，人们聚在楼下的人行道上拍照，为它的安全加油。

paras.en: Online, office workers posted photos and videos of the raccoon resting on window edges and climbing up the building’s concrete exterior.
paras.zh: 网上，上班族们纷纷发帖，晒出浣熊在窗沿上歇脚、沿着大楼的混凝土外墙往上爬的照片和视频。

paras.en: One online post said that the raccoon has succeeded in uniting the country the way no politician could.
paras.zh: 有一条网帖说，这只浣熊把全国人民团结在一起，这是任何政客都做不到的。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What does the news report say about the raccoon, a small cat-like animal?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于浣熊这种长得像猫的小动物，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What will the Wildlife Management Company do with the captured raccoon?
paras.zh: 第六题：野生动物管理公司会怎样处理抓到的浣熊？

paras.en: Question seven: What did one online post say?
paras.zh: 第七题：有一条网帖说了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you’ll hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I have really amazing news.
paras.zh: 我有个特别好的消息。

w.m: adj. 令人惊喜的；了不起的

paras.en: I just got a text message from my bank saying my salary has been deposited in my account.
paras.zh: 我刚收到银行发来的短信，说我的工资已经打到我账户上了。

paras.en: Getting paid is good, but I don’t understand why you’re so excited.
paras.zh: 发工资是好事，可我不明白你干吗这么激动。

paras.en: It happens every month.
paras.zh: 每个月都有啊。

paras.en: Well, I’ve been working for a few years.
paras.zh: 嗯，我工作好几年了。

paras.en: In fact, I worked all through university, but I only had part-time jobs then.
paras.zh: 其实我整个大学期间都在打工，不过那时候只做兼职。

paras.en: So this is the first time I’ve ever been paid for a month of full-time work.
paras.zh: 所以这是我第一次领到一整个月的全职工资。

paras.en: Wow, then you must feel great.
paras.zh: 哇，那你一定感觉很棒。

paras.en: I mean it’s been two decades, but I can still remember when I got my first real salary.
paras.zh: 我是说，虽然已经过去二十年了，可我还记得自己领到第一份真正工资时的情景。

paras.en: I was happy for days.
paras.zh: 我高兴了好几天。

paras.en: And I felt like it was a small fortune, even though it wasn’t.
paras.zh: 我还觉得那是一笔小财富，其实并不是。

paras.en: Yeah, I’ve never earned so much money before, and there’s so many things I’d like to do with it.
paras.zh: 是啊，我以前从没挣过这么多钱，有好多事想拿它去做。

paras.en: What did you do with your first pay?
paras.zh: 你拿到第一份工资时做了什么？

paras.en: I bought a new suit for work and took my parents to a nice restaurant to celebrate.
paras.zh: 我给自己买了一套上班穿的新西装，还带爸妈去一家不错的餐馆庆祝了一下。

paras.en: Maybe you could do the same.
paras.zh: 也许你也可以这样做。

paras.en: I have enough professional clothes, and my parents are across the country, so seeing them isn’t possible.
paras.zh: 我上班穿的衣服已经够多了，我爸妈又在国家另一头，回去看他们不现实。

paras.en: But some people from the office are members of a gym I want to join, and my university classmates are arranging a trip to visit our old campus, and I’d love to go with them.
paras.zh: 不过办公室有几个人是一家健身房的会员，我也想去办卡；还有，我的大学同学在组织回母校看看，我很想跟他们一起去。

paras.en: But I can’t afford both.
paras.zh: 但两样我都负担不起。

paras.en: If I were you, I’d join the gym, because it’s a good way to stay healthy, and it might help you build a stronger relationship with your colleagues, and good relationships are key to a successful career.
paras.zh: 要是我，我就去健身房办卡，因为这是保持健康的好办法，还可能帮你和同事搞好关系，而好的人际关系是事业成功的关键。

paras.en: Hm, you’re right.
paras.zh: 嗯，你说得对。

paras.en: Thanks for the advice.
paras.zh: 谢谢你的建议。

paras.en: I’m taking it.
paras.zh: 我就听你的。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: Why did the woman feel excited?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士为什么感到激动？

paras.en: Question nine: When did the man get his first full-time job?
paras.zh: 第九题：男士是什么时候找到第一份全职工作的？

paras.en: Question 10: What did the man do when he got his first pay?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士领到第一份工资时做了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman say she is going to do?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士说她打算做什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: What’s going on with you lately?
paras.zh: 你最近怎么了？

paras.en: You seem so distracted, like you aren’t really listening to anything I say.
paras.zh: 你好像总心不在焉，我说什么你都没在听似的。

w.m: adj. 心不在焉的；分心的

paras.en: I know.
paras.zh: 我知道。

paras.en: I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 不好意思。

paras.en: I can’t seem to focus on anything because I still haven’t decided if I should accept the offer for that PhD programme in London, or if I should take the job offer in New York.
paras.zh: 我好像什么都没法专心，因为我还没决定是接受伦敦那个博士项目的录取，还是接受纽约那份工作。

paras.en: Look, it’s a tough decision, but you’re running out of time, aren’t you?
paras.zh: 听着，这个决定确实很难，可你时间不多了，不是吗？

paras.en: I thought you said the company expected an answer by the end of the month.
paras.zh: 我记得你说过，公司要你在月底前给答复。

paras.en: Actually, it’s the beginning of next month for the job.
paras.zh: 其实工作那边是下个月初。

paras.en: But the university needs a decision by the end of the week.
paras.zh: 但大学那边要我在这周末前做决定。

paras.en: So I have to act quickly.
paras.zh: 所以我得赶紧行动。

paras.en: You definitely need advice for an important decision like this.
paras.zh: 这么重要的决定，你肯定需要听听别人的建议。

paras.en: So who have you talked to about it?
paras.zh: 那你跟谁商量过了？

paras.en: What does your family think?
paras.zh: 你家里人怎么想？

paras.en: And your advisor for your master’s program?
paras.zh: 还有你读硕士时的导师呢？

paras.en: I’ve asked their advice, and that’s part of the problem.
paras.zh: 我问过他们的意见，问题就出在这儿。

paras.en: My parents want me to get the degree, but my advisor thinks it’s time for me to get more work experience.
paras.zh: 我爸妈想让我读完学位，可我导师觉得我该多积累些工作经验了。

paras.en: What do you mean by part of the problem?
paras.zh: 你说问题就出在这儿，是什么意思？

paras.en: Oh, wait.
paras.zh: 哦，等等。

paras.en: It’s your girlfriend, isn’t it?
paras.zh: 是你女朋友的事吧？

paras.en: You’ve been dating since your first year of university.
paras.zh: 你们从大一就开始谈恋爱了。

paras.en: So that’s six years now.
paras.zh: 到现在都六年了。

paras.en: She must have an opinion about all this.
paras.zh: 她对这一切肯定有自己的看法。

paras.en: I mean, isn’t it time for you to think about getting married?
paras.zh: 我是说，你们是不是该考虑结婚了？

paras.en: Well, I do want to get married, but she thinks we need to wait until we’ve launched our careers.
paras.zh: 嗯，我确实想结婚，可她觉得我们得等到事业起步以后。

paras.en: Plus she’s not sure what she’ll be doing next year.
paras.zh: 再说，她也不确定明年会做什么。

paras.en: She’s considering a job in England and one in Australia, and her parents are pushing for the latter.
paras.zh: 她在考虑英国的一份工作和澳大利亚的一份工作，她父母在极力劝她选后者。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: Why does the man seem to be distracted?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士为什么好像心不在焉？

w.m: adj. 心不在焉的；分心的

paras.en: Question 13: What does the woman say the man should do?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士说男士应该怎么做？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the man say is part of his problem?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士说他的问题有一部分出在哪儿？

paras.en: Question fifteen: Why doesn’t the man’s girlfriend agree to get married right now?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士的女朋友为什么不同意现在就结婚？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Analytical skills are our ability to understand and solve problems using the information we have available.
paras.zh: 分析能力是指我们利用手头的信息理解问题、解决问题的能力。

paras.en: These skills are extremely important for our professional, social and intellectual lives.
paras.zh: 这些能力对我们的工作、社交和思想生活都极其重要。

paras.en: What are the best ways to improve them?
paras.zh: 提高这些能力的最好办法有哪些？

paras.en: One way is to expand your world view.
paras.zh: 一个办法是开阔你的眼界。

paras.en: Unfortunately, this takes time.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，这需要时间。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: Ultimately, it will help you better evaluate information and analyze different ideas and outcomes.
paras.zh: 不过最终，它会帮你更好地评估信息，分析不同的观点和结果。

paras.en: Traveling is a great way to expand your world view, although it can be expensive.
paras.zh: 旅行是开阔眼界的好办法，只是花费可能不小。

paras.en: An entertaining way of enhancing your analytical skills is to engage them by playing brain games.
paras.zh: 玩益智游戏来锻炼分析能力，是提高分析能力的一个有趣办法。

paras.en: These are games that challenge you to think deeply and to develop your analytical skills.
paras.zh: 这些游戏要求你深入思考，培养你的分析能力。

paras.en: These games will get you used to thinking in a certain way.
paras.zh: 这些游戏会让你习惯用某种方式思考。

paras.en: As a result, they will help improve your ability to think.
paras.zh: 这样一来，它们就能帮助提高你的思考能力。

paras.en: However, opinions vary on whether video games are effective.
paras.zh: 不过，电子游戏是否有用，大家看法不一。

paras.en: The general consensus is that the best ones avoid mindless violence and instead focus on strategy and challenge us to solve problems and achieve broad goals.
paras.zh: 大家普遍认为，最好的游戏不会有无脑的暴力内容，而是注重策略，让我们去解决问题、实现更大的目标。

w.m: adj. 无脑的；不动脑子的

paras.en: Joining a debate or reading club or group is also a good idea.
paras.zh: 参加辩论社、读书会或者类似的团体也是个好主意。

paras.en: This provides people with the opportunity to come together and discuss ideas, literature and problems.
paras.zh: 这为人们提供了聚在一起讨论观点、文学作品和问题的机会。

paras.en: Groups like these will help you refine your analytical skills and enable you to express yourself better.
paras.zh: 这样的团体能帮你提升分析能力，让你更好地表达自己。

paras.en: Any social group that encourages free exchange of ideas and pursuit of knowledge is beneficial.
paras.zh: 任何鼓励自由交流思想、追求知识的社交团体都有好处。

paras.en: It helps you to actively develop your analytical skills.
paras.zh: 它能帮你主动培养分析能力。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What kind of ability do analytical skills refer to in the passage?
paras.zh: 第十六题：短文里说的分析能力指的是哪种能力？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the passage say is an entertaining way of enhancing one’s analytical skills?
paras.zh: 第十七题：短文说，提高分析能力的一个有趣办法是什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What else does the speaker advise people to do to improve their analytical skills?
paras.zh: 第十八题：为了提高分析能力，说话人还建议人们做什么？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: There’s an endless amount of scientific data proving that dogs can develop strong bonds with their owners.
paras.zh: 有数不清的科学数据证明，狗能和主人建立深厚的感情。

w.m: adj. 无穷的；没完没了的

paras.en: People aren’t kidding when they say they love their dog or their dog loves them, but we’re rather ignorant about the nature of the relationships that form between dogs.
paras.zh: 人们说他们爱自己的狗、他们的狗也爱他们，这可不是开玩笑；可是狗和狗之间形成的是什么样的关系，我们却了解得很少。

paras.en: In an effort to understand the matter further, I spoke with Dr. Marc Bekoff, a researcher and former professor of animal behavior.
paras.zh: 为了进一步弄清这个问题，我采访了马克·贝科夫博士，他是一名研究人员，曾经是动物行为学教授。

paras.en: The doctor’s response to the question of whether or not dogs can fall in love like humans do was a straight “Of course.”
paras.zh: 有人问狗会不会像人一样坠入爱河，贝科夫博士的回答很干脆：“当然会。”

paras.en: He went on to say that if love is defined as a long-term commitment, meaning dogs seek one another out when they’re apart, they’re happy when they’re reunited, they protect one another, they feed one another, they raise their children together, then of course dogs love each other.
paras.zh: 他接着说，如果把爱定义为一种长期的承诺，也就是狗分开时会互相寻找，重逢时会很开心，它们互相保护、互相喂食、一起抚养孩子，那么狗当然是彼此相爱的。

paras.en: Now our furry friends don’t really experience romantic love like in the movies, but they can form deep and lasting bonds with their fellow dogs as well as humans.
paras.zh: 其实，我们这些毛茸茸的朋友并不会像电影里那样体验浪漫的爱情，但它们能和别的狗、也能和人建立深厚而持久的感情。

paras.en: In fact, evidence shows that most dogs stay with one partner their whole lives.
paras.zh: 事实上，有证据表明，大多数狗一辈子都跟同一个伴侣在一起。

paras.en: In actuality, love between dogs can be even more intimate than human relationships.
paras.zh: 实际上，狗之间的爱可能比人类的感情还要亲密。

paras.en: When they interact, they aren’t afraid to smell each other and will express themselves clearly and honestly.
paras.zh: 它们互动的时候，不怕互相闻闻对方，会清楚、坦诚地表达自己。

paras.en: Once again, it seems we have a lot to learn from dogs.
paras.zh: 看来，我们又一次有很多东西要向狗学习。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the passage say we don’t know much about?
paras.zh: 第十九题：短文说，我们对什么了解不多？

paras.en: Question 20: What does Dr. Marc Bekoff say about dogs?
paras.zh: 第二十题：马克·贝科夫博士对狗有什么看法？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say about most dogs?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于大多数狗，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: A piece of history has been found thanks to a boy tripping on a rare one point two million-year-old animal fossil.
paras.zh: 一个男孩被一块罕见的、一百二十万年前的动物化石绊了一跤，一段历史因此被发现了。

paras.en: In November 2016, Jude Sparks, now 10, was on an outing with his family near their New Mexico home when he tripped over what he thought was a cowbone.
paras.zh: 二〇一六年十一月，现年十岁的裘德·斯帕克斯和家人在新墨西哥州的家附近出游，被一块他以为是牛骨的东西绊了一跤。

paras.en: Now, researchers at New Mexico State University are preserving the discovery, which was identified as an ancient elephant-like animal.
paras.zh: 现在，新墨西哥州立大学的研究人员正在保存这件发现物，它被鉴定为一种古代的、长得像大象的动物。

paras.en: Kyle Sparks, father of Jude, said he let his son decide what to do with the fossil.
paras.zh: 裘德的父亲凯尔·斯帕克斯说，他让儿子自己决定怎么处理这块化石。

paras.en: So Jude reached out to Peter Houde, a professor at New Mexico State University, who had experience with the same type of fossil in the past.
paras.zh: 于是裘德联系了新墨西哥州立大学的教授彼得·豪德，他以前处理过同类化石。

paras.en: The next day Houde came out to see the fossil for himself.
paras.zh: 第二天，豪德亲自来看了这块化石。

paras.en: Houde told ABC News that he was quite excited about the find.
paras.zh: 豪德告诉美国广播公司新闻台，他对这一发现相当兴奋。

paras.en: It was fortunate that the family didn’t try to dig up the fossil, because that could destroy the specimen.
paras.zh: “幸亏这家人没有自己动手挖化石，因为那样可能会毁掉标本。

paras.en: They did the right thing by calling someone who would know what to do.
paras.zh: 他们做得对，打电话找了懂行的人。

paras.en: It’s great for the community because now everybody can appreciate it,” he added.
paras.zh: 这对整个社区都是件好事，因为现在大家都能欣赏到它，”他补充道。

paras.en: Houde and his fellow faculty members dug up the fossil in late May.
paras.zh: 豪德和他的同事们在五月底把化石挖了出来。

paras.en: They hoped to return to the site with geologists for an additional search as there could be more fossils near the site.
paras.zh: 他们希望和地质学家一起回到现场再找一找，因为附近可能还有更多化石。

paras.en: Jude and his family had been invited by the researchers to see the fossil being preserved at the university.
paras.zh: 研究人员已经邀请裘德一家去大学看正在保存的化石。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What did the boy, Jude Sparks, think he had discovered?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：男孩裘德·斯帕克斯以为自己发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What are the researchers at New Mexico State University doing with the boy’s discovery?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：新墨西哥州立大学的研究人员正在怎样处理男孩发现的东西？

paras.en: Question 24: What did Professor Peter Houde say when interviewed by ABC News?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：彼得·豪德教授接受美国广播公司新闻台采访时说了什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What do the researchers plan to do?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：研究人员打算做什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
