passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲苏格兰本周晚些时候将迎来大雪，交通部长建议橙色预警地区的人周三不要出行，道路警察负责人提醒司机做好准备、小心驾驶。第二篇新闻报道讲罗马尼亚多瑙河三角洲的湿地在当地社区、世界自然基金会和欧盟资金的帮助下恢复了生机，政府还打算禁渔十年，保护濒危野生鱼类。第三篇新闻报道讲美国高中生斯科特·邓恩因车祸错过了毕业典礼，同学们专门为他一个人重新办了一场。第一段长对话里，两人聊在家办公的孤独，以及去咖啡馆办公的好处和给店主带来的麻烦。第二段长对话里，女士想辞职找新工作，男士担心频繁跳槽会让雇主觉得她不够忠诚，女士却认为换工作让她积累了丰富经验。第一篇短文讲孤独和独处的区别，以及怎样让独处变成好事。第二篇短文里，讲述者回忆父亲做事一丝不苟，自己当理货员时也以把活儿干好为荣。第三篇短文讲一项研究：老年人每天看电视超过三小时，记忆衰退会加倍，研究人员建议多做别的活动。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须选出最佳答案，

paras.en: from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Good morning.
paras.zh: 早上好。

paras.en: In today’s headlines, Scotland’s Transport Minister has warned of potentially extreme weather conditions as heavy snow is forecast across the country later this week.
paras.zh: 今天的头条新闻：苏格兰交通部长发出警告，本周晚些时候全国预计将有大雪，可能出现极端天气。

paras.en: Orange warnings are in force for many areas for Wednesday and Thursday.
paras.zh: 周三和周四，许多地区都发布了橙色预警。

paras.en: The Transport Minister advised people in parts of Scotland covered by the Orange Alert to avoid travel on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 交通部长建议，苏格兰橙色预警覆盖地区的人周三不要出行。

paras.en: This is what he said to us.
paras.zh: 以下是他对我们说的话。

paras.en: The orange warning may be raised to red in some areas.
paras.zh: 在一些地区，橙色预警可能会升级为红色预警。

paras.en: That is a warning for snow that has never been seen since the modern system came into place in Scotland.
paras.zh: 那是苏格兰启用现行预警系统以来从没发布过的暴雪预警。

paras.en: The orange warning has been extended until 6pm on Thursday.
paras.zh: 橙色预警已经延长到周四下午六点。

paras.en: Trains, planes and ferries are also likely to be affected, with a wind chill that could see parts of Britain feeling as cold as minus fifteen degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 火车、飞机和渡轮也很可能受到影响，风寒效应会让英国部分地区的体感温度低至零下十五摄氏度。

paras.en: The head of road policing said, I would urge drivers to take extra care on the roads for their journeys.
paras.zh: 道路警察负责人说：“我要敦促司机们出行时在路上格外小心。”

paras.en: Drivers should make sure they are prepared for their journey with warm clothing, food and drink, sufficient fuel and a charged mobile phone.
paras.zh: 司机们要确保出行前做好准备：带上保暖衣物、食物和饮料，加足油，手机充好电。

paras.en: There could be significant traffic delays, so please start to plan your journey now and consider if you really need to travel when conditions are this poor.
paras.zh: 交通可能会严重拥堵，所以请现在就开始规划行程，并且想一想，在路况这么差的时候，你是不是真的需要出门。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What were people in parts of Scotland advised to do?
paras.zh: 第一题：苏格兰部分地区的人被建议做什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What did the head of road policing urge drivers to do?
paras.zh: 第二题：道路警察负责人敦促司机们做什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Romania’s wetlands are coming back to life, thanks to help from local communities, the World Wildlife Fund, and funding from the European Union.
paras.zh: 罗马尼亚的湿地正在恢复生机，这多亏了当地社区和世界自然基金会的帮助，还有欧盟的资金。

paras.en: Roughly two thousand two hundred twenty four acres of the picturesque Danube Delta, home to three hundred species of birds, have filled with wildlife.
paras.zh: 风景如画的多瑙河三角洲是三百种鸟类的家园，其中大约两千二百二十四英亩的土地又充满了野生动物。

paras.en: The land has been connected to the network of lakes and streams in the area.
paras.zh: 这片土地已经和当地的湖泊、溪流网络连通了。

paras.en: A lot of birds have migrated to the area, and one doesn’t need to travel long hours any more or go to other lakes to watch the birds, says Ian Muta, deputy mayor of Mahmudia.
paras.zh: 马胡迪亚副镇长伊恩·穆塔说：“很多鸟都迁徙到了这里，人们不用再长途跋涉，也不用去别的湖边看鸟了。”

paras.en: The area around Mahmudia, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is the third most biodiverse in the world, after Australia’s Great Barrier Reef and the Galapagos Islands.
paras.zh: 马胡迪亚周边地区是联合国教科文组织认定的世界遗产地，生物多样性位居世界第三，仅次于澳大利亚的大堡礁和加拉帕戈斯群岛。

paras.en: Groups used earth moving equipment to restore the waterways.
paras.zh: 各团体用土方设备修复了水道。

paras.en: Government officials propose to protect the area’s endangered wild fish by issuing a fishing ban over the next decade.
paras.zh: 政府官员打算在未来十年实行禁渔，来保护该地区濒危的野生鱼类。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What is the news report mainly about?
paras.zh: 第三题：这篇新闻报道主要讲了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What did government officials propose to do to protect the endangered fish?
paras.zh: 第四题：政府官员打算怎样保护濒危鱼类？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Scott Dunn recently awoke from the medically induced sleep he’d been in after a car accident.
paras.zh: 斯科特·邓恩出车祸后医生用药物让他一直昏睡，最近他才醒过来。

paras.en: He was heartbroken after realizing he had missed his high school graduation, so his classmates decided to give him another chance.
paras.zh: 发现自己错过了高中毕业典礼，他非常伤心，于是同学们决定再给他一次机会。

paras.en: It was just a month ago that East Juniata High School seniors met in their school’s auditorium for graduation and last week they did it again.
paras.zh: 就在一个月前，东朱尼亚塔高中的毕业班学生在学校礼堂里举行了毕业典礼，上周他们又办了一次。

paras.en: Scott’s car accident was on May 22nd, just three days before the ceremony.
paras.zh: 斯科特的车祸发生在五月二十二日，就在典礼前三天。

paras.en: I remember waking up in the hospital and asking mum what date it was.
paras.zh: 我记得在医院醒来时，问妈妈今天几号。

paras.en: She told me it was the twenty eighth, he said, I looked at her and said, I missed my graduation.
paras.zh: 他说：“她告诉我是二十八号，我看着她说：‘我错过毕业典礼了。’”

paras.en: The school’s principal, Mr Fawsey, called Scott’s mum, Karen, and said that everybody wanted to do something special for him.
paras.zh: 学校的校长福西先生给斯科特的妈妈卡伦打了电话，说大家都想为斯科特做点特别的事。

paras.en: Students wore their caps and gowns and sat in the front of the auditorium.
paras.zh: 学生们穿上学位帽和学位服，坐在礼堂前排。

paras.en: Scott’s parents, Karen and Scott Senior, sat front and center.
paras.zh: 斯科特的父母卡伦和老斯科特坐在正前方的中间位置。

w.m: 正前方中间；最显眼的位置

paras.en: After brief speeches, Scott’s name was called, only Scott’s name.
paras.zh: 简短致辞之后，台上念了斯科特的名字，而且只念了他一个人的名字。

paras.en: He walked across the stage as the audience cheered.
paras.zh: 他走过舞台，观众欢呼起来。

paras.en: A graduation for one.
paras.zh: 一个人的毕业典礼。

paras.en: I’m speechless, Scott said.
paras.zh: 斯科特说：“我都不知道说什么好了。”

paras.en: I don’t know how to even explain it.
paras.zh: 我甚至都不知道该怎么形容。

paras.en: I’m speechless to know that so many people are behind me.
paras.zh: 知道有这么多人支持我，我感动得说不出话来。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What happened to Scott a month ago?
paras.zh: 第五题：一个月前斯科特出了什么事？

paras.en: Question six: What did Scott ask about when he regained consciousness?
paras.zh: 第六题：斯科特恢复意识后问了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: Why was Scott speechless at the graduation ceremony?
paras.zh: 第七题：斯科特在毕业典礼上为什么说不出话来？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: How do you like your new flexible working arrangement?
paras.zh: 你觉得新的弹性工作安排怎么样？

paras.en: Do you enjoy working from home?
paras.zh: 你喜欢在家办公吗？

paras.en: Yes and no.
paras.zh: 可以说喜欢，也可以说不喜欢。

paras.en: I find the isolation challenging at times.
paras.zh: 我有时候觉得那种孤立的状态挺难熬的。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；难应付的

paras.en: Apart from my mother, not too many people I know have time for phone chats during working hours.
paras.zh: 除了我妈妈，我认识的人里没几个在工作时间有空打电话聊天。

paras.en: I tried the library but found I wasn’t really keen on working there.
paras.zh: 我试过去图书馆，但发现自己不太喜欢在那儿工作。

paras.en: No, neither would I. I find the library a bit too quiet.
paras.zh: 对，换我也不喜欢，我觉得图书馆有点太安静了。

paras.en: I’d lack inspiration or stimulation, which would be counterproductive to getting a lot of work done.
paras.zh: 我会缺少灵感和刺激，这反而不利于把很多工作做完。

paras.en: I found the same thing, so lately I’ve been going out to cafes occasionally.
paras.zh: 我也有同感，所以最近我偶尔会去咖啡馆。

paras.en: I love the noise, the people, the busyness of a cafe, the sense of being out in the world.
paras.zh: 我喜欢咖啡馆的嘈杂、人来人往和忙碌，那种置身外面世界的感觉。

paras.en: Coffee shops seem to have effectively become office spaces for so many people in this digital age.
paras.zh: 在这个数字时代，咖啡店似乎实际上已经成了很多人的办公场所。

paras.en: Though I’m not sure how cafe owners feel about it, having so many people who go to their places to work rather than drink and eat.
paras.zh: 不过我不确定咖啡馆老板对这件事怎么看，那么多人到店里是来工作的，而不是来吃喝的。

paras.en: Yes, some people seem to spend a lot of time there and not order much.
paras.zh: 是啊，有些人好像在那儿待很长时间，却不怎么点东西。

paras.en: The most annoying ones for cafe owners must surely be those, usually only two of them, who occupy a table for six with their laptops and paperwork.
paras.zh: 对咖啡馆老板来说，最烦人的肯定是那种人：通常就两个人，却带着笔记本电脑和一堆文件占了一张六人桌。

paras.en: They should sit at a table for two, not at a table for six.
paras.zh: 他们应该坐两人桌，而不是六人桌。

paras.en: Some obviously stay so long they need to plug their laptops into a power outlet.
paras.zh: 有些人显然待得太久，还得把笔记本电脑插到电源插座上。

paras.en: I nearly tripped over someone’s computer electrical lead the other day in my local cafe.
paras.zh: 前几天在我家附近的咖啡馆，我差点被别人电脑的电线绊倒。

paras.en: It’s a double-edged sword, no doubt about that, for a cafe owner.
paras.zh: 毫无疑问，对咖啡馆老板来说，这是一把双刃剑。

paras.en: While remote workers help to keep the cafe full in quiet times, they can take up valuable table space in busy periods.
paras.zh: 远程办公的人在冷清的时候能让咖啡馆坐满，可在忙的时候又会占用宝贵的座位。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the woman say is the disadvantage of working from home?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士说在家办公的缺点是什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the man say is counterproductive to getting work done in the library?
paras.zh: 第九题：男士说在图书馆里，什么会不利于把工作做完？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the woman like about doing one’s work in a cafe?
paras.zh: 第十题：女士喜欢在咖啡馆工作的哪一点？

paras.en: Question 11: What is most annoying for cafe owners according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第十一题：据女士说，对咖啡馆老板来说最烦人的是什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: I’m going to start looking for another job.
paras.zh: 我打算开始找别的工作了。

paras.en: I can’t see myself getting an opportunity to progress at my company any time in the near future.
paras.zh: 我看不出自己在近期有机会在公司里升职。

paras.en: and I really think my skills and abilities deserve a higher salary.
paras.zh: 而且我真心觉得，凭我的技能和能力应该拿更高的薪水。

paras.en: You’re not going to quit, are you?
paras.zh: 你不会要辞职吧？

paras.en: I’m thinking I might as well.
paras.zh: 我在想，干脆辞了算了。

paras.en: Then I can devote more time and energy to finding a better position at another company.
paras.zh: 这样我就能投入更多时间和精力，去别的公司找个更好的职位。

paras.en: But you’ve been at your present company less than two years, haven’t you?
paras.zh: 可你在现在的公司还不到两年，对吧？

paras.en: This will be the third time you’ve left a job in the last five years.
paras.zh: 这将是你五年里第三次辞职了。

paras.en: If you do several jobs in a relatively short span of time, prospective employers might perceive that you lack loyalty.
paras.zh: 如果你在比较短的时间内换了好几份工作，未来的雇主可能会觉得你不够忠诚。

paras.en: That could make them wary and reluctant to employ you.
paras.zh: 这会让他们心存戒备，不太愿意雇用你。

paras.en: Unfortunately, loyalty doesn’t pay.
paras.zh: 可惜，忠诚换不来回报。

paras.en: Even if I get a promotion at my company, it’s likely to be less sizable than if I were to get a job elsewhere.
paras.zh: 就算我在公司升了职，涨幅也很可能比不上去别的地方找份工作。

paras.en: And even if I get a promotion, I’m not guaranteed to get a raise.
paras.zh: 而且就算升了职，也不一定能加薪。

paras.en: I had that experience at another company I worked at.
paras.zh: 我在之前待过的另一家公司就碰到过这种事。

paras.en: They wanted you to take on more work and responsibility, but for the same amount of money?
paras.zh: 他们要你承担更多工作和责任，钱却一样多？

paras.en: More or less, yes.
paras.zh: 差不多是这样。

paras.en: The way I see it, through having different jobs, I’ve gathered a lot of experience in different jobs and in different industries.
paras.zh: 在我看来，通过换不同的工作，我积累了很多不同岗位的经验，还有不同行业的经验。

paras.en: But potential employers might worry that that experience is not deep or thorough enough.
paras.zh: 但未来的雇主可能会担心，你的经验不够深入、不够扎实。

paras.en: Perhaps.
paras.zh: 也许吧。

paras.en: But I feel pretty confident that I can sell myself.
paras.zh: 但我挺有信心能把自己推销出去。

paras.en: You know what they say.
paras.zh: 你知道人们常说什么。

paras.en: Fortune favors the brave.
paras.zh: 天助勇者。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What makes the woman think about changing her job?
paras.zh: 第十二题：是什么让女士想换工作？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the man say about people who keep changing their jobs?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于总是换工作的人，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the woman say would happen even if she got promoted in her current company?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士说，即使她在现在的公司升了职，会发生什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What benefit has the woman gained from changing her jobs frequently?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士从频繁换工作中得到了什么好处？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案，然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: There is a saying that goes something along the lines of You must love yourself first before you can love someone else.
paras.zh: 有句话大意是这样的：你得先爱自己，才能去爱别人。

paras.en: Similarly, I personally believe that you must be comfortable and happy in your own company, before you can truly be yourself in the company of others.
paras.zh: 同样，我个人认为，你得先能自在、开心地独处，才能在和别人相处时真正做自己。

paras.en: There is a massive difference between being lonely and being alone.
paras.zh: 孤独和独处之间有着巨大的区别。

paras.en: Loneliness is a horrible feeling.
paras.zh: 孤独是一种很糟糕的感觉。

paras.en: However, you don’t have to actually be alone to feel that way.
paras.zh: 不过，并不是真的一个人待着才会有那种感觉。

paras.en: Many times I’ve felt lonely when surrounded by a big group of people.
paras.zh: 很多时候，我被一大群人围着，却还是觉得孤独。

paras.en: In contrast, being alone can actually be a blessing, particularly when you’ve actively chosen it.
paras.zh: 相反，独处其实可以是一件幸事，尤其是你主动选择独处的时候。

paras.en: In my experience being bored and alone is dangerous and can easily lead to the feeling of loneliness.
paras.zh: 根据我的经验，又无聊又一个人待着很危险，很容易让人觉得孤独。

paras.en: The trick is to be active.
paras.zh: 诀窍是让自己活跃起来。

paras.en: Get outside, stretch your legs, do something cultural, buy yourself something tasty to eat, or something pretty to wear.
paras.zh: 出去走走，活动活动腿脚，做点有文化气息的事，给自己买点好吃的，或者买件好看的衣服穿。

paras.en: You don’t have to take anyone else into consideration, and can do whatever you please.
paras.zh: 你不用顾及别人，想做什么就做什么。

paras.en: Spending time alone also allows you to more efficiently take care of problems.
paras.zh: 一个人待着还能让你更高效地处理问题。

paras.en: And then, when it’s time to be social and meet up with your friends, you will be fully there because you won’t have too much other stuff floating around in your mind.
paras.zh: 这样，等到要社交、和朋友见面的时候，你就能全身心地投入，因为你脑子里不会有太多别的事情转来转去。

paras.en: Having been alone for a bit, you will also appreciate your friend’s company more and chances are your time spent together will be more worthwhile.
paras.zh: 一个人待过一阵子之后，你也会更珍惜朋友的陪伴，而且你们在一起的时光很可能会更有意义。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about being alone?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于独处，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the speaker say help reduce one’s feeling of loneliness?
paras.zh: 第十七题：说话人说什么有助于减轻孤独感？

paras.en: Question 18: What is an advantage of spending one’s time alone?
paras.zh: 第十八题：一个人度过时间有什么好处？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: When I turned twelve, I worked summers at my father’s small brick cleaning business.
paras.zh: 我十二岁那年，每到夏天就在父亲开的一家小小的砖墙清洗店里干活。

paras.en: I remember the harsh acid smell of the cleaning solution, and the scraping sound of stiff iron brushes against rough brick.
paras.zh: 我还记得清洗液那股刺鼻的酸味，还有硬铁刷刮在粗糙砖面上的声音。

paras.en: It was tempting to hurry a job just to finish.
paras.zh: 人很容易为了快点干完，把活儿草草了事。

w.m: adj. 诱人的；让人想做的

paras.en: But anybody who worked for Thomas Calhoun had to meet his standards, and that included me.
paras.zh: 但只要是给托马斯·卡尔霍恩干活的人，都得达到他的标准，我也不例外。

paras.en: If I messed up, he made me stay late until I got it right.
paras.zh: 要是我搞砸了，他就让我留下来加班，直到做好为止。

paras.en: My father wasn’t being mean; he demanded the same of himself.
paras.zh: 我父亲并不是故意刁难人，他对自己也是同样的要求。

w.m: adj. 刻薄的；不近人情的

paras.en: Every brick he cleaned on a house stood out like a red jewel in a white setting.
paras.zh: 他清洗过的房子上，每块砖都像白色底座上镶着的红宝石一样醒目。

paras.en: It was his signature.
paras.zh: 那是他的招牌。

paras.en: In 1970, when I was 20, I got married and moved out of my parents’ modest place into a housing project.
paras.zh: 一九七〇年我二十岁，那年我结了婚，从父母那简朴的家里搬了出去，住进了一个公共住宅区。

w.m: 公共住宅区；廉租房项目

paras.en: Drugs and gang violence were just beginning to plague the projects.
paras.zh: 那时毒品和帮派暴力刚开始困扰这些住宅区。

paras.en: Some of my friends went to jail, some were killed.
paras.zh: 我的朋友有的进了监狱，有的被人杀了。

paras.en: My wife, Verlin, was eighteen, and nobody gave our marriage a chance.
paras.zh: 我妻子维尔琳当时十八岁，没人看好我们的婚姻。

paras.en: But we believed in each other, and our faith made us strong.
paras.zh: 但我们相信彼此，这份信念让我们变得坚强。

paras.en: When we married, I worked as a stock clerk at Southwest Superfoods.
paras.zh: 我们结婚的时候，我在西南超级食品店当理货员。

paras.en: It was hard, tedious work.
paras.zh: 那是一份又累又单调的工作。

paras.en: Each Friday night a truck came with cases of food that had to be unloaded, priced and placed on shelves.
paras.zh: 每个星期五晚上，都会来一辆卡车，拉着一箱箱食品，得把它们卸下来、标好价，再摆到货架上。

paras.en: Most of the stock clerks tried to get Friday night off, but I was always ready to work.
paras.zh: 大多数理货员都想方设法让星期五晚上不用上班，可我总是随时准备干活。

paras.en: By Saturday morning all the cans and jars in my aisle were placed with the labels facing smartly out, like a line of soldiers on review.
paras.zh: 到了星期六早上，我负责的那条过道里，所有罐头和瓶子都摆得整整齐齐，标签朝外，就像一排接受检阅的士兵。

paras.en: That was my signature.
paras.zh: 那是我的招牌。

paras.en: I took pride in a job nobody wanted.
paras.zh: 一份没人想干的工作，我却干得很自豪。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What do we learn about the speaker’s father?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于说话人的父亲，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty: What does the speaker say about the housing project?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于那个公共住宅区，说话人说了什么？

w.m: 公共住宅区；廉租房项目

paras.en: Question twenty one: What do we learn about the speaker as a stock clerk?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于说话人当理货员的情况，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Watching more than three hours of television a day doubles memory loss in older people, a new study of more than three thousand adults suggests.
paras.zh: 一项针对三千多名成年人的新研究表明，每天看电视超过三个小时，会让老年人的记忆衰退加倍。

paras.en: Scientists at University College London used memory and fluency tests on the same group of people six years apart.
paras.zh: 伦敦大学学院的科学家对同一批人做了记忆力和语言流畅度测试，两次测试相隔六年。

paras.en: They found that those who watched on average less than three hours television a day showed a decline of around four to five per cent, while those who tended to watch more than three hours a day declined by an average of eight to ten per cent.
paras.zh: 他们发现，每天平均看电视不到三小时的人，记忆力下降了大约百分之四到五，而每天看电视往往超过三小时的人，平均下降了百分之八到十。

paras.en: The research team say they believe the alert but passive nature of television watching may be creating stress on the mind which contributes to memory decline.
paras.zh: 研究团队表示，他们认为看电视时人虽然清醒，却只是被动地接收，这可能给大脑造成压力，进而导致记忆衰退。

paras.en: Older people who watch more television are also less likely to undertake activities known to preserve mental functioning, such as reading, or interactive, screen-based pursuits, such as using the Internet or playing video games.
paras.zh: 看电视多的老年人，也更少去做那些已知能保持大脑功能的活动，比如阅读，或者上网、玩电子游戏这类互动性的屏幕活动。

paras.en: The researchers say that television viewing may be a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease, but more research is needed to establish a link.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，看电视可能是患阿尔茨海默病的一个风险因素，但要确定两者之间的关联，还需要更多研究。

paras.en: While watching television may have educational benefits and relaxation benefits, the researchers advise that adults over the age of fifty should try and ensure that television viewing is balanced with other contrasting activities.
paras.zh: 虽然看电视可能有教育作用，也能让人放松，但研究人员建议，五十岁以上的成年人应该尽量让看电视和其他不同类型的活动保持平衡。

w.m: adj. 不同的；对比鲜明的

paras.en: If you’re concerned that the amount of television you’re watching could have a negative impact on your health, you should limit the amount of T V you watch each day and undertake some healthy hobbies.
paras.zh: 如果你担心自己看电视太多会对健康有负面影响，就应该限制每天看电视的时间，再培养一些健康的爱好。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: By what means did scientists at University College London measure memory loss?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：伦敦大学学院的科学家用什么方法测量记忆衰退？

paras.en: Question 23: What contributed to memory decline in the participants?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：是什么导致了参与者的记忆衰退？

paras.en: Question 24: What do the researchers say about their finding concerning the link between T V viewing and Alzheimer’s disease?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于看电视和阿尔茨海默病之间的关联，研究人员对他们的这项发现是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question twenty five: What do the researchers suggest older people do?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：研究人员建议老年人做什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2020年9月大学英语四级 第1套
passages.name: 2020年9月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲美国国家航空航天局的卫星在葡萄牙上空拍到的照片：船只排出的废气让海面上空形成了一道道像伤疤一样的厚云，这些云可能会影响全球气候。第二篇新闻报道讲墨尔本郊区一家超市撤掉保安后，员工因多次遭顾客袭击、辱骂而联名要求配备长期保安，超市发言人则说已采取了有力措施。第三篇新闻报道讲一辆卡车在通往华沙的高速公路上侧翻，十二吨巧克力洒满路面，消防员用热的高压水才把它清理掉。第一段长对话里，丽莎说改用现金是为了攒钱，因为用手机付款时人对钱的价值感受不深，容易乱花。第二段长对话里，布朗先生打电话说送来的椅子不是他订的，商店答应第二天上门换货。第一篇短文讲近藤麻理惠的整理节目掀起了人们清理家中物品、捐赠旧物的热潮。第二篇短文讲十二岁的迈克·汉农给无家可归的人送午餐，感动了全国。第三篇短文讲一项研究显示手机会分散注意力，还列举了电子产品带来的其他坏处。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you’ll hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A NASA satellite orbiting over Portugal took photographs that reveal the effects of pollution from ships.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局的一颗卫星在葡萄牙上空运行时拍下了一些照片，照片显示出船只造成的污染有什么影响。

paras.en: One of the photos shows a thin film of clouds above the brilliant blue of the North Atlantic, cut by white lines of thicker clouds that look like scars.
paras.zh: 其中一张照片上，碧蓝的北大西洋上空飘着一层薄薄的云，一道道较厚的白色云线划过其间，看上去像伤疤一样。

paras.en: NASA officials explained those thicker clouds are signs of ship traffic below.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局的官员解释说，那些较厚的云说明下方有船只经过。

paras.en: When ships power their way through the ocean they pump exhaust into the atmosphere, just as cars do.
paras.zh: 船只在海上破浪前进时，会像汽车一样往大气里排放废气。

paras.en: And those massive amounts of particles can cause clouds to form.
paras.zh: 而那么多的颗粒就会促使云形成。

paras.en: Get enough of those particles in one place, as from the exhaust of a ship, and they can lead to the creation of new clouds easily visible from space.
paras.zh: 只要一个地方的颗粒足够多，比如来自一艘船的废气，就会形成新的云，从太空中都能轻易看到。

paras.en: These clouds can be huge.
paras.zh: 这些云可能非常大。

paras.en: Some of them stretch hundreds of kilometers from end to end, NASA officials said.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局的官员说，有些云从一头到另一头绵延几百公里。

paras.en: It’s likely that these sorts of clouds are having some effect on the global climate, according to NASA officials, but scientists aren’t yet sure what effect it has.
paras.zh: 据美国国家航空航天局的官员说，这类云很可能正在对全球气候产生某种影响，但科学家还不确定到底是什么影响。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What has caused the thick clouds in the photos taken by a NASA satellite?
paras.zh: 第一题：美国国家航空航天局卫星拍的照片里，那些厚云是什么造成的？

paras.en: Question two: What do NASA officials think about the thick clouds?
paras.zh: 第二题：美国国家航空航天局的官员对这些厚云有什么看法？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Staff at a suburban supermarket in Melbourne say they feel unsafe at work after security guards were removed.
paras.zh: 墨尔本郊区一家超市的员工说，保安被撤走以后，他们上班时觉得不安全。

paras.en: This came after a series of physical attacks and verbal abuse by customers.
paras.zh: 此前，这家店接连发生了顾客动手打人和辱骂员工的事。

paras.en: More than fifty workers at the store have signed a letter calling for a permanent security guard following a series of incidents, including a customer threatening to attack a supervisor with a knife.
paras.zh: 在发生了一系列事件之后，店里五十多名员工联名写信，要求配一名长期保安，其中一件是一名顾客扬言要拿刀袭击主管。

paras.en: A security worker had guarded the store each night from 7 p.m. until 12am.
paras.zh: 以前每晚七点到十二点，都有一名保安在店里值守。

paras.en: But that had stopped suddenly on Monday, employees said.
paras.zh: 但员工们说，从星期一开始，突然就没有保安了。

paras.en: One worker said an angry customer had thrown a chicken at his head after complaining about how long she had waited to be served.
paras.zh: 一名员工说，有位女顾客抱怨等了太久才轮到她，一气之下拿一只鸡砸向他的头。

paras.en: Another worker said the lack of protection at the store made her feel uncomfortable at work.
paras.zh: 另一名员工说，店里缺少保护，让她上班时很不自在。

w.m: adj. 不自在的；不舒服的

paras.en: However, a spokesman of the supermarket said the store had taken strong action in response to incidents.
paras.zh: 不过，超市的一名发言人说，店里已经对这些事件采取了强有力的措施。

paras.en: We have found very few instances of bad customer behaviour at our store in the past year.
paras.zh: 过去一年里，我们店里顾客行为恶劣的情况非常少。

paras.en: In the rare cases we have seen bad behaviour, we have taken strong action in response, including banning a customer from the store.
paras.zh: 在我们碰到的少数行为恶劣的情况里，我们都采取了强有力的措施来应对，包括禁止顾客进店。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: For what purpose did the staff at a supermarket in Melbourne sign a letter?
paras.zh: 第三题：墨尔本一家超市的员工联名写信是为了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What did the spokesman of the supermarket say regarding the employees’ demand?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于员工的要求，超市发言人说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Drivers on their way to the Polish capital of Warsaw on Wednesday morning found the road blocked by an unusual obstacle: tons of liquid chocolate that spilled onto the motorway.
paras.zh: 星期三早上，开车前往波兰首都华沙的司机们发现，道路被一个不寻常的障碍物挡住了：好几吨液态巧克力洒在了高速公路上。

paras.en: A truck carrying the sweet load hit a road barrier and overturned, blocking two lanes.
paras.zh: 一辆装着这些甜食的卡车撞上路边护栏后翻了车，堵住了两条车道。

paras.en: The cracked tank spilled a pool of rapidly hardening chocolate, which quickly covered the width of the road.
paras.zh: 罐体裂开，流出一大摊迅速凝固的巧克力，很快就铺满了整个路面。

paras.en: While the driver was taken to hospital with a broken arm, firefighters struggled to remove a reported 12 tons of solid chocolate from the road.
paras.zh: 司机手臂骨折被送往医院，而消防员们费了好大劲，才把据说有十二吨的固态巧克力从路上清走。

paras.en: A representative for the firefighters told the local TV that removing the chocolate was worse than dealing with snow.
paras.zh: 消防员的一名代表对当地电视台说，清理巧克力比清理积雪还难。

paras.en: After contacting the chocolate manufacturer, the firefighters resorted to spraying hot, pressurized water to get rid of the sticky substance.
paras.zh: 消防员联系了巧克力生产商之后，只好喷热的高压水，才把这种黏糊糊的东西清除掉。

paras.en: The local TV also noted that the cleanup spanned more than a mile because drivers simply drove through the chocolate after the crash, leaving a long chocolate trail.
paras.zh: 当地电视台还提到，清理范围超过一英里，因为撞车后司机们直接从巧克力上开了过去，留下了一长条巧克力痕迹。

paras.en: But despite the sticky situation, firefighters and police attending to the cleanup were reportedly cheerful about the long task ahead.
paras.zh: 不过，尽管局面这么棘手，据说负责清理的消防员和警察对接下来的漫长工作还挺乐呵。

paras.en: After all, who could be mad about twelve tons of chocolate?
paras.zh: 毕竟，谁会因为十二吨巧克力生气呢？

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What did drivers on the motorway to Warsaw find?
paras.zh: 第五题：在通往华沙的高速公路上，司机们发现了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the report say about the accident?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于这起事故，报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What did the firefighters’ representative tell the local TV?
paras.zh: 第七题：消防员的代表对当地电视台说了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Lisa, why did you pay for your meal with cash instead of the payment apps on your phone?
paras.zh: 丽莎，你吃饭为什么付现金，不用手机上的支付软件呢？

paras.en: Well, I’ve gone back to cash.
paras.zh: 嗯，我又改回用现金了。

paras.en: I’m only using payment apps if that’s the only option.
paras.zh: 只有在别无选择的时候，我才用支付软件。

paras.en: I’m trying to save money for a new phone, and I find that using cash rather than payment apps helps me to save.
paras.zh: 我在攒钱买新手机，我发现用现金而不用支付软件，能帮我存下钱。

paras.en: But how?
paras.zh: 可这是为什么呢？

paras.en: Money is money, isn’t it?
paras.zh: 钱就是钱，不是吗？

paras.en: I don’t think it matters whether you take it out of the bank and put it in your wallet, or simply transfer it from your bank account to the seller’s bank account using an app.
paras.zh: 我觉得，不管是把钱从银行取出来放进钱包，还是直接用软件从你的银行账户转到卖家的银行账户，都没什么区别。

paras.en: No, I believe it does matter.
paras.zh: 不，我觉得确实有区别。

paras.en: It’s a psychological phenomenon.
paras.zh: 这是一种心理现象。

paras.en: I believe we have less connection with the value of our money when we just tap the approve buttons on our phones.
paras.zh: 我认为，如果我们只是在手机上点一下确认按钮，就不太会感受到钱的价值。

paras.en: You might have a point.
paras.zh: 你说得也许有道理。

paras.en: Since I stopped carrying cash around and started using my phone apps to pay, I may have developed a tendency to buy more small or non-essential items.
paras.zh: 自从我不再随身带现金、开始用手机软件付钱以后，我可能慢慢养成了多买小东西或者不必要的东西的习惯。

paras.en: That’s highly possible.
paras.zh: 很有可能。

paras.en: Think about the amount of time we spend with our phones in our hands and all the things we do with our phones.
paras.zh: 想想看，我们每天手里拿着手机的时间有多长，又用手机做了多少事。

paras.en: It sometimes seems that our phone is buying the product for us, not ourselves.
paras.zh: 有时候好像是手机在替我们买东西，而不是我们自己在买。

paras.en: So cashless payment affects our ability to budget?
paras.zh: 那么，无现金支付会影响我们控制开支的能力？

paras.en: I believe so.
paras.zh: 我觉得是这样。

paras.en: If we spend a hundred yuan in cash, we realize that we don’t have that hundred yuan to spend on something else.
paras.zh: 如果我们花一百块现金，就会意识到，这一百块不能再拿去买别的了。

paras.en: But if we’re spending electronically, we are less likely to make that mental calculation.
paras.zh: 但如果我们用电子方式花钱，就不太会在心里算这笔账。

paras.en: I stopped using my credit card because I found I was spending excessively.
paras.zh: 我不用信用卡了，因为我发现自己花钱太多了。

paras.en: Perhaps I should take the same approach of paying using my phone.
paras.zh: 也许我对用手机付钱也该这么做。

paras.en: It’s worth considering.
paras.zh: 值得考虑一下。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: Why did the woman decide to go back to cash for payment?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士为什么决定改回用现金付钱？

paras.en: Question nine: What happens when people use apps for payment according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第九题：据女士说，人们用软件付钱时会怎么样？

paras.en: Question 10: What might the man tend to buy with payment apps?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士用支付软件可能会倾向于买什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the man think of electronic payment?
paras.zh: 第十一题：男士觉得电子支付怎么样？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hello, Mr. Brown.
paras.zh: 您好，布朗先生。

paras.en: I was expecting your call.
paras.zh: 我正等着您的电话呢。

paras.en: My secretary told me you were having some problems with the wooden table.
paras.zh: 我的秘书跟我说，您那张木桌出了点问题。

paras.en: Is that right?
paras.zh: 是这样吗？

paras.en: No, no, the table is fine.
paras.zh: 不，不，桌子没问题。

paras.en: The problem is the chairs.
paras.zh: 问题出在椅子上。

paras.en: Oh, the chairs.
paras.zh: 哦，是椅子啊。

paras.en: So what exactly is the issue?
paras.zh: 那具体是什么问题呢？

paras.en: Well, put simply, these are not the chairs my wife and I selected in your store last week.
paras.zh: 嗯，简单说吧，这些不是我和我妻子上周在你们店里选的那几把椅子。

paras.en: There must have been some confusion with our order.
paras.zh: 我们的订单肯定是哪里弄混了。

paras.en: Oh, I see.
paras.zh: 哦，我明白了。

paras.en: I’m looking through my files now, and I see that the delivery was this morning.
paras.zh: 我正在查我的档案，我看到是今天上午送的货。

paras.en: Is that correct?
paras.zh: 对吗？

paras.en: Yes.
paras.zh: 对。

paras.en: Do you mind describing the chairs that were delivered to your apartment, Mr Brown?
paras.zh: 布朗先生，您能描述一下送到您公寓的椅子是什么样的吗？

paras.en: Sure.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: These have a flat back with a rounded top and are very heavy.
paras.zh: 这些椅子靠背是平的，顶部是圆的，而且很重。

paras.en: They’re light brown and look kind of cheap.
paras.zh: 颜色是浅棕色，看上去有点廉价。

paras.en: The ones we ordered were dark brown to match the table.
paras.zh: 我们订的是深棕色的，为了跟桌子配套。

paras.en: Right, of course.
paras.zh: 对，没错。

paras.en: It says here you purchased the Arlington table and four Milano chairs.
paras.zh: 这里写着，您买的是阿灵顿桌和四把米兰诺椅。

paras.en: As you said, there must have been some confusion with the order.
paras.zh: 正像您说的，订单肯定是哪里弄混了。

paras.en: I’m terribly sorry.
paras.zh: 真是太抱歉了。

paras.en: We will send a van to collect those four and replace them with the Milano you purchased.
paras.zh: 我们会派一辆货车去把那四把椅子取回来，换成您买的米兰诺椅。

paras.en: Will tomorrow, nine AM be okay, Mr Brown?
paras.zh: 布朗先生，明天上午九点可以吗？

paras.en: Yes, that would be great.
paras.zh: 可以，那太好了。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。

paras.en: Good.
paras.zh: 很好。

paras.en: Did everything else you ordered from us arrive okay?
paras.zh: 您从我们这儿订的其他东西都送到了吧？

paras.en: Yes, I think so.
paras.zh: 是的，我想是吧。

paras.en: Let me check.
paras.zh: 我看看。

paras.en: The mirror and two paintings are here.
paras.zh: 镜子和两幅画都在。

paras.en: The two coffee tables are also here.
paras.zh: 两张咖啡桌也在。

paras.en: And the sofa.
paras.zh: 还有沙发。

paras.en: Yes, we haven’t noticed anything else wrong or missing, but if we do, we will certainly let you know.
paras.zh: 对，我们没发现别的东西有问题或者少了，要是发现了，一定会告诉你们。

paras.en: Okay, great.
paras.zh: 好的，太好了。

paras.en: Once again, I’m sorry for the confusion and trouble caused.
paras.zh: 再次为造成的混乱和麻烦向您道歉。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: Why did the man call the woman?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士为什么给女士打电话？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What did the woman ask the man to do?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士让男士做什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What did the woman promise to do for the man?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士答应为男士做什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What did the woman do at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：对话结束时，女士做了什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I, with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Do you have too much stuff?
paras.zh: 你的东西是不是太多了？

paras.en: Are you, dare we say it, untidy?
paras.zh: 恕我们直言，你是不是不太爱收拾？

w.m: adj. 不整洁的；不爱收拾的

paras.en: Say hello to a T V show called Tidying Up with Marie Kondo, a home improvement show based on her wildly popular book, The Life-Changing Magic of Tidying Up.
paras.zh: 来认识一下一档叫《和近藤麻理惠一起整理》的电视节目吧，这是一档家居改造节目，改编自她那本大受欢迎的书《怦然心动的人生整理魔法》。

paras.en: In the show Marie Kondo acts as a tiny garbage fairy for messy people, visiting their houses to share the wisdom of the KonMari method.
paras.zh: 在节目里，近藤麻理惠就像一个专帮邋遢人家清理垃圾的小仙子，上门拜访他们，分享“怦然心动整理法”的智慧。

paras.en: This method is simple in theory, but can be endlessly complex in practice.
paras.zh: 这种方法理论上很简单，做起来却可能复杂得没完没了。

w.m: adv. 没完没了地；无止境地

paras.en: You divide all the stuff in your house, all of it, into several categories, and then examine each item, all of them, to see if it sparks joy.
paras.zh: 你把家里所有的东西，一样不落，分成几大类，然后检查每一件物品，件件都要看，看它能不能让你怦然心动。

paras.en: If it does, you keep it.
paras.zh: 如果能，就留下它。

paras.en: If it doesn’t, you thank it and neatly discard it.
paras.zh: 如果不能，就感谢它，然后把它好好地处理掉。

paras.en: So is the T V show inspiring people to tidy up?
paras.zh: 那么，这档电视节目有没有激励人们去整理呢？

paras.en: First-hand accounts seem to indicate a small wave of people bringing piles of donation bags to used goods stores.
paras.zh: 从亲历者的讲述来看，似乎出现了一股小热潮：人们拎着一袋袋要捐的东西去二手商店。

paras.en: One store received thousands of bags of used possessions in one day.
paras.zh: 有一家店一天就收到了好几千袋旧物。

paras.en: January is usually the store’s slow season for donations, because it’s cold and people don’t want to bother, but not this January.
paras.zh: 一月份通常是这家店接收捐赠的淡季，因为天冷，人们懒得折腾，可今年一月不一样。

paras.en: People seem determined to clean up their homes.
paras.zh: 人们似乎下定决心要把家里收拾干净。

paras.en: One used book store received a month’s worth of books and donations in a week when a man gave over fifty boxes of books from his home.
paras.zh: 有一家二手书店一周就收到了相当于平时一个月的书和捐赠物，因为有个男人从家里捐出了五十多箱书。

paras.en: It seems Marie’s T V show is having a big impact after all.
paras.zh: 看来，麻理惠的电视节目终究还是产生了很大的影响。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What is Marie Kondo’s TV show about?
paras.zh: 第十六题：近藤麻理惠的电视节目讲的是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What things can be kept in one’s home, according to Marie Kondo?
paras.zh: 第十七题：据近藤麻理惠说，家里可以留下什么东西？

paras.en: Question 18: What do we learn about one used bookstore this January?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于今年一月的一家二手书店，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: At just 12 years old, Mike Hannon is making a difference in his community, one lunch at a time.
paras.zh: 迈克·汉农才十二岁，就在为他的社区带来改变，一次送一份午餐。

paras.en: Mike’s Lunches of Love has fed more than 2,000 of the town’s most vulnerable residents.
paras.zh: 迈克的“爱心午餐”已经为镇上两千多名最困难的居民送去了饭。

w.m: adj. 弱势的；易受伤害的

paras.en: Mike delivers meals to the homeless.
paras.zh: 迈克给无家可归的人送饭。

paras.en: It’s like a way to give people joy, maybe spark something in them that can change them, Mike told WBZ TV.
paras.zh: 迈克对WBZ电视台说：“这就像是一种给人们带去快乐的方式，也许能触动他们，让他们有所改变。”

paras.en: The mayor of Mike’s town feels that Mike is a great community leader, especially in such times of so much negative news, while his father commented on how proud he was of his son.
paras.zh: 迈克所在小镇的镇长觉得，迈克是一位了不起的社区带头人，尤其是在负面新闻这么多的时候，而迈克的父亲也说起自己有多为儿子骄傲。

paras.en: Yet Mike isn’t looking for praise, but kindness in return.
paras.zh: 不过，迈克并不求别人表扬，只希望别人也能善待他人作为回报。

paras.en: He hopes his acts of charity will influence others to spread positive actions in their own towns.
paras.zh: 他希望自己的善举能影响别人，让他们在自己的家乡也传递正能量。

paras.en: Mike includes a handwritten message of joy on each bag.
paras.zh: 迈克在每个袋子上都附上一张亲手写的快乐寄语。

paras.en: His message and star power has spread all over the country.
paras.zh: 他的寄语和明星效应已经传遍了全国。

paras.en: To date, his online page to raise funds has brought in more than $44,000 and counting, raising more than $17,000 in just one day, with the help of many famous actors and others.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，在许多著名演员和其他人的帮助下，他的网上募捐页面已经筹到了四万四千多美元，而且还在增加，其中仅一天就筹了一万七千多美元。

paras.en: People from all over the country are sending special, hand-crafted bags to help the young man with his mission to help those in need.
paras.zh: 全国各地的人都在寄来亲手制作的特别袋子，帮这个年轻人完成他帮助穷困者的使命。

paras.en: Many are hoping the simple act of kindness spreads.
paras.zh: 很多人都希望这种简单的善举能传播开来。

paras.en: Mike is seen as hope for the future of the town, the country, and the world.
paras.zh: 人们把迈克看作这个小镇、这个国家乃至整个世界未来的希望。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does Mike Hannon do to help people in his town?
paras.zh: 第十九题：迈克·汉农做了什么来帮助镇上的人？

paras.en: Question 20: What does Mike hope others will do?
paras.zh: 第二十题：迈克希望别人做什么？

paras.en: Question 21: How are people all over the country responding to what Mike is doing?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：全国各地的人对迈克的所作所为有什么反应？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: In a recent study carried out by psychologists on the disruptive effects of smartphones, two groups of college students were given word search puzzles.
paras.zh: 心理学家最近做了一项研究，探讨智能手机会怎样干扰人，研究中两组大学生都拿到了单词搜索谜题。

paras.en: The first group was told to complete the puzzles with its participants’ smartphones in their line of sight.
paras.zh: 第一组被要求在智能手机就放在视线范围内的情况下完成谜题。

paras.en: The second group, however, was told that the phones would interfere with the equipment in the experiment and would need to be moved away from the testing area.
paras.zh: 而第二组被告知，手机会干扰实验中的设备，需要拿到测试区域以外。

paras.en: Midway through the second group’s solving of the puzzles, the experimenter called one of the phones and let it ring for a while before hanging up.
paras.zh: 第二组解谜解到一半时，实验人员拨打了其中一部手机，让它响了一会儿才挂断。

paras.en: Many of the students in that group were unable to focus from then on, becoming anxious and performing more poorly than the first group.
paras.zh: 从那以后，这一组很多学生都没法集中注意力，变得焦虑不安，表现也比第一组差。

paras.en: Use of electronics has also been known to lead to a decline in human interactions.
paras.zh: 人们还知道，使用电子产品会导致人与人之间的交流减少。

paras.en: Rather than having real-life conversations, many express emotions and engage in deep conversations through social media sites.
paras.zh: 很多人不在现实生活中面对面交谈，而是通过社交媒体网站表达情感、深入交流。

paras.en: Many students use their phones and computers during class for non-academic activities, which leads to poor grades.
paras.zh: 很多学生上课时用手机和电脑做跟学习无关的事，结果成绩很差。

paras.en: Perhaps the most dramatic impact is the reduction in the amount of sleep, which leads to poor health and weight gain.
paras.zh: 也许最严重的影响是睡眠减少，这会导致身体变差、体重增加。

paras.en: Technology is a great tool; however, it’s important to recognize its downsides.
paras.zh: 科技是很好的工具，不过认清它的坏处也很重要。

paras.en: Lack of sleep, reduction of productivity and weight gain are only a few.
paras.zh: 睡眠不足、效率降低和体重增加，这只是其中几个。

paras.en: If we are not careful about all these minor problems right now, the effect on the future generation is going to be much bigger.
paras.zh: 如果我们现在不注意这些小问题，对下一代的影响会大得多。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What were the college students in both groups required to do in the study?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：在这项研究中，两组大学生都被要求做什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What do we learn about many of the students in the second test group after the phone rang?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：手机响了之后，第二组很多学生怎么样了？

paras.en: Question 24: According to the passage, what is the most dramatic impact of smartphone use?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：根据短文，使用智能手机最严重的影响是什么？

paras.en: Question twenty five: What does the speaker suggest people do?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人建议人们做什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一种毒刺能致人死亡的毒鱼“魔鬼火鱼”正在入侵地中海，环保人士担心它会危及其他海洋生物。第二篇新闻报道讲巴黎在世界无车日这天把近一半市中心留给步行和骑车，去年无车日让部分城区污染下降了四成。第三篇新闻报道讲菲律宾一名渔民家中失火，被迫卖掉藏了十年的大珍珠，才知道这是世界上最大的珍珠，价值七千六百万英镑。第一段长对话里，咨询公司的休斯顿女士向史密斯先生介绍公司业务，史密斯先生讲了自家石材公司面临的竞争难题，女士建议先做财务分析。第二段长对话里，西蒙靠杂志上的灵感和哥哥的帮忙自己装修了房子，花费不多，女士想请他帮忙出主意装修客厅。第一篇短文讲英国每年花近三百万英镑从孩子的耳朵和鼻子里取出异物，原因多是好奇心。第二篇短文讲慈善组织“再骑行”送自行车、开骑车课，帮助新西兰的新移民，现正急需志愿者。第三篇短文讲美国国家航空航天局把老鼠送上国际空间站，发现老鼠很快适应了失重，还保持着原来的生活习惯。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet One with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A poisonous fish which has a sting strong enough to kill a human is invading the Mediterranean, warned scientists.
paras.zh: 科学家警告说，一种毒刺足以致人死亡的毒鱼正在入侵地中海。

paras.en: The International Union for the Conservation of Nature has raised concerns after the poisonous fish was spotted in the waters around Turkey, Cyprus and the Eastern Mediterranean.
paras.zh: 有人在土耳其、塞浦路斯和地中海东部周边海域发现这种毒鱼后，世界自然保护联盟表示了担忧。

w.h: International Union for the Conservation of Nature

paras.en: Native to the South Pacific and Indian Ocean, the potentially deadly fish has poisonous hooks and a painful sting capable of killing people.
paras.zh: 这种鱼原产于南太平洋和印度洋，可能致命，长着有毒的钩刺，刺一下非常疼，能要人命。

paras.en: Although fatalities are rare, the stings can cause extreme pain and stop people breathing.
paras.zh: 虽然被刺死的情况很少，但被刺后会剧痛，还会让人停止呼吸。

paras.en: The fish, often known as devil firefish, is a highly invasive species, and environmentalists fear its arrival could endanger other types of marine life.
paras.zh: 这种鱼常被叫作魔鬼火鱼，是一种入侵性很强的物种，环保人士担心它的到来会危及其他海洋生物。

w.m: 魔鬼火鱼（一种有毒的狮子鱼）

paras.en: After being spotted in the Mediterranean, a marine scientist says the fish is spreading and that’s a cause for concern.
paras.zh: 在地中海发现这种鱼之后，一位海洋科学家说，这种鱼正在扩散，这令人担忧。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What is reported in the news?
paras.zh: 第一题：这篇新闻报道了什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What is the environmentalist’s concern about the spread of devil firefish in the Mediterranean?
paras.zh: 第二题：对于魔鬼火鱼在地中海扩散，环保人士担心的是什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Almost half the center of Paris will be accessible only by foot or bicycle this Sunday to mark World Car Free Day.
paras.zh: 为了纪念世界无车日，这个星期天，巴黎市中心将有近一半区域只允许步行或骑自行车进入。

w.m: adj. 可进入的；可到达的

paras.en: This is in response to rising air pollution that made Paris the most polluted city in the world for a brief time.
paras.zh: 这是为了应对日益严重的空气污染，空气污染曾让巴黎一度成为全世界污染最严重的城市。

w.m: adj. 上升的；日益增加的

paras.en: Mayor Anne Hidalgo promoted the first World Car Free Day last year.
paras.zh: 市长安妮·伊达尔戈去年推动了第一届世界无车日。

paras.en: Hidalgo also has supported a Paris Breathes Day.
paras.zh: 伊达尔戈还支持设立“巴黎呼吸日”。

w.m: n. 伊达尔戈（巴黎市长）

paras.en: On the first Sunday of every month, Paris clears traffic from eight lanes of the main road.
paras.zh: 每个月的第一个星期天，巴黎都会清空主干道上八条车道的车辆。

paras.en: About 400 miles of streets will be closed to cars.
paras.zh: 大约四百英里的街道将禁止汽车通行。

paras.en: It is expected to bring significant reduction in pollution levels.
paras.zh: 预计这会大大降低污染水平。

paras.en: Last year’s Car Free Day showed a 40% drop in pollution levels in some parts of the city, according to an independent air pollution monitor, reports The Guardian, and sound levels dropped by 50% in the city’s center.
paras.zh: 据《卫报》报道，一家独立的空气污染监测机构的数据显示，去年无车日那天，城里一些地区的污染水平下降了百分之四十，市中心的噪音也下降了百分之五十。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What will happen on World Car Free Day in Paris?
paras.zh: 第三题：巴黎在世界无车日这天会发生什么？

paras.en: Question four: What motivated the Mayor of Paris to promote the first World Car Free Day in her city?
paras.zh: 第四题：是什么促使巴黎市长在她的城市推动第一届世界无车日？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A Philippine fisherman was feeling down on his luck when a house fire forced him to clear out his possessions and change locations.
paras.zh: 一名菲律宾渔民正觉得自己运气不好，因为一场房屋火灾，他被迫清走家当、搬到别处。

paras.en: Then a good luck charm that he had kept under his bed changed his life.
paras.zh: 后来，他一直放在床底下的一件幸运物改变了他的人生。

paras.en: The unidentified man had fished out a giant pearl from the ocean when his anchor got stuck on the rock while sailing off a coastal island in the Philippines ten years ago.
paras.zh: 十年前，这名身份不明的男子在菲律宾一座沿海岛屿附近航行时，船锚卡在了石头上，他就从海里捞出了一颗巨大的珍珠。

w.m: adj. 身份不明的；未透露姓名的

paras.en: When he was forced to sell it, the shocked tourist agent at Puerto Princesa told him that the seventy-seven-pound giant pearl that he had kept hidden in his rundown wooden house was the biggest pearl in the world, which was valued at 76 million pounds.
paras.zh: 他被迫卖掉珍珠时，公主港的一位旅游代理人大吃一惊，告诉他，他藏在破旧木屋里的这颗七十七磅重的大珍珠是世界上最大的珍珠，价值七千六百万英镑。

paras.en: The Pearl of Allah, which is currently on display in a New York museum, only weighs 14 pounds.
paras.zh: 目前在纽约一家博物馆展出的“真主之珠”只有十四磅重。

paras.en: That is five times smaller than the pearl that the fisherman just handed in.
paras.zh: 这颗珍珠只有渔民刚上交的那颗的五分之一左右。

paras.en: The monstrous pearl measured at one foot wide and two point two feet long is going to be verified by local experts and international authorities before hopefully going on display to attract more tourists in the little town.
paras.zh: 这颗巨型珍珠宽一英尺，长二点二英尺，将由当地专家和国际权威机构进行鉴定，之后有望公开展出，为这座小镇吸引更多游客。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What happened to the Philippine fisherman one day?
paras.zh: 第五题：这名菲律宾渔民有一天遇到了什么事？

paras.en: Question six: What was the fisherman forced to do?
paras.zh: 第六题：渔民被迫做了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What did the fisherman learn from the tourist agent?
paras.zh: 第七题：渔民从旅游代理人那里得知了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation 1.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Mr. Smith, it’s a pleasure meeting you.
paras.zh: 史密斯先生，很高兴见到您。

paras.en: Nice to meet you too.
paras.zh: 我也很高兴见到你。

paras.en: What can I do for you?
paras.zh: 有什么我能帮你的吗？

w.h: what can I do for you

paras.en: Well, I’m here to show you what our firm can do for you.
paras.zh: 嗯，我来是想给您介绍一下我们公司能为您做些什么。

paras.en: Astra Consultants has branches in over fifty countries, offering different business services.
paras.zh: 阿斯特拉咨询公司在五十多个国家设有分公司，提供各种商务服务。

paras.en: We are a global company with 75 years of history, and our clients include some of the world’s largest companies.
paras.zh: 我们是一家有七十五年历史的跨国公司，客户里有一些全世界最大的企业。

paras.en: Thank you, Mrs. Houston.
paras.zh: 谢谢你，休斯顿夫人。

paras.en: I know Astra Consultants is a famous company, but you said you would show me what you could do for me.
paras.zh: 我知道阿斯特拉咨询是一家有名的公司，可你说你要给我看看你们能为我做什么。

paras.en: Well, what exactly can your firm do for my company?
paras.zh: 那么，你们公司到底能为我的公司做些什么呢？

paras.en: We advise businesses on all matters, from market analysis to legal issues.
paras.zh: 从市场分析到法律问题，我们在各个方面为企业提供咨询。

w.m: v. 给……出主意；向……提供咨询

paras.en: Anything a business like yours could need, our firm offers expert advice.
paras.zh: 像您这样的企业可能需要的任何东西，我们公司都能提供专业建议。

paras.en: Could I ask you, Mr. Smith, to tell me a little about your company and the challenges you face?
paras.zh: 史密斯先生，能不能请您给我讲讲您的公司，还有您面临的挑战？

paras.en: That way I could better respond as to how we can help you.
paras.zh: 这样我就能更好地回答我们可以怎样帮您。

paras.en: Okay, sure.
paras.zh: 好的，没问题。

paras.en: This is a family business started by my grandfather in 1950.
paras.zh: 这是我祖父在一九五〇年创办的家族企业。

paras.en: We employ just over 100 people.
paras.zh: 我们只雇了一百多人。

paras.en: We manufacture and export stone for buildings and other constructions.
paras.zh: 我们生产和出口建筑以及其他工程用的石材。

paras.en: Our clients usually want a special kind of stone cut in a special design.
paras.zh: 我们的客户通常要按特别的设计切割一种特别的石材。

paras.en: And that’s what we do in our factory.
paras.zh: 这就是我们工厂做的事。

paras.en: Our main challenge is that our national currency is rising and we’re losing competitive advantage to stone producers in India.
paras.zh: 我们的主要难题是本国货币在升值，我们在跟印度石材生产商的竞争中正在失去优势。

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: That’s very interesting.
paras.zh: 这很有意思。

paras.en: I would suggest that you let us first conduct a financial analysis of your company, together with an analysis of your competitors in India.
paras.zh: 我建议您先让我们给贵公司做一次财务分析，同时分析一下您在印度的竞争对手。

paras.en: That way we could offer the best advice on different ways forward for you.
paras.zh: 这样我们就能就您今后的几种出路给出最好的建议。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What do we learn about the woman’s company?
paras.zh: 第八题：关于女士的公司，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the man say about his own company?
paras.zh: 第九题：男士是怎么说他自己的公司的？

paras.en: Question ten: What is the main problem with the man’s company?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士的公司主要的问题是什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman suggest doing to help the man’s company?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士建议做什么来帮助男士的公司？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Wow, congratulations, Simon.
paras.zh: 哇，恭喜你，西蒙。

paras.en: The place looks absolutely amazing.
paras.zh: 这地方看起来真是太棒了。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；了不起的

paras.en: Really?
paras.zh: 真的吗？

paras.en: You think so?
paras.zh: 你这么觉得？

paras.en: Of course.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: I love it.
paras.zh: 我太喜欢了。

paras.en: It looks like you had a professional interior designer.
paras.zh: 看起来像是请了专业的室内设计师。

paras.en: But you didn’t, did you?
paras.zh: 可你没请，对吧？

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 对，没请。

paras.en: I did it all by myself, with a little help from my brother Greg.
paras.zh: 全是我自己弄的，我哥哥格雷格帮了点忙。

paras.en: He’s actually in the construction business, which was really helpful.
paras.zh: 他其实就是做建筑这一行的，帮了我大忙。

paras.en: I honestly am impressed.
paras.zh: 说实话，我真的很佩服。

w.m: adj. 佩服的；印象深刻的

paras.en: I know I could probably repaint the walls in my house over a weekend or something, but not a full renovation.
paras.zh: 我知道我大概能花一个周末之类的时间把家里的墙重新刷一遍，可全面翻修就不行了。

paras.en: Where did you get your ideas?
paras.zh: 你的点子是从哪儿来的？

paras.en: I wouldn’t know where to start.
paras.zh: 我都不知道从哪儿下手。

paras.en: Well, for a while now, I’ve been regularly buying home design magazines.
paras.zh: 嗯，这段时间以来，我一直定期买家装设计杂志。

paras.en: Every now and then, I’d save a picture I liked.
paras.zh: 时不时地，我会把喜欢的图片留下来。

paras.en: Believe it or not, I had a full notebook of magazine pages.
paras.zh: 信不信由你，我攒了满满一本杂志剪页。

paras.en: Since my overall style was quite minimal, I thought, and hoped, a whole renovation wouldn’t be too difficult.
paras.zh: 因为我整体的风格很简约，我就想，也希望，整个翻修不会太难。

paras.en: And sure enough, with Greg’s help, it was very achievable.
paras.zh: 果然，有格雷格帮忙，这事很容易就办成了。

w.m: adj. 可以做到的；可实现的

paras.en: Was it very expensive?
paras.zh: 花了很多钱吗？

paras.en: I imagine a project like this could be.
paras.zh: 我想像这样的工程应该挺贵的。

paras.en: Actually, it was surprisingly affordable.
paras.zh: 其实，价钱出奇地实惠。

w.m: adj. 负担得起的；实惠的

paras.en: I managed to sell a lot of my old furniture and put that extra money towards the new material.
paras.zh: 我把很多旧家具卖了，多出来的钱就拿去买新材料。

paras.en: Greg was also able to get some discounted materials from a recent project he was working on as well.
paras.zh: 格雷格最近在做一个工程，他也从那儿弄到了一些打折的材料。

paras.en: Great.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: If you don’t mind, I’d like to pick your brain a bit more.
paras.zh: 你要是不介意的话，我想再向你多讨教讨教。

paras.en: Jonathan and I are thinking of renovating our sitting-room.
paras.zh: 我和乔纳森正想重新装修我们的客厅。

paras.en: Not the whole house, not yet, anyway.
paras.zh: 不是整个房子，至少现在还不打算。

paras.en: And we’d love to get some inspiration from your experience.
paras.zh: 我们很想从你的经历里得到一些灵感。

paras.en: Are you free to come over for a coffee early next week?
paras.zh: 下周早些时候你有空过来喝杯咖啡吗？

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What do we learn about the woman from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十二题：从对话中，我们对女士了解到什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: Where did the man get his ideas for the project?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士这次装修的点子是从哪儿来的？

paras.en: Question 14: What did the man say about the project he recently completed?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于他最近完成的工程，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: Why does the woman invite the man to her house next week?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士为什么请男士下周到她家来？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you’ll hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Removing foreign objects from ears and noses costs England almost 3 million pounds a year, a study suggests.
paras.zh: 一项研究显示，英国每年要花将近三百万英镑从人们的耳朵和鼻子里取出异物。

paras.en: Children were responsible for the vast majority of cases, 95% of objects removed from noses and 85% from ears.
paras.zh: 绝大多数病例都是孩子，从鼻子里取出的异物有百分之九十五、耳朵里的有百分之八十五来自孩子。

paras.en: Every year, an average of 1,218 nose and 2,479 ear removals took place between 2010 and 2016.
paras.zh: 二〇一〇年到二〇一六年间，平均每年有一千二百一十八例鼻腔异物取出和二千四百七十九例耳道异物取出。

paras.en: According to England’s Hospital Episode Statistics, children aged 1 to 4 were the most likely to need help from doctors for a foreign object in their nose.
paras.zh: 据英国医院诊疗统计数据，一到四岁的孩子最有可能因为鼻子里有异物而需要医生帮忙。

paras.en: Five- to nine-year-olds come to the hospital with something in their ears the most.
paras.zh: 五到九岁的孩子因为耳朵里有东西来医院的最多。

paras.en: Jewelry items accounted for up to forty percent of cases in both the ears and noses of children.
paras.zh: 在孩子耳朵和鼻子的病例里，首饰类物品最多占到百分之四十。

paras.en: Paper and plastic toys were the items removed next most from noses.
paras.zh: 从鼻子里取出最多的其次是纸和塑料玩具。

paras.en: Cotton buds and pencils were also found in ears.
paras.zh: 耳朵里还发现过棉签和铅笔。

paras.en: According to the study, the occurrence of foreign objects in children is generally attributed to curiosity.
paras.zh: 这项研究认为，孩子身上出现异物，一般是因为好奇心。

paras.en: Children have an impulse to explore their noses and ears.
paras.zh: 孩子们总有一种冲动，想去探探自己的鼻子和耳朵。

paras.en: This results in the accidental entry of foreign objects.
paras.zh: 这就导致异物不小心进到里面。

paras.en: Any ear, nose, and throat surgeon has many weird stories about wonderful objects found in the noses and ears of children and adults.
paras.zh: 每个耳鼻喉科医生都有很多离奇的故事，讲的是在孩子和大人的鼻子、耳朵里发现的各种稀奇东西。

paras.en: Batteries can pose a particular danger.
paras.zh: 电池可能特别危险。

paras.en: In all cases, prevention is better than cure.
paras.zh: 不管什么情况，预防都胜于治疗。

paras.en: This is why many toys contain warnings about small parts.
paras.zh: 这就是为什么很多玩具上都有小零件的警示。

paras.en: Recognizing problems early and seeking medical attention is important.
paras.zh: 及早发现问题、及时就医很重要。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What does England spend an annual three million pounds on?
paras.zh: 第十六题：英国每年花三百万英镑用在什么上？

paras.en: Question 17: What do we learn from England’s Hospital Episode Statistics?
paras.zh: 第十七题：从英国医院诊疗统计数据中我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What is generally believed to account for children putting things in their ears or noses?
paras.zh: 第十八题：人们一般认为孩子把东西放进耳朵或鼻子里是什么原因？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Good morning.
paras.zh: 早上好。

paras.en: Today I would like to talk to you about my charity ReBicycle.
paras.zh: 今天我想跟大家讲讲我的慈善机构“再骑行”。

paras.en: But before that, let me introduce someone.
paras.zh: 不过在那之前，我先介绍一个人。

paras.en: This is Layla Rahimi.
paras.zh: 这位是蕾拉·拉希米。

paras.en: She was so scared when she first moved to New Zealand that she struggled to leave the house and would spend days working up the courage to walk to the supermarket for basic supplies.
paras.zh: 她刚搬到新西兰时特别害怕，连出门都很难，要花好几天鼓起勇气，才敢走路去超市买些基本的日用品。

paras.en: After a few months of being quite down and unhappy, she was invited to join a local bike club.
paras.zh: 她有好几个月都情绪低落、闷闷不乐，后来有人邀请她加入当地的一个自行车俱乐部。

paras.en: At this time, ReBicycle got involved and gave Leila a second-hand bicycle.
paras.zh: 这时，“再骑行”参与进来，送给蕾拉一辆二手自行车。

paras.en: Within weeks, her depression had begun to ease as she cycled.
paras.zh: 骑上车没过几周，她的抑郁就开始缓解了。

paras.en: The bicycle totally changed her life, giving her hope and a true feeling of freedom.
paras.zh: 这辆自行车彻底改变了她的生活，给了她希望，让她真正感受到了自由。

paras.en: To date, ReBicycle has donated more than 200 bikes to those in need and is now expanding bike riding lessons as demand soars.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，“再骑行”已经向有需要的人捐赠了两百多辆自行车，现在随着需求激增，还在扩大骑车课程。

paras.en: With a bike, newcomers here can travel farther but for almost no cost.
paras.zh: 有了自行车，刚来这里的人能去更远的地方，却几乎不花钱。

paras.en: The three hours a day they used to spend walking to and from English language lessons has been reduced to just one hour.
paras.zh: 他们以前每天来回英语课要走三个小时，现在只要一个小时了。

paras.en: Our bike riding lessons are so successful that we are urgently looking for more volunteers.
paras.zh: 我们的骑车课非常成功，所以我们正急需更多志愿者。

paras.en: Learning to ride a bike is almost always more difficult for an adult and this can take days and weeks rather than hours.
paras.zh: 对成年人来说，学骑自行车几乎总是更难，可能要花几天、几周，而不是几个小时。

paras.en: So if any of you have some free time during the weekend, please come join us at ReBicycle and make a difference in someone’s life.
paras.zh: 所以，如果你们谁周末有空，请来“再骑行”加入我们，改变别人的生活。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What did ReBicycle do to help Leila Rahimi?
paras.zh: 第十九题：“再骑行”做了什么来帮助蕾拉·拉希米？

paras.en: Question 20: What is ReBicycle doing to help those in need?
paras.zh: 第二十题：“再骑行”正在做什么来帮助有需要的人？

paras.en: Question 21: What do we learn from the passage about ReBicycle?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：从短文中我们对“再骑行”了解到什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Thanks to the International Space Station, we know quite a bit about the effects of low gravity on the human body.
paras.zh: 多亏了国际空间站，我们对低重力对人体的影响已经了解了不少。

paras.en: But NASA scientists want to learn more.
paras.zh: 可是美国国家航空航天局的科学家想了解得更多。

paras.en: To that end, they have been studying how other species deal with low gravity, specifically focusing on mice.
paras.zh: 为此，他们一直在研究其他物种如何应对低重力，特别关注的是老鼠。

paras.en: The results are both interesting and humorous.
paras.zh: 结果既有意思又好笑。

paras.en: The scientists first sent some mice in a specially designed cage to the International Space Station.
paras.zh: 科学家先把一些老鼠装进一个特别设计的笼子，送上了国际空间站。

paras.en: The cage allowed them to study the behavior of the mice remotely from Earth via video.
paras.zh: 有了这个笼子，他们就能在地球上通过视频远程研究老鼠的行为。

paras.en: As you’ll notice in the video, the mice definitely seem uncomfortable at the beginning of the experiment.
paras.zh: 你会在视频里注意到，实验刚开始时，老鼠显然很不自在。

w.m: adj. 不舒服的；不自在的

paras.en: They move around clumsily, drifting within the small confines of the cage, and do their best to figure out which way is up, but without success.
paras.zh: 它们笨手笨脚地四处移动，在笼子的狭小空间里飘来飘去，想尽办法弄清哪边是上，却怎么也弄不清。

paras.en: However, it’s not long before the mice begin to catch on.
paras.zh: 不过，没过多久，老鼠就开始掌握窍门了。

paras.en: They adapt remarkably well to their new environment and even use the lack of gravity to their advantage as they push themselves around the cage.
paras.zh: 它们出奇地适应了新环境，甚至利用失重，在笼子里推着自己到处跑。

paras.en: That’s when things really get wild.
paras.zh: 这时候，事情才真正热闹起来。

paras.en: The eleventh day of the experiment shows the mice are not just dealing with the gravity change, but actually seem to be enjoying it.
paras.zh: 实验第十一天的情况表明，老鼠不只是在应对重力变化，而且好像真的很享受。

paras.en: Several of the mice are observed running around the cage walls.
paras.zh: 研究人员看到几只老鼠沿着笼壁跑来跑去。

paras.en: The scientist wanted to see whether the mice would continue doing the same kinds of activities they were observed doing on Earth.
paras.zh: 科学家想看看老鼠是否会继续做它们在地球上被观察到的那些活动。

paras.en: The study showed that the mice kept much of their routines intact, including cleaning themselves and eating when hungry.
paras.zh: 研究显示，老鼠在很大程度上保持了原来的日常习惯，包括清洁自己、饿了就吃东西。

w.m: adj. 完整无损的；保持原样的

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do NASA scientists want to learn about?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：美国国家航空航天局的科学家想了解什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the passage say about the mice at the beginning of the experiment?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于实验刚开始时的老鼠，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What was observed about the mice on the eleventh day of the experiment?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：实验第十一天，人们观察到老鼠有什么表现？

paras.en: Question 25: What did the scientists find about the mice from the experiment?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：科学家从实验中发现了老鼠的什么情况？

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
