passages.name: 2020年12月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一名服务员捡到一位退休社工遗失的近四十二万四千美元支票，设法还给了她，还婉拒了她的酬谢。第二篇新闻报道讲阿拉斯加的希什马廖夫村因为全球变暖、海平面上升，投票决定搬到本州大陆，但搬迁费用高昂，短期内难以实现。第三篇新闻报道讲加拿大哈利法克斯一名男子做社会实验，替人扶门，一百人里有九十九人道了谢。第一段长对话里，温斯顿打电话向太阳能公司咨询安装太阳能板，问到能省多少钱、要花多少钱。第二段长对话里，女士到旅行社咨询圣诞节去澳大利亚的跟团游，工作人员介绍了一个十四晚的套餐。第一篇短文讲印度尼西亚巴厘岛将向游客征收环保税，并禁止一次性塑料袋和吸管。第二篇短文讲濒危的北大西洋露脊鲸今年出现小规模生育高峰，观鲸者不得靠得太近。第三篇短文讲牛奶越来越不受欢迎，很多人喝牛奶会不舒服，因为体内缺少分解乳糖的蛋白质，但牛奶也很有营养。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet One with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A waiter has returned a check worth nearly four hundred twenty four thousand dollars to a retired social worker who lost it.
paras.zh: 一名服务员把一张近四十二万四千美元的支票还给了丢失它的退休社工。

paras.en: The waiter found a bank envelope while cleaning off a table last Saturday at a restaurant.
paras.zh: 上周六，这名服务员在一家餐馆擦桌子时发现了一个银行信封。

paras.en: He ran outside, but the customer was gone.
paras.zh: 他跑到外面，可那位顾客已经走了。

paras.en: He opened the envelope and got a shock.
paras.zh: 他打开信封，吓了一跳。

paras.en: After an unsuccessful search, the restaurant’s owner called the Daily News for help.
paras.zh: 找了一圈没找到，餐馆老板就打电话向《每日新闻》求助。

paras.en: The relieved customer was reunited with her check on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 星期三，这位顾客终于拿回了支票，松了一口气。

paras.en: It contained money from her apartment sale, already planned for a down payment on a new home.
paras.zh: 支票里是她卖公寓的钱，原本打算用来付新房子的首付。

paras.en: The customer did not tip the waiter after her meal.
paras.zh: 这位顾客吃完饭没给服务员小费。

paras.en: She tried to give him money later on, but he graciously declined.
paras.zh: 后来她想给他钱，可他客气地谢绝了。

paras.en: The waiter, who’s working his way through school, did accept the customer’s apology and gratitude and said he was happy to have helped her.
paras.zh: 这名服务员正在半工半读，他接受了顾客的道歉和感谢，说很高兴帮到了她。

w.m: 半工半读；靠打工读完书

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What does the news report say about the waiter?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于这名服务员，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What did the customer try to do when she got her check back?
paras.zh: 第二题：顾客拿回支票后想做什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The village of Merif in Alaska voted on Tuesday to move to the state’s mainland.
paras.zh: 星期二，阿拉斯加的希什马廖夫村投票决定搬到本州的大陆上。

paras.en: The move is due to global warming and rising sea levels.
paras.zh: 搬迁是因为全球变暖和海平面上升。

paras.en: Most of the village’s 169 registered voters took part in the town hall meeting.
paras.zh: 村里一百六十九名登记选民大多参加了这次镇民大会。

paras.en: They decided in a vote of 89 to 78 to move from their land on Sarichef Island, near the Arctic Circle.
paras.zh: 他们以八十九票对七十八票决定从北极圈附近萨里切夫岛上的家园搬走。

paras.en: Merif Council Secretary Donna Barr said the vote was largely symbolic.
paras.zh: 希什马廖夫村议会秘书唐娜·巴尔说，这次投票很大程度上只是象征性的。

w.m: adv. 很大程度上；主要地

paras.en: It will be costly financially to the community.
paras.zh: 这对整个社区来说经济上代价会很大。

paras.en: About 15 years ago, they estimated the cost at $180 million.
paras.zh: 大约十五年前，他们估计费用是一亿八千万美元。

paras.en: I would figure it’s much higher now, Barr said.
paras.zh: 巴尔说：“我估计现在要高得多。”

paras.en: We don’t see the move happening in our lifetime because of the funding.
paras.zh: “因为资金问题，我们这辈子都看不到搬迁的那一天。”

paras.en: The village’s roughly 650 residents have seen warming temperatures melt sea ice and permanently frozen land.
paras.zh: 村里大约六百五十名居民眼看着气温升高，海冰和永久冻土都在融化。

paras.en: This has resulted in houses falling into the water.
paras.zh: 这已经导致一些房子塌进水里。

paras.en: At least 31 villages in Alaska face immediate threats due to climate change, the Government Accountability Office reported in 2009.
paras.zh: 美国政府问责局二〇〇九年报告说，阿拉斯加至少有三十一个村庄因为气候变化面临迫在眉睫的威胁。

w.m: adj. 迫在眉睫的；直接的

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What is Meriff’s vote on Tuesday about?
paras.zh: 第三题：希什马廖夫村星期二的投票是关于什么的？

paras.en: Question four: Why did Donna Barr say they wouldn’t see the plan carried out any time soon?
paras.zh: 第四题：唐娜·巴尔为什么说他们短期内看不到这个计划实施？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A man in Halifax, Canada, wanted to find out if people were thankful for someone holding the door open for them.
paras.zh: 加拿大哈利法克斯的一名男子想弄清楚，有人替别人扶着门时，大家会不会心存感激。

paras.en: The social experiment showed that 99 out of 100 people expressed gratitude.
paras.zh: 这项社会实验表明，一百人里有九十九人表达了感谢。

paras.en: I didn’t think we were going to get 99.
paras.zh: “我没想到会有九十九个人。

paras.en: I don’t know why, but I was pleasantly surprised because it went beyond just thank you.
paras.zh: 不知道为什么，但我又惊又喜，因为这远远不止一句谢谢。

paras.en: People got into conversations with us, said Steve Foran, CEO of Gratitude at Work.
paras.zh: 大家还跟我们聊了起来。”“职场感恩”公司的首席执行官史蒂夫·福兰说。

paras.en: What we know from research is that from grateful people come good things, he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“研究告诉我们，心怀感激的人会带来好事。”

paras.en: A simple way to induce gratitude in people is opening doors and so we went to six places and opened the doors for people.
paras.zh: “让人心生感激的一个简单方法就是给人开门，所以我们去了六个地方给人开门。”

paras.en: For the experiment, Foran’s team went to a shopping centre, a mall, two office buildings and a coffee shop.
paras.zh: 为了做这个实验，福兰的团队去了一家购物中心、一家商场、两栋写字楼和一家咖啡店。

paras.en: The door was held for 15 to 20 people at a time at each location.
paras.zh: 在每个地点，他们一次为十五到二十人扶门。

paras.en: We did have one that didn’t say thank you.
paras.zh: “确实有一个人没说谢谢。

paras.en: We’re not here to judge them, because on any given day, that could be me or you.
paras.zh: 我们不是来评判他们的，因为不管哪天，那都可能是我，也可能是你。

paras.en: I suspect out of the 100 people there were probably a bunch of them having a bad day.
paras.zh: 我猜这一百个人里，可能有不少人那天过得不顺。

paras.en: But grateful people make people grateful, said Foran.
paras.zh: 但心怀感激的人会让别人也心怀感激。”福兰说。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is the purpose of the social experiment?
paras.zh: 第五题：这项社会实验的目的是什么？

paras.en: Question six: What did Steve Ferran and his team do in the experiment?
paras.zh: 第六题：史蒂夫·福兰和他的团队在实验中做了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What do we learn from the news report?
paras.zh: 第七题：从这篇新闻报道中我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Ray’s Solar.
paras.zh: 雷氏太阳能。

paras.en: Lisa speaking.
paras.zh: 我是丽莎。

paras.en: How can I help?
paras.zh: 有什么可以帮您的？

paras.en: Hi, my name is Winston.
paras.zh: 你好，我叫温斯顿。

paras.en: I wish to inquire about solar panel installations.
paras.zh: 我想咨询一下安装太阳能板的事。

paras.en: Yes.
paras.zh: 可以。

paras.en: What would you like to know?
paras.zh: 您想了解什么？

paras.en: Well, my neighbor installed panels on his roof about a year ago in order to power his hot water.
paras.zh: 嗯，我邻居大约一年前在他家屋顶装了太阳能板，用来烧热水。

paras.en: He tells me it has saved him over five hundred dollars thus far.
paras.zh: 他跟我说，到目前为止已经给他省了五百多美元。

paras.en: Does that sound about right to you?
paras.zh: 你觉得这个数差不多吗？

paras.en: Well, I’m not familiar with your neighbor or his particular setup, but that amount is definitely possible.
paras.zh: 嗯，我不了解您的邻居，也不了解他家具体的装置，但这个数目完全有可能。

paras.en: I can tell you that the average four-bedroom house may typically have a roof with fifty square meters of surface area.
paras.zh: 我可以告诉您，普通的四居室房子，屋顶一般有五十平方米的面积。

paras.en: Four panels on one side of that roof could save a family of four around three hundred dollars a year.
paras.zh: 在屋顶的一面装四块板，一个四口之家一年能省三百美元左右。

paras.en: Okay, that sounds about right then.
paras.zh: 好的，那听起来差不多。

paras.en: My house is about the size you described, but my neighbor’s is bigger.
paras.zh: 我家房子差不多就是你说的那么大，不过我邻居家的更大。

paras.en: I’m not sure how many panels he has up there, but he does have a large family of six.
paras.zh: 我不清楚他屋顶上装了几块板，不过他家确实人多，一家六口。

paras.en: Are you interested in installing some solar panels on your roof, sir?
paras.zh: 先生，您有兴趣在您家屋顶装一些太阳能板吗？

paras.en: Yes, I’m considering it.
paras.zh: 是的，我正在考虑。

paras.en: If you wish to come into our office, we could show you the different solutions we offer.
paras.zh: 如果您愿意来我们办公室，我们可以给您介绍我们提供的各种方案。

paras.en: Okay, I might do that.
paras.zh: 好的，我可能会去。

paras.en: But just quickly, if you don’t mind, could you tell me approximately how much a typical installation costs?
paras.zh: 不过如果你不介意，能不能简单说一下，一套普通的安装大概要多少钱？

paras.en: Like, say, four panels?
paras.zh: 比如说，四块板？

paras.en: Prices do vary depending on different factors, but as a rough estimate, it’s around $2,000.
paras.zh: 价格确实会因为各种因素有所不同，不过粗略估计，大概两千美元。

paras.en: But you know, a typical household will make back that initial investment in about five years.
paras.zh: 不过您知道，普通家庭大约五年就能收回最初的投资。

paras.en: Okay, I see.
paras.zh: 好的，我明白了。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What is the man’s purpose for calling the woman?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士给女士打电话的目的是什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What do we learn about the man’s neighbor from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第九题：从对话中，我们对男士的邻居了解到什么？

paras.en: Question ten: What is one of the man’s chief concerns?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士主要关心的事情之一是什么？

paras.en: Question 11: How long will it take a typical household to make back the initial investment?
paras.zh: 第十一题：一个普通家庭要多久才能收回最初的投资？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Good afternoon.
paras.zh: 下午好。

paras.en: Sorry to have kept you waiting.
paras.zh: 抱歉，让您久等了。

paras.en: How can I help you?
paras.zh: 有什么可以帮您的？

paras.en: Oh, no problem.
paras.zh: 哦，没关系。

paras.en: I’m interested in booking a holiday to Australia, and wonder if you could tell me what deals you have.
paras.zh: 我想订一个去澳大利亚的度假行程，不知道你们这儿有什么优惠。

paras.en: Sure.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: Are you only looking for flights, or a package holiday with everything included?
paras.zh: 您是只要机票，还是要一个全包的跟团游套餐？

paras.en: When you say everything, what do you mean?
paras.zh: 你说全包，是指哪些？

paras.en: Well, a package holiday would include your flights, hotels, meals, day trips to different places of interest, and transport to and from the airport.
paras.zh: 嗯，跟团游套餐包括机票、酒店、餐食、去各个景点的一日游，还有机场接送。

paras.en: Yeah, that sounds pretty good.
paras.zh: 嗯，听起来挺不错的。

paras.en: I’m going with my family, so it would be nice to have everything taken care of.
paras.zh: 我是跟家人一起去，所以什么都有人安排好就再好不过了。

paras.en: So what sort of deals do you have for package holidays, then?
paras.zh: 那你们的跟团游套餐都有哪些优惠呢？

paras.en: All sorts, really.
paras.zh: 各种各样的都有。

paras.en: How long do you want to go for, and on what dates?
paras.zh: 您想去多久，哪几天去？

paras.en: Two weeks around Christmastime would be great.
paras.zh: 圣诞节前后两个星期就太好了。

paras.en: Okay, let me check that for you.
paras.zh: 好的，我给您查一下。

paras.en: Here’s one: fourteen nights in southeastern Australia.
paras.zh: 有一个：澳大利亚东南部十四晚。

paras.en: Five nights in Sydney and five nights in Melbourne.
paras.zh: 悉尼五晚、墨尔本五晚。

paras.en: And then for the other four nights, you can choose from a list of trips to other places nearby.
paras.zh: 然后剩下的四晚，您可以从附近其他地方的一系列行程里挑选。

paras.en: You could visit Canberra, for example, or the Blue Mountains.
paras.zh: 比如说，您可以去堪培拉，或者去蓝山。

paras.en: Or you could go for a drive down the Great Ocean Road.
paras.zh: 或者您可以开车沿着大洋路兜兜风。

paras.en: Also, if you’re interested in wine, you could go on a tour of the places where they grow grapes and make wine.
paras.zh: 另外，如果您对葡萄酒感兴趣，还可以参加一个行程，参观种葡萄、酿葡萄酒的地方。

paras.en: That sounds great.
paras.zh: 听起来太好了。

paras.en: It’s good we can choose some activities ourselves.
paras.zh: 能自己挑一些活动真好。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: Where is the conversation taking place?
paras.zh: 第十二题：这段对话是在哪里进行的？

paras.en: Question thirteen: Why is the woman interested in package holidays?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士为什么对跟团游套餐感兴趣？

paras.en: Question fourteen: How long does the woman want to go for the holiday?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士想去度假多久？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the woman say she likes about the holiday package?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士说她喜欢这个度假套餐的哪一点？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you’ll hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Tourists taking a holiday in the Indonesian island of Bali are facing a new $14 per person tax when they arrive on the holiday island from next year.
paras.zh: 从明年起，到印度尼西亚巴厘岛度假的游客一上岛就要交一笔每人十四美元的新税。

paras.en: But this is a green tax which Bali Governor Wayan Koster has been working on for months, and which is designed to help clean up the island’s natural environment.
paras.zh: 不过这是一项环保税，巴厘省长瓦扬·科斯特已经为此忙了好几个月，目的是帮助清理岛上的自然环境。

paras.en: And with good reason, too.
paras.zh: 而且这么做也确实有充分的理由。

paras.en: Indonesia is drowning in plastics.
paras.zh: 印度尼西亚被塑料垃圾淹没了。

paras.en: Recycling is not one of the country’s strong points.
paras.zh: 回收利用不是这个国家的强项。

paras.en: It’s not uncommon to be offered many more plastic bags than one could ever need when visiting supermarkets and shopping malls.
paras.zh: 在超市和购物中心买东西时，店家塞给你的塑料袋比你需要的多得多，这种事并不少见。

paras.en: But, slowly, things are starting to change for the better.
paras.zh: 不过，情况正慢慢开始好转。

paras.en: Back in 2016, the medium-sized city of Banjarmasin banned single-use plastic bags.
paras.zh: 早在二〇一六年，中等规模的城市马辰就禁用了一次性塑料袋。

paras.en: The city of Bogor followed suit in 2018.
paras.zh: 二〇一八年，茂物市也跟着这样做了。

paras.en: A few months ago, Koster announced a plan that would not only ban single-use plastic bags from supermarkets and convenience stores, but plastic bags and straws across the island.
paras.zh: 几个月前，科斯特宣布了一项计划，不仅要禁止超市和便利店使用一次性塑料袋，还要在全岛禁用塑料袋和吸管。

paras.en: The regulation will come into full effect next month.
paras.zh: 这项规定下个月将全面生效。

paras.en: We received a fast and quick response from the Balinese people.
paras.zh: “巴厘人很快就给了我们回应。

paras.en: Not only positive responses from the Balinese, we received good responses from the central government, other local governments, and even from overseas.
paras.zh: 不光巴厘人反应积极，中央政府、其他地方政府，甚至国外，也都给了我们很好的反馈。”

paras.en: Koster told the Sydney Morning Herald this week during an interview.
paras.zh: 科斯特本周在接受《悉尼先驱晨报》采访时这样说。

paras.en: The Governor is a determined environmentalist, and he has more laws planned to protect the island’s waterways, in particular, and to support the introduction of electric vehicles too.
paras.zh: 这位省长是个坚定的环保主义者，他还计划出台更多法规，特别是要保护岛上的水道，也要支持推广电动汽车。

w.m: adj. 坚定的；下定决心的

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What will tourists have to do when they visit Indonesia’s Bali Island?
paras.zh: 第十六题：游客去印度尼西亚的巴厘岛时，必须做什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What does the passage say about Indonesia?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于印度尼西亚，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What is the new plan Governor Koster recently announced?
paras.zh: 第十八题：科斯特省长最近宣布的新计划是什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: An endangered species of whale is experiencing a small baby boom off the coast of America.
paras.zh: 一种濒危的鲸鱼正在美国沿海迎来一个小小的生育高峰。

paras.en: The North Atlantic right whale is one of the rarest species of whale on the planet, numbering only about 411.
paras.zh: 北大西洋露脊鲸是地球上最稀有的鲸鱼之一，总数只有大约四百一十一头。

paras.en: But the Centre for Coastal Studies said Friday that its aerial survey team spotted a mum with two babies in Cape Cod Bay a day earlier.
paras.zh: 不过，海岸研究中心星期五说，前一天，他们的空中调查小组在科德角湾看到一头鲸鱼妈妈带着两头幼鲸。

paras.en: That brings the number seen in nearby waters alone this year to three.
paras.zh: 这样一来，今年光在附近海域看到的幼鲸就有三头了。

paras.en: That’s big news because the whale population has been falling and no baby whales were seen last year.
paras.zh: 这可是大新闻，因为这种鲸的数量一直在下降，去年一头幼鲸也没看到。

paras.en: In all, seven baby whales have been spotted so far this year.
paras.zh: 今年到目前为止，总共已经发现了七头幼鲸。

paras.en: The whale population has become endangered due to commercial whaling activities in recent years.
paras.zh: 近年来由于商业捕鲸活动，这种鲸已经濒临灭绝。

paras.en: This is because they are sometimes hunted for their meat or their skin.
paras.zh: 这是因为它们有时会因为肉或皮被人捕杀。

paras.en: Overhunting could lead to the disappearance of the whale population, possibly causing major problems to the global food chain.
paras.zh: 过度捕杀可能导致这种鲸灭绝，还可能给全球食物链带来大问题。

paras.en: The whales give birth off the southeast coast of America in the winter and travel to feeding grounds off the northeast coast in the early spring.
paras.zh: 这种鲸冬天在美国东南沿海产崽，早春时游到东北沿海的觅食地。

paras.en: The northeast coast is a critically important source of food.
paras.zh: 东北沿海是至关重要的食物来源。

paras.en: The animals often feed close to shore.
paras.zh: 这种动物常在离岸边很近的地方觅食。

paras.en: This provides watchers on land with unbeatable views of one of the rarest of marine mammals.
paras.zh: 这让岸上的观鲸者能以绝佳的视角看到最稀有的海洋哺乳动物之一。

w.m: adj. 无与伦比的；绝佳的

paras.en: It’s illegal to get within 1,500 feet of the animals without a federal research permit, so whale watchers are discouraged from attempting to get close to the whales.
paras.zh: 没有联邦研究许可证，靠近这种动物一千五百英尺以内是违法的，所以观鲸者不得试图接近鲸鱼。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What do we learn from the passage about the North Atlantic right whale?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于北大西洋露脊鲸，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What has caused the decline of the whale population in recent years?
paras.zh: 第二十题：近年来是什么导致了这种鲸的数量下降？

paras.en: Question 21: Why do the whales travel to the northeast coast of America in the early spring?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：这种鲸为什么在早春游到美国东北沿海？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: An average person consumes 144 pints of milk a year.
paras.zh: 一个普通人一年要喝一百四十四品脱牛奶。

paras.en: But 40% of that is poured onto cereal, and 60% of those people are children.
paras.zh: 可其中百分之四十是倒在麦片上的，而这些人里百分之六十是孩子。

paras.en: But what was once advertised as nutritious is becoming unpopular.
paras.zh: 可是，曾经被宣传为有营养的牛奶，正变得不受欢迎。

paras.en: Americans drink 37% less milk than they did in the 1970s.
paras.zh: 美国人现在喝的牛奶比二十世纪七十年代少了百分之三十七。

paras.en: And in the UK, dairy consumption overall has fallen by a third in the past 20 years.
paras.zh: 在英国，过去二十年里，乳制品的总体消费量下降了三分之一。

paras.en: Milk is increasingly being described in a negative light.
paras.zh: 牛奶越来越多地被说成是不好的东西。

paras.en: A recent blog suggested, maybe people are drinking less milk because it is poisonous to many of us.
paras.zh: 最近有篇博客说，人们喝牛奶少了，也许是因为牛奶对我们很多人来说是有毒的。

paras.en: Lactose is the sugar found in milk and dairy products.
paras.zh: 乳糖是牛奶和乳制品里的一种糖。

paras.en: It needs a series of complex proteins to break it down.
paras.zh: 要分解它，需要一系列复杂的蛋白质。

paras.en: Without enough of these proteins, the lactose is broken down by bacteria in the human body.
paras.zh: 如果这些蛋白质不够，乳糖就会在人体内被细菌分解。

paras.en: This can cause physical pain and produce gas in the stomach.
paras.zh: 这会让身体疼痛，还会让胃里产生气体。

paras.en: However, after we have finished breast or formula feeding, most of us don’t continue producing the complex proteins in our body, which are necessary to break down the lactose.
paras.zh: 不过，我们大多数人结束母乳或配方奶喂养之后，体内就不再继续产生分解乳糖所必需的那些复杂蛋白质了。

paras.en: Despite the problems in digesting milk, it does provide many benefits.
paras.zh: 虽然牛奶不好消化，但它确实有很多好处。

paras.en: Milk is nutritious, it contains vitamins A and D, as well as protein, and isn’t full of calories.
paras.zh: 牛奶有营养，含有维生素A和维生素D，还有蛋白质，热量也不高。

paras.en: You can test yourself by drinking a large glass of milk.
paras.zh: 你可以喝一大杯牛奶来测一测自己。

paras.en: If you get sick in your stomach within the next 24 hours, you are lacking the proteins to digest milk.
paras.zh: 如果接下来二十四小时内你胃里不舒服，就说明你缺少消化牛奶的蛋白质。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What does the passage say about Americans?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于美国人，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: How do Americans and British people think of milk nowadays?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：如今美国人和英国人怎么看待牛奶？

paras.en: Question 24: Why does drinking milk cause pain in some people?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：为什么有些人喝牛奶会疼？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the passage say is a benefit of milk?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：短文说牛奶有什么好处？

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲英国纽卡斯尔一个九岁男孩乔上课不让画画，父母送他去学画，老师把他的作品发到网上后，一家餐厅请他来画餐厅的墙。第二篇新闻报道讲柯丝廷·马歇尔的爱犬被偷，她在社交媒体上发视频求助，全家悬赏五千英镑找狗。第三篇新闻报道讲伦敦一家咖啡馆让顾客随意付钱吃早餐，店主希望借此把邻里联系起来。第一段长对话里，两人商量周六聚会的时间、食物、饮料和音乐。第二段长对话里，女士想买车，男士推荐她找自己卖二手车的朋友咨询。第一篇短文讲北美的野猪怎样破坏庄稼、传播疾病、威胁本地物种。第二篇短文讲两位企业家打算把咖啡豆送上太空，借返回大气层的热量烘焙。第三篇短文讲阿拉斯加小村塔科特纳每年为雪橇犬比赛的选手准备水果派，这一传统始于简·牛顿。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: And finally, in tonight’s news, a nine-year-old boy named Joe, told not to draw in class, lands a job decorating a restaurant with his drawings.
paras.zh: 最后来看今晚的新闻：一个名叫乔的九岁男孩，上课时被告知不许画画，如今却得到了一份工作——用他的画装饰一家餐厅。

paras.en: Rather than shutting down the habit of drawing in his school’s workbook, Joe’s parents decided to encourage his creativity by sending their son to an after-school art class.
paras.zh: 乔的父母没有制止他在学校练习本上画画的习惯，而是把儿子送去参加课外美术班，鼓励他发挥创造力。

paras.en: His teacher recognized Joe’s talent and posted all his work online, which led to something pretty wonderful.
paras.zh: 他的老师发现了乔的天赋，把他的所有作品都发到了网上，结果发生了一件很棒的事。

paras.en: A restaurant named Number Four in Newcastle contacted Joe’s teacher to ask if the nine-year-old could come and decorate its dining room with his drawings.
paras.zh: 纽卡斯尔一家名叫“四号”的餐厅联系了乔的老师，问这个九岁的孩子能不能来，用他的画装饰餐厅的就餐区。

paras.en: Every day after school Joe’s dad drives him to the restaurant so he can put his ideas straight on the wall.
paras.zh: 每天放学后，乔的爸爸都开车送他去餐厅，好让他把自己的想法直接画到墙上。

paras.en: Once he’s all done, the work will remain there permanently.
paras.zh: 他画完以后，这些作品会永久留在那里。

paras.en: Joe’s dad said Joe is a really talented little boy.
paras.zh: 乔的爸爸说，乔是个非常有天赋的小男孩。

w.m: adj. 有天赋的；有才能的

paras.en: He’s excellent at school, he’s great at football, but drawing is definitely what he is most passionate about.
paras.zh: 他学习成绩优秀，足球也踢得很好，但他最热爱的无疑是画画。

w.m: adj. 热爱的；充满激情的

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What did Joe’s parents decide to do?
paras.zh: 第一题：乔的父母决定做什么？

paras.en: Question two: What did the restaurant, number four, do?
paras.zh: 第二题：“四号”餐厅做了什么？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Kirsteen Marshall, a 34-year-old mum of one, posted a tearful video on social media Wednesday begging for the safe return of her beloved pet dog.
paras.zh: 柯丝廷·马歇尔今年三十四岁，有一个孩子。周三她在社交媒体上发了一段哭着求助的视频，恳求大家帮忙让她心爱的宠物狗平安回家。

w.m: adj. 哭泣的；眼里含着泪的

paras.en: After combing through the security video outside a Gorbals shop, Kirsteen has now posted an image of a man suspected of stealing the dog.
paras.zh: 柯丝廷仔细查看了戈尔巴尔斯一家商店外的监控录像，现在她发布了一张偷狗嫌疑人的照片。

paras.en: The image appears to show a man carrying the dog in his arms.
paras.zh: 照片上似乎是一个男人把狗抱在怀里。

paras.en: Kirsteen also believes the video obtained from the shop shows the dog being stolen by a man before driving off in a car which had been waiting nearby.
paras.zh: 柯丝廷还认为，从商店拿到的视频拍到了狗被一个男人偷走，随后那人坐上一辆早就等在附近的车开走了。

paras.en: The family is now offering a £5,000 reward for the safe return of the dog after launching a social media campaign to find the thief.
paras.zh: 一家人在社交媒体上发起寻找小偷的行动之后，现在又悬赏五千英镑，求狗平安回家。

paras.en: The dog is six and a half years old and was last seen wearing a red collar.
paras.zh: 这只狗六岁半，最后一次被人看到时戴着一个红色项圈。

paras.en: Kirsteen said, “We will pay that to anyone who brings him home as long as they are not responsible for his disappearance.”
paras.zh: 柯丝廷说：“谁把它送回家，我们就把这笔钱给谁，只要他跟狗的失踪无关。”

paras.en: Police are investigating the incident.
paras.zh: 警方正在调查这起事件。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What is Kirsteen Marshall trying to do?
paras.zh: 第三题：柯丝廷·马歇尔在设法做什么？

paras.en: Question 4: What does the news report say about Kirsteen Marshall’s family?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于柯丝廷·马歇尔一家，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: London’s Eggs and Bread Cafe offers boiled eggs, toast, jam, and bacon, as well as tea, coffee, and orange juice.
paras.zh: 伦敦的“鸡蛋和面包”咖啡馆供应水煮蛋、吐司、果酱和培根，还有茶、咖啡和橙汁。

paras.en: But at the end of the meal, customers don’t have to worry about the bill.
paras.zh: 不过吃完饭，顾客不用为账单发愁。

paras.en: Hungry customers can pay whatever amount they can afford to eat at the cafe, or nothing at all.
paras.zh: 饥饿的顾客在这家咖啡馆吃饭，能付多少就付多少，一分不付也行。

paras.en: Owner Guy Wilson says his cafe aims to build community rather than profits.
paras.zh: 店主盖伊·威尔逊说，他的咖啡馆为的是建立社区联系，而不是赚钱。

paras.en: He wants to provide a bridge for people to connect in an area that has been divided by class and wealth by providing affordable breakfasts.
paras.zh: 这个地区因阶层和贫富而分化，他希望通过提供人人吃得起的早餐，为人们架起一座相互联系的桥梁。

w.m: adj. 买得起的；负担得起的

paras.en: The cafe is open in the mornings every day of the year and has two members of staff or supervisors on shift every day.
paras.zh: 这家咖啡馆一年到头每天上午营业，每天都有两名员工或主管当班。

paras.en: The cafe doesn’t use volunteers but pays its staff to ensure consistency in its service.
paras.zh: 咖啡馆不用志愿者，而是给员工付工资，以保证服务始终如一。

paras.en: It doesn’t take donations and doesn’t want to be seen as a charity.
paras.zh: 它不接受捐款，也不想被人看成慈善机构。

paras.en: Mr Wilson says when people start to know other people around them, they realize they’re not that different.
paras.zh: 威尔逊先生说，人们一旦开始认识身边的人，就会发现彼此其实没那么不同。

paras.en: And whatever their financial background or their educational background, most people will have something in common with each other.
paras.zh: 而且不论经济背景或教育背景如何，大多数人彼此之间都会有共同点。

paras.en: He says it’s important that his cafe can offer his customers security and permanence.
paras.zh: 他说，重要的是他的咖啡馆能给顾客带来安全感和稳定感。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does Guy Wilson say his cafe aims to do?
paras.zh: 第五题：盖伊·威尔逊说他的咖啡馆宗旨是什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the news report say about Eggs and Bread Cafe?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于“鸡蛋和面包”咖啡馆，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question 7: What happens when people start to know each other, according to Guy Wilson?
paras.zh: 第七题：据盖伊·威尔逊说，人们开始相互认识时会怎么样？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: So what time do you think we should have the party on Saturday?
paras.zh: 那你觉得周六的聚会几点开比较好？

paras.en: How about inviting people to come at six PM?
paras.zh: 请大家晚上六点来怎么样？

paras.en: Then we’ll have the afternoon to prepare food and drink and stuff like that.
paras.zh: 这样我们下午就有时间准备吃的、喝的这些东西了。

paras.en: Yes, I was thinking that around six would be good too.
paras.zh: 好啊，我也觉得六点左右挺好。

paras.en: What food should we provide?
paras.zh: 我们准备什么吃的？

paras.en: Well, I had thought about baking a cake and some biscuits, and now I think we should prepare some sandwiches and snacks and some other kinds of food so that people can just help themselves, rather than getting everyone to sit down at the table to eat a meal.
paras.zh: 嗯，我本来想烤个蛋糕、做些饼干，现在我觉得我们应该准备一些三明治、小吃和别的吃的，让大家自己随便拿，而不是让每个人都坐到桌边吃一顿正餐。

paras.en: I think that’s a bit too formal.
paras.zh: 我觉得那样有点太正式了。

paras.en: It’s better to let people walk around and talk to each other, or sit where they like.
paras.zh: 最好让大家走来走去、互相聊聊，或者想坐哪儿就坐哪儿。

paras.en: Yes, that sounds good.
paras.zh: 对，听起来不错。

paras.en: I’ll go to the supermarket to get some drinks.
paras.zh: 我去超市买些饮料。

paras.en: I think I might try that big new supermarket on the other side of town and see what they have.
paras.zh: 我想去城那头那家新开的大超市看看有什么。

paras.en: I’ve not been there before.
paras.zh: 我以前没去过那儿。

paras.en: I think we should get some beer and wine, and some fruit juice and other soft drinks.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们应该买些啤酒、葡萄酒，再买些果汁和别的软饮料。

w.m: 软饮料；不含酒精的饮料

paras.en: What do you think?
paras.zh: 你怎么看？

paras.en: Sounds great.
paras.zh: 听起来很棒。

paras.en: I think those drinks will be enough.
paras.zh: 我觉得这些饮料够了。

paras.en: And I heard that the new supermarket offers some big discounts to attract customers.
paras.zh: 而且我听说那家新超市为了吸引顾客，打了很大的折扣。

paras.en: So going there should be a great idea.
paras.zh: 所以去那儿应该是个好主意。

paras.en: What should we do about music?
paras.zh: 音乐怎么办？

paras.en: Maybe we should ask Paul to bring his computer and speakers so that we can play some music.
paras.zh: 也许我们可以请保罗带上他的电脑和音箱，这样就能放音乐了。

paras.en: He has a great collection of different stuff.
paras.zh: 他收藏了很多各种各样的音乐。

paras.en: Yes, all right.
paras.zh: 好，行。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
paras.zh: 第八题：说话人主要在谈什么？

paras.en: Question 9: Why does the woman say it is a good idea to serve foods that guests can help themselves to?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士为什么说提供客人可以自己随便拿的食物是个好主意？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the woman say about the new supermarket?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于那家新超市，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the man suggest they ask Paul to do?
paras.zh: 第十一题：男士建议他们请保罗做什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: I’m thinking of buying a car.
paras.zh: 我在考虑买辆车。

paras.en: I wouldn’t need to use it every day, but I think it would be very convenient to have one for the weekends.
paras.zh: 我不用每天开，不过我觉得周末有辆车会很方便。

paras.en: That’s exciting.
paras.zh: 真让人激动。

paras.en: Would this be your first car?
paras.zh: 这会是你的第一辆车吗？

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不是的。

paras.en: I actually owned a car for a little while when I lived in Miami.
paras.zh: 其实我在迈阿密住的时候有过一辆车，开了一小段时间。

paras.en: You see, in America, many cities don’t have good public transport.
paras.zh: 你知道，在美国，很多城市的公共交通都不好。

paras.en: So most people need their own car to get around.
paras.zh: 所以大多数人都需要有自己的车出行。

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: So have you got your mind set on a specific model?
paras.zh: 那你心里已经看中某个具体车型了吗？

paras.en: No, not really.
paras.zh: 没有，还没定。

paras.en: I’ve heard that German cars are very reliable, but I haven’t decided on a specific model yet.
paras.zh: 我听说德国车很可靠，不过还没定下具体买哪一款。

paras.en: I’d also like it to be small, so that it’s easy to drive in the city.
paras.zh: 我还希望车小一点，这样在城里开起来方便。

paras.en: I have a friend who sells second-hand cars.
paras.zh: 我有个朋友是卖二手车的。

paras.en: In fact, I think his family owns the business.
paras.zh: 其实，我觉得这生意是他家里开的。

paras.en: He’s a really nice guy, and he knows a lot about cars.
paras.zh: 他人特别好，对车也很懂。

paras.en: I could give you his phone number if you want, and you could call him and ask him questions.
paras.zh: 你要是愿意，我可以把他的电话号码给你，你可以打电话问问他。

paras.en: Hmm, that’s nice of you, but I don’t want to feel obliged to buy one of his cars.
paras.zh: 嗯，你真好，不过我不想觉得自己非得买他的车不可。

paras.en: Oh no, he’s not like that.
paras.zh: 哦，不会的，他不是那种人。

paras.en: He’s a good friend of mine, and he would never try to pressure you or cheat you.
paras.zh: 他是我的好朋友，绝不会给你施压，也不会骗你。

paras.en: Well, if you trust him, then I guess it should be okay.
paras.zh: 嗯，既然你信得过他，那我想应该没问题。

paras.en: To be honest, I could use some help in deciding what type of vehicle would best suit my needs.
paras.zh: 说实话，我确实需要有人帮我看看哪种车最适合我。

paras.en: Speaking to an expert would be a good idea.
paras.zh: 跟懂行的人聊聊是个好主意。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 一点没错。

paras.en: You have nothing to worry about.
paras.zh: 你什么都不用担心。

paras.en: He’s a lovely guy, and he’ll be happy to help.
paras.zh: 他人很好，会很乐意帮忙的。

w.m: adj. 可爱的；令人愉快的

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Why does the woman want to have a car?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士为什么想买车？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the woman say about German cars?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于德国车，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the man recommend the woman do?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士建议女士做什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What do we learn about the man’s friend from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：从对话中，我们对男士的朋友了解到什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer, from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Pigs are not native to North America.
paras.zh: 猪并不是北美本土的动物。

paras.en: They were first introduced to California by Spanish and Russian explorers and settlers many centuries ago.
paras.zh: 许多世纪以前，西班牙和俄国的探险者和移民最早把猪带到了加利福尼亚。

paras.en: In the early times, pigs were allowed to wander freely in search of food.
paras.zh: 早年间，猪可以随意四处觅食。

paras.en: This practice also allowed many pigs to escape from farms and live in the wild, which became a problem.
paras.zh: 这种做法也让许多猪逃出农场、到野外生活，这就成了问题。

paras.en: In fact, they’re one of the most damaging invasive species on the continent.
paras.zh: 事实上，它们是这片大陆上破坏性最大的入侵物种之一。

paras.en: Wild pigs cause millions of dollars in crop damage yearly.
paras.zh: 野猪每年给庄稼造成数百万美元的损失。

paras.en: They also harbor dozens of diseases that threaten both humans and farm animals.
paras.zh: 它们还携带几十种疾病，威胁人类和家畜的健康。

paras.en: Forest patches with wild pigs have been found to have considerably reduced plant and animal diversity.
paras.zh: 人们发现，有野猪出没的林地，动植物的多样性明显降低。

paras.en: In addition to either eating other animals or their food supply, wild pigs damage native habitats by rooting up grasses and rubbing on trees.
paras.zh: 野猪不光吃别的动物、抢它们的食物来源，还会拱草、蹭树，破坏本地动植物的栖息地。

paras.en: Their activities may also create opportunities for invasive plants to colonize these areas.
paras.zh: 它们的活动还可能让入侵植物有机会占据这些地方。

paras.en: Wild pigs will eat almost anything containing calories.
paras.zh: 只要含热量的东西，野猪几乎什么都吃。

paras.en: Mice, deer, birds, snakes, and frogs are among their victims.
paras.zh: 老鼠、鹿、鸟、蛇和青蛙都在它们的捕食对象之列。

paras.en: They can also harm other wild species through indirect competition rather than eating them or shrinking their food supply.
paras.zh: 除了吃掉别的野生物种或者让它们的食物来源减少，野猪还能通过间接竞争伤害它们。

paras.en: On one particular United States island, wild pigs themselves became an attractive food source for a species of mainland eagle.
paras.zh: 在美国的某个岛上，野猪本身成了大陆上一种鹰的诱人食物来源。

paras.en: The eagles began breeding on the island and also feeding on a species of native fox.
paras.zh: 这些鹰开始在岛上繁殖，同时也捕食岛上一种本地狐狸。

paras.en: The foxes were almost wiped out completely.
paras.zh: 这些狐狸几乎被彻底消灭了。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What do we learn about early pigs in North America?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于北美早年的猪，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: Why are wild pigs a threat to humans?
paras.zh: 第十七题：野猪为什么对人类是一种威胁？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the passage say about the native foxes on a U.S. island?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于美国某个岛上的本地狐狸，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: A pair of entrepreneurs are planning to build and launch a spacecraft that would carry and roast coffee beans in outer space.
paras.zh: 两位企业家正计划制造并发射一艘航天器，用它把咖啡豆带到外太空烘焙。

paras.en: The craft will use the heat of reentry to roast coffee beans as they float inside it in a pressurized tank.
paras.zh: 咖啡豆漂浮在航天器内的一个加压舱里，航天器利用返回大气层时产生的热量来烘焙它们。

paras.en: The effect would be to roast the beans all over and produce perfect coffee.
paras.zh: 这样咖啡豆的每一面都能烘到，做出完美的咖啡。

paras.en: The businessmen say that on Earth, beans can easily break apart and get burned in the roaster.
paras.zh: 这两位商人说，在地球上，咖啡豆在烘焙机里很容易碎裂、烤焦。

paras.en: But if gravity is removed, the beans float around in a heated oven, receive 360 degrees of evenly distributed heat, and roast to near perfection.
paras.zh: 但如果没有重力，咖啡豆就会在加热的烤箱里四处漂浮，三百六十度均匀受热，烘得近乎完美。

paras.en: The spacecraft will reach a height of around 200 kilometers.
paras.zh: 这艘航天器将飞到大约两百公里的高度。

paras.en: The beans would then be roasted in the heat generated by the craft’s 20-minute reentry into Earth’s atmosphere.
paras.zh: 然后，航天器返回地球大气层要用二十分钟，咖啡豆就靠这期间产生的热量来烘焙。

paras.en: Temperatures in the pressurized tank will be kept to around 200 degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 加压舱里的温度会保持在两百摄氏度左右。

paras.en: Once back on Earth, the planet’s first space-roasted beans would be used to make coffee that would be sold for the first time in Dubai.
paras.zh: 回到地球后，这批全球首次在太空烘焙的咖啡豆将用来做咖啡，首次在迪拜出售。

paras.en: This is where the pair’s company is based.
paras.zh: 两人的公司就设在那里。

paras.en: It is not clear how much they would charge for a cup.
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚一杯会卖多少钱。

paras.en: Surprisingly, the space roaster concept, should it go ahead, will not be the first attempt to take coffee into space.
paras.zh: 出人意料的是，太空烘焙咖啡这个设想如果真的实施，也不会是第一次把咖啡带进太空的尝试。

paras.en: In 2015, two Italian companies collaborated on the construction of a similar type of spacecraft, which was the first coffee machine designed for use in space.
paras.zh: 二〇一五年，两家意大利公司合作制造了一台类似的航天设备，那是第一台专为太空使用设计的咖啡机。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What are a pair of entrepreneurs planning to do?
paras.zh: 第十九题：两位企业家正计划做什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the passage say about coffee beans roasted on earth?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于在地球上烘焙的咖啡豆，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What did the two Italian companies do in 2015?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：两家意大利公司在二〇一五年做了什么？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: In cold and snowy Alaska there’s a village called Takotna.
paras.zh: 在寒冷多雪的阿拉斯加，有一个村子叫塔科特纳。

paras.en: It has a population of a mere forty-nine souls.
paras.zh: 村里的人口只有区区四十九人。

paras.en: Each March this tiny village swells up in numbers because it is located in the middle of a race that takes place every year.
paras.zh: 每年三月，这个小村庄人数大增，因为它就在每年举行的一场比赛的途中。

paras.en: It is a seven-day race called the Iditarod Trail, and participants stop at Takotna for their obligatory 24-hour rest.
paras.zh: 这是一场为期七天的比赛，叫艾迪塔罗德小道赛，参赛者都要在塔科特纳停下来，进行规定的二十四小时休整。

paras.en: Lucky for them, Takotna is famous for its delicious fruit pies.
paras.zh: 他们运气好，塔科特纳的水果派很有名，特别好吃。

paras.en: Weeks before the competitors arrive, the residents of Takotna start preparing for what is without question their biggest event of the year.
paras.zh: 参赛者到达前几个星期，塔科特纳的居民就开始准备这件毫无疑问是一年中最大的事情。

paras.en: The whole village chips in to help, including the kids, who end up developing their baking skills at an early age.
paras.zh: 全村人都来帮忙，连孩子们也不例外，结果他们小小年纪就练出了烘焙的手艺。

paras.en: The exhausted and hungry racers are greeted with delightful pies of all kinds, such as apple, orange, lemon, or banana.
paras.zh: 迎接筋疲力尽、饥肠辘辘的选手的，是各种美味的馅饼，比如苹果派、橙子派、柠檬派和香蕉派。

w.m: adj. 令人愉快的；美妙的

paras.en: They consume the pies as stomach-warming race fuel.
paras.zh: 他们把这些馅饼当作暖胃的比赛“燃料”吃下去。

paras.en: The toughness of the race allows for racers to eat pretty much whatever they want.
paras.zh: 比赛非常艰苦，所以选手们想吃什么基本上都可以吃。

paras.en: The more calories, the better.
paras.zh: 热量越高越好。

paras.en: Takotna has gained a reputation for its dessert-based hospitality since the 1970s.
paras.zh: 从二十世纪七十年代起，塔科特纳就以用甜点款待客人出了名。

paras.en: It started with one person, Jan Newton.
paras.zh: 这一切都是从一个人开始的，她叫简·牛顿。

paras.en: Jan moved from Idaho with her husband in 1972 and opened a restaurant.
paras.zh: 一九七二年，简和丈夫从爱达荷州搬到这里，开了一家餐馆。

paras.en: Her rich and filling fruit pies quickly got the racers’ attention, and the village gained some fame as a result.
paras.zh: 她做的水果派料足又顶饱，很快就引起了选手们的注意，村子也因此有了些名气。

paras.en: Proud residents then started to refer to Jan as Queen of Takotna.
paras.zh: 自豪的居民们后来开始把简称为“塔科特纳女王”。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: Why do a lot of people come to the village of Takotna every March?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：为什么每年三月有很多人来到塔科特纳村？

paras.en: Question 23: What is the village of Takotna famous for?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：塔科特纳村以什么出名？

paras.en: Question 24: Who comes to help with the event of the year?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：谁来为这一年中最大的事情帮忙？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the passage say about Jan Newton?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于简·牛顿，短文说了什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2021年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2021年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一位八十一岁的英国老人想开车去罗马见教皇，却把导航输错，开到了德国北部一个也叫“罗马”的小镇，车还溜坡撞上了写着“罗马”的路牌。第二篇新闻报道讲格拉斯哥承诺成为英国第一个碳中和城市，苏格兰首席部长和苏格兰电力公司总裁都表示支持。第三篇新闻报道讲日本一家IT公司允许员工带猫上班，还奖励收养流浪猫的员工。第一段长对话里，男士来打听向他们借钱的吉米，两人怀疑吉米借钱的理由是编的。第二段长对话里，马克斯向女士介绍网上订购商品送货上门的好处，打消了她的顾虑。第一篇短文讲英国一成儿童有数学焦虑，而且大多数其实成绩不差。第二篇短文讲世界卫生组织把电脑游戏成瘾认定为一种疾病，但也有专家不同意。第三篇短文讲护照封面的颜色和设计：没有官方规定，各国多用深色，内页图案还能防伪。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: An eighty-one-year-old man ended up in Germany by accident after trying to get from Newcastle, Great Britain, to Rome, Italy.
paras.zh: 一位八十一岁的老人想从英国纽卡斯尔前往意大利罗马，结果阴差阳错到了德国。

paras.en: The old age pensioner was on a mission to see the Pope, who is head of the Catholic Church, and decided to make his way there by car.
paras.zh: 这位领养老金的老人一心要去见天主教会的领袖教皇，决定开车去那儿。

paras.en: He was surprised when his GPS system told him he had arrived, although there were no signs of any of the famous buildings or architecture.
paras.zh: 导航系统告诉他已经到了，他很惊讶，因为根本看不到任何一座著名的建筑。

w.m: n. 全球定位系统；导航

paras.en: The man parked but didn’t put on the handbrake of his car properly.
paras.zh: 老人停了车，却没把手刹拉好。

paras.en: His car rolled backwards and, in a striking display of irony, hit a sign saying Rome, the small town in North Germany he had mistakenly plugged into the GPS system.
paras.zh: 他的车往后溜，极具讽刺意味的是，正好撞上了一块写着“罗马”的路牌，罗马是德国北部的一个小镇，正是他错输进导航系统的地方。

w.m: n. 全球定位系统；导航

paras.en: Police said that the car had come to a halt after hitting the sign, but did not appear to be seriously damaged, although an ambulance was called to check on the pensioner.
paras.zh: 警方说，车撞上路牌后停了下来，看上去没有严重损坏，不过还是叫了救护车来查看老人的情况。

paras.en: The man who lives in the UK and is originally Italian might have been confused by the fact that Rome is written Roma in Italian and Rom in German.
paras.zh: 这位老人住在英国，原籍意大利，他可能是被这样一个事实弄糊涂了：罗马在意大利语里写作Roma，在德语里写作Rom。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What did the old age pensioner plan to do?
paras.zh: 第一题：这位领养老金的老人打算做什么？

paras.en: Question two: What finally happened to the old man?
paras.zh: 第二题：这位老人最后怎么样了？

paras.en: News report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Glasgow has pledged to become the first carbon-neutral city in the UK.
paras.zh: 格拉斯哥承诺要成为英国第一个碳中和城市。

paras.en: The City’s Council and Scottish Power have announced a range of strategies in an attempt to reduce carbon emissions ahead of the new national target of 2045.
paras.zh: 格拉斯哥市议会和苏格兰电力公司宣布了一系列措施，力争在新的二〇四五年国家目标之前减少碳排放。

paras.en: First Minister Nicola Sturgeon welcomed the pledge and said, “Today’s announcement between Scottish Power and Glasgow City Council to make Glasgow the UK’s first net-zero city is a very welcome step.
paras.zh: 苏格兰首席部长妮古拉·斯特金对这一承诺表示欢迎，她说：“今天苏格兰电力公司和格拉斯哥市议会宣布，要让格拉斯哥成为英国第一个净零排放城市，这是非常可喜的一步。

paras.en: Reaching our goals will need exactly this kind of partnership approach, with government, business, local authorities and citizens all playing their part.”
paras.zh: 要实现我们的目标，需要的正是这种合作的方式，让政府、企业、地方当局和市民都发挥各自的作用。”

w.m: 发挥作用；尽自己的一份力

paras.en: Speaking ahead of the all-energy conference being held in Glasgow, Scottish Power Chief Executive Keith Anderson said, “We have a large supply of renewable energy on our doorstep and one of the only two low-emission zones in action across the UK.
paras.zh: 在格拉斯哥举行的全能源大会召开前，苏格兰电力公司总裁基思·安德森说：“我们身边就有大量的可再生能源，还有全英国仅有的两个正在运行的低排放区之一。

w.m: 在我们身边；就在家门口

paras.en: Now we need to invest in the technologies and programmes that transform the rest of Glasgow’s economy and make us net zero before anyone else.”
paras.zh: 现在我们需要投资那些能改变格拉斯哥其他经济领域的技术和项目，让我们比谁都先实现净零排放。”

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What do we learn from the news report?
paras.zh: 第三题：从新闻报道中我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 4: What did Scottish Power’s Chief Executive say ahead of the All Energy Conference?
paras.zh: 第四题：在全能源大会召开前，苏格兰电力公司总裁说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A Japanese IT firm has officially introduced an office cat policy to combat the stressful environment of the workplace.
paras.zh: 日本一家IT公司正式推出了“办公室养猫”政策，以缓解职场的紧张氛围。

paras.en: A total of nine furry friends freely wander around in the office and do whatever their little hearts desire.
paras.zh: 一共九只毛茸茸的小伙伴在办公室里自由地走来走去，想干什么就干什么。

paras.en: Hidenobu Fukuda, who heads the firm, introduced the pet policy upon request from one of his employees, allowing staff to bring their own cats to work.
paras.zh: 公司负责人福田英伸应一名员工的请求推出了这项宠物政策，允许员工带自己的猫来上班。

paras.en: Employee Eri Ito is grateful for the animal’s comforting ways.
paras.zh: 员工伊藤绘里很感激这些猫给人的安慰。

paras.en: “Cats are sleeping just beside us.
paras.zh: “猫就睡在我们旁边。

paras.en: It’s healing,” she said.
paras.zh: 能治愈人心。”她说。

w.m: adj. 有治愈作用的；抚慰人心的

paras.en: Not only does Fukuda encourage bringing cats to the job, but he also encourages his employees to rescue cats from overpopulated shelters or streets.
paras.zh: 福田不仅鼓励员工带猫上班，还鼓励他们从收容过多的收容所或街头救助流浪猫。

paras.en: He gives 5,000 yen, about 45 US dollars, a month to those who rescue a cat.
paras.zh: 谁救助一只猫，他每个月就给谁五千日元，大约合四十五美元。

paras.en: While the positives are many, there are still some obstacles.
paras.zh: 好处虽然很多，但还是有一些麻烦。

paras.en: “Sometimes a cat will walk on a phone and cut off the call, or they shut down the computers by walking onto the off switch,” Ito says.
paras.zh: 伊藤说：“有时候猫会踩到电话上，把电话挂断，或者走到关机键上，把电脑关掉。”

paras.en: Still, cats in the workplace have been a tremendous success for the company.
paras.zh: 不过，猫进职场还是给公司带来了巨大的成功。

paras.en: The policy has led to various other companies doing the same.
paras.zh: 这项政策还带动了其他好几家公司也这么做。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn from the news report about the Japanese IT firm?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于这家日本IT公司，我们从新闻报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does Fukuda encourage his employees to do?
paras.zh: 第六题：福田鼓励员工做什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the news report say about the firm’s policy?
paras.zh: 第七题：关于这家公司的政策，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Has Jimmy been coming in lately?
paras.zh: 吉米最近来过吗？

paras.en: No, I haven’t seen him around.
paras.zh: 没有，最近没见他来过。

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么呢？

paras.en: Has he been causing any trouble?
paras.zh: 他惹什么麻烦了吗？

paras.en: Not that I know of, but I need to see him because my friends and I lent him some money last month, and we haven’t heard from him since.
paras.zh: 据我所知没有，不过我得见见他，因为上个月我和几个朋友借给他一些钱，之后就再没有他的消息了。

paras.en: I heard he comes here a lot, so I thought I’d come in and check with you.
paras.zh: 我听说他常来这儿，所以想过来问问你。

paras.en: Well, that’s funny.
paras.zh: 嗯，这就怪了。

paras.en: Some other fellow came in asking for Jimmy just yesterday.
paras.zh: 就在昨天，另外有个人也来找吉米。

paras.en: A real nervous, pushy type of fellow, saying he needed Jimmy for some study project they were working on.
paras.zh: 那人特别紧张，又很强势，说他找吉米是为了他们一起在做的一个学习项目。

w.m: adj. 强势的；咄咄逼人的

paras.en: But I can’t quite remember what it was all about.
paras.zh: 不过我记不太清到底是怎么回事了。

paras.en: Is this a lot of money we’re talking about here?
paras.zh: 我们说的是一大笔钱吗？

paras.en: Nah, just sixty pounds between the three of us, but still, a bit too much to just let go.
paras.zh: 不是，我们三个人加起来才六十英镑，不过就这么算了，还是有点多。

paras.en: He told us he’d got into an accident.
paras.zh: 他跟我们说他出了车祸。

paras.en: Nothing serious, mind you.
paras.zh: 不过倒也不严重。

paras.en: But he damaged someone’s car and wanted to get some money together to make up for the damage he’d caused.
paras.zh: 可他把别人的车撞坏了，想凑点钱来赔损失。

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

paras.en: Isn’t that sort of thing usually covered by insurance?
paras.zh: 这种事通常不是有保险赔吗？

paras.en: And then, if he still wanted to give money as some sort of apology or something, he probably shouldn’t have to go around borrowing it from people.
paras.zh: 再说，就算他还想拿点钱出来道个歉什么的，他大概也不至于到处找人借钱吧。

paras.en: You think Jimmy’s just making it all up?
paras.zh: 你觉得吉米这些全是编的？

paras.en: See, I did think it was a bit weird for him to be asking for money for that sort of thing, and his story was a bit vague to begin with.
paras.zh: 你看，我确实觉得他为这种事借钱有点怪，而且他的说法一开始就有点含糊。

paras.en: But I thought maybe he doesn’t want his parents to know about what happened.
paras.zh: 不过我想，他大概是不想让父母知道出了什么事吧。

paras.en: So he’d rather come to us and keep things quiet.
paras.zh: 所以他宁可来找我们，不把事情声张出去。

w.m: adv. 宁愿（与 would 连用）

paras.en: Anyway, Jimmy’s a good guy, so we didn’t make a fuss about it.
paras.zh: 反正吉米人挺好的，所以我们也就没跟他计较。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the man want to do?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士想做什么？

paras.en: Question 9: What do we learn about the man who came to see the woman yesterday?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于昨天来找女士的那个男人，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question ten: What did Jimmy say happened to him one day?
paras.zh: 第十题：吉米说他有一天出了什么事？

paras.en: Question 11: Why did Jimmy borrow money, according to the man?
paras.zh: 第十一题：据男士说，吉米为什么借钱？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi Max, how are you?
paras.zh: 嗨，马克斯，你好吗？

paras.en: Listen, I wanted to ask you about ordering shopping online.
paras.zh: 跟你说，我想问问你网上订购商品的事。

paras.en: I’ve never done it before, and I know that you’ve been doing it for ages.
paras.zh: 我从来没在网上买过，我知道你已经这样买了很久了。

paras.en: Sure, I love getting my shopping delivered.
paras.zh: 当然，我喜欢让人把东西送上门。

paras.en: It makes life so much simpler.
paras.zh: 这让生活简单多了。

paras.en: No carrying heavy shopping bags in the rain or trying to park the car in those huge supermarket car parks, then not being able to find it again after you come out of the shops.
paras.zh: 不用在雨里提着沉甸甸的购物袋，也不用在超市那些巨大的停车场里找地方停车，从商店出来后还找不到车在哪儿。

paras.en: But there must be some problems.
paras.zh: 不过肯定会有些问题吧。

paras.en: I mean, how do you know that you won’t get bad fruit?
paras.zh: 我是说，你怎么知道送来的水果不是坏的？

paras.en: Or that the eggs won’t be broken?
paras.zh: 或者鸡蛋不会碎？

paras.en: Oh, come on.
paras.zh: 哦，得了吧。

paras.en: The food is exactly the same as the stuff you buy in a conventional shop.
paras.zh: 送来的食品跟你在普通商店里买的完全一样。

paras.en: They aren’t going to deliver you food that is out of date.
paras.zh: 他们不会给你送过期的食品。

paras.en: And if you get a broken egg, well, that could happen in a conventional shop too.
paras.zh: 就算碰上一个碎鸡蛋，嗯，在普通商店里也可能碰上啊。

paras.en: If anything is really wrong, you can just take photographs of the damage and they will give you the money back or replace the item.
paras.zh: 要是真有什么问题，你只要把损坏的地方拍下来，他们就会退钱，或者给你换货。

paras.en: How about delivery fees?
paras.zh: 那送货费呢？

paras.en: Is it not more expensive to get everything delivered?
paras.zh: 什么东西都让人送上门，不是更贵吗？

paras.en: I actually found that it was cheaper for me as I live quite far away from my local supermarket.
paras.zh: 其实我发现这样对我来说更便宜，因为我住得离附近的超市挺远。

paras.en: So with the deliveries, I’m actually saving on petrol.
paras.zh: 所以让人送货，其实还帮我省了油钱。

paras.en: I never thought of that.
paras.zh: 我从来没想到这一点。

paras.en: If you aren’t driving your own car, then you are saving on fuel.
paras.zh: 你要是不用自己开车，就省了油钱。

paras.en: Right, you’ve convinced me.
paras.zh: 好吧，你说服我了。

paras.en: I’m going to go on the computer now and give it a try.
paras.zh: 我现在就上电脑试试。

paras.en: So which supermarket do you think is the best to order from?
paras.zh: 那你觉得在哪家超市订最好？

paras.en: Oh no, that’s definitely up to you.
paras.zh: 哦，不，那肯定得你自己定。

paras.en: Otherwise, we’ll be here all day.
paras.zh: 不然我们一整天都得耗在这儿了。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What did the woman want to ask Max about?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士想问马克斯什么事？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the man think is a problem with shopping in supermarkets?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士认为在超市购物有什么问题？

paras.en: Question 14: What is the woman’s concern about shopping online?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士对网购有什么顾虑？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the man find about shopping online?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士觉得网购怎么样？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: A recent study found that 10% of British children suffer from math anxiety.
paras.zh: 最近一项研究发现，百分之十的英国儿童有数学焦虑。

paras.en: This means they have overwhelming negative emotions towards the subject, ranging from rage to despair.
paras.zh: 也就是说，他们对这门课有着强烈的负面情绪，从愤怒到绝望都有。

w.m: adj. 强烈的；难以抵挡的

paras.en: Other emotions triggered by math include feelings of tension and frustration.
paras.zh: 数学引发的其他情绪还有紧张和挫败感。

paras.en: Physical symptoms include a racing heart or struggling to catch breath.
paras.zh: 身体上的症状有心跳加速或者喘不过气来。

paras.en: The phenomenon of math anxiety is characterised as a general sense of feeling that the subject is hard compared with other subjects, leading to a subsequent lack or loss of confidence.
paras.zh: 数学焦虑这种现象的特点是，总体上觉得这门课比别的课难，接着就会缺乏自信或者丧失信心。

paras.en: The researchers said they investigated individuals’ attitudes towards mathematics because of what could be referred to as a mathematics crisis in the UK.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，他们之所以调查人们对数学的态度，是因为英国出现了可以称为“数学危机”的情况。

paras.en: There is a widespread misunderstanding that only low-performing children suffer from math anxiety.
paras.zh: 人们普遍有一种误解，以为只有成绩差的孩子才会有数学焦虑。

w.m: adj. 成绩差的；表现差的

paras.en: People automatically assume children are anxious about math because they are poor achievers.
paras.zh: 人们会想当然地认为，孩子之所以怕数学，是因为成绩不好。

w.m: adv. 自然而然地；不假思索地

paras.en: In fact, more than three-quarters of children with high levels of math anxiety are normal to high achievers.
paras.zh: 事实上，数学焦虑程度高的孩子里，四分之三以上成绩处于中等到优秀之间。

paras.en: Probably their math anxiety will go unnoticed because their performance is good.
paras.zh: 他们的数学焦虑可能不会被人注意到，因为他们成绩不错。

paras.en: But in the long term, their performance is negatively affected.
paras.zh: 但从长远来看，他们的成绩会受到负面影响。

paras.en: So a real danger here is that children who are completely able to do math at a normal level may keep away from it because they feel anxious.
paras.zh: 所以，这里真正的危险是，完全有能力学好一般水平数学的孩子，可能因为焦虑而躲开数学。

paras.en: Math anxiety can severely disrupt students’ performance in the subject in both primary and secondary school.
paras.zh: 无论在小学还是中学，数学焦虑都会严重影响学生这门课的成绩。

paras.en: But importantly, and surprisingly, this new study suggests that the majority of students experiencing math anxiety have normal to high math ability.
paras.zh: 但重要而且出人意料的是，这项新研究表明，有数学焦虑的学生大多数数学能力处于中等到优秀之间。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What did a recent study find about some British children?
paras.zh: 第十六题：最近一项研究对一些英国儿童有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 17: What is the widespread misunderstanding about math anxiety?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于数学焦虑，人们普遍有什么误解？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the passage say about British students with math anxiety?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于有数学焦虑的英国学生，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: People spend a lot of time using phones and computers.
paras.zh: 人们花很多时间用手机和电脑。

paras.en: Much of that time is devoted to text messages and social media.
paras.zh: 其中很多时间都花在了发短信和社交媒体上。

paras.en: But many people choose to spend their time playing computer games.
paras.zh: 但也有很多人选择花时间玩电脑游戏。

paras.en: For years, parents and teachers have worried that these games might be addictive.
paras.zh: 多年来，家长和老师一直担心这些游戏会让人上瘾。

paras.en: And now, the World Health Organization has recognized addiction to computer games as a disease.
paras.zh: 现在，世界卫生组织已经把电脑游戏成瘾认定为一种疾病。

paras.en: The organization explains that this decision reflects general agreement among experts around the world that some people have a problem with these games.
paras.zh: 该组织解释说，这个决定反映了世界各地专家的普遍共识：有些人玩这些游戏确实成了问题。

paras.en: They show a pattern of behavior characterized by a lack of control.
paras.zh: 这些人表现出一种以失去控制为特征的行为模式。

paras.en: Such people make computer games a priority over their responsibilities.
paras.zh: 这样的人把玩电脑游戏放在自己该负的责任之前。

paras.en: They may play games instead of attending school or work or socializing.
paras.zh: 他们可能会玩游戏而不去上学、上班或者和别人交往。

paras.en: According to the World Health Organization experts, people’s use of computer games is different from their use of the internet, social media, and online shopping.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织的专家认为，人们玩电脑游戏跟使用互联网、社交媒体和网购不一样。

paras.en: These experts claim there is not sufficient data to indicate that people’s reliance on those other activities is an addiction.
paras.zh: 这些专家称，没有足够的数据表明人们对那些活动的依赖是一种成瘾。

paras.en: But they argue that playing computer games to excess is different.
paras.zh: 但他们认为，过度玩电脑游戏就不一样了。

paras.en: This behavior can become a disorder.
paras.zh: 这种行为可能会变成一种疾病。

paras.en: To meet the new definition for addiction, the behavior must damage a person’s relationships or performance at school or work, and this must last for at least a year.
paras.zh: 要符合成瘾的新定义，这种行为必须损害一个人的人际关系或者学业、工作表现，而且要持续至少一年。

paras.en: Still, not all behavior experts agree.
paras.zh: 不过，并不是所有行为学专家都同意。

paras.en: Some argue that there is not enough research on the subject.
paras.zh: 有些人认为，这方面的研究还不够。

paras.en: Thus, they claim it is too early to call computer game addiction a disorder.
paras.zh: 因此，他们说把电脑游戏成瘾称为一种疾病还为时过早。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What conclusion has the World Health Organization come to recently?
paras.zh: 第十九题：世界卫生组织最近得出了什么结论？

paras.en: Question 20: What is said of people with addictive behavior?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于有成瘾行为的人，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What do some behavior experts think of addiction to computer games?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：一些行为学专家对电脑游戏成瘾怎么看？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Maybe you carry the most powerful passport in the world, or perhaps the rarest passport.
paras.zh: 你拿的也许是世界上最有分量的护照，也许是最稀有的护照。

w.m: adj. 强有力的；有分量的

paras.en: Whatever the case, your passport will likely be one of four colors: red, blue, green, or black, although there are slight variations.
paras.zh: 不管哪种情况，你的护照多半是这四种颜色之一：红、蓝、绿或者黑，不过会有细微的差别。

w.m: 无论如何；不管哪种情况

paras.en: Switzerland’s passport is dark red, for example, while most European countries prefer a shade of red that’s almost brown.
paras.zh: 比如，瑞士的护照是深红色的，而大多数欧洲国家更喜欢一种近乎棕色的红。

paras.en: There are no official rules regarding passport colors.
paras.zh: 关于护照颜色，并没有官方规定。

paras.en: But countries follow a certain set of norms when designing them.
paras.zh: 但各国在设计护照时会遵循一套惯例。

paras.en: The International Civil Aviation Organization, which works to define the principles of air travel, suggests that countries use a suitable type, size and style for official documents like passports.
paras.zh: 国际民用航空组织负责制定航空旅行的原则，它建议各国在护照这类正式证件上采用合适的字体、尺寸和样式。

paras.en: There are also a few compulsory aspects of passports: they must be made from a material that bends.
paras.zh: 护照还有几项硬性要求：护照必须用能弯折的材料制作。

w.m: adj. 强制的；必须遵守的

paras.en: They should be able to be read by a machine at temperatures ranging from 10 degrees Celsius to fifty degrees Celsius and conditions where the air can be extremely dry or moist.
paras.zh: 在十摄氏度到五十摄氏度的温度下，以及空气极其干燥或潮湿的条件下，护照都应该能被机器读取。

paras.en: Despite these existing recommendations, there is nothing regarding the cover colour.
paras.zh: 尽管有这些现行的建议，却没有一条是关于封面颜色的。

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么呢？

paras.en: Simply put, countries stick to darker and more conservative colors because they appear more official, and they can also hide dirt and wear.
paras.zh: 简单地说，各国坚持用较深、较保守的颜色，是因为这些颜色看起来更正式，还能遮住污渍和磨损。

paras.en: While there’s little innovation when it comes to passport cover colour, the same cannot be said for the pages.
paras.zh: 护照封面颜色上虽然没什么创新，内页可不是这样。

paras.en: The passports of many countries contain images of their well-known geographical features and wildlife, which also function as security features, as some are only visible under a special light.
paras.zh: 很多国家的护照里印有本国著名的地理风貌和野生动物图案，这些图案还起到防伪作用，因为有些只有在特殊光线下才能看到。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do we learn about most European passports?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于大多数欧洲护照，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the passage say about the design of passports?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于护照的设计，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: Why are dark colors chosen for passport covers?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：护照封面为什么选用深色？

paras.en: Question 25: What is one special function of the images inside many passports?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：很多护照内页的图案有什么特殊作用？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
