passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲美国联合航空公司弄错航线，把一只宠物狗错送到了日本，事后道歉并把狗送回美国。第二篇新闻报道讲亚利桑那州一家动物园迎来一头小象，母子平安，象群扩大到六头。第三篇新闻报道讲一家海滩餐厅更换木平台时找到一枚三年前掉落的结婚戒指，通过脸书找到了失主，还发现了一枚珍贵的金币。第一段长对话里，两人谈到野鸭数量减少的原因、猎鸭的历史，以及农民过去对野鸭的态度。第二段长对话里，油漆工给布赖特女士报价刷房子，她发现刷漆期间得搬出去住，比想象的麻烦得多。第一篇短文讲不同年龄段家庭作业的目的，以及家长怎样帮孩子写好作业。第二篇短文讲墨西哥一家石油公司按体重给员工发健康奖金引起的争议，专家建议改为提倡健康行为。第三篇短文讲英国活动人士批评政府没有帮助左撇子学生，要求教育部记录他们的情况。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: United Airlines has apologized for mistakenly shipping an American family’s pet dog thousands of miles in the wrong direction to Japan.
paras.zh: 美国联合航空公司因为弄错了航线，把一个美国家庭的宠物狗朝相反方向运到了几千英里外的日本，已经为此道歉。

paras.en: The dog owner’s beloved ten-year-old dog named Buddy took an unexpected sixteen-hour flight to Tokyo following a mix-up by the airline.
paras.zh: 由于航空公司的一次失误，主人心爱的十岁狗狗巴迪意外地坐了十六个小时的飞机，飞到了东京。

w.m: adj. 心爱的；深受喜爱的
adj. 意想不到的；出乎意料的

paras.en: The dog owner’s family are currently in the process of moving.
paras.zh: 狗主人一家目前正在搬家。

paras.en: They were meant to be reunited with the pet in their new home city in Texas.
paras.zh: 他们本来要在得克萨斯州的新家所在的城市和宠物团聚。

paras.en: But when they arrived at the United Airlines cargo facility in the southern US state, they found a stranger’s dog waiting in Buddy’s place.
paras.zh: 可是，当他们到了这个南部州的联合航空货运站时，却发现等在那里的不是巴迪，而是一只陌生人的狗。

paras.en: Both of the dogs had been sent to the wrong destinations on connecting flights from Denver, with Buddy mistakenly being sent to Japan instead.
paras.zh: 两只狗都在从丹佛出发的转机航班上被送错了地方，巴迪被错送到了日本。

paras.en: Buddy was given a physical checkup when he arrived at Tokyo’s International Airport.
paras.zh: 巴迪抵达东京国际机场后，接受了一次身体检查。

paras.en: The dog was then sent back to the US on a private charter jet.
paras.zh: 随后，这只狗搭乘一架私人包机被送回了美国。

paras.en: I’m so glad he’s alive and coming home soon, said the relieved dog owner.
paras.zh: “看到它还活着、很快就能回家，我太高兴了。”松了一口气的狗主人说。

w.m: adj. 松了一口气的；宽慰的

paras.en: An error occurred during the connections in Denver.
paras.zh: “在丹佛转机的时候出了差错。

paras.en: We have notified our customers that their pets arrived safely.
paras.zh: 我们已经通知顾客，他们的宠物都平安到达了。

paras.en: We will arrange to return the pets to them as soon as possible, a spokesperson of United Airlines said.
paras.zh: 我们会安排尽快把宠物送还给他们。”美国联合航空公司的一位发言人说。

paras.en: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What does the news report say about United Airlines?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于美国联合航空公司，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What did the spokesperson for a United Airlines say they would do after the incident?
paras.zh: 第二题：美国联合航空公司的发言人说，事件发生后他们会做什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Officials at Reid Park Zoo in Tucson, Arizona, are celebrating the birth of a baby elephant.
paras.zh: 亚利桑那州图森市里德公园动物园的工作人员，正在庆祝一头小象的出生。

paras.en: Zoo officials say the baby was born on Monday.
paras.zh: 动物园工作人员说，小象是星期一出生的。

paras.en: It is a female and she weighs nearly 130 kilograms.
paras.zh: 这是一头母象，体重将近一百三十公斤。

paras.en: Semba, her mother, is a thirty-year-old African elephant.
paras.zh: 它的妈妈森巴是一头三十岁的非洲象。

paras.en: The pregnancy lasted twenty two months.
paras.zh: 森巴怀孕了二十二个月。

paras.en: Officials describe the baby elephant as healthy, standing, and nursing.
paras.zh: 工作人员说，小象很健康，能站立，也能吃奶了。

paras.en: The baby hasn’t been given a name yet.
paras.zh: 小象还没有起名字。

paras.en: Semba has given birth before.
paras.zh: 森巴以前生过小象。

paras.en: Zoo officials said during this pregnancy she was closely monitored through physical exams and blood tests.
paras.zh: 动物园工作人员说，这次怀孕期间，通过身体检查和验血对它进行了密切监测。

paras.en: Dr Sue Tagelski is the Zoo’s Director of Zoological Operations.
paras.zh: 休·塔格尔斯基博士是这家动物园的动物运营主管。

paras.en: She said the elephant’s birth went smoothly, and that there were no complications.
paras.zh: 她说，小象的出生很顺利，没有出现任何并发症。

paras.en: The new baby expands the zoo’s elephant herd to six.
paras.zh: 这头小象出生后，动物园的象群扩大到了六头。

paras.en: That includes the baby’s parents, a sister, a brother, and an adult female.
paras.zh: 其中包括小象的父母、一个姐姐、一个哥哥和一头成年母象。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What do we learn about the mother elephant Semba?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于象妈妈森巴，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question four: What does the report say about the birth of the new baby elephant?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于这头小象的出生，报道说了什么？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Three years ago, a couple was enjoying a meal at a beach restaurant.
paras.zh: 三年前，一对夫妇在一家海滩餐厅吃饭。

paras.en: The restaurant was built on a wooden structure above the sea water.
paras.zh: 这家餐厅建在海水上方的木结构上。

paras.en: During the meal, the man’s wedding ring slipped off his finger.
paras.zh: 吃饭的时候，男士的结婚戒指从手指上滑落了。

paras.en: It fell through the wooden floorboards, apparently lost forever.
paras.zh: 它从木地板的缝里掉了下去，看来是永远找不回来了。

paras.en: Recently, the restaurant manager Ryan Cravoy decided to replace the wooden deck, and he found an old gold coin, some $100 bills, and a silver wedding ring while replacing the deck.
paras.zh: 最近，餐厅经理瑞安·克拉沃伊决定更换木平台，在更换的时候，他找到了一枚古老的金币、几张一百美元的钞票和一枚银质结婚戒指。

paras.en: The restaurant’s waitress Sasha Formica posted a picture of the ring on Facebook.
paras.zh: 餐厅的女服务员萨莎·福米卡把戒指的照片发到了脸书上。

paras.en: The post was shared about 5,000 times.
paras.zh: 这条帖子被转发了大约五千次。

paras.en: Three days later, the happy wife called to claim the ring.
paras.zh: 三天后，那位高兴的妻子打来电话认领戒指。

paras.en: She even texted pictures of her and her husband eating there in 2017 as proof.
paras.zh: 她甚至发来了二〇一七年她和丈夫在那里吃饭的照片作为证据。

paras.en: The restaurant mailed the ring back to the happy couple.
paras.zh: 餐厅把戒指寄回给了这对高兴的夫妇。

paras.en: Meanwhile Truvois discovered that the gold coin was very rare.
paras.zh: 与此同时，克拉沃伊发现那枚金币非常稀有。

paras.en: It was from eighteen fifty five and worth as much as two thousand dollars.
paras.zh: 它是一八五五年的，价值高达两千美元。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What do we learn about the restaurant?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于这家餐厅，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question six: What did the restaurant manager decide to do recently?
paras.zh: 第六题：餐厅经理最近决定做什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What did the waitress do about the recovered ring?
paras.zh: 第七题：对找回的戒指，女服务员做了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter, on answer sheet one, with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I can’t believe that duck hunting is still legal in so many parts of the world.
paras.zh: 真不敢相信，世界上还有这么多地方允许猎野鸭。

paras.en: The scientific evidence from countries like Australia, Canada and the USA clearly indicates a decline in the bird’s numbers.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚、加拿大、美国等国的科学证据都清楚地表明，这种鸟的数量在减少。

paras.en: But can anyone be sure if the decline is really caused by the hunting or by climate change?
paras.zh: 可是，谁能确定数量减少真的是打猎造成的，还是气候变化造成的呢？

paras.en: It’s caused by both, in fact.
paras.zh: 其实两方面的原因都有。

paras.en: We see more droughts in countries like Australia.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚这些国家的干旱越来越多了。

paras.en: Ducks are birds that feed and breed in areas where there is a lot of water, but their habitats have been shrinking in recent decades because of the droughts.
paras.zh: 鸭子这种鸟在水多的地方觅食、繁殖，可是近几十年来，因为干旱，它们的栖息地一直在缩小。

paras.en: And I guess, with fewer places to inhabit, they concentrate in greater numbers in fewer areas, which surely makes them easier targets for the hunters.
paras.zh: 我想，能栖身的地方少了，它们就更多地聚集在更少的几个地方，这肯定让它们更容易成为猎人的目标。

paras.en: It does.
paras.zh: 确实是这样。

w.m: v. （用于代替前面的动词）确实

paras.en: My grandfather was a duck hunter.
paras.zh: 我爷爷以前是猎鸭子的。

paras.en: He told me hunting ducks and geese began in the 19th century.
paras.zh: 他跟我说，猎野鸭和大雁是从十九世纪开始的。

paras.en: They were an easily found and plentifully available food source in farming areas, especially for poor immigrants.
paras.zh: 在农业地区，它们是一种容易找到、数量又多的食物来源，对穷苦的移民来说尤其如此。

paras.en: What did they use for hunting during that period?
paras.zh: 那个时候他们用什么打猎？

paras.en: They used new types of guns, and birds could easily be shot down in flight, and in such great numbers that commercial hunting of ducks and geese became an industry, yet there’s no commercial farming of these birds nowadays.
paras.zh: 他们用新式的枪，鸟在飞的时候很容易就被打下来，而且打下来的数量特别多，于是商业化捕猎野鸭和大雁成了一个行业，可是如今却没有人商业化养殖这些鸟了。

paras.en: Their meat is hardly eaten in Western countries.
paras.zh: 西方国家几乎没人吃它们的肉。

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 是啊，没人吃。

paras.en: Duck hunting seemingly exists as the continuation of a tradition.
paras.zh: 猎野鸭似乎只是作为一种传统延续了下来。

paras.en: Wild ducks have never been popular with farmers like my grandfather anyway, because they sometimes destroy crops.
paras.zh: 反正像我爷爷这样的农民从来都不喜欢野鸭，因为它们有时候会糟蹋庄稼。

paras.en: In fact, farmers used to poison them in large numbers.
paras.zh: 事实上，农民们过去常常大量毒杀它们。

paras.en: That somehow doesn’t surprise me.
paras.zh: 不知怎么的，我一点也不意外。

paras.en: Nobody places much value on the lives of these poor birds or on their meat.
paras.zh: 没有人在乎这些可怜的鸟的性命，也没人看重它们的肉。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What does the woman find unbelievable?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士觉得什么事难以置信？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman say has caused the shrinking of ducks’ habitats in Australia?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士说是什么导致了澳大利亚鸭子栖息地的缩小？

paras.en: Question 10: Why is there no commercial farming of ducks and geese in Western countries?
paras.zh: 第十题：西方国家为什么没有商业化养殖野鸭和大雁？

paras.en: Question eleven: What does a woman say about farmers in her grandfather’s time?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于她爷爷那个年代的农民，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Okay, Miss Bright.
paras.zh: 好了，布赖特女士。

paras.en: I finished calculating.
paras.zh: 我算完了。

paras.en: I estimate you have between 210 and 240 square meters of walls and ceiling.
paras.zh: 我估计，墙面和天花板一共有二百一十到二百四十平方米。

paras.en: So how much would the paint job cost?
paras.zh: 那刷漆要花多少钱？

paras.en: That would depend on the quality of paint you choose.
paras.zh: 那要看你选什么档次的漆。

paras.en: We carry two brands.
paras.zh: 我们有两个牌子的漆。

paras.en: One costs sixty cents every square meter and the other ninety cents.
paras.zh: 一种每平方米六十美分，另一种九十美分。

paras.en: The second is guaranteed to look great for about ten years, whereas the cheaper one will start to dull after around six or seven years.
paras.zh: 第二种保证大约十年都很好看，而便宜的那种六七年后就开始暗淡了。

paras.en: In that case we would prefer the more expensive option.
paras.zh: 那样的话，我们还是选贵一点的吧。

paras.en: All right then.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: So including labor costs, taxes and everything, this job would come to three thousand dollars.
paras.zh: 那么，算上人工费、税费等等所有费用，这活儿一共是三千美元。

paras.en: To be perfectly honest, that’s more than I expected.
paras.zh: 说实话，这比我预想的要贵。

paras.en: Please bear in mind that the price includes moving all the furniture, and the whole task would take two days.
paras.zh: 请注意，这个价钱里包括搬动所有家具，而且整个活儿要干两天。

paras.en: Really?
paras.zh: 真的吗？

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么呢？

paras.en: Well, we can’t paint the walls without clearing all the furniture first, so every time we paint a room we first have to move the furniture to another room.
paras.zh: 嗯，不先把家具全部挪开，我们就没法刷墙，所以每刷一个房间，都得先把家具搬到另一个房间去。

paras.en: So that takes more time.
paras.zh: 所以就更费时间。

paras.en: Plus it requires two people, which works out more expensive.
paras.zh: 再说，这得两个人干，算下来就更贵了。

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: But does that mean I could not live here in my own house during those two days?
paras.zh: 可是，这是不是说，这两天我不能住在自己家里了？

paras.en: That is correct.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: Oh, well, that changes everything, I’m afraid.
paras.zh: 哦，这样的话，恐怕情况就全变了。

paras.en: I would have to stay with a friend, or check into a hotel.
paras.zh: 我得去朋友家住，或者住酒店。

paras.en: I hadn’t considered any of that.
paras.zh: 这些我完全没考虑过。

paras.en: I’m starting to realize that painting my house is far more troublesome than I had anticipated.
paras.zh: 我开始意识到，给房子刷漆比我预想的麻烦多了。

paras.en: This is usually the case.
paras.zh: 一般都是这样。

paras.en: Most of our clients go through the same realization, I see.
paras.zh: 我发现，我们大多数客户都会有同样的体会。

paras.en: You have my number.
paras.zh: 你有我的电话号码。

paras.en: Please feel free to call me for any further questions.
paras.zh: 还有什么问题，随时给我打电话。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What is the woman planning to do?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士打算做什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What is the woman’s chief concern?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士最关心的是什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the woman have to do while the paint job is being done?
paras.zh: 第十四题：刷漆期间，女士得做什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What has the woman come to realize at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：对话结束时，女士意识到了什么？

paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Homework is an important part of schooling, but the purposes of giving children homework will change as they grow older.
paras.zh: 家庭作业是学校教育的重要一环，不过，给孩子布置作业的目的会随着他们长大而变化。

paras.en: At the primary level, the main aim is to cultivate good habits, like learning to plan and exercising self-discipline.
paras.zh: 小学阶段，主要目的是培养好习惯，比如学会做计划、学会自律。

paras.en: During the secondary school years, extending what is learnt at school is positively related to academic achievement, so the content of homework becomes more important.
paras.zh: 中学阶段，拓展课堂上学到的东西和学业成绩正相关，所以作业的内容就变得更重要了。

paras.en: So how can you help your child do their best?
paras.zh: 那么，怎样才能帮孩子发挥出最好的水平呢？

paras.en: Creating an ideal working environment will make it easier for them to get down to their assignments quickly.
paras.zh: 营造一个理想的学习环境，能让他们更容易很快投入到作业中去。

paras.en: Make sure it’s free of distractions and for primary school children at least, somewhere near you so you can answer questions and offer encouragement.
paras.zh: 一定要保证那里没有让人分心的东西，至少对小学生来说，地方要离你近一些，这样你就能回答他们的问题、给他们鼓励。

paras.en: You’ll probably have to help younger children plan their session, but it’s important that by the end of primary school it’s second nature.
paras.zh: 你可能得帮年龄小一点的孩子安排写作业的时间，但重要的是，到小学毕业的时候，这应该成为他们的习惯。

paras.en: Get them to tell you everything they have to do, then encourage them to establish an order in which they do work.
paras.zh: 让他们把要做的事全都告诉你，然后鼓励他们定好做作业的顺序。

paras.en: When there’s several different assignments, make sure they begin with one they enjoy so it seems easy to get started.
paras.zh: 有好几项不同的作业时，一定要让他们从自己喜欢的那项开始，这样开头就显得容易。

paras.en: It’s best to take on the most difficult task second, once they’re settled, but before they get tired.
paras.zh: 最难的那项最好第二个做，也就是在他们安下心来之后、还没累的时候。

paras.en: If older children have more than an hour of homework, encourage them to schedule a short break to stretch.
paras.zh: 如果大一点的孩子作业超过一个小时，就鼓励他们安排一次短暂的休息，伸展一下身体。

paras.en: If you encourage them to tell you what they’ve learned, they’ll absorb the information more deeply and remember it more readily.
paras.zh: 如果你鼓励他们把学到的东西讲给你听，他们就会吸收得更深，也记得更牢。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What is the main aim of homework for primary school kids?
paras.zh: 第十六题：对小学生来说，家庭作业的主要目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the passage suggest parents do to help their children?
paras.zh: 第十七题：短文建议家长怎样帮助孩子？

paras.en: Question 18: What should children do to deal with multiple assignments?
paras.zh: 第十八题：孩子应该怎样应对多项作业？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Workers at Mexican Oil Company will receive a health incentive of almost $300 a year if they meet certain body weight standards.
paras.zh: 墨西哥石油公司的员工如果体重达到一定的标准，每年就能领到将近三百美元的健康奖励。

paras.en: To qualify for the bonus, they must maintain a healthy weight.
paras.zh: 要拿到这笔奖金，他们必须保持健康的体重。

paras.en: For those who are overweight or obese, they can receive the bonus if they reduce their weight by ten per cent during the year.
paras.zh: 超重或肥胖的人，如果一年内体重减了百分之十，也能拿到奖金。

paras.en: Some applaud the policy as fair, because it rewards both individuals who maintain a healthy weight, and those who are working towards achieving it.
paras.zh: 有人称赞这项政策很公平，因为保持健康体重的人和正在努力达到健康体重的人，它都会奖励。

paras.en: But critics say the policy contradicts recommendations by many health experts, who warn that a person’s weight is influenced by genetic and environmental factors.
paras.zh: 但批评的人说，这项政策和许多健康专家的建议是相矛盾的，这些专家提醒说，一个人的体重受基因和环境因素的影响。

paras.en: That means weight can be hard for individuals to control, which makes the bonus unfair.
paras.zh: 也就是说，体重可能是个人很难控制的，所以这项奖金是不公平的。

paras.en: Some experts say the policy is inconsistent with the science of what we know about body weight regulation.
paras.zh: 有的专家说，这项政策和我们对体重调节的科学认识不相符。

w.m: adj. 不一致的；不相符的

paras.en: These experts argue that focusing on weight is the wrong approach.
paras.zh: 这些专家认为，把注意力放在体重上是错误的做法。

paras.en: A more productive method of encouraging health among employees is to promote healthy behaviors.
paras.zh: 要促进员工的健康，更有成效的办法是提倡健康的行为。

paras.en: For example, companies can give workers gym memberships, or encourage participation in lectures on healthy eating and living.
paras.zh: 比如，公司可以给员工办健身卡，或者鼓励他们参加健康饮食、健康生活方面的讲座。

paras.en: They can also reduce sweets and provide healthier snacks in the office and healthier meals at the company canteen, or they can give employees more time during their lunch break to exercise.
paras.zh: 公司还可以在办公室少放甜食、多提供健康零食，在公司食堂提供更健康的饭菜，或者在午休时多给员工一些时间去锻炼。

paras.en: These are much better and much more productive ways for companies to move forward on their employees’ well-being.
paras.zh: 要让员工过得更健康，公司用这些办法要好得多，也有成效得多。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: Who will qualify for the bonus in Mexican oil company?
paras.zh: 第十九题：在墨西哥石油公司，什么人能拿到奖金？

paras.en: Question 20: What do critics think of Mexican oil companies’ bonus policy?
paras.zh: 第二十题：批评的人怎么看墨西哥石油公司的奖金政策？

paras.en: Question 21: What do experts propose companies do about workers’ well-being?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于员工的健康，专家建议公司怎么做？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Campaigners have warned that the British government is not doing enough to prevent left-handed pupils from falling behind their peers.
paras.zh: 一些活动人士提醒说，英国政府在防止左撇子学生落后于同龄人方面做得不够。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: They claim that thousands of children are still being penalised for being left-handed.
paras.zh: 他们说，现在仍有成千上万的孩子因为是左撇子而吃亏。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: This is due to a lack of action from ministers who have failed to take any meaningful action for years.
paras.zh: 这是因为大臣们没有作为，多年来一直没有采取任何有意义的行动。

paras.en: It is feared that a failure to address early year challenges such as poor handwriting leads to much more serious problems down the line with these pupils facing reduced career prospects.
paras.zh: 人们担心，如果不解决他们低年级时遇到的难题，比如字写得不好，以后就会导致严重得多的问题，这些学生将来的职业前景会变差。

paras.en: Studies in recent years show that left-handed children are more likely to suffer with learning difficulties and their scores are lower on IQ tests.
paras.zh: 近几年的研究表明，左撇子孩子更容易有学习困难，智商测试的分数也更低。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: Campaigners feel it’s strange that children in British schools are penalised because they happen to be left-handed.
paras.zh: 活动人士觉得很奇怪：英国学校的孩子只因为碰巧是左撇子，就要吃亏。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: They don’t understand why successive governments have failed to act on this.
paras.zh: 他们不明白，为什么历届政府在这件事上都没有作为。

paras.en: They want the Department of Education to record which children are left-handed and what their educational attainments are, since they make up some ten per cent of the population.
paras.zh: 他们希望教育部记录哪些孩子是左撇子，以及这些孩子的学业成绩怎么样，因为左撇子大约占人口的百分之十。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: In early year education, left-handed children are struggling and making a mess of their handwriting.
paras.zh: 在低年级教育中，左撇子孩子学得很吃力，字也写得一团糟。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: Educators don’t know how to deal with this.
paras.zh: 教育工作者不知道该怎么应对。

paras.en: In many cases, there’s no active help and a lack of teacher training.
paras.zh: 很多时候，既没有积极的帮助，教师培训也跟不上。

paras.en: Campaigners point out that a high percentage of the prison population is left-handed.
paras.zh: 活动人士指出，监狱服刑人员中，左撇子的比例很高。

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: They say that these prison numbers are unusually high and ask why it is the case.
paras.zh: 他们说，监狱里左撇子的数量高得反常，想知道这是为什么。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: Why are some people criticizing the British government?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：为什么有人批评英国政府？

paras.en: Question 23: What do studies in recent years show about left-handed children?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于左撇子孩子，近几年的研究表明了什么？

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: Question 24: What do the campaigners demand the Department of Education do?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：活动人士要求教育部做什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What do the campaigners want to know about left-handed prisoners?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于左撇子囚犯，活动人士想知道什么？

w.m: adj. 惯用左手的；左撇子的

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2021年12月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2021年12月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲山东一名女子咳嗽了十四年，最后在青岛做全身扫描，发现肺里卡着一块鸡骨头，手术取出后完全康复。第二篇新闻报道讲澳大利亚一只白羊在二零一三年的丛林大火中跑丢，被新修的围栏挡在外面，七年后自己回了家。第三篇新闻报道讲俄罗斯一架货机舱门在半空中打开，几吨黄金掉落，飞机紧急降落，警方正在调查。第一段长对话里，女士打电话给客服，问退货的钱为什么还没退回，原来是她换了新银行卡。第二段长对话里，两人商量叫什么外卖，挑来挑去，最后定了越南菜。第一篇短文讲一项研究：猫主人的性格会影响猫的行为和健康。第二篇短文讲跑步不仅能延长寿命，还能增强学习能力、帮人调节情绪。第三篇短文是导游介绍希尔别墅的设计和保存情况。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A twenty-two-year-old Chinese woman who suffered from a persistent cough was shocked to learn that she had a piece of chicken bone lodged in her lung.
paras.zh: 中国一名二十二岁的女子长期咳嗽，后来得知自己肺里卡着一块鸡骨头，大吃一惊。

paras.en: The unnamed woman from the province of Shandong started to have coughing problems when she was seven or eight years old.
paras.zh: 这名来自山东省、没有公开姓名的女子，从七八岁起就开始咳嗽。

paras.en: For fourteen years she made numerous hospital visits.
paras.zh: 十四年来，她去了很多次医院。

paras.en: However, no doctor could identify any problem.
paras.zh: 可是，没有一个医生能查出问题在哪儿。

paras.en: Her uncontrollable coughing was a mystery.
paras.zh: 她咳嗽止不住，谁也说不清是怎么回事。

paras.en: Finally the woman got a full body scan at a hospital in the city of Qingdao.
paras.zh: 最后，这名女子在青岛市的一家医院做了全身扫描。

paras.en: This special medical procedure revealed she had a chicken bone stuck in her lung.
paras.zh: 这项特殊的医学检查显示，她肺里卡着一块鸡骨头。

paras.en: Doctors performed surgery and removed the bone.
paras.zh: 医生给她做了手术，把骨头取了出来。

paras.en: The simple procedure went smoothly, and the woman has recovered fully.
paras.zh: 这个简单的手术做得很顺利，这名女子已经完全康复了。

paras.en: With the bone finally removed from her lung, the woman is very happy that she no longer suffers from that annoying cough.
paras.zh: 骨头终于从肺里取出来了，这名女子非常高兴，再也不用受那种恼人的咳嗽折磨了。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What was the woman’s problem?
paras.zh: 第一题：这名女子有什么问题？

paras.en: Question two: How was the woman’s problem eventually solved?
paras.zh: 第二题：这名女子的问题最后是怎么解决的？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A white sheep named Prickles, that ran away from an Australian farm during the twenty thirteen bush fires, recently returned home.
paras.zh: 一只名叫普里克尔斯的白羊，在二零一三年的丛林大火中从澳大利亚的一个农场跑丢了，最近回到了家。

paras.en: According to farmer Alice Gray, Prickles was only a lamb when she ran away.
paras.zh: 据农场主艾丽斯·格雷说，普里克尔斯跑丢的时候还只是一只小羊羔。

paras.en: The bush fires that hit the area back then destroyed a large part of her family’s massive property.
paras.zh: 当年袭击那一带的丛林大火，烧毁了她家大片的土地。

paras.en: They thought Prickles had died in the fire, but instead the young sheep escaped into a two hundred acre forest near the farm.
paras.zh: 他们以为普里克尔斯已经死在大火里了，可是，这只小羊并没有死，而是逃进了农场附近一片两百英亩的森林。

paras.en: Once the fires were over, the family had to fix the damage done to the farm.
paras.zh: 大火过后，这家人得修复农场受到的损毁。

paras.en: As it was such a large property, this included rebuilding about 50 kilometers of fencing.
paras.zh: 由于农场很大，这其中就包括重建大约五十公里的围栏。

paras.en: It was this huge fencing that prevented Prickles from finding her way back.
paras.zh: 正是这道长长的围栏挡住了普里克尔斯回家的路。

paras.en: Over the years the family spotted her a few times.
paras.zh: 这些年里，这家人看到过它几次。

paras.en: They even recorded her with cameras installed to monitor deer activity.
paras.zh: 他们为了监测鹿的活动装了摄像头，甚至还拍到过它。

paras.en: But while they knew Prickles was alive, they couldn’t find her, and never expected her to return by herself.
paras.zh: 可是，他们虽然知道普里克尔斯还活着，却找不到它，也从没指望它能自己回来。

paras.en: Seven years later they were proven wrong.
paras.zh: 七年后，事实证明他们想错了。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What does the news report say about the white sheep Prickles?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于白羊普里克尔斯，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

w.m: n. 普里克尔斯（羊的名字）

paras.en: Question four: What did the family do after the bushfires?
paras.zh: 第四题：丛林大火过后，这家人做了什么？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Tons of gold have fallen out of the sky in Russia, after a cargo plane malfunctioned in mid-air this morning.
paras.zh: 在俄罗斯，好几吨黄金从天上掉了下来，原因是今天上午一架货机在半空中出了故障。

paras.en: The aircraft was carrying two hundred and sixty-five million pounds’ worth of gold and diamonds when the door flew open, sending the precious metal back to earth.
paras.zh: 这架飞机载着价值两亿六千五百万英镑的黄金和钻石，舱门突然打开，这些贵金属就掉回了地面。

paras.en: According to the official news agency, Russian authorities have recovered more than one hundred and seventy gold bars weighing twenty kilograms each.
paras.zh: 据官方通讯社报道，俄罗斯当局已经找回了一百七十多根金条，每根重二十公斤。

paras.en: The plane was travelling from Yakutsk airport in a major diamond-producing region to the city Krasnoyarsk in Siberia.
paras.zh: 这架飞机是从钻石主要产区的雅库茨克机场起飞，飞往西伯利亚的克拉斯诺亚尔斯克市的。

paras.en: However, the aircraft made an emergency landing in Magan, after it began losing some of its valuable cargo.
paras.zh: 可是，飞机开始掉落一些贵重的货物后，在马甘紧急降落了。

paras.en: Reports suggest some bars of gold were scattered up to fifteen miles away from the airport.
paras.zh: 有报道说，有些金条散落在离机场远达十五英里的地方。

paras.en: Nine tons of gold on plane AN-12 belonged to a gold mine company.
paras.zh: 安-12飞机上的九吨黄金属于一家金矿公司。

paras.en: Police have sealed off the runway and say it is unclear if it was an accident or an attempted robbery.
paras.zh: 警方已经封锁了跑道，说还不清楚这是一场事故，还是有人企图抢劫。

paras.en: Technical engineers who worked on the plane prior to take-off are reportedly going to be questioned by the police.
paras.zh: 据报道，起飞前检修过这架飞机的技术工程师将接受警方问询。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is the news report mainly about?
paras.zh: 第五题：这篇新闻报道主要讲了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What did the aircraft do when the incident happened?
paras.zh: 第六题：事故发生时，这架飞机做了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the news report say about the technical engineers who worked on the plane before take-off?
paras.zh: 第七题：对于起飞前检修过这架飞机的技术工程师，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hello, you’re through to customer service.
paras.zh: 您好，这里是客服中心。

paras.en: This is Michael speaking.
paras.zh: 我是迈克尔。

paras.en: Before we continue, I just want to make you aware that this call is being recorded and may be used in the future for training purposes.
paras.zh: 在继续之前，我想先告诉您，这通电话正在录音，以后可能会用于员工培训。

paras.en: What can I help you with today?
paras.zh: 今天有什么可以帮您？

paras.en: Hi.
paras.zh: 你好。

paras.en: My name is Jean Seaman.
paras.zh: 我叫琼·西曼。

paras.en: I recently bought an office chair from your company, but I returned it about a week ago.
paras.zh: 我最近在你们公司买了一把办公椅，可是大概一周前我把它退了。

paras.en: I’m just calling to inquire when I will be able to get my money back.
paras.zh: 我打电话就是想问问，什么时候能把钱退给我。

paras.en: It says on your website that your company will pay back the money within three working days of you receiving the returned item.
paras.zh: 你们网站上说，公司收到退货后三个工作日内会把钱退回。

paras.en: But it’s been five working days and I haven’t received anything.
paras.zh: 可是已经过了五个工作日了，我什么也没收到。

paras.en: I’m sorry to hear that, Mrs Seaman.
paras.zh: 听到这个情况我很抱歉，西曼太太。

paras.en: What’s your customer reference number, please?
paras.zh: 请问您的客户参考号是多少？

paras.en: It’s three eight nine four six o.
paras.zh: 是三八九四六零。

paras.en: Okay.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: Three eight nine four six zero.
paras.zh: 三八九四六零。

paras.en: I’m just looking on the system here, and, according to our records, the chair you returned was received by our warehouse on Friday morning.
paras.zh: 我在系统里查一下。根据我们的记录，您退的椅子我们仓库周五上午已经收到了。

paras.en: The payment was made on Wednesday, but there seems to be a problem with your card number.
paras.zh: 退款周三就付了，可是您的卡号好像有点问题。

paras.en: My card number?
paras.zh: 我的卡号？

paras.en: Oh, maybe it has something to do with my new card.
paras.zh: 哦，可能跟我的新卡有关。

paras.en: It was sent to me on Tuesday.
paras.zh: 新卡是星期二寄给我的。

paras.en: Maybe the bank cancelled my old one before you made the payment.
paras.zh: 也许你们付款之前，银行就把我的旧卡注销了。

paras.en: Well, you’ll need to update your card details directly on our website.
paras.zh: 嗯，您得直接在我们网站上更新银行卡信息。

paras.en: Just make sure you’re logged in and then under the description of your personal information you should see an option for updating payment methods.
paras.zh: 您只要确认已经登录，然后在个人信息说明那一栏下面，就能看到更新付款方式的选项。

paras.en: I am logged in, and I’ll give that a go.
paras.zh: 我已经登录了，我试一试。

paras.en: I’ll make a note here on the system for you so that the payment will be made tomorrow morning.
paras.zh: 我在系统里给您备注一下，这样明天上午就能把钱付给您。

paras.en: Thank you very much.
paras.zh: 非常感谢。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: Why does the man have his conversation with the woman recorded?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士为什么要给他和女士的通话录音？

paras.en: Question nine: What is the woman’s purpose of calling the Furniture Company?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士给这家家具公司打电话是为了什么？

paras.en: Question ten: What does the woman say about her bank card?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于自己的银行卡，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question eleven: What does the man advise the woman to do?
paras.zh: 第十一题：男士建议女士做什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: I’m getting a bit hungry.
paras.zh: 我有点饿了。

paras.en: Yes, me too.
paras.zh: 是啊，我也是。

paras.en: I’m starving.
paras.zh: 我饿坏了。

paras.en: Are you going to prepare a meal for us?
paras.zh: 你要给我们做饭吗？

paras.en: No, sorry.
paras.zh: 不了，抱歉。

paras.en: I’m actually pretty worn out.
paras.zh: 我其实挺累的。

paras.en: Let’s just go out somewhere close to eat.
paras.zh: 我们就去附近随便找个地方吃吧。

paras.en: Well, I think we should stay in and save some cash.
paras.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们还是待在家里，省点钱吧。

paras.en: Can we get a meal delivered?
paras.zh: 能叫外卖吗？

paras.en: Yeah, great.
paras.zh: 好啊，太好了。

paras.en: I’ll use that food delivery app on my phone.
paras.zh: 我用手机上那个外卖软件。

paras.en: What do you want?
paras.zh: 你想吃什么？

paras.en: Fried chicken, hamburgers, or fish and chips?
paras.zh: 炸鸡、汉堡，还是炸鱼薯条？

paras.en: Oh, can we stay away from the junk food?
paras.zh: 哦，我们能不吃垃圾食品吗？

paras.en: How about something healthy?
paras.zh: 吃点健康的东西怎么样？

paras.en: Okay.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: Well, there’s a place that does salads.
paras.zh: 嗯，有一家店做沙拉。

paras.en: Let me have a look at that.
paras.zh: 我看一看。

paras.en: Yeah, that looks delicious.
paras.zh: 嗯，看着挺好吃的。

paras.en: But, to be honest, I’d prefer something hot, not cold.
paras.zh: 不过说实话，我更想吃热的，不想吃凉的。

paras.en: How about Indian food?
paras.zh: 印度菜怎么样？

paras.en: That’s not the kind of hot I mean.
paras.zh: 我说的不是那种辣。

paras.en: I’m just not a fan of sauces that make me sweat and cry.
paras.zh: 我就是不喜欢那种辣得人直冒汗、直流眼泪的酱汁。

paras.en: I need something mild.
paras.zh: 我想吃点清淡的。

paras.en: Okay, so would you consider Mexican?
paras.zh: 好吧，那墨西哥菜你考虑吗？

paras.en: Oh, no, sorry.
paras.zh: 哦，不了，抱歉。

paras.en: There’s also very hot pepper in that.
paras.zh: 那里面也有很辣的辣椒。

paras.en: Would you like some Italian food perhaps?
paras.zh: 要不要来点意大利菜？

paras.en: It’s a bit heavy, but it’s great food for a cold night like this.
paras.zh: 有点油腻，不过像今晚这么冷，吃这个正好。

paras.en: Pizza, spaghetti with creamy sauce?
paras.zh: 披萨，还是奶油酱意大利面？

paras.en: I know it’s really tasty, and great comfort food, but it’s too fattening for me.
paras.zh: 我知道那真的很好吃，吃了也让人心里舒坦，可是太容易长胖了。

w.m: 安慰食物；吃了让人舒心的食物

paras.en: I’m trying to keep a slim figure, you know.
paras.zh: 你知道的，我想保持苗条的身材。

paras.en: Oh, you’re really difficult to please.
paras.zh: 哦，你可真难伺候。

paras.en: Well, there’s a nice Chinese restaurant that delivers.
paras.zh: 嗯，有一家不错的中餐馆能送外卖。

paras.en: Yes, I love Chinese food.
paras.zh: 好啊，我很喜欢中国菜。

paras.en: Let me see.
paras.zh: 我看看。

paras.en: Oh, it’s fifteen kilometers away.
paras.zh: 哦，要十五公里远。

paras.en: That’s a bit too far away.
paras.zh: 有点太远了。

paras.en: Do you feel like Vietnamese food, then?
paras.zh: 那你想吃越南菜吗？

paras.en: Yeah, awesome.
paras.zh: 好啊，太棒了。

paras.en: It’s healthy, and we can afford it.
paras.zh: 越南菜健康，我们也吃得起。

paras.en: Great.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: Let’s order Vietnamese right away.
paras.zh: 我们马上点越南菜吧。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: Why isn’t the man going to cook?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士为什么不打算做饭？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the man say he’ll do on his phone?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士说他要用手机做什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the woman think of Indian food?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士觉得印度菜怎么样？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the man think of the woman?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士觉得女士怎么样？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: A new study carried out by the University of Lincoln has found a link between the personalities of cat owners and the behaviour and well-being of their cats.
paras.zh: 林肯大学的一项新研究发现，猫主人的性格和猫的行为、健康之间有关联。

paras.en: The findings suggest that just as a parent’s personality can affect the personality of a child, the same is true for a cat and its owner.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，就像父母的性格会影响孩子的性格一样，猫和主人之间也是这样。

paras.en: Owners defined as individuals with high levels of anxiety, fear, anger, depression, and loneliness were more likely to have cats with behavioural issues.
paras.zh: 那些被认为焦虑、恐惧、愤怒、抑郁和孤独程度高的主人，他们的猫更容易出现行为问题。

paras.en: Such cats displayed more aggressive and anxious behavioural styles as well as more stress-related sickness.
paras.zh: 这类猫表现出更强的攻击性、更多的焦虑行为，与压力有关的病也更多。

paras.en: They were also more likely to have an ongoing medical condition and be overweight.
paras.zh: 它们也更容易长期患病、体重超标。

paras.en: The research also found that mentally well-adjusted owners had calmer, happier, and healthier cats.
paras.zh: 研究还发现，心理调适得好的主人，养的猫也更平静、更快乐、更健康。

w.m: adj. 调适得好的；适应良好的

paras.en: The researchers explained that many owners regard their pets as a family member and form close social bonds with them.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说，很多主人把宠物当成家里的一员，和它们建立了亲密的社会关系。

paras.en: The majority of owners want to provide the best care for their pets, and it is therefore possible that pets could be affected by the way their owners interact with and manage them.
paras.zh: 大多数主人都想给宠物最好的照顾，所以，主人和宠物相处、照管它们的方式，有可能会影响到宠物。

paras.en: The study highlights an important relationship between our personalities and the well-being of our pets.
paras.zh: 这项研究突出了我们的性格与宠物健康之间的重要关系。

paras.en: Further research is needed to investigate the causal nature of this relationship, and to look at how owners’ personalities are directly influencing their pets’ behaviour and well-being.
paras.zh: 还需要进一步研究，查明这种关系是不是因果关系，并且看看主人的性格是怎样直接影响宠物的行为和健康的。

paras.en: It is possible that the well-being of pets is driven by the underlying nature of the owner, not simply by their conscious decisions and behaviours.
paras.zh: 宠物健康不健康，可能取决于主人内在的天性，而不只是主人有意识做出的决定和行为。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What do we learn from the new study by the University of Lincoln?
paras.zh: 第十六题：从林肯大学的这项新研究中，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What does the passage say most pet owners want to do?
paras.zh: 第十七题：短文说大多数宠物主人想做什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the passage say is still needed to understand the effects of owners’ personalities on their pets?
paras.zh: 第十八题：短文说，要弄清主人性格对宠物的影响，还需要什么？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: One sixty-minute run can add seven hours to your life.
paras.zh: 跑六十分钟步，能让你多活七个小时。

paras.en: This was a claim made by The Times last week.
paras.zh: 这是《泰晤士报》上周提出的说法。

paras.en: The claim was based on a new review of studies about the effects of running.
paras.zh: 这个说法依据的是一篇新的综述，它总结了关于跑步效果的多项研究。

paras.en: The review concluded that on average runners live three years longer than non-runners, and that running does more to extend life than any other form of exercise.
paras.zh: 这篇综述的结论是，平均来看，跑步的人比不跑步的人多活三年，而且，在延长寿命方面，跑步比其他任何运动都更有效。

paras.en: But there’s more to running than its health benefits.
paras.zh: 不过，跑步的好处可不只是健康方面的。

paras.en: Research published in recent years has shown that running changes your brain and mind in some fascinating ways, from increasing your brain function to regulating your emotions.
paras.zh: 近些年发表的研究表明，跑步会以一些很奇妙的方式改变你的大脑和心理，从增强大脑功能到调节情绪，都有作用。

paras.en: However, the precise effects vary according to whether you engage in short fast running or long-distance running.
paras.zh: 不过，具体效果并不一样，要看你是短距离快跑，还是长跑。

paras.en: For example, in one study researchers compared participants’ ability to learn new words after several minutes of intense running, and after forty minutes of gentle running.
paras.zh: 比如，在一项研究中，研究人员比较了参与者在几分钟剧烈跑步之后和四十分钟轻松跑步之后学新单词的能力。

paras.en: Participants were able to learn twenty per cent faster after the intense running, and they showed a superior memory when tested again a week later.
paras.zh: 剧烈跑步之后，参与者学单词的速度快了百分之二十，一周后再测试，他们的记忆也更好。

paras.en: In another study, researchers asked volunteers to jog for thirty minutes and then showed them clips from a sad movie.
paras.zh: 在另一项研究中，研究人员让志愿者慢跑三十分钟，然后给他们看一部悲伤电影的片段。

paras.en: Participants who usually struggled to handle negative emotions were more intensely affected by the sad clips, just as you expect, but crucially this was less so if they had completed the thirty-minute jog.
paras.zh: 那些平时就很难应对负面情绪的参与者，看了悲伤的片段，受到的影响更强烈，这和你想的一样；可关键是，如果他们之前慢跑了三十分钟，受到的影响就没那么大了。

paras.en: The researchers said moderate exercise appears to have helped those participants to be less vulnerable to the impact of the sad movie.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，适度的运动似乎让这些参与者不那么容易受悲伤电影的影响。

w.m: adj. 易受影响的；脆弱的

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What did the new review of studies claim?
paras.zh: 第十九题：那篇新的研究综述得出了什么说法？

paras.en: Question twenty: What is one effect that running has on people according to recent research?
paras.zh: 第二十题：根据近期的研究，跑步对人有什么作用？

paras.en: Question twenty one: What did another study find about the participants after they had a thirty-minute jog?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：另一项研究发现，参与者慢跑三十分钟后怎么样？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Welcome to the Tour of the Hill House.
paras.zh: 欢迎参观希尔别墅。

paras.en: This house, built in 1904, is one of the most well-known works of Charles Hill, the famous architect.
paras.zh: 这座房子建于一九零四年，是著名建筑师查尔斯·希尔最有名的作品之一。

paras.en: It was designed and built for a local entrepreneur and his family.
paras.zh: 它是为当地一位企业家和他的家人设计建造的。

paras.en: Before starting the tour, let me give you a brief introduction about the design of this amazing building.
paras.zh: 参观开始之前，我先简单介绍一下这座了不起的建筑是怎么设计的。

w.m: adj. 了不起的；令人惊叹的

paras.en: Prior to beginning his design, the architect spent some time in the client’s old home, observing their life and studying their habits.
paras.zh: 开始设计之前，建筑师在委托人的旧宅里待了一段时间，观察他们的生活，研究他们的习惯。

paras.en: This meant that he could design the house according to the needs of the family.
paras.zh: 这样一来，他就能根据这家人的需要来设计房子。

paras.en: The client’s main desire was to have a home with a unique design, so the architect was given complete freedom.
paras.zh: 委托人最主要的愿望，是要一座设计独一无二的房子，所以建筑师得到了完全的自由。

w.m: adj. 独一无二的；独特的

paras.en: The building style is radically different from what was the fashion of the period.
paras.zh: 这座建筑的风格和当时流行的风格截然不同。

paras.en: At the time most large homes were constructed of timber and brick.
paras.zh: 当时，大多数大房子都是用木材和砖建造的。

paras.en: This one, however, is made of concrete, a novel construction material in those days.
paras.zh: 这一座却是用混凝土建的，混凝土在那个年代是一种新式的建筑材料。

paras.en: The interior of the house, including fittings and furniture, was also designed by the same person.
paras.zh: 房子的内部，包括装修和家具，也都是这位建筑师设计的。

paras.en: Most of the furniture you will see is original, and in good condition.
paras.zh: 您将看到的家具大多是原物，而且保存完好。

paras.en: However, those pieces in the children’s bedrooms are copies built to the designs of the architect.
paras.zh: 不过，孩子们卧室里的那些家具是按建筑师的设计图做的复制品。

paras.en: Fortunately, all the blueprints for both the building and its contents have been preserved, so we have been able to replace badly damaged furniture.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，这座建筑和里面所有东西的设计图都保存了下来，所以我们才能把损坏严重的家具换掉。

paras.en: Let’s begin our tour, starting from the rooms.
paras.zh: 我们从这些房间开始参观吧。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What do we learn about the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于说话人，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty three: What did the architect do before beginning his design?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：建筑师在开始设计之前做了什么？

paras.en: Question twenty four: What do the architect’s client mainly want?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：建筑师的委托人主要想要什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What do we learn about the pieces of furniture in the children’s bedrooms?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于孩子们卧室里的家具，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道介绍一项研究：含添加糖的饮料喝得越多，研究期间的死亡风险越高，研究人员建议少喝这类饮料、多喝水。第二篇新闻报道讲德国一名六十四岁的男子在高速公路休息站的垃圾堆里捡到两幅十七世纪油画，交给了科隆警方，警方正在寻找失主。第三篇新闻报道讲西伯利亚一名四岁女孩穿过八公里雪林，为病重的外婆求救，女孩的母亲因此面临刑事诉讼。第一段长对话里，女士介绍她新结识的南非朋友苏珊，聊到开普敦、桌山、南非多元的人口和橄榄球。第二段长对话里，男士为这学期的课业发愁，珍妮弗建议他做学习指南，并按自己的学习类型整理笔记。第一篇短文讲黄金法则的含义、受到的批评以及人们怎样看待它。第二篇短文讲一项关于职场多元化态度的研究：事情跟自己有关时，人们更愿意选和自己相似的队友。第三篇短文讲不同文化对口头约定和书面合同的看法不同，这会给国际商务带来麻烦。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A new study finds that beverages containing added sugar might be harmful.
paras.zh: 一项新研究发现，含添加糖的饮料可能有害健康。

paras.en: In the study, researchers analyzed information from over 80,000 women and 37,000 men.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员分析了八万多名女性和三万七千名男性的信息。

paras.en: Participants worked in the health profession.
paras.zh: 参与者都在医疗卫生行业工作。

paras.en: They were followed for approximately three decades.
paras.zh: 研究人员对他们跟踪调查了大约三十年。

paras.en: They completed surveys about their diet every four years.
paras.zh: 他们每四年填一次关于饮食的调查问卷。

paras.en: They also answered questions about sleep and exercise and health every two years.
paras.zh: 他们还每两年回答一次关于睡眠、运动和健康的问题。

paras.en: The more beverages containing added sugar that people drank, the greater their risk of death was during the study period.
paras.zh: 人们喝的含添加糖饮料越多，在研究期间的死亡风险就越高。

paras.en: These beverages included soda, energy drinks, and sports drinks.
paras.zh: 这些饮料包括汽水、能量饮料和运动饮料。

paras.en: Beverages like pure fruit juice, which are sweet but do not contain added sugar, were not part of the study.
paras.zh: 像纯果汁这样的饮料，虽然是甜的，但不含添加糖，所以不在这项研究的范围内。

paras.en: The findings held even after the researchers considered other factors that could affect people’s health.
paras.zh: 即使研究人员考虑了其他可能影响健康的因素，这些发现依然成立。

paras.en: These factors included lack of exercise and not eating enough vegetables.
paras.zh: 这些因素包括缺乏运动、蔬菜吃得不够。

paras.en: They also included consuming too much meat.
paras.zh: 还包括吃肉太多。

paras.en: The scientists say that their results support limiting beverages with added sugar.
paras.zh: 科学家们说，他们的研究结果支持少喝含添加糖的饮料。

paras.en: They argue we should replace them with other drinks, with water being the best choice.
paras.zh: 他们主张用别的饮品代替这类饮料，最好是喝水。

paras.en: However, the researchers admit this is simply their recommendation.
paras.zh: 不过，研究人员承认，这只是他们的建议。

paras.en: The study found only an association.
paras.zh: 这项研究只发现了一种关联。

paras.en: It did not prove that drinks with added sugar cause early death.
paras.zh: 它并没有证明含添加糖的饮料会导致过早死亡。

paras.en: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What do we learn about the new study from the news report?
paras.zh: 第一题：从这篇新闻报道中，我们对这项新研究了解到什么？

paras.en: Question two: What is the scientists’ recommendation?
paras.zh: 第二题：科学家们的建议是什么？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: German police appealed Friday for information about the possible owners of two 17th century oil paintings.
paras.zh: 德国警方周五发出呼吁，希望知情人提供这两幅十七世纪油画可能的主人的线索。

paras.en: Police said a 64-year-old man found the paintings in a garbage pile at a highway rest stop last month.
paras.zh: 警方说，上个月，一名六十四岁的男子在一个高速公路休息站的垃圾堆里发现了这两幅画。

paras.en: He later handed them in to the Cologne Police.
paras.zh: 后来，他把画交给了科隆警方。

paras.en: An initial assessment by an art expert concluded the two framed paintings were originals, police said.
paras.zh: 警方说，一位艺术专家初步鉴定后认为，这两幅带框的画都是真迹。

paras.en: One is a landscape painted by the Italian artist Pietro Bellotti, dating to sixteen sixty-five.
paras.zh: 其中一幅是意大利画家彼得罗·贝洛蒂画的风景画，创作于一六六五年。

paras.en: The other is a painting of a boy by the seventeenth century Dutch artist Samuel van Hoogstraten, date unknown.
paras.zh: 另一幅是十七世纪荷兰画家塞缪尔·范·霍赫斯特拉滕画的一个男孩，创作年代不详。

paras.en: Their combined worth is estimated to be around 1 million euros.
paras.zh: 两幅画加起来估计价值一百万欧元左右。

paras.en: Authorities have not yet confirmed what will happen if the rightful owner is not found.
paras.zh: 如果找不到真正的主人，这两幅画会怎么处理，当局还没有确定。

paras.en: Nevertheless, it is speculated that they could either be handed over to the National Art Museum of Cologne or sold to the public by the local government.
paras.zh: 不过，有人推测，这两幅画可能会交给科隆国家艺术博物馆，或者由当地政府卖给公众。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What did German police say about a sixty four year old man?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于那名六十四岁的男子，德国警方说了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What is the art expert’s conclusion about the two framed paintings?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于这两幅带框的画，艺术专家的结论是什么？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A four-year-old girl has walked eight kilometers through a snowy forest to seek help for her sick grandmother, who later died of a heart attack.
paras.zh: 一名四岁女孩穿过白雪覆盖的森林，走了八公里，为生病的外婆求救，外婆后来死于心脏病发作。

paras.en: The young girl braved the threat of bears, wolves, and temperatures far below freezing.
paras.zh: 这个小女孩不顾熊和狼的威胁，冒着远低于零度的严寒前行。

paras.en: She made the journey through a remote region in Siberia after waking up to find her grandmother motionless.
paras.zh: 她一觉醒来，发现外婆一动不动，于是穿过西伯利亚一个偏远地区，走了这一路。

paras.en: Named locally as Karla, she lives alone with her elderly grandmother and her blind grandfather.
paras.zh: 当地人称她为卡拉，她和年迈的外婆、失明的外公一起生活，身边没有别的人。

w.m: adj. 年长的；上了年纪的

paras.en: As a result, the girl’s mother is facing a criminal case.
paras.zh: 因此，女孩的母亲正面临一起刑事诉讼。

paras.en: She stands accused of leaving a minor in danger in the care of the elderly.
paras.zh: 她被指控把未成年人交给老人照顾，使其处于危险之中。

w.m: n. 老人；上了年纪的人

paras.en: She also faces investigation from child care services, who will also be asking why Karla was left alone with her vulnerable relatives.
paras.zh: 她还要接受儿童保护机构的调查，他们也会追问为什么卡拉被留下来，独自跟体弱的亲人生活在一起。

w.m: adj. 脆弱的；易受伤害的

paras.en: The journey took place in February, when temperatures average negative 26 degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 这段路程是在二月走的，那时的平均气温是零下二十六摄氏度。

paras.en: Russian reports on social media suggest the forest may have been as cold as negative 34 degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯社交媒体上的消息说，那片森林当时可能冷到零下三十四摄氏度。

paras.en: The journey was only recently confirmed by authorities.
paras.zh: 当局最近才证实了这段经历。

paras.en: But though she was suffering from the effects of extreme cold, the child reportedly suffered no life-threatening effects.
paras.zh: 不过，虽然孩子受到了极度寒冷的影响，但据报道，她并没有生命危险。

paras.en: Last year, a three-year-old boy survived alone for three days in a remote forest in the same region.
paras.zh: 去年，一个三岁男孩在同一地区的一片偏远森林里独自活了三天。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What did the four-year-old girl attempt to do?
paras.zh: 第五题：这个四岁女孩想做什么？

paras.en: Question six: What do we learn from the news report about the girl’s mother?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于女孩的母亲，我们从这篇新闻报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 7: What happened to the little girl, according to the news report?
paras.zh: 第七题：根据这篇新闻报道，这个小女孩怎么样了？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation 1.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I’ve made a new friend recently.
paras.zh: 我最近交了个新朋友。

paras.en: Her name is Susan and she’s from South Africa.
paras.zh: 她叫苏珊，是南非人。

paras.en: How did you meet her?
paras.zh: 你们是怎么认识的？

paras.en: We met over WeChat.
paras.zh: 我们是在微信上认识的。

paras.en: She has very cool photos on her social media.
paras.zh: 她的社交媒体上有好多特别酷的照片。

paras.en: The photos of her hometown look amazing.
paras.zh: 她家乡的照片看起来美极了。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；美极了的

paras.en: What’s her hometown called?
paras.zh: 她家乡叫什么？

paras.en: It’s called Cape Town.
paras.zh: 叫开普敦。

paras.en: It’s in the southwest of South Africa.
paras.zh: 在南非的西南部。

paras.en: She says it’s very green and windy.
paras.zh: 她说那里到处都是绿色，而且风很大。

paras.en: The city was built by European settlers.
paras.zh: 这座城市是欧洲移民建起来的。

paras.en: And there’s a big mountain that overlooks the city.
paras.zh: 还有一座大山俯瞰着整座城市。

paras.en: The mountain is called Table Mountain because it’s flat at the top.
paras.zh: 这座山叫桌山，因为它的山顶是平的。

paras.en: That sounds interesting.
paras.zh: 听起来很有意思。

paras.en: What are the people there like?
paras.zh: 那里的人怎么样？

paras.en: Well, Susan says South Africa is very mixed.
paras.zh: 嗯，苏珊说南非人种很多元。

paras.en: There are black people and white people and Indian people.
paras.zh: 有黑人、白人，还有印度人。

paras.en: Susan is white.
paras.zh: 苏珊是白人。

paras.en: She says her ancestors were from Britain.
paras.zh: 她说她的祖先来自英国。

paras.en: Many languages are spoken in South Africa, but she only speaks English.
paras.zh: 南非有很多种语言，可她只会说英语。

paras.en: Didn’t South Africa host the Football World Cup a few years ago?
paras.zh: 南非前几年不是举办过足球世界杯吗？

paras.en: They must play football a lot then, right?
paras.zh: 那他们肯定经常踢足球吧？

paras.en: I think they play football, but it’s not as popular as rugby.
paras.zh: 我觉得他们也踢足球，不过足球没有橄榄球那么受欢迎。

paras.en: Rugby?
paras.zh: 橄榄球？

paras.en: What’s rugby?
paras.zh: 橄榄球是什么？

paras.en: Rugby is a sport with two teams and the players carry the ball in their arms and throw it at each other.
paras.zh: 橄榄球是一项运动，分两队，球员把球抱在怀里，互相传球。

paras.en: The ball is not round, and the players push each other.
paras.zh: 球不是圆的，球员还会互相推挤。

paras.en: I don’t really understand the rules.
paras.zh: 我其实不太懂它的规则。

paras.en: I think it’s very complicated.
paras.zh: 我觉得规则很复杂。

paras.en: That sounds like a very strange sport indeed.
paras.zh: 那听起来确实是一项很奇怪的运动。

paras.en: Is it only South Africa that plays it?
paras.zh: 只有南非打橄榄球吗？

paras.en: No, it’s also popular in Britain and in other former British colonies, like Australia and New Zealand.
paras.zh: 不是，它在英国，还有其他前英国殖民地，比如澳大利亚和新西兰，也很受欢迎。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the woman say about her new friend Susan?
paras.zh: 第八题：关于她的新朋友苏珊，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman say about Table Mountain?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于桌山，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What do we learn from the conversation about the woman’s friend Susan?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于女士的朋友苏珊，我们从对话中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman say about rugby in South Africa?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于南非的橄榄球，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi, Jennifer.
paras.zh: 嗨，珍妮弗。

paras.en: I’m really struggling with this semester’s workload.
paras.zh: 这学期的课业实在压得我喘不过气来。

paras.en: Do you have any advice?
paras.zh: 你有什么建议吗？

paras.en: Have you considered making a study guide?
paras.zh: 你有没有想过做一份学习指南？

paras.en: It’s a tool you can make yourself to take the stress out of studying.
paras.zh: 这是一种你可以自己动手做的工具，能让学习不再那么有压力。

paras.en: I’ve been using one since the start of last semester, and it has really helped relieve a lot of study pressure.
paras.zh: 我从上学期开学就一直在用，它真的帮我减轻了不少学习压力。

paras.en: sounds like just what I need.
paras.zh: 听起来正是我需要的。

paras.en: My main problem is that my study folder is full of notes and worksheets and is badly disorganized.
paras.zh: 我主要的问题是，我的学习资料夹里塞满了笔记和练习题，乱七八糟的。

paras.en: I don’t know where to start.
paras.zh: 我都不知道从哪儿下手。

paras.en: Okay.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: Well, the main thing is to have everything in the right place.
paras.zh: 嗯，最重要的是把所有东西都放在该放的地方。

paras.en: Whatever you’re reviewing, it’s important that it’s arranged for your particular needs of that subject, and in the most user-friendly way you can.
paras.zh: 不管你复习什么，重要的是要按照那门科目的特定需要来整理，而且要尽可能整理得方便好用。

w.m: adj. 方便使用的；好用的

paras.en: What kind of learner are you?
paras.zh: 你是哪一类学习者？

paras.en: Hmm, I’m not sure.
paras.zh: 嗯，我不太确定。

paras.en: Well, visual learners prefer using images, pictures, colors, and maps to organize information.
paras.zh: 嗯，视觉型学习者喜欢用图像、图片、颜色和地图来整理信息。

paras.en: Logical learners have a linear mind and would rather use logic, reasoning and systems.
paras.zh: 逻辑型学习者思维是线性的，更愿意运用逻辑、推理和体系。

paras.en: I’m an emotional learner, which means I need to connect to information emotionally to understand it.
paras.zh: 我是情感型学习者，也就是说，我要在情感上和信息产生联系，才能理解它。

paras.en: Oh, I’m very much dependent on vision as a way of taking in information.
paras.zh: 哦，我接收信息非常依赖视觉。

paras.en: Well, I suggest reorganizing your notes using color-coded sections in your study guides, or using idea mapping to lay out the information and make it more quickly accessible.
paras.zh: 嗯，我建议你在学习指南里用不同颜色区分各个部分，重新整理你的笔记，或者用思维导图把信息铺排开来，这样查找起来更快。

w.m: adj. 易获取的；容易找到的

paras.en: So you think I should arrange my notes using color and pictures in place of text?
paras.zh: 那你觉得我应该用颜色和图片代替文字来整理笔记？

paras.en: Yes, you’ll probably start to grasp information a lot quicker that way.
paras.zh: 对，那样你大概会更快地掌握信息。

paras.en: As an emotional learner, I organize my notes into a story that I can connect to and recite to myself.
paras.zh: 我是情感型学习者，我会把笔记整理成一个故事，让自己能和它产生联系，还能讲给自己听。

paras.en: That’s amazing.
paras.zh: 太神奇了。

paras.en: I didn’t know there were so many different ways to learn.
paras.zh: 我都不知道原来有这么多不同的学习方法。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the woman advise the man to do?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士建议男士做什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What is the biggest problem the man has with his studies?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士在学习上最大的问题是什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What kind of learner does the woman say she is?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士说她是哪一类学习者？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the woman think the man can do with his notes?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士认为男士可以怎样处理他的笔记？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: The golden rule is a moral principle which states that you should treat others the way you want to be treated yourself.
paras.zh: 黄金法则是一条道德准则，它说的是：你希望别人怎样对待你，你就应该怎样对待别人。

paras.en: For example, if you want people to treat you with respect, you should treat them with respect.
paras.zh: 比如，如果你希望别人尊重你，你就应该尊重别人。

paras.en: Different people tend to be exposed to different forms of the Golden Rule, based on factors such as the religion in their society.
paras.zh: 不同的人往往接触到不同形式的黄金法则，这取决于他们所在社会的宗教等因素。

paras.en: However, all forms of the Golden Rule revolve around the same concept.
paras.zh: 不过，各种形式的黄金法则都围绕着同一个理念。

paras.en: Namely, they help you treat others better by using the way you yourself would want to be treated as a guide of how to behave.
paras.zh: 也就是说，它们教你拿自己希望被对待的方式作为行为的准则，从而更好地对待别人。

paras.en: A notable criticism of the Golden Rule is that its application can lead to undesirable outcomes when it conflicts with laws and ethical principles.
paras.zh: 对黄金法则的一个主要批评是：当它与法律和道德准则冲突时，照着做可能会带来不好的后果。

w.m: adj. 显著的；值得注意的
adj. 不好的；不受欢迎的

paras.en: For example, if someone breaks the law, the Golden Rule would suggest that we should let them go, because we would not want to be punished ourselves.
paras.zh: 比如，如果有人违法，按照黄金法则，我们就应该放过他们，因为我们自己也不希望受到惩罚。

paras.en: However, this issue with the Golden Rule can be dealt with in a general manner, by viewing this principle as one of several principles that we use to guide our behavior as individuals and as a society.
paras.zh: 不过，黄金法则的这个问题可以笼统地解决：把它看作我们用来指导个人和社会行为的几条原则之一。

paras.en: Specifically, in the example described above, most individuals and societies choose to place laws and ethical principles above the Golden Rule.
paras.zh: 具体来说，在上面举的例子里，大多数个人和社会都会选择把法律和道德准则放在黄金法则之上。

paras.en: This means that they strive to implement the golden rule whenever possible, as long as it doesn’t clash with a more important concept.
paras.zh: 也就是说，他们会尽可能践行黄金法则，只要它不与更重要的理念冲突。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What do we learn from the passage about the Golden Rule?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于黄金法则，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What is a notable criticism of the Golden Rule?
paras.zh: 第十七题：对黄金法则的一个主要批评是什么？

w.m: adj. 显著的；值得注意的

paras.en: Question 18: What does the example of someone breaking the law serve to show?
paras.zh: 第十八题：有人违法的例子是用来说明什么的？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Today many large corporations stress the importance of diversity on their websites.
paras.zh: 如今，许多大公司都在官网上强调多元化的重要性。

paras.en: But current statistics show that the typical manager in America still tends to be white and male.
paras.zh: 可现在的统计数据显示，美国典型的经理仍然多是白人男性。

paras.en: Obviously, the desire to bring about diversity has not translated into corporate reality.
paras.zh: 显然，推动多元化的愿望并没有变成企业的现实。

paras.en: Why is this?
paras.zh: 这是为什么呢？

paras.en: A team of researchers from the University of Basel published their new study about people’s attitudes towards diversity at work.
paras.zh: 巴塞尔大学的一个研究团队发表了他们的新研究，内容是人们对职场多元化的态度。

paras.en: They found that people have a wide range of opinions concerning diversity.
paras.zh: 他们发现，人们对多元化的看法五花八门。

paras.en: On the one hand, many see value in diversity, which can contribute a variety of perspectives, encourage new ideas and generate innovative solutions.
paras.zh: 一方面，许多人看到了多元化的价值：它能带来各种视角，激发新想法，产生创新的解决办法。

paras.en: On the other hand, they assume that it might be difficult to work with someone who has completely different views, speaks a different language or has a different style of work.
paras.zh: 另一方面，他们又觉得，跟观点完全不同、说另一种语言或者工作风格不同的人一起工作，可能会很难。

paras.en: The actual value they attribute to diversity depends on the decision-making perspective.
paras.zh: 他们实际上认为多元化有多大价值，取决于做决定的角度。

paras.en: Doubts about the practicability of diversity have a greater weight if a person is directly affected.
paras.zh: 如果一个人直接受到影响，他对多元化是否可行的疑虑就更重。

paras.en: In other words, when a person’s own work group is involved, they tend to prefer team members who are similar to themselves.
paras.zh: 换句话说，如果涉及自己的工作小组，人们往往更喜欢和自己相似的组员。

paras.en: But when people make decisions for others, they typically put together a more diverse team.
paras.zh: 但当人们替别人做决定时，通常会组建一个更多元的团队。

paras.en: These findings could help organizations become more diverse.
paras.zh: 这些发现可以帮助各类组织变得更加多元。

paras.en: Companies need to pay attention to who makes hiring and team decisions.
paras.zh: 公司需要注意由谁来做招聘和组建团队的决定。

paras.en: These decisions should not only be made by those directly affected.
paras.zh: 这些决定不应该只由直接受影响的人来做。

paras.en: People who are not directly involved in the group’s daily work should also take part.
paras.zh: 不直接参与小组日常工作的人也应该参与进来。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn from the current statistics about diversity in large corporations?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于大公司的多元化，我们从现在的统计数据中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty: What is the newly published study focused on?
paras.zh: 第二十题：这项新发表的研究关注的是什么？

paras.en: Question twenty-one: What do the findings of the new study show?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：这项新研究的发现说明了什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Communication can essentially be divided into two categories: the written and the spoken.
paras.zh: 交流基本上可以分为两类：书面交流和口头交流。

paras.en: How the balance is struck between these two forms of communication.
paras.zh: 这两种交流形式之间如何取得平衡，

paras.en: The point at which one needs to be exchanged for another, really depends on individual cultures.
paras.zh: 以及什么时候需要从一种换成另一种，其实取决于各自的文化。

paras.en: Understanding when it’s appropriate to exchange one form for another can be a major key to success in international business.
paras.zh: 弄清楚什么时候适合把一种形式换成另一种，可能是国际商务成功的一大关键。

paras.en: Many cultures place a much greater value on the spoken word than the American working culture does.
paras.zh: 很多文化比美国职场文化更看重口头说的话。

paras.en: In parts of the Middle East, you’ll find spoken word agreements are seen as seriously binding.
paras.zh: 在中东部分地区，你会发现口头约定被看作非常有约束力。

paras.en: A person’s word is linked to their honor, so verbal agreements are seen as important, whereas written contracts are taken as memos of understanding.
paras.zh: 一个人说的话关系到他的名誉，所以口头约定被看得很重要，而书面合同只被当作谅解备忘录。

paras.en: Western working culture tends to place a high value on the written word, and this reaches its highest level of intensity when it comes to contracts.
paras.zh: 西方职场文化往往很看重书面文字，在合同上更是看重到了极点。

paras.en: In the US, France, and Germany, written contracts tend to be seen as something that must be strictly carried out, the written contract as quite so binding.
paras.zh: 在美国、法国和德国，书面合同往往被看作必须严格执行的东西；而在日本，人们并不认为书面合同有那么强的约束力。

paras.en: It can prove a challenge to Western businesses if your business partner wants to renegotiate terms that you thought were already agreed on.
paras.zh: 如果你的商业伙伴想重新谈判你以为已经谈妥的条款，这对西方企业来说可能是个挑战。

paras.en: For example, a Japanese firm may have signed a contract, but they may not feel bound by every detail of it, particularly if circumstances later change.
paras.zh: 比如，一家日本公司也许已经签了合同，但他们未必觉得合同的每一个细节都要遵守，尤其是后来情况发生了变化的时候。

paras.en: Such differences in value that different working cultures place on the written word tend to cause many problems when it comes to business relationships.
paras.zh: 不同的职场文化对书面文字的重视程度不同，这种差异往往会在商业关系中引发许多问题。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What is a major key to success in international business, according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：根据短文，国际商务成功的一大关键是什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the passage say about spoken word agreements in some Middle East countries?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于一些中东国家的口头约定，短文是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 24: What do we learn about the Western working culture?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于西方职场文化，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 25: How does a Japanese firm tend to view a written contract?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：日本公司往往怎样看待书面合同？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2022年9月大学英语四级 第1套
passages.name: 2022年9月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道介绍一项研究：白肉和红肉一样会升高血液胆固醇，研究人员建议两种肉都少吃、多吃植物蛋白。第二篇新闻报道讲一辆货车的拖车在高街路口翻倒，几百只冻火鸡撒了一地，可能影响交通和圣诞晚餐，这个路口是事故多发地段。第三篇新闻报道讲印度班加罗尔开通直升机出租车服务，十五分钟把乘客从科技园送到机场，主要面向赶时间的企业高管。第一段长对话里，女士要为周末烧烤买奶酪，店员推荐了一种软奶酪和一种硬奶酪。第二段长对话里，男士和女士争论学校改用电子课本的利弊。第一篇短文讲社会心理学里的“人际知觉”以及社会归类可能带来的偏见。第二篇短文讲一项研究：智能手机时代的孩子社交能力并不比上一代差。第三篇短文讲被动灵感和主动灵感的区别，最好的灵感来自把想法付诸实践。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: White meat, such as chicken, may raise blood cholesterol levels as much as red meat does.
paras.zh: 像鸡肉这样的白肉，可能和红肉一样会升高血液中的胆固醇水平。

paras.en: This finding surprised researchers who admitted they didn’t expect that eating white meat would lead to higher blood cholesterol levels.
paras.zh: 这一发现让研究人员很吃惊，他们承认，没想到吃白肉也会让血液胆固醇水平升高。

paras.en: In the study, researchers looked at one hundred thirteen healthy people.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员观察了一百一十三名健康的人。

paras.en: The participants ate three different diets.
paras.zh: 参与者吃了三种不同的饮食。

paras.en: These were a red meat diet, which is primarily beef, a white meat diet, which is mostly chicken and turkey, and a vegetarian protein diet.
paras.zh: 分别是以牛肉为主的红肉饮食，以鸡肉和火鸡肉为主的白肉饮食，还有素食蛋白饮食。

paras.en: Each diet period was four weeks.
paras.zh: 每种饮食吃四周。

paras.en: Between the diet periods participants had a break, during which they ate their regular foods.
paras.zh: 两段饮食期之间，参与者会休息一段时间，这期间吃他们平常吃的食物。

paras.en: In addition, participants had blood tests at the start and finish of each new diet.
paras.zh: 另外，参与者在每种新饮食开始和结束时都要验血。

paras.en: The results showed that white and red meat diets had the same effects on blood cholesterol levels.
paras.zh: 结果显示，白肉饮食和红肉饮食对血液胆固醇水平的影响相同。

paras.en: Further, both diets increased blood cholesterol levels compared with the diet built on vegetarian protein sources.
paras.zh: 而且，跟以素食蛋白为主的饮食相比，这两种饮食都会升高血液胆固醇水平。

paras.en: The team acknowledged that it is possible that white meat is better for our health than red meat, despite their findings.
paras.zh: 研究团队也承认，尽管有这样的研究结果，白肉还是有可能比红肉更有益健康。

paras.en: This is because other effects of red meat consumption could contribute to heart disease independent of cholesterol.
paras.zh: 这是因为吃红肉的其他影响可能会导致心脏病，而这与胆固醇无关。

paras.en: Their main recommendations are that people eat less of both kinds of meat and more vegetarian protein.
paras.zh: 他们的主要建议是，两种肉都少吃，多吃素食蛋白。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What do we learn from the news report about the study?
paras.zh: 第一题：从这篇新闻报道中，我们对这项研究了解到什么？

paras.en: Question two: What did the researchers acknowledge?
paras.zh: 第二题：研究人员承认了什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At around half past nine this morning, a trailer attached to a lorry turned over at the crossing of High Street and Milton.
paras.zh: 今天上午九点半左右，一辆货车挂着的拖车在高街和米尔顿路的交叉口翻倒了。

paras.en: Hundreds of frozen turkeys were spilled all over the road.
paras.zh: 几百只冷冻火鸡撒了一路。

paras.en: It is reported that nobody was hurt in the incident, but police said it may affect traffic and Christmas dinners.
paras.zh: 据报道，事故中没有人受伤，但警方说，这可能会影响交通，也会影响大家的圣诞晚餐。

paras.en: With just one week to go before Christmas, there are worries that local supermarket supplies of this holiday favorite may be affected.
paras.zh: 离圣诞节只剩一周了，人们担心当地超市里这种节日必备的火鸡可能会供应不上。

paras.en: A police spokeswoman said that officers were currently in attendance at the scene.
paras.zh: 一名警方女发言人说，警察目前正在现场处理。

paras.en: She stated that the driver of the lorry had been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving.
paras.zh: 她说，货车司机因涉嫌危险驾驶已被逮捕。

paras.en: The crossing on High Street is a well-known accident black spot.
paras.zh: 高街上的这个路口是出了名的事故多发地段。

w.m: adj. 出名的；众所周知的

paras.en: This year alone, there have been seven traffic accidents at this location.
paras.zh: 光是今年，这个地点就发生了七起交通事故。

paras.en: Thankfully, none of these accidents have resulted in serious injury.
paras.zh: 幸好，这些事故都没有造成重伤。

w.m: adv. 幸好；值得庆幸的是

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What does the news report say about the accident at the crossing of High Street and Milton?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于高街和米尔顿路交叉口的那起事故，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What do we learn about the crossing on High Street?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于高街上的那个路口，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: India launched its helicopter taxi service on Monday, promising to ferry customers the 40 miles between Bangalore’s Electronic City tech hub and the international airport terminal in fifteen minutes.
paras.zh: 印度周一开通了直升机出租车服务，承诺十五分钟就能把乘客从班加罗尔的电子城科技中心送到四十英里外的国际机场航站楼。

paras.en: Customers can book their helicopter ride through a mobile app.
paras.zh: 乘客可以用手机应用预订直升机。

paras.en: The service, which claims to be the first of its kind in India, offers only one route, but Bangalore Airport will add more once it gets approval.
paras.zh: 这项服务号称是印度首个此类服务，目前只有一条航线，不过班加罗尔机场说，一获得批准就会增加航线。

paras.en: Helicopter taxi is not an affordable option for many travelers.
paras.zh: 对很多出行的人来说，直升机出租车并不是负担得起的选择。

w.m: adj. 负担得起的；价格实惠的

paras.en: A car ride for the same journey costs less than half as much.
paras.zh: 同样的路程，坐汽车的费用还不到它的一半。

paras.en: But Bangalore Airport says it is a competitive alternative to a car ride for tech executives in a hurry.
paras.zh: 但班加罗尔机场说，对赶时间的科技公司高管来说，它比坐汽车更有竞争力。

paras.en: A large number of high-class travelers, including CEOs, have to spend more than three hours by road to get there, and that is a loss of time, a Bangalore Airport spokesperson said.
paras.zh: 班加罗尔机场的一位发言人说：“很多高端出行人士，包括首席执行官，走公路去那里要花三个多小时，这是在浪费时间。”

paras.en: This is not a low-cost option, but it is an option, she added.
paras.zh: 她还说：“这不是一个便宜的选择，但总归是一个选择。”

paras.en: The helicopters ferried around eight customers to the airport on their first day.
paras.zh: 开通第一天，直升机送了大约八位乘客去机场。

paras.en: The company that owns and operates the service is called Thumby Aviation.
paras.zh: 拥有并运营这项服务的公司叫图姆比航空公司。

paras.en: It previously specialized in private charter flights for government officials.
paras.zh: 这家公司以前专做政府官员的私人包机业务。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。
