paras.en: She watched her mother order the doll online.
paras.zh: 她看着妈妈在网上订了这个玩偶。

paras.en: The next day, Kate asked if she could check the shipping status, so her mom clicked on the webpage and then walked out of the room.
paras.zh: 第二天，凯特问能不能查一下物流状态，于是妈妈点开网页，然后就走出了房间。

paras.en: Kate saw that her doll would be arriving the next afternoon, but then she noticed something else: suggestions about other dolls and toys she could order.
paras.zh: 凯特看到玩偶第二天下午就能送到，可接着她又注意到了别的东西，推荐她可以订的其他玩偶和玩具。

paras.en: Fifteen minutes and a few clicks later, with more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart, Kate placed the order and ran off to play.
paras.zh: 十五分钟、点了几下之后，购物车里已经有了价值三百五十多美元的玩偶，凯特下了单，就跑去玩了。

paras.en: The next day, while checking on another online order, her mother noticed a long list of dolls on the way.
paras.zh: 又过了一天，妈妈在查另一个网购订单时，发现有一长串玩偶正在路上。

paras.en: She was able to cancel two of them, but it was too late to cancel the rest.
paras.zh: 她取消了其中两个，可剩下的已经来不及取消了。

paras.en: She told her daughter that they were going to be returned.
paras.zh: 她告诉女儿，这些玩偶都要退回去。

paras.en: When the packages arrived, Kate wanted to open them, but her parents said no.
paras.zh: 包裹到了以后，凯特想拆开，可爸爸妈妈没同意。

paras.en: Instead of sending back the dolls, her father suggested giving them to the local children’s hospital.
paras.zh: 爸爸没有把玩偶退回去，而是建议把它们送给当地的儿童医院。

paras.en: So the next week, Kate’s family loaded up their car and took all the dolls to the playroom at the children’s hospital.
paras.zh: 于是第二周，凯特一家把玩偶装满车，全部送到了儿童医院的游戏室。

paras.en: Kate was depressed at first, but then she sat with some girl patients and they opened up all the boxes together, laughing and playing.
paras.zh: 凯特一开始很沮丧，可后来她和几个女孩病人坐在一起，大家一起拆开所有的盒子，有说有笑地玩了起来。

w.m: adj. 沮丧的；情绪低落的

paras.en: She had a lot of fun and learned a really good lesson.
paras.zh: 她玩得很开心，也学到了很好的一课。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: How did Kate earn the reward from her mother?
paras.zh: 第十九题：凯特是怎么从妈妈那里得到奖励的？

paras.en: Question 20: What did Kate do after her mother left the room?
paras.zh: 第二十题：妈妈离开房间后，凯特做了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What did Kate’s family do after the packages arrived?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：包裹到了以后，凯特一家做了什么？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Can the date you were born affect how successful your life is?
paras.zh: 你出生的日子会影响你这辈子有多成功吗？

paras.en: According to recent research done in Australia, the answer is yes.
paras.zh: 根据澳大利亚最近的一项研究，答案是肯定的。

paras.en: The researchers found that the time when a person starts school has an enduring impact on their lives.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，一个人开始上学的时间会对他的一生产生长久的影响。

paras.en: Those who are relatively old compared to their classmates have certain advantages over them.
paras.zh: 在班里年龄相对偏大的孩子，比同班同学多一些优势。

paras.en: Previous research has found that older students achieve better results.
paras.zh: 以前的研究发现，年龄大一些的学生成绩更好。

paras.en: They are also more likely to attend university and become professional athletes, chief executives, and even important politicians.
paras.zh: 他们也更有可能上大学，成为职业运动员、首席执行官，甚至是重要的政治家。

paras.en: But the Australian researchers wanted to discover what was driving these differences.
paras.zh: 可澳大利亚的研究人员想弄清楚，是什么造成了这些差别。

paras.en: They suspected older, more mature students obtained more self-confidence than their peers because they achieved better grades.
paras.zh: 他们猜想，年龄大一些、更成熟的学生成绩更好，因此比同龄人更自信。

paras.en: To test this out, they conducted two studies.
paras.zh: 为了验证这一点，他们做了两项研究。

paras.en: One was with high school students and the other with more than a thousand Australian adults, aged between 24 and 60 years old.
paras.zh: 一项是针对高中生的，另一项是针对一千多名二十四到六十岁的澳大利亚成年人的。

paras.en: In the first study, more than 600 high school students were surveyed about their tendency to take risks and feel confident.
paras.zh: 在第一项研究中，研究人员就冒险倾向和自信程度对六百多名高中生做了调查。

paras.en: In the second study, those born on both sides of the cutoff date for starting school were asked to complete online math questions and rate their performance.
paras.zh: 在第二项研究中，出生日期在入学截止日期前后的人被要求在网上做数学题，并给自己的表现打分。

paras.en: They were also asked about the risks they took while riding bicycles and managing their finances.
paras.zh: 他们还被问到骑自行车和理财时冒过哪些风险。

paras.en: The researchers found that older students displayed greater risk-taking tendencies.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，年龄大一些的学生表现出更强的冒险倾向。

paras.en: While risk-taking can be considered a negative attribute, it’s also a characteristic of successful people, including athletes, political leaders, and entrepreneurs.
paras.zh: 虽然冒险可以看作一种负面特质，但它也是成功人士的一个特点，包括运动员、政治领袖和企业家。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: According to recent research conducted in Australia, what has a lasting impact on one’s life?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：根据澳大利亚最近开展的一项研究，什么会对人的一生产生持久的影响？

paras.en: Question 23: What was the purpose of the Australian research?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：这项澳大利亚研究的目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 24: Who were the participants in the researchers’ first study?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：研究人员第一项研究的参与者是谁？

paras.en: Question 25: According to the researchers, what is one characteristic of successful people?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：根据研究人员的说法，成功人士有什么特点？

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2023年6月大学英语四级 第1套
passages.name: 2023年6月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一名男子掀起马桶座圈时被一条四英尺长的蛇咬伤，蛇没有毒，被送到动物医院治疗，主人是谁还不清楚。第二篇新闻报道讲安德烈娅·贝尔彻受一位影星启发，每周盛装打扮去倒垃圾，视频在社交媒体上很受欢迎，也提醒了邻居按时把垃圾桶放出去。第三篇新闻报道讲弗兰克餐厅设立免费餐板，顾客付钱买餐券贴在板上，饿了的人可以取下来换饭吃。第一段长对话里，心理学家史蒂夫·平克解释朋友为什么会突然消失：这跟童年形成的依恋类型有关，缺乏安全感的人一有分歧就可能逃避。第二段长对话里，男士请要去日本的女士帮他买一条日本牛仔裤，说日本牛仔裤做工传统、布料好、经久耐穿。第一篇短文讲超级英雄电影情节老套、被精英看不起，却满足了人们对冒险的渴望，也能激励人。第二篇短文讲讲故事是领导者影响和激励他人的有力手段，能建立联系和信任、帮助学习。第三篇短文用统计数据说明美国移民更爱创业、负债更少，这和他们从家乡带来的价值观和习惯有关。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案，然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Police have reported a man being bitten by a four-foot snake when he lifted his toilet seat on Sunday morning.
paras.zh: 据警方通报，一名男子周日早上掀起马桶座圈时，被一条四英尺长的蛇咬了。

paras.en: The snake was not poisonous, so the man did not have to go to the hospital, but his arm was medically treated at the scene.
paras.zh: 这条蛇没有毒，所以男子不用去医院，不过他的手臂在现场接受了治疗。

paras.en: The police officer interviewed told news reporters the snake didn’t belong to the man and it was unclear how it got into the apartment.
paras.zh: 接受采访的警官告诉记者，这条蛇不是这名男子的，也不清楚它是怎么进到公寓里的。

paras.en: The snake was eventually captured by the local animal handlers and taken to an animal hospital afterward.
paras.zh: 这条蛇最后被当地的动物管理员抓住，之后被送到了一家动物医院。

paras.en: It was being treated for an outer skin infection.
paras.zh: 它正在接受皮肤外层感染的治疗。

paras.en: It was unclear who the owner was.
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚蛇的主人是谁。

paras.en: The snake may be taken to a local zoo for care, if the owner does not come forward.
paras.zh: 如果主人一直不出面，这条蛇可能会被送到当地的动物园照顾。

paras.en: Over the years other creatures like frogs and fish have found their way into toilets, but this was the first instance of a snake in recent years.
paras.zh: 这些年来，青蛙、鱼之类的动物也钻进过马桶，但这是近几年来第一次出现蛇。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn from the police report?
paras.zh: 第一题：从警方的通报中，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the report say was still unclear?
paras.zh: 第二题：报道说什么事情仍然不清楚？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Every week since last April, Andrea Belcher has been doing something slightly unusual and amusing when she takes out her trash.
paras.zh: 从去年四月起，安德烈娅·贝尔彻每周倒垃圾的时候，都会做一件有点不寻常、又很好玩的事。

paras.en: It all started off when a movie star shared a photo of herself putting her trash bins out in a ball gown.
paras.zh: 这件事起因是一位影星分享了一张自己穿着舞会礼服把垃圾桶放出去的照片。

paras.en: This inspired Andrea to get dressed up to take out the trash.
paras.zh: 这启发了安德烈娅，她也打扮起来去倒垃圾。

paras.en: She was too embarrassed to do it during the day, so one dark evening she put on her black off-the-shoulder gown and put her trash bin out.
paras.zh: 她不好意思白天这么做，于是在一个漆黑的晚上，穿上她那件黑色露肩礼服，把垃圾桶放了出去。

paras.en: Her daughter filmed it, and the whole family laughed.
paras.zh: 她女儿把这一幕拍了下来，全家人都笑了。

paras.en: But it seemed to go down well.
paras.zh: 没想到这件事很受欢迎。

paras.en: The following weeks she found other outfits in her dressing-up box, and dressed up as different characters and famous people, sharing her exploits on social media.
paras.zh: 接下来的几周，她又从自己的化装服装箱里找出别的服装，打扮成各种角色和名人，并在社交媒体上分享自己的这些趣事。

paras.en: Before long people started offering up their own fancy dresses for her to wear, and, before she knew it, she had done twenty weeks.
paras.zh: 没过多久，就有人拿出自己的化装礼服给她穿，不知不觉她已经坚持了二十周。

paras.en: Explaining why she has kept up the videos, Andrea explained how nice it was to have a little bit of fun and craziness that made people smile.
paras.zh: 说到为什么一直坚持拍视频，安德烈娅说，有点乐趣、来点疯狂、让大家笑一笑，这种感觉真好。

paras.en: Besides, it also helps to remind people in the community to put out their trash bins each week.
paras.zh: 另外，这也有助于提醒社区里的人每周把垃圾桶放出去。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What has Andrea Belcher been doing since last April?
paras.zh: 第三题：从去年四月起，安德烈娅·贝尔彻一直在做什么？

paras.en: Question four: Why has Andrea Belcher kept up her videos?
paras.zh: 第四题：安德烈娅·贝尔彻为什么一直坚持拍视频？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: No money but still hungry?
paras.zh: 没钱又饿了？

paras.en: No problem.
paras.zh: 没问题。

paras.en: Welcome to Frank’s Restaurant, where customers are paying for meals and leaving receipts on a board.
paras.zh: 欢迎来到弗兰克餐厅，在这里，顾客付钱买餐，把餐券贴在一块板上。

paras.en: Anyone who is hungry and wants something to eat can take one, no questions asked, and hand it to the staff for some food.
paras.zh: 任何饿了想吃东西的人都可以取一张，没人会多问，交给店员就能换到食物。

paras.en: The idea for the Board of Free Meals started after a donor came in with one hundred dollars for each member of its staff.
paras.zh: 免费餐板这个主意，源于一位捐赠者来店里给每位员工送了一百美元。

paras.en: After two staffers returned their share, there was seven hundred dollars left over, according to Tara Morris, the owner of the restaurant, so they decided to do something more by creating the board.
paras.zh: 据餐厅老板塔拉·莫里斯说，有两名员工把自己那份退了回来，于是剩下了七百美元，所以他们决定多做点事，设立了这块餐板。

paras.en: The board of free meals inside the restaurant shows a host of potential meals already paid for by customers, each costing about ten dollars.
paras.zh: 餐厅里的免费餐板上贴着许多顾客已经付了钱的餐，每份大约十美元。

paras.en: The Board has messages of kindness, like If you want more kindness in the world, put it here.
paras.zh: 板上还写着一些善意的话，比如“如果你想让世界上多一些善意，就把它放在这里”。

paras.en: The drive has been going on for two weeks, and Morris said just under fifty customers have picked up a free meal.
paras.zh: 这项活动已经进行了两周，莫里斯说，有将近五十名顾客领取了免费餐。

paras.en: There have been no reports of anyone taking advantage of the situation.
paras.zh: 目前还没有听说有人钻这个空子。

paras.en: In fact, there are a lot more people giving tickets than receiving.
paras.zh: 事实上，送餐券的人比领餐券的人多得多。

paras.en: It seems people want to help and are driven by helping others.
paras.zh: 看来大家都乐意帮忙，帮助别人就是他们的动力。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What can people do at Frank’s Restaurant?
paras.zh: 第五题：人们在弗兰克餐厅可以做什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the owner of the restaurant say about the idea for the board of free meals?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于免费餐板的主意，餐厅老板说了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What has happened at Frank’s restaurant since the Board of Free Meals was created?
paras.zh: 第七题：免费餐板设立以来，弗兰克餐厅发生了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Welcome to our program, Friends and Relationships.
paras.zh: 欢迎收听我们的节目《朋友与人际关系》。

paras.en: Our guest today is psychologist Steve Pinker from McGill University.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是麦吉尔大学的心理学家史蒂夫·平克。

paras.en: Glad to be here, Jane.
paras.zh: 很高兴来到这里，简。

paras.en: Hi, Steve.
paras.zh: 你好，史蒂夫。

paras.en: Our question today is why friends suddenly disappear?
paras.zh: 我们今天的问题是：朋友为什么会突然消失？

paras.en: They may block us on their social media accounts and stop responding to our emails.
paras.zh: 他们可能会在社交媒体账号上把我们拉黑，也不再回我们的邮件。

paras.en: They simply vanish without a trace.
paras.zh: 他们就这样消失得无影无踪。

paras.en: The answer may lie in childhood, the way the person related to their mum and dad.
paras.zh: 答案可能要从童年找起，看这个人跟爸爸妈妈是怎么相处的。

paras.en: It’s related to their attachment styles.
paras.zh: 这跟他们的依恋类型有关。

paras.en: Attachment styles?
paras.zh: 依恋类型？

paras.en: Yeah, there are two different attachment styles, an anxious attachment style and an avoidant attachment style.
paras.zh: 对，依恋类型有两种，一种是焦虑型依恋，一种是回避型依恋。

paras.en: When there is a relationship breakdown with their parents, children with an anxious attachment style scream and cry to get their parents to come back, but other children simply shut down and try to deal with their emotions by ignoring the situation.
paras.zh: 跟父母的关系破裂时，焦虑型依恋的孩子会又喊又哭，想让父母回来，而别的孩子干脆封闭自己，用不理会的办法来应对自己的情绪。

paras.en: And these attachment styles carry on into adulthood.
paras.zh: 而这些依恋类型会一直延续到成年。

paras.en: Does avoidance reduce their stress levels?
paras.zh: 回避能减轻他们的压力吗？

paras.en: Not really.
paras.zh: 不太会。

paras.en: Their stress levels are actually the same as those experienced by the children who yell and scream.
paras.zh: 他们的压力其实和那些又喊又叫的孩子一样大。

paras.en: And I assume both might be termed insecure.
paras.zh: 那我想这两种都可以说是缺乏安全感。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 一点没错。

paras.en: And it’s a very insecure attachment.
paras.zh: 这是一种很没有安全感的依恋。

paras.en: How does an insecure attachment affect relationships between friends, co-workers, and romantic relationships?
paras.zh: 缺乏安全感的依恋会怎样影响朋友之间、同事之间的关系，还有恋爱关系呢？

paras.en: It’s the same as conflicts.
paras.zh: 这跟处理冲突是一样的。

paras.en: So if you have a disagreement with a securely attached person, they’re not going to panic.
paras.zh: 所以，如果你跟一个有安全感的人意见不合，他不会慌。

paras.en: They’re able to hear what the other person is saying and express their own feelings and thoughts effectively.
paras.zh: 他能听进去对方说的话，也能有效地表达自己的感受和想法。

paras.en: However, an insecurely attached person won’t.
paras.zh: 可是缺乏安全感的人就做不到。

paras.en: They might either attack you, get defensive, or just disappear from your life.
paras.zh: 他们可能会攻击你、产生戒备，或者干脆从你的生活中消失。

paras.en: To them a difference, no matter how small in your eyes, signals the end of the relationship.
paras.zh: 在他们看来，一个分歧不管在你眼里有多小，都意味着这段关系结束了。

paras.en: That explains why they suddenly disappear.
paras.zh: 这就是他们为什么会突然消失。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What do we learn about the man?
paras.zh: 第八题：关于这位男士，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
paras.zh: 第九题：两位说话人主要在谈什么？

paras.en: Question 10: How do children with an anxious attachment style react to a breakdown in their relationship with parents?
paras.zh: 第十题：焦虑型依恋的孩子跟父母关系破裂时会有什么反应？

paras.en: Question eleven: What does the man say about insecurely attached people?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于缺乏安全感的人，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: I hear you’re going to Japan soon.
paras.zh: 听说你很快要去日本了。

paras.en: Yes, that’s right.
paras.zh: 对，没错。

paras.en: Could I ask you a favor?
paras.zh: 能请你帮个忙吗？

paras.en: Sure.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: What is it?
paras.zh: 什么事？

paras.en: I was wondering if you could get me some jeans while you’re there.
paras.zh: 我想问问，你在那边能不能帮我买条牛仔裤。

paras.en: I’ll pay you back, of course.
paras.zh: 当然，我会把钱还给你的。

paras.en: A pair of jeans?
paras.zh: 一条牛仔裤？

paras.en: Okay.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: I don’t see why not.
paras.zh: 我看没什么不可以的。

paras.en: But what’s wrong with jeans here?
paras.zh: 可是这里的牛仔裤有什么不好？

paras.en: Well, I just love good jeans, and Japan happens to make the best in the world.
paras.zh: 嗯，我就是喜欢好的牛仔裤，而日本恰好做得全世界最好。

paras.en: My friend brought me a pair from there five years ago, and they still look new.
paras.zh: 我朋友五年前从那边给我带回来一条，到现在看着还跟新的一样。

paras.en: Really, I had no idea Japan made jeans.
paras.zh: 真的吗？我都不知道日本还做牛仔裤。

paras.en: I would have thought America made the best jeans, because it’s a typical American garment.
paras.zh: 我还以为美国的牛仔裤最好，因为牛仔裤是典型的美国服装。

paras.en: Yeah, I thought so, too.
paras.zh: 是啊，我以前也是这么想的。

paras.en: But it turns out Japan still has some very old mills with the traditional weaving tools used to make jeans the original way.
paras.zh: 可是没想到，日本还有一些老工厂，用传统织布工具按最原始的方法做牛仔裤。

paras.en: It’s a slower process of making clothing, but the end result is surely superior.
paras.zh: 这种做衣服的方法慢一些，但最后做出来的东西肯定要好得多。

paras.en: Also, the fabric they use is of a higher quality, and the dyes are natural.
paras.zh: 而且他们用的布料质量更好，染料也是天然的。

paras.en: They have a denser weave and are more durable than any other jeans in the world.
paras.zh: 这种牛仔裤织得更密，比世界上任何别的牛仔裤都耐穿。

paras.en: That sounds cool.
paras.zh: 听起来很酷。

paras.en: What size do you want, and how much are they?
paras.zh: 你要多大号的，多少钱一条？

paras.en: I have a thirty four waist and size thirty or thirty two in length.
paras.zh: 我腰围三十四，裤长三十或者三十二号。

paras.en: Either is fine.
paras.zh: 哪个都行。

w.m: pron. 两者之一；任何一个

paras.en: They should be around five hundred dollars, but make double certain they are made in Japan.
paras.zh: 大概五百美元左右，不过一定要再三确认是日本产的。

paras.en: Five hundred dollars?
paras.zh: 五百美元？

paras.en: Boy, that’s expensive.
paras.zh: 天哪，真贵。

paras.en: Do you typically spend that much on a pair of casual trousers?
paras.zh: 你平常买一条休闲裤也花这么多钱吗？

paras.en: They are a little pricey, yes, but they are very special.
paras.zh: 是有点贵，没错，可它们很特别。

paras.en: Bear in mind they will last me several years, and they are very fashionable too.
paras.zh: 要知道，它们能穿好几年，而且也很时髦。

paras.en: I think they’re totally worth it.
paras.zh: 我觉得完全值。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What makes the man choose to buy jeans made in Japan?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士为什么要买日本产的牛仔裤？

paras.en: Question thirteen: Why is the woman puzzled by the man’s request?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士为什么对男士的请求感到不解？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the man say about the dyes of Japanese jeans?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于日本牛仔裤的染料，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the man say about Japanese jeans at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：对话最后，男士对日本牛仔裤是怎么说的？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从四个选项中选出最佳答案，选项标有A、B、C、D。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet One with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Every time I walk out of a superhero movie I feel the same way.
paras.zh: 每次看完超级英雄电影走出影院，我都有同样的感觉。

paras.en: I experience a sense of longing, realizing that there should be more in life.
paras.zh: 我会感到一种渴望，意识到生活中应该有更多的东西。

paras.en: The desire for adventure is a human one.
paras.zh: 对冒险的渴望是人类共有的。

paras.en: Superhero films capture this desire perfectly.
paras.zh: 超级英雄电影把这种渴望抓得恰到好处。

w.m: adv. 完美地；恰到好处地

paras.en: The plot of each superhero film has become relatively predictable.
paras.zh: 每部超级英雄电影的情节都已经变得比较好猜了。

paras.en: The world is in peril.
paras.zh: 世界陷入危险。

paras.en: The world needs a hero.
paras.zh: 世界需要一位英雄。

paras.en: The hero is in peril.
paras.zh: 英雄陷入危险。

paras.en: The hero resolves the peril.
paras.zh: 英雄化解危险。

paras.en: The hero saves the world.
paras.zh: 英雄拯救世界。

paras.en: Each film has an attractive lead, several expensive explosions, a few jokes to lighten the mood, and numerous punches that land unrealistically well.
paras.zh: 每部电影都有一个有魅力的主角、几场烧钱的爆炸、几个缓和气氛的笑话，还有很多拳拳到肉、假得离谱的打斗。

w.m: adj. 有吸引力的；有魅力的
adv. 不真实地；不切实际地

paras.en: Even though we basically know what will happen, we keep coming back for more.
paras.zh: 虽然我们基本上知道会发生什么，可还是一次次回来看。

paras.en: The elites of our society have rejected superhero films.
paras.zh: 社会上的精英们一向排斥超级英雄电影。

paras.en: They say the films lack any form of artistry.
paras.zh: 他们说这些电影毫无艺术性可言。

paras.en: These movies are criticized as being too simple, but they give the fans what they want: entertainment.
paras.zh: 这些电影被批评太简单，可它们给了影迷想要的东西：娱乐。

paras.en: No matter the form in which they reveal themselves, hero stories will always be present in life.
paras.zh: 不管以什么形式出现，英雄故事永远会存在于生活中。

paras.en: It’s not just about being entertained, but also being inspired.
paras.zh: 这不只是为了娱乐，也是为了受到激励。

paras.en: One author has mentioned that women desire to play an irreplaceable role in a great adventure.
paras.zh: 一位作家说过，女性渴望在一场伟大的冒险中扮演不可替代的角色。

paras.en: Most young women want to be a part of something grand, something important.
paras.zh: 大多数年轻女性都想成为某件宏大、重要的事的一部分。

paras.en: It seems clear that this principle applies to men as well.
paras.zh: 这个道理显然也适用于男性。

paras.en: So next time you see your favorite superhero film, be entertained, but also be inspired.
paras.zh: 所以下次你看你最喜欢的超级英雄电影时，既要享受娱乐，也要受到激励。

paras.en: Let that small longing you feel motivate you to make a difference.
paras.zh: 让你心里那点小小的渴望激励你去做出改变。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: How does the speaker feel every time he walks out of a superhero movie?
paras.zh: 第十六题：每次看完超级英雄电影走出影院，说话人有什么感觉？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What does the passage say about the plot of all superhero movies?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于所有超级英雄电影的情节，短文是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 18: What do the elites of American society think of superhero movies?
paras.zh: 第十八题：美国社会的精英怎么看超级英雄电影？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Telling stories is one of the most powerful means leaders have to influence, teach, and inspire.
paras.zh: 讲故事是领导者影响、教导和激励他人最有力的手段之一。

paras.en: Storytelling forges connections among people.
paras.zh: 讲故事能在人与人之间建立联系。

paras.en: When it comes to our countries, our communities, and our families, we understand instinctively that the stories we hold in common are an important part of the ties that bind.
paras.zh: 说到我们的国家、社区和家庭，我们凭直觉就明白，大家共有的故事是把我们联结在一起的纽带中很重要的一部分。

w.m: v. 捆绑；把……联结在一起

paras.en: This understanding also holds true in the business world, where an organization’s stories and the stories its leaders tell help solidify relationships in a way that factual statements don’t.
paras.zh: 这个道理在商界同样适用：一家机构的故事以及它的领导者讲的故事，能以陈述事实做不到的方式巩固关系。

paras.en: Good stories do more than create a sense of connection.
paras.zh: 好故事的作用不只是让人有联系的感觉。

paras.en: They build familiarity and trust.
paras.zh: 它们能建立熟悉感和信任。

paras.en: They allow the listener to enter the story, making them more open to learning.
paras.zh: 它们让听的人走进故事里，因而更愿意学习。

paras.en: Good stories can contain multiple meanings so they’re surprisingly economical in conveying complex ideas in graspable ways.
paras.zh: 好故事可以包含多层含义，所以用容易理解的方式传达复杂的道理时，出奇地简洁高效。

w.m: adj. 节约的；简洁高效的
adj. 可理解的；能掌握的

paras.en: And stories are more engaging than the recital of data points or a discussion of abstract ideas.
paras.zh: 而且故事比罗列一个个数据、讨论抽象的道理更吸引人。

paras.en: Stories about professional mistakes and what leaders learned from them are another great avenue for learning.
paras.zh: 讲职业上犯的错，以及领导者从中学到了什么，这类故事也是学习的好途径。

paras.en: Because people identify so closely with stories, they can imagine how they would have acted in similar circumstances.
paras.zh: 因为人们很容易把自己代入故事，所以能想象自己在类似的情况下会怎么做。

paras.en: They’re able to work through situations in a way that’s risk-free.
paras.zh: 他们能毫无风险地把各种情况想清楚、处理好。

paras.en: There are extra benefits for leaders.
paras.zh: 对领导者来说，还有额外的好处。

paras.en: With a simple personal story they can convey fundamental values.
paras.zh: 用一个简单的个人故事，他们就能传达基本的价值观。

paras.en: They can offer insight into the evolution of their own experience and knowledge, presenting themselves as more approachable, and then they are more likely to inspire others to want to know more.
paras.zh: 他们还能让人了解自己的经验和知识是怎样一步步积累起来的，显得更平易近人，这样也更有可能激励别人想去了解更多。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What does the passage say about storytelling?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于讲故事，短文是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 20: What can good stories do to listeners according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第二十题：根据短文，好故事能给听的人带来什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What can leaders do with a simple personal story?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：领导者用一个简单的个人故事能做什么？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: The US was founded by successive waves of immigrants, and immigrants are still contributing to America today.
paras.zh: 美国是由一批又一批移民建立的，直到今天，移民仍在为美国作贡献。

paras.en: Statistics prove it.
paras.zh: 统计数据证明了这一点。

paras.en: On two key measures of financial performance, immigrants outperform native-born Americans.
paras.zh: 在衡量经济表现的两个关键指标上，移民都胜过在美国本土出生的人。

paras.en: First, they’re more likely to be entrepreneurs.
paras.zh: 首先，他们更有可能成为企业家。

paras.en: From nineteen ninety six to twenty sixteen, the pace at which immigrants started businesses was double that of US-born individuals.
paras.zh: 从一九九六年到二〇一六年，移民创业的速度是美国本土出生的人的两倍。

paras.en: Immigrants aren’t just becoming entrepreneurs more frequently, they’re often succeeding.
paras.zh: 移民不只是更常成为企业家，他们往往还很成功。

paras.en: Over forty percent of Fortune five hundred companies had a founder who was either an immigrant or the child of one.
paras.zh: 《财富》五百强企业中，有百分之四十以上的创始人是移民或者移民的子女。

paras.en: Another key measure of financial strength is debt level.
paras.zh: 衡量经济实力的另一个关键指标是负债水平。

paras.en: Immigrants do better in this area too.
paras.zh: 在这方面移民也做得更好。

paras.en: Immigrants use credit less often for purchasing cars, homes, or starting businesses.
paras.zh: 移民买车、买房或者创业时，较少用信贷。

paras.en: This results in significantly lower levels of debt than native-born Americans.
paras.zh: 因此，他们的负债水平明显比美国本土出生的人低。

paras.en: For example, thirty four per cent of Americans born in Latin America report no credit card or instalment loan debt.
paras.zh: 比如，在拉丁美洲出生的美国人中，有百分之三十四说自己没有信用卡债务或分期贷款债务。

paras.en: This can be compared to just nineteen per cent of the general population.
paras.zh: 相比之下，在总人口中这一比例只有百分之十九。

paras.en: Why are immigrants doing so well?
paras.zh: 移民为什么做得这么好？

paras.en: The values and habits they bring from their own homelands help explain some of the success.
paras.zh: 他们从自己家乡带来的价值观和习惯，能部分解释他们的成功。

paras.en: Unemployment tends to be higher in developing countries.
paras.zh: 在发展中国家，失业率往往更高。

paras.en: That means more people must become entrepreneurs.
paras.zh: 这就意味着更多人只能去当企业家。

paras.en: Credit is also scarcer in most developing countries.
paras.zh: 在大多数发展中国家，信贷也更难获得。

paras.en: This means individuals must save more in order to achieve their goals, or they borrow money from friends and family rather than a bank.
paras.zh: 这就意味着人们必须多存钱才能实现自己的目标，或者向亲朋好友借钱，而不是向银行借。

paras.en: That means less debt and potentially better credit outcomes when they reach the US.
paras.zh: 这就意味着他们来到美国后负债更少，信用状况也可能更好。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the passage say statistics prove?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：短文说统计数据证明了什么？

paras.en: Question twenty three: What do we learn about immigrants in the US compared with native-born Americans?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：和美国本土出生的人相比，我们对美国的移民有什么了解？

paras.en: Question twenty four: What does the passage say about immigrants in the US in terms of financial strength?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于美国移民的经济实力，短文是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 25: What do immigrants do to achieve their goals in the U.S.?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：在美国，移民为了实现目标会怎么做？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2023年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2023年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲美国罗得岛州一名五十五岁的女子因涉嫌违反禁止喂养野生动物的规定被起诉，邻居怪她让当地的鼠患更严重了，她说自己只是在喂鸟。第二篇新闻报道讲美国国家航空航天局招募四名志愿者，在休斯敦一处模拟火星的居住舱里生活一年，为将来送宇航员上火星做准备，并介绍了报名条件。第三篇新闻报道讲日本名古屋市长河村隆之当众咬了垒球运动员后藤希友的奥运金牌，引来大量投诉，他公开道歉。第一段长对话里，两人谈到防蓝光贴膜：蓝光本身不一定有害，但电子设备的蓝光太多会影响视力和睡眠，而睡不好会带来各种健康问题。第二段长对话里，两人都讨厌大人总问孩子“长大想做什么”，认为这种问法只会带来不切实际的期望，大人应该帮孩子认识自己。第一篇短文讲非洲农村上网难，KaiOS 公司推出只要二十美元的简易智能手机，帮助缩小数字鸿沟。第二篇短文讲再生塑料现在比新塑料贵，英国政府打算征税并采取措施增加再生塑料的使用。第三篇短文讲曼哈顿一家卖午睡时间的店，作者认为午睡能让人精力加倍，值得花钱。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案，然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A woman was charged with allegedly violating a Rhode Island city law against feeding wild animals.
paras.zh: 一名女子被指控涉嫌违反罗得岛州一座城市禁止喂养野生动物的法规。

paras.en: The fifty-five-year-old woman’s neighbors blame her for making the area’s rat problem worse.
paras.zh: 这名五十五岁女子的邻居们怪她让这一带的鼠患变得更严重了。

paras.en: Newly installed cameras captured several rats active in the middle of the day.
paras.zh: 新装的摄像头拍到好几只老鼠大中午就在外面活动。

paras.en: Neighbors say that it’s even worse during the night.
paras.zh: 邻居们说，夜里情况更糟。

paras.en: The woman and her parents, who own the home, told reporters that she’s being charged for feeding birds.
paras.zh: 这名女子和她父母（房子是她父母的）告诉记者，她被起诉是因为喂鸟。

paras.en: Who would have known just loving animals gets you that much trouble?
paras.zh: 谁能想到，只是喜欢动物也会惹上这么大的麻烦？

paras.en: she said.
paras.zh: 她说。

paras.en: It is prohibited to feed any wild animals, including birds, in Rhode Island City.
paras.zh: 罗得岛州这座城市禁止喂养任何野生动物，包括鸟类。

paras.en: Nevertheless, while the woman’s intention was to feed birds, it is clear that rats were also benefiting.
paras.zh: 不过，虽说这名女子本意是喂鸟，但老鼠显然也跟着得了好处。

paras.en: Anthony Moretti, director of the city administration, said he saw more than twenty rats near the woman’s home.
paras.zh: 市政管理部门负责人安东尼·莫雷蒂说，他在这名女子家附近看到了二十多只老鼠。

w.m: n. 管理部门；行政机构

paras.en: He said it will take months to get the problem under control.
paras.zh: 他说，要把这个问题控制住得花好几个月。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn from the report about the fifty-five-year-old woman?
paras.zh: 第一题：从报道中，我们对这名五十五岁的女子了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What did the director of the city administration say at the end of the news report?
paras.zh: 第二题：在新闻报道的最后，市政管理部门负责人说了什么？

w.m: n. 管理部门；行政机构

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: To prepare for eventually sending astronauts to Mars, NASA began taking applications Friday for four people to live for a year in Mars Dune Alpha.
paras.zh: 为将来送宇航员上火星做准备，美国国家航空航天局周五开始接受报名，招募四个人在“火星沙丘阿尔法”里生活一年。

paras.en: That’s a 1,700-square-foot Martian habitat inside a building in Houston.
paras.zh: 那是休斯敦一栋楼里一处一千七百平方英尺的火星模拟居住舱。

paras.en: The paid volunteers will work in an environment similar to Mars.
paras.zh: 这些有报酬的志愿者将在类似火星的环境里工作。

paras.en: They will have limited communications with family, restricted food and resources.
paras.zh: 他们和家人的联系会受到限制，食物和各种物资也有限。

paras.en: NASA is planning three experiments with the first one starting in the fall next year.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局计划进行三次实验，第一次明年秋天开始。

paras.en: Food will all be ready-to-eat space food.
paras.zh: 食物方面，全都是即食的太空食品。

paras.en: Some plants will be grown, but not potatoes like in the movie The Martian.
paras.zh: 会种一些植物，但不会像电影《火星救援》里那样种土豆。

paras.en: We want to understand how humans perform in them, said lead scientist Grace Douglas.
paras.zh: 首席科学家格雷丝·道格拉斯说：“我们想了解人在这种环境里的表现。”

paras.en: We’re looking at Mars-realistic situations.
paras.zh: 我们研究的是贴近火星真实情况的各种处境。

w.m: adj. 贴近火星真实情况的

paras.en: The application process opened Friday and they’re not seeking just anybody.
paras.zh: 报名周五开始，他们可不是随便什么人都要。

paras.en: The requirements are strict, including a master’s degree in a science, engineering or math field or pilot experience.
paras.zh: 条件很严格，包括要有理科、工程或数学领域的硕士学位，或者有飞行员经验。

paras.en: Only American citizens or permanent US residents are acceptable.
paras.zh: 只接受美国公民或美国永久居民。

paras.en: Applicants must be between thirty and fifty five and in good physical health.
paras.zh: 报名者年龄要在三十到五十五岁之间，身体健康。

paras.en: Attitude is key, said former Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield.
paras.zh: 加拿大前宇航员克里斯·哈德菲尔德说，态度是关键。

paras.en: He said that participants need to be super competent, resourceful and not rely on other people to feel comfortable.
paras.zh: 他说，参与者必须能力超强、会想办法，而且不靠别人也能过得自在。

w.m: adj. 足智多谋的；会想办法的

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What does NASA require the paid volunteers to do?
paras.zh: 第三题：美国国家航空航天局要求这些有报酬的志愿者做什么？

paras.en: Question four: What will the participants in the project eat?
paras.zh: 第四题：这个项目的参与者会吃什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A Japanese mayor apologized Thursday for biting the Olympic gold medal of a softball player.
paras.zh: 日本一位市长周四道歉，因为他咬了一名垒球运动员的奥运金牌。

paras.en: Nagoya mayor Takashi Kawamura had praised athlete Miyo Goto during a public media event.
paras.zh: 名古屋市长河村隆之在一场公开的媒体活动上夸奖了运动员后藤希友。

paras.en: He asked her to put the medal around his neck.
paras.zh: 他让她把奖牌挂到他的脖子上。

paras.en: Kawamura then bit into it.
paras.zh: 接着河村隆之就咬了一口。

paras.en: Biting a medal in front of journalists and photographers has become a common pose for Olympic medalists.
paras.zh: 当着记者和摄影师的面咬奖牌，已经成了奥运奖牌得主常摆的姿势。

paras.en: However, it is only for the winners themselves, not others.
paras.zh: 不过，这个动作只属于获奖者本人，别人不能做。

paras.en: I’m really sorry that I hurt the treasure of the gold medalist, Kawamura told reporters Thursday.
paras.zh: 河村隆之周四对记者说：“我伤害了金牌得主的宝贝，真的很抱歉。”

paras.en: The mayor said the medal was undamaged, though he offered to pay for the cost of a new one.
paras.zh: 市长说奖牌没有损坏，不过他还是提出由他出钱换一块新的。

paras.en: Goto, however, has accepted the International Olympic Committee’s offer of a replacement, according to Japanese media reports.
paras.zh: 不过据日本媒体报道，后藤希友已经接受了国际奥委会提出的换一块新奖牌的提议。

paras.en: The scene, broadcast on television, prompted thousands of complaints to City Hall.
paras.zh: 这一幕在电视上播出后，市政厅收到了上千条投诉。

paras.en: Some Olympians said they treat their medals as treasures and that it was disrespectful and unacceptable for Kawamura to bite one.
paras.zh: 一些奥运选手说，他们把奖牌当成宝贝，河村隆之去咬奖牌是不尊重人的，让人无法接受。

paras.en: I would cry if that happened to me, said another athlete, Naohisa Takato.
paras.zh: “这事要是发生在我身上，我会哭的。”另一名运动员高藤直寿说。

paras.en: I handle my own gold medal so gently that I would not scratch it.
paras.zh: “我拿自己的金牌时都非常小心，从来不会刮到它。”

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the news report say about the Japanese mayor Takashi Kawamura?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于日本名古屋市长河村隆之，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What did Mayor Takashi Kawamura offer to do?
paras.zh: 第六题：河村隆之市长提出要做什么？

paras.en: Question 7: What did some Olympians say they would do with their medals?
paras.zh: 第七题：一些奥运选手说，他们会怎么对待自己的奖牌？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: What’s that orange thing on your computer screen?
paras.zh: 你电脑屏幕上那个橙色的东西是什么？

paras.en: It’s something I bought yesterday.
paras.zh: 是我昨天买的。

paras.en: It’s a plastic sheet that blocks blue light.
paras.zh: 是一张防蓝光的塑料膜。

paras.en: I have one that I use to cover my phone screen, too.
paras.zh: 我还有一张贴在手机屏幕上。

paras.en: What do you mean by blue light?
paras.zh: 你说的蓝光是什么意思？

paras.en: Blue light includes natural light, but it also includes light that isn’t natural, for example, from computers, phones, televisions, and other electronic devices.
paras.zh: 蓝光包括自然光，但也包括不是自然产生的光，比如电脑、手机、电视和其他电子设备发出的光。

paras.en: So blue light is harmful and that’s why you want to block it?
paras.zh: 那么蓝光是有害的，所以你才要把它挡住？

paras.en: It isn’t that simple.
paras.zh: 没那么简单。

paras.en: Blue light isn’t necessarily bad for us.
paras.zh: 蓝光对我们不一定有坏处。

paras.en: In fact we need blue light during the day to be healthy.
paras.zh: 事实上，白天我们需要蓝光才能保持健康。

paras.en: But too much blue light, especially from electronic devices, can harm our health by weakening our vision and making it harder for us to fall asleep.
paras.zh: 但蓝光太多，尤其是电子设备发出的蓝光，会损害我们的视力，让我们更难入睡，从而危害健康。

paras.en: And poor sleep can cause all sorts of health problems.
paras.zh: 而睡不好会引起各种各样的健康问题。

paras.en: I’m not so sure that sleep is nearly as important as people always say it is.
paras.zh: 我倒不太相信睡眠真有大家常说的那么重要。

paras.en: I haven’t slept enough in months because I have too much work to do.
paras.zh: 好几个月我都没睡够了，因为要干的活太多。

paras.en: And I feel fine.
paras.zh: 可我感觉挺好的。

paras.en: And it’s the same for most of my friends.
paras.zh: 我大多数朋友也是这样。

paras.en: Poor sleep might be a problem for older people, but surely young people can handle late nights.
paras.zh: 睡不好对年纪大的人也许是个问题，可年轻人肯定扛得住熬夜。

paras.en: Well, the research I’ve read shows that sleep is probably even more important than we thought, and that not having enough sleep can contribute to serious health problems, like obesity and heart disease.
paras.zh: 嗯，我读过的研究表明，睡眠可能比我们以为的还要重要，睡眠不足会导致严重的健康问题，比如肥胖和心脏病。

paras.en: And all the artificial blue light from electronic devices means we have to try harder to sleep well.
paras.zh: 再加上电子设备发出的各种人造蓝光，我们就得更加努力才能睡个好觉。

paras.en: Maybe you’re right.
paras.zh: 也许你说得对。

paras.en: I’m on my computer very late most nights, and that’s probably why I don’t sleep enough.
paras.zh: 我大多数晚上都在电脑前待到很晚，可能这就是我睡不够的原因。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What did the woman do to her computer?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士对她的电脑做了什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman say about blue light?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于蓝光，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: Why does the man say he hasn’t slept enough for months?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士说他为什么好几个月都没睡够？

paras.en: Question 11: What has the woman learned from the research she has read?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士从她读过的研究中了解到什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: As a kid, did you know what job you wanted to do when you grew up?
paras.zh: 你小时候知道自己长大想做什么工作吗？

paras.en: No, I didn’t.
paras.zh: 不知道。

paras.en: And I got sick every time adults asked me what I wanted to be when I grew up.
paras.zh: 每次大人问我长大想当什么，我都烦透了。

paras.en: It’s the same with me.
paras.zh: 我也是。

paras.en: And I’m tired of people asking that question of my ten-year-old daughter.
paras.zh: 现在别人老拿这个问题问我十岁的女儿，我也烦了。

paras.en: My daughter’s stock answers are basketball player, pop singer, mechanical engineer.
paras.zh: 我女儿的标准答案是篮球运动员、流行歌手、机械工程师。

paras.en: Adults love that last one, as it’s the perfect mix of the sensible and the ambitious.
paras.zh: 大人们最爱听最后那个，因为它把务实和远大志向结合得恰到好处。

w.m: adj. 有抱负的；有雄心的

paras.en: When she was much younger, my daughter used to say she wanted to be queen of the clouds, which I loved.
paras.zh: 她小时候常说想当云朵女王，我很喜欢这个说法。

paras.en: That’s the kind of goal setting I like to see in children, springing from their boundless imaginations.
paras.zh: 我就喜欢孩子们这样定目标，全凭他们无边无际的想象力。

w.m: adj. 无限的；无边无际的

paras.en: Yes, we grown-ups can be tedious and limiting in our need for reality, and we teach a very gloomy image of adulthood that whatever our children’s future holds, it must be seen within the context of a job.
paras.zh: 是啊，我们大人一心讲现实，可能会很乏味、很死板，我们还给孩子描绘了一幅很灰暗的成年图景：不管孩子将来怎样，都得放在一份工作里来看。

w.m: adj. 阴暗的；令人沮丧的

paras.en: How utterly overwhelming and dull.
paras.zh: 这实在太让人喘不过气，也太无聊了。

paras.en: When people ask my son what he wants to be when he grows up, I have to swallow the urge to say Hey, back off my kids’ dreams.
paras.zh: 别人问我儿子长大想当什么的时候，我都得忍住冲动，才没说出：“喂，别管我孩子的梦想。”

paras.en: We can’t dismiss the idea that teenagers have to plan to do something after they finish school, and parents are entitled to hope it’s more than simply spending ten hours a day playing computer games.
paras.zh: 我们不能否认，青少年毕业后得有个打算，父母也有理由希望孩子不只是每天花十个小时打电脑游戏。

paras.en: But asking “What do you want to be?”
paras.zh: 可是问孩子“你长大想做什么？”，

paras.en: isn’t going to lead a child to a fulfilled life.
paras.zh: 并不能让孩子过上充实的人生。

paras.en: Rather, it leads to false expectations and a high chance of disappointment.
paras.zh: 相反，这只会带来不切实际的期望，很可能还会让孩子失望。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 一点没错。

paras.en: We should be helping our kids understand who they are, even if that means letting go of who we think they should be.
paras.zh: 我们应该帮孩子弄清楚自己是什么样的人，哪怕这意味着要放下我们认为他们应该成为的样子。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What question were both speakers fed up with when they were kids?
paras.zh: 第十二题：两位说话人小时候都烦透了哪个问题？

paras.en: Question 13: What occupation do adults see as both sensible and ambitious, according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第十三题：在女士看来，大人们认为哪种职业既务实又有抱负？

w.m: adj. 有抱负的；有雄心的

paras.en: Question 14: What kind of goal setting does the woman like to see in children?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士喜欢看到孩子们怎样定目标？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the woman suggest adults should do?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士建议大人应该怎么做？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1, with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Greater internet access correlates directly with improved health care, education and economic development.
paras.zh: 互联网越普及，医疗、教育和经济发展就越好，二者直接相关。

paras.en: People living in rural areas, however, lag behind in online use, which limits their access to government services, banking and job opportunities.
paras.zh: 然而，住在农村地区的人上网比别人少，这限制了他们享受政府服务、银行服务和找工作的机会。

paras.en: Nowhere is this challenge clearer than in Africa.
paras.zh: 这个难题在非洲最为突出。

paras.en: Most Africans live in rural areas that are tough to wire for Internet access.
paras.zh: 大多数非洲人住在农村，那里很难铺设网线、接入互联网。

paras.en: Now, some phone companies are trying to introduce Internet-ready phones into African markets.
paras.zh: 现在，一些手机公司正努力把能上网的手机引入非洲市场。

paras.en: Certain companies have started selling simple smartphones for only $20.
paras.zh: 有些公司已经开始卖只要二十美元的简易智能手机。

paras.en: Previously, the lowest price had been around $40, well out of reach for many people.
paras.zh: 以前最低价格大约是四十美元，很多人根本买不起。

paras.en: These devices are powered by software from the giant electronics company KaiOS Technologies Limited.
paras.zh: 这些手机用的是电子巨头KaiOS科技有限公司的软件。

w.m: n. 电子产品；电子技术

paras.en: Most companies are trying to make phones ever more powerful and capable, but KaiOS went the other way.
paras.zh: 大多数公司都在想办法让手机性能越来越强、功能越来越多，KaiOS却反其道而行之。

w.m: adj. 有能力的；功能强的

paras.en: It made every effort to keep the essential capabilities of smartphones but strip out costs and preserve battery life for people who likely have inadequate access to electricity.
paras.zh: 它尽一切努力保留智能手机必不可少的功能，同时降低成本、延长电池续航时间，因为它的用户很可能用不上足够的电。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；极其重要的

paras.en: The KaiOS devices offer an alternative to the more expensive models that remain out of reach of many Africans and contribute to the digital divide.
paras.zh: KaiOS手机给了人们另一种选择：更贵的机型很多非洲人仍然买不起，加深了数字鸿沟。

w.m: n. 替代品；另一种选择

paras.en: The body of KaiOS phones is as basic as it gets.
paras.zh: KaiOS手机的机身要多简单有多简单。

paras.en: Instead of a touch screen, they’re controlled with an old-school keypad.
paras.zh: 它们没有触摸屏，而是用老式键盘来操作。

paras.en: They’re designed for 3G networks because 4G coverage doesn’t reach two thirds of Africa’s customers.
paras.zh: 它们是为三G网络设计的，因为四G网络覆盖不到三分之二的非洲用户。

paras.en: In total, KaiOS phones are made from about fifteen dollars worth of parts, while Apple’s top-of-the-line iPhone has three hundred and ninety dollars worth of stuff.
paras.zh: 总的算下来，KaiOS手机的零件只值大约十五美元，而苹果的顶配iPhone里的东西值三百九十美元。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What are a number of phone companies trying to do in Africa?
paras.zh: 第十六题：一些手机公司正努力在非洲做什么？

paras.en: Question 17: How do KaiOS smartphones differ from smartphones of most other companies?
paras.zh: 第十七题：KaiOS智能手机和其他大多数公司的智能手机有什么不同？

paras.en: Question eighteen: What are KaiOS smartphones equipped with?
paras.zh: 第十八题：KaiOS智能手机配的是什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: For years using recycled plastic to make plastic products was cheap.
paras.zh: 多年来，用再生塑料做塑料产品很便宜。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: By contrast, fossil fuel plastic was more expensive.
paras.zh: 相比之下，用化石燃料做的塑料更贵。

paras.en: Thus the sustainable option was an economic option too.
paras.zh: 所以，环保的选择同时也是省钱的选择。

paras.en: But now it is cheaper for major manufacturers to use new plastic.
paras.zh: 可是现在，大厂商用新塑料反倒更便宜。

paras.en: According to one recent business report, recycled plastic now costs an extra seventy two dollars a ton compared with newly made plastic.
paras.zh: 据最近一份商业报告，现在再生塑料每吨比新生产的塑料贵七十二美元。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: This may be because of consumer demands.
paras.zh: 这可能是消费者的需求造成的。

paras.en: They are pushing for more recycled plastics in new products.
paras.zh: 他们要求新产品里多用再生塑料。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: Meanwhile, new plastic is becoming cheaper.
paras.zh: 与此同时，新塑料越来越便宜。

paras.en: This is because of a boom in petroleum chemical production from the US.
paras.zh: 这是因为美国的石油化工生产正在蓬勃发展。

paras.en: The price increase of recycled plastic could cost sustainable manufacturers an extra two hundred fifty million dollars a year.
paras.zh: 再生塑料涨价，可能会让环保厂商每年多花两亿五千万美元。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: Smaller manufacturers may also be forced to use new plastic to reduce costs.
paras.zh: 小一些的厂商可能也会被迫用新塑料来降低成本。

paras.en: Makers of clear plastic bottles may also opt for new fossil-fuel-based plastic to save money.
paras.zh: 生产透明塑料瓶的厂家可能也会为了省钱，选用以化石燃料为原料的新塑料。

w.m: adj. 以化石燃料为原料的

paras.en: Plastic packaging makers are being pressured to use more recycled plastic.
paras.zh: 塑料包装厂家正受到压力，被要求多用再生塑料。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: This is done in hopes of reducing the enormous amount of plastic pollution in the oceans.
paras.zh: 这样做是希望减少海洋里大量的塑料污染。

paras.en: The UK Government plans to tax companies which don’t use at least thirty per cent recycled plastic in their products.
paras.zh: 英国政府计划对产品中再生塑料用量不到百分之三十的公司征税。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: Additionally, the Government is planning to increase the quantity of recycled plastic in the market.
paras.zh: 此外，政府还计划增加市场上再生塑料的数量。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: This could mean incentives for new recycling plants.
paras.zh: 这可能意味着为新建的回收厂提供激励。

paras.en: Additionally, recycling facilities may be improved at a local council level and recycled plastic could be imported.
paras.zh: 此外，地方议会也可能改善回收设施，还可能进口再生塑料。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: This would help increase the amount of recycled plastic in circulation.
paras.zh: 这将有助于增加流通中的再生塑料数量。

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What is said about using recycled plastic to make plastic products in the past?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于过去用再生塑料做塑料产品，短文是怎么说的？

w.m: adj. 回收利用的；再生的

paras.en: Question 20: What has led to a more competitive price for new plastic?
paras.zh: 第二十题：是什么让新塑料的价格更有竞争力？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the UK government plan to do about plastic?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于塑料，英国政府打算做什么？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: At the Dreamery, a business in Manhattan, naps are for sale.
paras.zh: 在曼哈顿一家叫“梦乡馆”的店里，可以花钱买午睡。

paras.en: A forty-five-minute session in a darkened enclosure with peace and quiet costs twenty five dollars.
paras.zh: 在一个光线昏暗、安安静静的小隔间里睡四十五分钟，要二十五美元。

w.m: n. 隔间；围起来的地方

paras.en: To be clear, this institution is no hotel.
paras.zh: 说清楚一点，这个地方可不是旅馆。

paras.en: This is a nap joint.
paras.zh: 这是一家午睡店。

paras.en: It sells the idea of the nap as much as the nap itself.
paras.zh: 它卖的是午睡这个理念，也是午睡本身。

paras.en: Is a nap worth twenty five dollars?
paras.zh: 午睡一次值二十五美元吗？

paras.en: The answer is obviously yes.
paras.zh: 答案显然是值。

paras.en: Here at this point in the argument, it’s traditional for me to bring up all the studies that show the benefits of napping.
paras.zh: 讨论到这里，按惯例我该把那些证明午睡有好处的研究统统搬出来了。

paras.en: But do you really need experts to tell you that?
paras.zh: 可这还用专家来告诉你吗？

paras.en: Just look at the world around you at two thirty in the afternoon.
paras.zh: 下午两点半的时候，看看你周围的世界就知道了。

paras.en: I’ve been working from home for more than ten years now, and the quality and quantity of work I can do emerges directly from my ability to concentrate.
paras.zh: 我在家办公已经十多年了，我能干多少活、活干得好不好，直接取决于我能不能集中精力。

paras.en: I don’t understand how people have creative careers without napping.
paras.zh: 我不明白，有些人不午睡，怎么能干好创造性的工作。

paras.en: Every day at about 1pm everyone faces the same choice, sleep until 2pm and then work until 5, or daydream and drift around social media and attend pointless meetings until 7pm.
paras.zh: 每天下午一点左右，每个人都面临同样的选择：要么睡到两点，然后工作到五点；要么做白日梦、刷社交媒体、参加毫无意义的会议，一直耗到晚上七点。

paras.en: The friends I have who still work in offices inform me their bosses insist that they take the second option and that napping is associated with laziness.
paras.zh: 我那些还在坐办公室的朋友告诉我，他们的老板坚持要他们选第二种，还觉得午睡就是偷懒。

paras.en: I genuinely find it odd, for if you nap properly, it’s like waking up from a full night’s sleep and you can double your day’s worth of concentration.
paras.zh: 我真觉得这很奇怪，因为如果午睡睡得好，就像睡了一整夜刚醒来一样，一天能集中精力的时间可以翻一倍。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What do we learn about the Dreamery, a business in Manhattan?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于曼哈顿的“梦乡馆”这家店，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 23: Why does the speaker ask us to look at the world around us at 2.30 in the afternoon?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：说话人为什么让我们在下午两点半看看周围的世界？

paras.en: Question 24: What do we learn about the quantity and quality of the speaker’s work?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于说话人工作的数量和质量，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty five: What does the speaker say he finds odd?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人说他觉得什么事很奇怪？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2023年12月大学英语四级 第1套
passages.name: 2023年12月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲美国一名五岁男孩趁姐姐午睡开走家里的车，上了高速，说要去加利福尼亚买兰博基尼跑车。第二篇新闻报道讲澳大利亚的一项研究：年轻人低头看手机，后脑勺长出了多余的骨头。第三篇新闻报道讲一个村子要给常去当地商店串门的橘猫威尔伯办十岁生日派对。第一段长对话里，两位同事商量中午去哪儿吃饭，最后决定去街角新开的意大利餐馆。第二段长对话里，帕特森一家到酒店办理入住，前台介绍了房间安排、租车、坐船出游和夜市。第一篇短文讲一项研究：人们让人工智能代理替自己谈判时，更愿意用欺骗手段。第二篇短文讲为期七周的健康烹饪课程能改善心理健康，还能缩小男女在下厨信心上的差距。第三篇短文讲个人空间分成大小不同的几层“气泡”，大小因文化和场合而异，十几岁时就定型了。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A police officer in the US stopped a large SUV car that was going very slowly and drifting across lanes on a highway.
paras.zh: 美国一名警察在高速公路上拦下了一辆大型SUV，这辆车开得很慢，还在几条车道之间来回飘。

paras.en: He expected to find a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency.
paras.zh: 他以为会看到一个喝得烂醉的司机，或者是突发急病的司机。

paras.en: Instead, the officer discovered a five-year-old boy sat on the edge of the driver’s seat.
paras.zh: 没想到，警察发现驾驶座边上坐着一个五岁的小男孩。

paras.en: His feet could barely reach the brake, and his head was only just high enough to see out of the windows.
paras.zh: 他的脚勉强够得着刹车，头也只是刚刚高到能看见窗外。

paras.en: The child had taken the keys to the family car while his teenage sister was napping.
paras.zh: 这孩子趁十几岁的姐姐午睡，拿走了家里那辆车的钥匙。

paras.en: He then drove three kilometres across town before getting on the highway.
paras.zh: 接着他开车穿过城区，开了三公里，然后上了高速。

paras.en: The boy later told confused officers that he was planning to travel to California and buy a Lamborghini sports car.
paras.zh: 男孩后来告诉一头雾水的警察，他打算去加利福尼亚买一辆兰博基尼跑车。

paras.en: Although he only had three dollars in his wallet, at least he was driving in the right direction.
paras.zh: 虽然他钱包里只有三美元，但至少方向没开错。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: Why did the police officer stop the SUV car?
paras.zh: 第一题：警察为什么拦下那辆SUV？

paras.en: Question 2: What did the boy tell the police officers he was planning to do?
paras.zh: 第二题：男孩告诉警察他打算做什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Mobile phones have changed the way we live, how we read, work, communicate, and shop.
paras.zh: 手机改变了我们的生活方式，也改变了我们阅读、工作、交流和购物的方式。

paras.en: But we already know this.
paras.zh: 不过这些我们早就知道了。

paras.en: What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave, but even the very shape of our bodies.
paras.zh: 我们还没弄明白的是，眼前这些小小的机器正在怎样改变我们的骨骼，可能不光改变我们的行为方式，甚至还在改变我们身体的形状。

paras.en: New scientific research at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Queensland, Australia suggests that young people are developing extra pieces of bone at the backs of their heads.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚昆士兰州阳光海岸大学的一项新科学研究表明，年轻人的后脑勺正在长出多余的骨头。

paras.en: These pieces of bone are caused by the way people bend their heads when they use the phone.
paras.zh: 这些骨头是人们用手机时低头的姿势造成的。

paras.en: This shifts weight on to the muscles at the back of the head and causes the bone to grow in a way that is not normal.
paras.zh: 这样一来，重量就转移到了后脑勺的肌肉上，导致骨头以不正常的方式生长。

paras.en: This process can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure.
paras.zh: 这个过程可以比作皮肤因为经常摩擦或受压而变硬。

paras.en: The result is a piece of bone like a horn that sticks out from the head by the neck.
paras.zh: 结果就是在靠近脖子的地方，从头上凸出一块像角一样的骨头。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What does the report say we have not yet understood about mobile phones?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于手机，这篇报道说我们还有什么没弄明白？

paras.en: Question four: What happens to the skin when rubbed or pressed constantly?
paras.zh: 第四题：皮肤经常受到摩擦或按压时会怎么样？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur, who has become famous for making a regular appearance at local shops.
paras.zh: 一个村子要给一只名叫威尔伯的橘猫办生日派对，它经常在当地的商店里露面，因此出了名。

paras.en: Wilbur has his own Internet pages as he approaches his tenth birthday on July seventh.
paras.zh: 七月七日威尔伯就要满十岁了，它还有自己的网页。

paras.en: Wilbur is both bold and friendly.
paras.zh: 威尔伯胆子大，又很友好。

paras.en: He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village.
paras.zh: 它大部分时间都待在村子周围的商店和公司里。

paras.en: He’ll just take himself into any shop anywhere.
paras.zh: 不管是哪家店，它都会自己溜达进去。

paras.en: There was one time when the doctor’s receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair.
paras.zh: 有一次，诊所的接待员回来，发现它正坐在她的椅子上。

paras.en: Among his favourite haunts are a local hairdresser, two pubs, and the Nottingham Primary School.
paras.zh: 它最常去的地方有当地一家理发店、两家酒吧和诺丁汉小学。

paras.en: Leslie Harper, who runs one of the pubs, said the cat has been a big hit with their customers.
paras.zh: 经营其中一家酒吧的莱斯利·哈珀说，这只猫非常受顾客欢迎。

w.m: 非常受欢迎的人（或事物）

paras.en: He’s been a regular visitor for most of this year, she told the Press Association.
paras.zh: 她告诉英国报业联合社：“今年大部分时间，它都是这里的常客。”

paras.en: He’s a very relaxed cat, happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello.
paras.zh: “它是一只特别放松的猫，不管顾客还是村民，不管老少，进来跟它打招呼它都很高兴。”

paras.en: She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes who likes his high-priced cat food.
paras.zh: 她还说，它口味挺讲究，就爱吃高价猫粮。

paras.en: Sarah Godfrey, who is organizing Wilbur’s party, told the local newspaper Wilbur is part of our lives, as he is for everyone who lives in the village.
paras.zh: 负责筹办威尔伯生日派对的萨拉·戈弗雷告诉当地报纸：“威尔伯是我们生活的一部分，对村里的每个人都是这样。”

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the report say the village is going to do for the cat?
paras.zh: 第五题：报道说村子要为这只猫做什么？

paras.en: Question six: What do we learn from the report about the cat?
paras.zh: 第六题：从报道中，我们对这只猫了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the pub owner Leslie Harper say about the cat?
paras.zh: 第七题：酒吧老板莱斯利·哈珀是怎么说这只猫的？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: So, where do you want to go for lunch?
paras.zh: 那么，中午你想去哪儿吃？

paras.en: I don’t know.
paras.zh: 我不知道。

paras.en: Do you have anything in mind?
paras.zh: 你有想去的地方吗？

paras.en: What about the Sandwich Place on Camden Street?
paras.zh: 卡姆登街上的那家三明治店怎么样？

paras.en: No, sorry.
paras.zh: 不行，抱歉。

paras.en: I don’t feel like sandwiches today.
paras.zh: 我今天不想吃三明治。

paras.en: It’s a great place, but I think we go there too often.
paras.zh: 那家店很好，不过我觉得我们去得太勤了。

paras.en: That’s true.
paras.zh: 那倒是。

paras.en: Remember that’s where we saw Bridget Clark, the famous movie star.
paras.zh: 记得吗，我们就是在那儿看到大明星布里奇特·克拉克的。

paras.en: Of course.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: How could I ever forget?
paras.zh: 我怎么可能忘呢？

paras.en: There were crowds of people around her, asking for a photo with her.
paras.zh: 她身边围了一大群人，都想跟她合影。

paras.en: What about hamburgers, then?
paras.zh: 那吃汉堡怎么样？

paras.en: There’s that American style diner on the way to the mall.
paras.zh: 去商场的路上有一家美式小餐馆。

paras.en: I like that place.
paras.zh: 我喜欢那家店。

paras.en: Their chips are great.
paras.zh: 他们家的薯条很好吃。

paras.en: But their service takes a long time, and I need to get back by two thirty for a conference call.
paras.zh: 不过他们上菜太慢，我两点半之前得回去，要开电话会议。

paras.en: How about trying something new?
paras.zh: 要不试试新地方？

paras.en: We could try Mario’s, the new Italian restaurant on the corner.
paras.zh: 我们可以去拐角那家新开的意大利餐馆马里奥。

paras.en: It looks all right.
paras.zh: 看着还不错。

paras.en: Have you been there?
paras.zh: 你去过吗？

paras.en: No, I haven’t, but I’ve noticed that it has great reviews on the Internet.
paras.zh: 没去过，不过我注意到它在网上的评价很好。

paras.en: It’s supposed to be one of the best Italians in town.
paras.zh: 据说它是城里最好的意大利餐馆之一。

paras.en: I think Jeremy has been there, and said it was amazing.
paras.zh: 我记得杰里米去过，他说特别棒。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；极好的

paras.en: I’m up for that.
paras.zh: 我同意去。

paras.en: Cool.
paras.zh: 好极了。

paras.en: Have you asked Jeremy if he would like to come with us?
paras.zh: 你问过杰里米要不要跟我们一起去吗？

paras.en: I already have.
paras.zh: 我已经问过了。

paras.en: He says he can’t.
paras.zh: 他说他去不了。

paras.en: He has brought his own lunch today, so he will stay in.
paras.zh: 他今天自己带了午饭，所以就不出去了。

paras.en: I think his wife made him soup.
paras.zh: 我猜是他老婆给他做了汤。

paras.en: Poor Jeremy.
paras.zh: 可怜的杰里米。

paras.en: His wife is a terrible cook.
paras.zh: 他老婆做饭可难吃了。

paras.en: He should throw that soup in the bin and join us.
paras.zh: 他应该把汤倒进垃圾桶，跟我们一起去。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What are the speakers talking about in this conversation?
paras.zh: 第八题：说话人在这段对话中谈的是什么？

paras.en: Question nine: Where did the speakers see Bridget Clark, the famous movie star?
paras.zh: 第九题：说话人是在哪里看到大明星布里奇特·克拉克的？

paras.en: Question 10: Why does the woman say she needs to get back by 2:30?
paras.zh: 第十题：女士为什么说她得在两点半之前回去？

paras.en: Question 11: Why does the woman say Jeremy should throw his soup in the bin?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士为什么说杰里米应该把汤倒进垃圾桶？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi there, how are you today?
paras.zh: 您好，今天怎么样？

paras.en: Do you have a reservation with us already?
paras.zh: 您在我们这儿已经预订过了吗？

paras.en: Good afternoon.
paras.zh: 下午好。

paras.en: Yes, we reserved our rooms yesterday morning on your website for three nights.
paras.zh: 是的，我们昨天上午在你们网站上订了房间，住三晚。

paras.en: The name’s Patterson.
paras.zh: 我姓帕特森。

paras.en: Okay, let me have a look.
paras.zh: 好的，我查一下。

paras.en: Yes, we have it here.
paras.zh: 有了，在这儿。

paras.en: You brought the whole family with you, I see.
paras.zh: 我看您是带着全家来的。

paras.en: Yes, the two kids, my wife and I, and her parents too.
paras.zh: 是的，两个孩子、我和我太太，还有她父母。

paras.en: Great.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: So we have a family room for you and your wife and the kids, and another double room for your parents-in-law.
paras.zh: 那我们给您、您太太和孩子安排了一间家庭房，再给您的岳父岳母安排一间双人房。

paras.en: They are right next to each other on the ground floor, since you mentioned in your message that they have trouble with stairs.
paras.zh: 两间房在一楼，紧挨着，因为您在留言里提到他们上下楼梯不方便。

paras.en: That’s wonderful.
paras.zh: 太好了。

paras.en: My father-in-law has had terrible problems getting up and down stairs since his knee operation last April.
paras.zh: 我岳父去年四月做了膝盖手术以后，上下楼梯就特别困难。

w.m: adj. 极其严重的；糟糕的

paras.en: I’m sorry to hear that.
paras.zh: 听到这个我很难过。

paras.en: And if you need any help to find transportation for the whole family, we can definitely recommend someone for you.
paras.zh: 如果您全家出行需要帮忙找交通工具，我们肯定能给您推荐人。

paras.en: We were thinking of renting a car, but we will explore all the options available for sure.
paras.zh: 我们本来想租辆车，不过肯定会把能选的办法都看一看。

paras.en: So yes, that would be very helpful in comparing prices.
paras.zh: 所以，您能推荐的话，我们比较价格就方便多了。

paras.en: We’re also wondering what tours and day trips are available.
paras.zh: 我们还想知道有哪些观光游和一日游可以参加。

paras.en: We have bunches of brochures here.
paras.zh: 我们这儿有一大堆宣传册。

paras.en: I would recommend getting out on a boat trip.
paras.zh: 我推荐您坐船出去玩一趟。

paras.en: The kids will love it, and there are so many islands nearby to explore.
paras.zh: 孩子们会很喜欢的，而且附近有很多小岛可以去看看。

paras.en: There’s also a great night market further into town that has all kinds of food and cool little shops selling souvenirs and local jewelry and clothing made by hand.
paras.zh: 再往城里走还有一个很棒的夜市，那里有各种各样的吃的，还有很有意思的小店，卖纪念品、当地的首饰和手工做的衣服。

paras.en: That all sounds marvelous.
paras.zh: 听起来都很棒。

paras.en: Now all I need is to photocopy your passports, and then I can get you all checked in and show you to your rooms.
paras.zh: 现在我只需要复印一下你们的护照，然后就能给你们全家办好入住，带你们去房间。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Who is the man talking to in the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十二题：这段对话中男士在跟谁说话？

paras.en: Question 13: What do we learn about the man’s father-in-law from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十三题：从对话中，我们对男士的岳父了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 14: Why does the man say they will explore all the options available?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士为什么说他们会把能选的办法都看一看？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the woman suggest the man and his family do close to the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：快到对话结束时，女士建议男士一家做什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Artificial intelligence agents play ever more influential roles in our lives.
paras.zh: 人工智能代理在我们生活中的作用越来越大。

paras.en: They do everything from suggesting new friends to recommending purchases.
paras.zh: 从推荐新朋友到推荐买什么东西，它们什么都干。

paras.en: They’re even beginning to drive our cars.
paras.zh: 它们甚至开始替我们开车了。

paras.en: Another role that they are expected to take over is negotiating on our behalf in commercial transactions or legal disputes.
paras.zh: 人们预计它们还会接手另一项工作：在商业交易或法律纠纷中代表我们谈判。

paras.en: So it’s important to know whether using an artificial intelligence agent might affect how we negotiate.
paras.zh: 所以，弄清楚用人工智能代理会不会影响我们谈判的方式很重要。

paras.en: Research indicates that it does.
paras.zh: 研究表明，确实会。

paras.en: In a new study, participants were told to imagine that they were negotiating for something important to them, like a house.
paras.zh: 在一项新研究中，参与者被要求想象自己正在为一样对自己很重要的东西谈判，比如一套房子。

paras.en: Next, they were told either that they would negotiate for themselves, or they would program an artificial intelligence agent to negotiate for them.
paras.zh: 接着，研究人员告诉他们，要么自己去谈判，要么给一个人工智能代理编好程序，让它替他们谈判。

paras.en: Participants then completed a survey indicating how tough, deceptive, and pleasant or otherwise they wanted to be, or wanted their agent to be, in the negotiations.
paras.zh: 然后参与者填了一份调查问卷，说明自己（或自己的代理）在谈判中想表现得多强硬、多会骗人，友善还是不友善。

w.m: adj. 友好的；讨人喜欢的

paras.en: For example, participants could choose to be tough by making an opening demand far greater than what they’d be willing to accept.
paras.zh: 比如，参与者可以选择表现得强硬，一开口提的要求就远高于自己愿意接受的价码。

paras.en: They could also choose to express sympathy with their opponent to appear pleasant, but they could also indicate that they or their agent would strategically express anger toward the opponent to gain advantage.
paras.zh: 他们也可以选择对对手表示同情，显得友善；但他们也可以表明，自己或自己的代理会有策略地向对手发火，来占上风。

w.m: adj. 友好的；讨人喜欢的

paras.en: Or they could opt to convey dissatisfaction with the encounter, so that the other party would think they were losing interest.
paras.zh: 或者他们可以选择对这次交锋表示不满，让对方以为他们快没兴趣了。

paras.en: These are both examples of deceptive strategies.
paras.zh: 这两种都是欺骗策略的例子。

paras.en: Participants were more willing to employ deceptive strategies when assigned an agent to negotiate on their behalf.
paras.zh: 参与者被分配一个代理替自己谈判时，更愿意使用欺骗策略。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the passage say about artificial intelligence agents?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于人工智能代理，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the new study want to find out about using an artificial intelligence agent?
paras.zh: 第十七题：在使用人工智能代理这件事上，这项新研究想弄清楚什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What did participants tend to do when assigned an AI agent to negotiate on their behalf?
paras.zh: 第十八题：参与者被分配一个人工智能代理替自己谈判时，往往会怎么做？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: New research has studied the effects of a seven-week healthy cooking course.
paras.zh: 一项新研究考察了一门为期七周的健康烹饪课程有什么效果。

paras.en: Academics measured the programme’s effect on cooking confidence and self-perceived mental health.
paras.zh: 学者们测量了这门课程对下厨信心和自我感觉的心理健康有什么影响。

paras.en: Researchers also measured participants’ overall satisfaction around cooking and diet-related behaviours.
paras.zh: 研究人员还测量了参与者对烹饪和饮食相关行为的总体满意度。

paras.en: What were the findings?
paras.zh: 研究发现了什么呢？

paras.en: Course participants saw significant improvements in general health.
paras.zh: 参加课程的人总体健康状况明显改善。

paras.en: They also reported improved mental health and subjective vitality immediately after the programme.
paras.zh: 他们还说，课程一结束，心理健康和主观活力就都有所提高。

paras.en: These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course.
paras.zh: 课程结束六个月后，这些好处依然存在。

paras.en: What caused these improvements?
paras.zh: 这些改善是什么带来的？

paras.en: Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and vegetables and improved longer-term mental health.
paras.zh: 研究人员以前就发现，多吃水果蔬菜和长期心理健康改善之间有关联。

paras.en: This would imply that the participants in the current study may have felt better due to improved diet.
paras.zh: 这就意味着，这次研究的参与者感觉变好，可能是因为饮食改善了。

paras.en: However, the study showed participants’ mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after completing the program.
paras.zh: 不过研究显示，参与者上完课以后，即使自己说饮食没变，心理健康也提高了。

paras.en: Also, the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range.
paras.zh: 而且，超重或肥胖的参与者和体重正常的参与者在心理健康上得到的好处一样多。

paras.en: This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking and mental health benefits.
paras.zh: 这说明，下厨信心、对烹饪的满意度和心理健康上的好处之间有关联。

paras.en: Who benefits most from learning to cook?
paras.zh: 学做饭谁受益最大？

paras.en: Gender plays a part.
paras.zh: 性别有一定影响。

paras.en: At the start of the program, 77% of female participants were confident about cooking, but just 23% of males were confident.
paras.zh: 课程刚开始时，百分之七十七的女性参与者对做饭有信心，而男性只有百分之二十三。

paras.en: At the end of the programme, cooking confidence and skills were equal across both counterparts.
paras.zh: 课程结束时，男女双方的下厨信心和技能都一样了。

paras.en: This change in confidence could lead to a gender balance in home cooking.
paras.zh: 信心上的这种变化可能让家里做饭的事男女分担得更均衡。

paras.en: This in turn could reduce consumption of unhealthy, high-calorie processed meals.
paras.zh: 这反过来又可能减少不健康的高热量加工食品的消费。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn about the benefits the participants gained from the healthy cooking course?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于参与者从健康烹饪课程中得到的好处，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What do the new research findings suggest about mental health benefits?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于心理健康上的好处，新的研究结果说明了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：在决定谁从学做饭中受益最大这件事上，什么起了作用？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: What is personal space?
paras.zh: 什么是个人空间？

paras.en: We often think of it as an invisible bubble of space surrounding us that others can’t enter without causing discomfort.
paras.zh: 我们常常把它想成包围着我们的一个看不见的空间气泡，别人一进来就会让我们不舒服。

paras.en: Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes.
paras.zh: 不过研究表明，我们其实有大小不同的几个气泡。

paras.en: Each of these bubbles applies to a different set of people.
paras.zh: 每个气泡适用于不同的一群人。

paras.en: The smallest zone, called intimate space, extends outward from our bodies eighteen inches in every direction.
paras.zh: 最小的那一层叫亲密空间，从我们身体往外向四面八方延伸十八英寸。

paras.en: Only family, pets, and one’s closest friends may enter it.
paras.zh: 只有家人、宠物和最亲密的朋友才能进入。

paras.en: A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space makes us uncomfortable.
paras.zh: 只是认识的人进入我们的亲密空间，就会让我们不舒服。

paras.en: Next is the bubble called personal space, extending from one point five feet to four feet away.
paras.zh: 下一层气泡叫个人空间，从一点五英尺延伸到四英尺远。

paras.en: Friends and acquaintances can comfortably occupy this zone, especially during informal conversations, but strangers are forbidden.
paras.zh: 朋友和认识的人可以自在地待在这个区域里，尤其是随意聊天的时候，但陌生人不许进来。

paras.en: Extending from four to twelve feet away from us is social space.
paras.zh: 离我们四到十二英尺的是社交空间。

paras.en: Here people feel comfortable conducting routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers.
paras.zh: 在这个范围里，人们和新认识的人、甚至完全陌生的人进行日常的社交往来，都会觉得自在。

paras.en: Those are the average sizes of Americans’ personal bubbles, anyway.
paras.zh: 不管怎么说，这些是美国人个人气泡的平均大小。

paras.en: It is important to keep in mind that personal space varies depending on culture and context.
paras.zh: 要记住，个人空间因文化和场合而异，这一点很重要。

paras.en: Furthermore, there are significant individual differences.
paras.zh: 此外，个人之间的差异也很大。

paras.en: As we all know, cultural or individual differences in personal bubble diameters are all too often the cause of discomfort.
paras.zh: 大家都知道，个人气泡的直径因文化或个人而不同，这往往让人不舒服。

paras.en: How did these personal bubbles arise?
paras.zh: 这些个人气泡是怎么形成的？

paras.en: According to research, we begin to develop our individual sense of personal space around age three or four.
paras.zh: 研究显示，我们大约在三四岁时开始形成自己的个人空间感。

paras.en: The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens.
paras.zh: 到了十几岁，我们气泡的大小就定型了。

paras.en: These bubbles are constructed and monitored by the brain region involved in fear.
paras.zh: 这些气泡是由大脑里跟恐惧有关的区域构建和监控的。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What does research show about our personal space?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于我们的个人空间，研究表明了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What happens if a mere acquaintance enters our intimate space?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：只是认识的人进入我们的亲密空间，会怎么样？

paras.en: Question 24: Where do people feel comfortable interacting with new acquaintances or strangers?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：人们在哪里和刚认识的人或陌生人交往会觉得自在？

paras.en: Question twenty five: When are the sizes of our bubbles fixed?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：我们的气泡大小是什么时候定型的？

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2023年12月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2023年12月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲加州大学的一项研究：朋友之间看视频时大脑活动更相似，相似到能据此判断两人是不是朋友。第二篇新闻报道讲在夏威夷做了六十年好朋友的两位老人，通过DNA配对网站发现他们竟是同母所生的亲兄弟。第三篇新闻报道讲五名游客在海滩上捡垃圾，被路人拍下传到网上，当地人看了很惭愧。第一段长对话里，本杰明崴了脚踝不能去跑步，女士下周六要陪小侄子去动物园，两人还聊到身体特别好的丹。第二段长对话里，《退休要趁早》的作者约翰·布莱克接受采访，谈到四十岁退休、财务自由和怎样攒钱。第一篇短文讲一项研究：人们在其他群体的人面前更愿意选健康食品，因为觉得会被外人评判。第二篇短文讲和治疗犬互动能帮压力大、学业有困难的大学生提高执行功能，效果胜过传统的减压课程。第三篇短文讲做生意要敢于冒险：冒险要靠周密的计划，失败是学习的机会，敢冒险的企业更有竞争优势。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Have you noticed how similar you are to your friends?
paras.zh: 你有没有注意到，你和你的朋友有多像？

paras.en: It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other.
paras.zh: 这可能是因为你们的大脑运转得很合拍。

paras.en: We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender, and ethnic background as each other.
paras.zh: 我们知道，朋友之间更有可能年龄相同、性别相同、民族背景相同。

paras.en: Now it seems their brains are alike too.
paras.zh: 现在看来，他们的大脑也很相像。

paras.en: Researchers at the University of California scanned the brains of 42 classmates while they watched videos intended to provoke varying responses.
paras.zh: 加利福尼亚大学的研究人员让四十二名同学观看一些视频，这些视频会引起各种不同的反应，研究人员在他们观看时对他们的大脑进行了扫描。

w.m: adj. 不同的；各种各样的

paras.en: Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance, while others would feel it was embarrassing.
paras.zh: 比如，有些人可能觉得一个浪漫的场景很感人，而另一些人会觉得很尴尬。

paras.en: The activity of friends’ brains was more similar than that of people who didn’t know each other, particularly in regions involved in attention, emotion, and language.
paras.zh: 朋友之间的大脑活动比互不相识的人更相似，尤其是在跟注意力、情绪和语言有关的区域。

paras.en: This similarity was strong enough that it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not.
paras.zh: 这种相似程度之高，甚至可以用来预测两个人是不是已经是朋友。

paras.en: The relationship probably goes two ways: we are drawn to people who think like us.
paras.zh: 这种关系可能是双向的：我们会被想法跟自己相像的人吸引。

paras.en: We then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own.
paras.zh: 然后，时间一长，我们又会影响他们的想法，这可能让他们的大脑活动变得跟我们更接近。

paras.en: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 1: What may be the reason that friends are similar to each other, according to the recent research?
paras.zh: 第一题：根据最近这项研究，朋友之间相似的原因可能是什么？
