paras.en: Question 2: What does the news report say about the relationship between friends?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于朋友之间的关系，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Two men who have been best friends for 60 years have just realized they are actually brothers.
paras.zh: 两个做了六十年好朋友的人刚刚发现，他们其实是亲兄弟。

paras.en: It’s reported that Alan Robinson and Walter McDonald met in the sixth grade at a school in Hawaii.
paras.zh: 据报道，艾伦·鲁滨逊和沃尔特·麦克唐纳是在夏威夷一所学校上六年级时认识的。

paras.en: They have been best friends ever since.
paras.zh: 从那以后他们一直是最好的朋友。

paras.en: Alan was given away for adoption soon after he was born, and Walter never knew his father.
paras.zh: 艾伦出生后不久就被送给别人收养了，沃尔特也从来不知道自己的父亲是谁。

paras.en: So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry.
paras.zh: 所以最近，他们各自在DNA配对网站上试了试，想多了解一些自己的家世。

paras.en: Walter was astonished to find that he matched with website user Robbie 737.
paras.zh: 沃尔特惊讶地发现，自己和网站上一个叫“罗比737”的用户配上了。

paras.en: He knew immediately that this was his best friend Alan, whose friends call him Robbie and flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot.
paras.zh: 他马上就知道这就是他最好的朋友艾伦：朋友们都叫艾伦罗比，他当飞行员时开的就是737飞机。

paras.en: The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.
paras.zh: 两人是同一个母亲生的，出生时间相差十五个月。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What did both Alan Robinson and Walter McDonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites?
paras.zh: 第三题：艾伦·鲁滨逊和沃尔特·麦克唐纳都想在DNA配对网站上做什么？

paras.en: Question four: What did the news report say about Alan Robinson and Walter McDonald?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于艾伦·鲁滨逊和沃尔特·麦克唐纳，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Amid all the election drama, air pollution problems and disease outbreaks, five tourists’ good work is being spread online.
paras.zh: 在铺天盖地的选举风波、空气污染和疾病暴发的新闻里，五名游客做的好事正在网上传开。

paras.en: Yesterday, two male and three female tourists were spotted walking the kilometer-long beach picking up trash.
paras.zh: 昨天，有人看到两男三女五名游客走遍一公里长的海滩捡垃圾。

paras.en: One of the male tourists from Australia commented that although there was a lot of trash, nobody was doing anything.
paras.zh: 其中一名来自澳大利亚的男游客说，虽然垃圾很多，却没有人管。

paras.en: The beach was not as nice or beautiful as it should be.
paras.zh: 这片海滩没有它本该有的那么好、那么美。

paras.en: He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash.
paras.zh: 看到这么漂亮的地方扔满了垃圾，他心里很难过。

w.m: adj. 非常漂亮的；极好的

paras.en: Thus, he and his friends decided to grab a few trash bags and clean it all up.
paras.zh: 所以，他和朋友们决定拿几个垃圾袋，把垃圾全部清理干净。

paras.en: A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet.
paras.zh: 一名路过的男子决定把他们做的好事拍下来，传到网上。

paras.en: It was unclear where the rest of the group was from, but they were most likely travelling together.
paras.zh: 不清楚这群人里其他几个人是哪里人，但他们很可能是一起旅行的。

paras.en: One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach.
paras.zh: 一名当地女子评论说，游客来清理他们的海滩，她觉得很惭愧。

paras.en: Another mentioned that it was actually the natives who brought food and drinks, then left trash all along the island.
paras.zh: 另一个人提到，其实是当地人带来吃的喝的，然后把垃圾扔得满岛都是。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: Why did one of the male tourists feel sad?
paras.zh: 第五题：其中一名男游客为什么感到难过？

paras.en: Question six: Who put the good deed video on the internet?
paras.zh: 第六题：是谁把做好事的视频传到网上的？

paras.en: Question seven: Why did one local woman say she was embarrassed?
paras.zh: 第七题：一名当地女子为什么说她觉得惭愧？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation 1.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hello, Benjamin.
paras.zh: 你好，本杰明。

paras.en: Dan and I will be going for a run along the canal Saturday morning.
paras.zh: 周六上午我和丹要沿着运河跑步。

paras.en: Would you like to join us?
paras.zh: 你想跟我们一起去吗？

paras.en: I’d love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.
paras.zh: 我很想去，可是上周末跟同事踢足球，把脚踝弄伤了。

paras.en: Oh dear, is it serious?
paras.zh: 哎呀，严重吗？

paras.en: No, not at all.
paras.zh: 没有，根本不严重。

paras.en: I landed badly during a fall and twisted it a little.
paras.zh: 我摔倒的时候落地没落好，把它扭了一下。

paras.en: But it’s no big deal.
paras.zh: 不过没什么大不了的。

paras.en: It’s just a little swollen, and I should be fine for next Saturday if you still want to go for a jog then.
paras.zh: 就是有点肿，如果你还想下周六去慢跑，我应该就没事了。

paras.en: I won’t be here next Saturday.
paras.zh: 下周六我不在。

paras.en: I’m going to the zoo.
paras.zh: 我要去动物园。

paras.en: The zoo?
paras.zh: 动物园？

paras.en: Yeah.
paras.zh: 是啊。

paras.en: My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo.
paras.zh: 我的小侄子要满六岁了，他特别喜欢动物园。

paras.en: So the whole family is going.
paras.zh: 所以全家都去。

paras.en: Oh, okay then.
paras.zh: 哦，那好吧。

paras.en: I haven’t been to a zoo since I was a kid.
paras.zh: 我从小时候起就再也没去过动物园。

paras.en: They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be when we were children.
paras.zh: 现在的动物园远远没有我们小时候那么受欢迎了。

paras.en: I personally feel sorry for the poor animals stuck in cages.
paras.zh: 我个人很同情那些关在笼子里的可怜动物。

paras.en: But there’s no denying they are fun and educational for children.
paras.zh: 不过不可否认，动物园对孩子来说既好玩又有教育意义。

paras.en: Do you know if Dan will be around next Saturday?
paras.zh: 你知道丹下周六在不在吗？

paras.en: Yeah, I think he will.
paras.zh: 嗯，我想他在。

paras.en: Just send him a text message.
paras.zh: 给他发个短信就行。

paras.en: He’s always keen on physical activities.
paras.zh: 他一向很喜欢运动。

paras.en: That’s true.
paras.zh: 那倒是。

paras.en: Dan is extremely fit and healthy.
paras.zh: 丹身体特别结实，特别健康。

paras.en: He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week.
paras.zh: 他差不多每天都去健身房，另外每周还打两三次网球。

paras.en: So what have you been doing to stay busy while you’ve had that swollen ankle?
paras.zh: 那你脚踝肿着的这段时间都在忙些什么？

paras.en: I’ve been catching up on some reading.
paras.zh: 我一直在补看一些书。

paras.en: I was given three books over Christmas, and I’m only now getting round to reading them.
paras.zh: 圣诞节的时候别人送了我三本书，我到现在才抽出时间来看。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: Why can’t the man go for a run Saturday morning?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士为什么周六上午不能去跑步？

paras.en: Question nine: Why is the woman’s whole family going to the zoo next Saturday?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士全家下周六为什么要去动物园？

paras.en: Question 10: What do we learn about Dan from the man’s description?
paras.zh: 第十题：从男士的描述中，我们对丹了解到什么？

paras.en: Question eleven: What has the man been doing since last weekend?
paras.zh: 第十一题：男士从上周末以来一直在做什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Our guest on today’s Book Talk is John Black, the author of the new bestseller, Retire Early.
paras.zh: 今天做客《读书漫谈》的是约翰·布莱克，他是新出的畅销书《退休要趁早》的作者。

paras.en: Thanks for having me on the show, Lisa.
paras.zh: 谢谢你请我来上节目，丽莎。

paras.en: John, your book is getting a lot of attention, partly because you write that most people can retire by 40.
paras.zh: 约翰，你的书很受关注，部分原因是你在书里写道，大多数人四十岁就能退休。

paras.en: Is that realistic?
paras.zh: 这现实吗？

w.m: adj. 现实的；切合实际的

paras.en: Definitely.
paras.zh: 当然现实。

paras.en: When researching this book, I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40.
paras.zh: 写这本书做调研的时候，我采访了好几百个四十岁之前就退休的人。

paras.en: Okay, but how much money does a person need to retire?
paras.zh: 好吧，那一个人需要多少钱才能退休呢？

paras.en: I’ve read articles recommending $1 million as a good figure for retirement.
paras.zh: 我看过一些文章，推荐把一百万美元当作退休的理想数字。

paras.en: While most financial planners do give numbers, I don’t think that’s useful, as people are living in different areas with different costs of living and have different needs and wants, which is why I suggest that people aim for financial independence.
paras.zh: 虽然大多数理财规划师确实会给出数字，但我觉得这没什么用，因为人们住在不同的地方，生活成本不一样，需要和想要的东西也不一样，所以我建议人们以财务自由为目标。

paras.en: What do you mean by financial independence?
paras.zh: 你说的财务自由是什么意思？

paras.en: Having investment income that’s greater than monthly expenses.
paras.zh: 就是投资收入高过每月的开支。

paras.en: That sounds risky to me.
paras.zh: 我听着觉得风险挺大的。

paras.en: What if an accident happens, or you get ill and need medical treatment?
paras.zh: 万一出了意外，或者生了病要治疗怎么办？

paras.en: Shouldn’t people have extra cash for emergencies?
paras.zh: 人们不是应该留些额外的现金以备急用吗？

paras.en: Too many people spend their lives working on jobs they hate because they’re afraid.
paras.zh: 太多人因为害怕，一辈子都在干自己讨厌的工作。

paras.en: So I counsel people to take risks.
paras.zh: 所以我劝大家要敢于冒险。

paras.en: Retirement doesn’t have to be permanent, and if people need to, they can go back to work.
paras.zh: 退休不一定是永久的，如果需要，还可以回去工作。

paras.en: But it’s not always easy to get back into the workforce after an extended absence.
paras.zh: 可是离开很长时间之后，再回到职场并不总是那么容易。

paras.en: True, but if you keep current with your skills, you will be attractive to employers.
paras.zh: 没错，但只要你不断更新自己的技能，雇主就会觉得你有吸引力。

paras.en: Maybe, but how can anyone save enough to retire by 40 when most people can’t retire at 60?
paras.zh: 也许吧，可大多数人六十岁都退不了休，谁能攒够钱四十岁就退休呢？

paras.en: Simple.
paras.zh: 很简单。

paras.en: By cutting housing, food, and transport expenses and investing half your monthly income.
paras.zh: 削减住房、饮食和交通开支，再把每月一半的收入拿去投资。

paras.en: That sounds impossible.
paras.zh: 听起来根本做不到。

paras.en: I admit it’s difficult, but it has worked for thousands.
paras.zh: 我承认这很难，但已经有好几千人做到了。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What do we learn about the man’s book published recently?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于男士最近出版的书，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What do the articles the woman read recommend?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士读过的文章推荐了什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the man say about retirement?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于退休，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: How does the man say his proposal about retirement can be carried out?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士说他关于退休的建议要怎样实现？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: New research from America studies the role that the presence of individuals from different social or racial groups has in influencing consumers’ food choices.
paras.zh: 美国的一项新研究考察了：身边有来自不同社会群体或种族群体的人，对消费者选择食物有什么影响。

paras.en: This research found college students were more likely to choose healthy food in the presence of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race.
paras.zh: 研究发现，旁边有不同种族的人看着时，大学生比旁边是同种族的人时更可能选健康食品。

paras.en: The same was true when they were with someone from a different university compared to someone from their own.
paras.zh: 和别的大学的人在一起，比起和本校的人在一起，情况也是一样。

paras.en: Researchers say this was because participants anticipated more negative judgment from an outsider group.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，这是因为参与者预料外群体的人会对自己作出更多负面评判。

paras.en: In contrast, they felt less judged by members of their own group.
paras.zh: 相比之下，他们觉得本群体的人对自己的评判少一些。

paras.en: In one experiment, participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack.
paras.zh: 在一个实验中，研究人员让参与者在糖果和水果之间挑一样当零食。

paras.en: When in the presence of an unknown student from their own university, only 12% of students selected the healthier option.
paras.zh: 旁边是本校一个不认识的学生时，只有百分之十二的学生选了更健康的那样。

paras.en: However, this number was 31% when in the presence of an unknown student from another university.
paras.zh: 不过，旁边是别的大学一个不认识的学生时，这个比例是百分之三十一。

paras.en: Other experiments showed similar results based on racial group.
paras.zh: 其他实验按种族群体分，也得出了类似的结果。

paras.en: What’s the reason for this pattern?
paras.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

paras.en: The study found that people feel judged to a larger extent by members of other groups.
paras.zh: 研究发现，人们觉得其他群体的人评判自己更多。

paras.en: Because of this, they strategically use healthy food choices to make a positive impression.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，他们会有策略地选健康食品，好给人留下好印象。

paras.en: There have been many attempts to help consumers make healthier choices, but consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet.
paras.zh: 为了帮消费者选得更健康，人们做过很多尝试，但消费者往往很难一直保持健康饮食。

paras.en: This research finds that one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social benefits of healthy choices.
paras.zh: 这项研究发现，推广健康饮食的一个办法，可能是宣传健康选择在社交上的好处。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What was the finding of the new research from America about consumers’ food choices?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于消费者选择食物，美国的这项新研究有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 17: When did 31% of students in the experiment select the healthier option?
paras.zh: 第十七题：实验中百分之三十一的学生在什么情况下选了更健康的那样？

paras.en: Question 18: How could a healthy diet be promoted according to the findings of the new research?
paras.zh: 第十八题：根据这项新研究的发现，怎样可以推广健康饮食？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: For college students under pressure, a dog may be the best stress fighter around, according to the finding of a recent study.
paras.zh: 最近一项研究发现，对压力大的大学生来说，狗可能是最好的减压帮手。

paras.en: It’s a really powerful finding, said Patricia Pendry, who led the study.
paras.zh: 负责这项研究的帕特里夏·彭德里说，这个发现很有说服力。

w.m: adj. 有力的；有说服力的

paras.en: Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically, especially those who may be at risk due to a history of mental health issues or academic and learning issues.
paras.zh: 各所大学为了帮学生在学业上取得成功，做了很多很好的工作，尤其是那些因为有过心理健康问题、或者有学业和学习问题而可能处于困境的学生。

paras.en: This study shows that traditional stress management approaches aren’t as effective for this population compared with programmes that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs.
paras.zh: 这项研究表明，对这类学生来说，传统的压力管理方法不如那些着重提供机会和治疗犬互动的项目有效。

paras.en: The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study.
paras.zh: 研究人员测量了参与研究的学生的执行功能。

paras.en: Executive function is a term for the skills one needs to plan, organize, motivate, concentrate, and memorize.
paras.zh: 执行功能指的是一个人在计划、组织、激励自己、集中注意力和记忆时所需要的技能。

paras.en: These are skills students need to succeed in college.
paras.zh: 这些都是学生在大学里取得成功需要的技能。

paras.en: The researchers found that students who were most at risk had the most improvements in executive functioning after interacting with therapy dogs.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，最处于困境的学生和治疗犬互动之后，执行功能提高得最多。

paras.en: These results remained when researchers followed up six weeks later.
paras.zh: 六周后研究人员回访时，这些效果依然存在。

paras.en: Many universities provide academic stress management programs and workshops.
paras.zh: 很多大学都开设学业压力管理课程和讲习班。

paras.en: These are traditionally very similar to college classes.
paras.zh: 这些课程向来跟大学的课很像。

paras.en: They often talk about ways to get more sleep, set goals, or manage stress or anxiety.
paras.zh: 它们常常讲怎样多睡点觉、怎样定目标，或者怎样应对压力、焦虑。

paras.en: Pendry acknowledges that these are really important topics and these workshops help typical students succeed.
paras.zh: 彭德里承认，这些确实是非常重要的话题，这些讲习班也能帮普通学生取得成功。

paras.en: But they’re less helpful for struggling students.
paras.zh: 可是对学习吃力的学生，它们就没那么有用了。

w.m: adj. 吃力的；处境困难的

paras.en: Pendry believes those students may experience the programmes as another lecture and feel even more stressed.
paras.zh: 彭德里认为，那些学生可能会把这些课程当成又一堂讲座，反而压力更大。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the recent study, led by Patricia Pendry, aim to examine?
paras.zh: 第十九题：帕特里夏·彭德里负责的这项最新研究要考察什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What did the new study measure in the participants?
paras.zh: 第二十题：这项新研究测量了参与者的什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does Patricia Pendry think traditional stress management programs may do?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：帕特里夏·彭德里认为传统的压力管理课程可能会怎么样？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Taking risks in business does not mean going into business blindly and then expecting great results.
paras.zh: 做生意冒险，并不是说盲目地投身商海，然后指望得到好结果。

paras.en: On the contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work.
paras.zh: 恰恰相反，创业冒险需要周密的计划和辛勤的工作。

paras.en: Nobody can really be sure if risks will be met with success, no matter how calculated they may be.
paras.zh: 不管风险计算得多么周全，谁也说不准冒险会不会成功。

w.m: adj. 经过计算的；有意的

paras.en: But this should not stop you from taking risks, as risks are necessary if you want your business to succeed.
paras.zh: 但这不应该阻止你去冒险，因为如果你想让生意成功，冒险是必要的。

paras.en: Some risks may not work out, but an optimistic risk taker will always look at failure as an opportunity to learn.
paras.zh: 有些冒险可能会失败，但乐观的冒险者总会把失败看作学习的机会。

paras.en: The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth.
paras.zh: 愿意尝试新想法，是生意发展的关键。

paras.en: As the old saying goes, nothing ventured, nothing gained.
paras.zh: 正如老话说的，不入虎穴，焉得虎子。

paras.en: Failure will teach you how to think and plan strategically.
paras.zh: 失败会教你怎样有策略地思考和计划。

paras.en: But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward.
paras.zh: 但要记住，不是所有的冒险都是好的，失败了就要从中吸取教训，继续往前走。

paras.en: Since most people tend to avoid risk, businesses that are brave enough to take risks already have a competitive advantage.
paras.zh: 因为大多数人往往回避风险，所以敢于冒险的企业已经有了竞争优势。

paras.en: They are the ones setting the standard with new ideas, fresh offers, and bold inventions.
paras.zh: 正是它们用新想法、新产品和大胆的发明来树立标准。

paras.en: Risk takers are best at adapting in difficult times.
paras.zh: 冒险者最善于在困难时期适应变化。

paras.en: Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for risk takers.
paras.zh: 简单地说，大多数人都远离风险，这对冒险者来说就意味着竞争更少。

paras.en: We don’t know if you’ll achieve what these risk takers have achieved, but for as long as you want to stay safe and for as long as you are content with where your business is right now, you will never find out.
paras.zh: 我们不知道你能不能取得这些冒险者那样的成就，但只要你还想求稳、还满足于自己生意现在的样子，你就永远不会知道。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do entrepreneurs have to do when taking risks according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：根据这篇短文，创业者冒险时必须做什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the passage say is key to business growth?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：短文说什么是生意发展的关键？

paras.en: Question 24: What are we advised to do when we fail?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：短文建议我们失败的时候怎么做？

paras.en: Question 25: What does it mean to risk-taking businesses when most people tend to avoid risk?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：大多数人往往回避风险，这对敢冒险的企业意味着什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第1套
passages.name: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲捷蓝航空一架从西棕榈滩飞往纽约的航班起飞几分钟后撞上飞鸟，只好返航降落，乘客虚惊一场，七个半小时后再次起飞。第二篇新闻报道讲一家动物园逃跑的毒蛇刚被找回不久，又第二次溜走了。第三篇新闻报道讲杰克逊维尔市中心试行电动自行车，很受欢迎，但夜间有人不守交通规则，带来安全隐患。第一段长对话里，一男一女交流怎样教孩子存钱、花钱：常谈钱的话题、用实例让钱变得真实、零花钱和家务挂钩、开储蓄账户。第二段长对话里，主持人采访畅销书《奖励成功》的作者约翰·班克斯，讨论他用现金奖励成绩好或有进步的学生的争议提议。第一篇短文劝大家别再抱怨“我很忙”，因为人人都忙，忙只是优先次序的问题。第二篇短文讲极限运动越来越流行的原因：克服恐惧、提高专注力、锻炼不同的肌肉、消耗更多热量、增强自信。第三篇短文讲团队里的冲突是自然的，在信任的基础上，有建设性的冲突能带来创新和更多信任。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A JetBlue Airlines flight from West Palm Beach to New York City was forced to turn around and land Sunday morning after the plane struck a bird.
paras.zh: 周日上午，捷蓝航空一架从西棕榈滩飞往纽约市的航班撞上一只鸟，被迫掉头降落。

paras.en: The flight from Palm Beach International Airport to LaGuardia Airport turned around just minutes after takeoff following the strike.
paras.zh: 这架从棕榈滩国际机场飞往拉瓜迪亚机场的航班起飞才几分钟就撞了鸟，随后掉头返航。

paras.en: No injuries were reported on the plane, and the flight took off once again seven and a half hours after the first attempt.
paras.zh: 据报道，飞机上没有人受伤，第一次起飞七个半小时后，这趟航班再次起飞。

paras.en: It was like a split second of panic that resulted in this nervous reaction on the plane, said passenger Brian Healy.
paras.zh: 乘客布赖恩·希利说：“就像一瞬间的恐慌，让飞机上的人都紧张起来。”

paras.en: There was total quiet and then there was relief when the plane came to a stop.
paras.zh: 飞机停稳的时候，机舱里先是一片寂静，然后大家都松了一口气。

paras.en: An email from JetBlue read: “Our team is working to accommodate customers on later flights.”
paras.zh: 捷蓝航空在一封邮件里说：“我们的团队正在为乘客安排后面的航班。”

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn about the JetBlue Airlines flight from the news report?
paras.zh: 第一题：从这篇新闻报道中，我们对捷蓝航空的这趟航班了解到什么？

paras.en: Question two: How did the passengers feel when the plane came to a stop, according to Brian Healy?
paras.zh: 第二题：据布赖恩·希利说，飞机停下来的时候乘客们感觉怎么样？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A deadly snake which had finally been tracked down after escaping a zoo has slipped away for the second time.
paras.zh: 一条从动物园逃跑的毒蛇好不容易被找到，现在又第二次溜走了。

paras.en: The poisonous snake forced the closure of the attraction last week when staff noticed the disappearance.
paras.zh: 上周工作人员发现这条毒蛇不见了，动物园被迫关门。

paras.en: After six days of desperate searching he was eventually found and placed in a supposedly secure area.
paras.zh: 经过六天的拼命搜寻，它终于被找到，关进了一个据说很安全的地方。

w.m: adj. 拼命的；不顾一切的

paras.en: But it seems the animal is no fan of the zoo, because yet again he is out on the loose.
paras.zh: 不过看来它一点也不喜欢这家动物园，因为它又跑出去了。

paras.en: The snake is a relative newcomer to the zoo, but has already been frustrating its staff.
paras.zh: 这条蛇来动物园的时间不算长，却已经让工作人员很头疼了。

paras.en: The staff believe he squeezed himself out of a gap located around new energy-saving bulbs installed inside the snake house.
paras.zh: 工作人员认为，它是从蛇馆里新装的节能灯泡周围的缝隙里挤出去的。

paras.en: He was only found the first time around because staff brought in a special machine to trace him inside a wall opening.
paras.zh: 第一次能找到它，只是因为工作人员搬来一台专门的仪器，在墙上的一个洞里追踪到了它。

paras.en: This kind of snake is one of the most deadly and poisonous in the wild, and they can range from three to five meters in length.
paras.zh: 这种蛇是野外毒性最强、最致命的蛇之一，身长可达三到五米。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What do we learn about the deadly snake from the news report?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于这条毒蛇，我们从新闻报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question four: How have the zoo staff been feeling about the snake?
paras.zh: 第四题：动物园工作人员对这条蛇一直是什么感受？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Electric bikes have been the craze in downtown Jacksonville since they were first introduced earlier this month as a one-year pilot program.
paras.zh: 杰克逊维尔市中心本月初推出电动自行车，作为为期一年的试点项目，从那以后就火了起来。

w.m: n. 风靡一时的东西；热潮

paras.en: But they’re leading to safety concerns, mainly at night, when some riders don’t follow the rules of the road.
paras.zh: 但它们带来了安全隐患，主要是在晚上，有些骑车的人不遵守交通规则。

paras.en: As the night goes on, groups of riders are often seen traveling in just about every direction in the streets and on pedestrian paths.
paras.zh: 夜越深，越常看到一群群骑车的人在街上和人行道上横冲直撞，往哪个方向骑的都有。

paras.en: That is increasing the probability of dangerous accidents.
paras.zh: 这就增加了发生危险事故的可能性。

paras.en: Electric bike riders have to follow all the same rules as you would if you were in an automobile.
paras.zh: 骑电动自行车的人要遵守的规则，和你开汽车时要遵守的完全一样。

paras.en: That means no running red lights or traveling in the opposite direction of traffic on one-way streets.
paras.zh: 也就是说，不能闯红灯，也不能在单行道上逆行。

paras.en: City Council Member Anna Cumber was instrumental in introducing the electric bikes to Jacksonville as a way to bring new life into downtown.
paras.zh: 市议会议员安娜·坎伯在把电动自行车引进杰克逊维尔这件事上出了大力，她想借此给市中心带来新的活力。

paras.en: And she’s aware of the concerns.
paras.zh: 她也知道大家有这些担忧。

paras.en: Cumber said people can have fun, but both drivers and riders are responsible for paying attention while on the road.
paras.zh: 坎伯说，大家可以玩得开心，但无论是开车的还是骑车的，上路时都有责任集中注意力。

paras.en: And never assume the driver is going to stop or see you.
paras.zh: 而且千万不要以为司机一定会停车或者看得见你。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What do we learn from the news report about the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于杰克逊维尔引进电动自行车，我们从新闻报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question six: What are electric bike riders supposed to do?
paras.zh: 第六题：骑电动自行车的人应该怎么做？

paras.en: Question seven: Why did city council member Anna Cumber advocate the introduction of electric bikes into Jacksonville?
paras.zh: 第七题：市议会议员安娜·坎伯为什么提倡把电动自行车引进杰克逊维尔？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: What’s the best way to teach children how to save and spend their money?
paras.zh: 教孩子怎样存钱、花钱，最好的办法是什么？

paras.en: You should make money a regular topic of discussion.
paras.zh: 你应该把钱当成一个经常讨论的话题。

paras.en: It’s best to start young, so it’s instinctive rather than a scary subject.
paras.zh: 最好从小开始，这样孩子会觉得这是很自然的事，而不是一个吓人的话题。

w.m: adj. 本能的；自然而然的

paras.en: In our family, we talk openly about things like the budget for holidays, how taxes reduce your income, and how to shop around for the best deals.
paras.zh: 在我们家，我们会公开地聊一些事，比如度假的预算、税收怎样让收入变少，还有怎样货比三家买到最划算的东西。

paras.en: Indeed, it’s also essential to make money real for children through practical examples.
paras.zh: 确实，通过实际的例子让孩子觉得钱是实实在在的，这也非常重要。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；非常重要的

paras.en: Working out how much we save using discount pizza coupons, for example, is much more relevant than abstract sums.
paras.zh: 比如，算一算用比萨优惠券能省多少钱，就比抽象的算术题贴近生活得多。

w.m: adj. 相关的；切合实际的

paras.en: We also give our kids pocket money, and the amount they get is linked to chores such as putting the bins out and emptying the dishwasher.
paras.zh: 我们也给孩子零花钱，给多少跟家务挂钩，比如把垃圾桶拿出去、把洗碗机里的碗碟拿出来。

paras.en: We do that too, and it’s paid according to their age: two pounds for each year, so they can see some progression.
paras.zh: 我们也这样做，而且按年龄给，每岁两英镑，这样他们能看到钱在一年年增加。

paras.en: Teaching them to save is important.
paras.zh: 教他们存钱很重要。

paras.en: We opened a savings account when they were young.
paras.zh: 孩子很小的时候，我们就给他们开了一个储蓄账户。

paras.en: After birthdays and Christmas, they would go to the branch and deposit their gift money.
paras.zh: 过完生日和圣诞节，他们就会去银行网点，把收到的礼金存进去。

paras.en: Oh, I hadn’t considered doing that.
paras.zh: 哦，我还没想过这么做。

paras.en: In our house, we have transparent money boxes for them to put small change in so they can see their savings grow.
paras.zh: 在我们家，我们给孩子准备了透明的存钱罐，让他们把零钱放进去，这样他们能看着自己的积蓄变多。

paras.en: When the time is right, I’ll start talking to our children about investing and show them how the money saved for their further education has grown.
paras.zh: 等时机合适了，我就开始跟孩子们讲投资，让他们看看给他们存着上学深造的钱涨了多少。

paras.en: I am always talking to my elder daughter about the importance of saving into a pension.
paras.zh: 我总是跟我大女儿说，往养老金里存钱有多重要。

paras.en: She’s just started a part-time job and was thinking of not contributing to her pension.
paras.zh: 她刚开始做一份兼职，本来还打算不交养老金。

paras.en: Luckily, I managed to persuade her otherwise.
paras.zh: 幸好我把她劝过来了。

paras.en: Yes, it’s such an important lesson to learn.
paras.zh: 是啊，这一课可太重要了。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What should we do with the topic of money, according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第八题：据女士说，我们该怎样对待钱这个话题？

paras.en: Question nine: How does the woman say money can be made real for children?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士说怎样才能让孩子觉得钱是实实在在的？

paras.en: Question 10: What is the common practice between the man and the woman?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士和女士有什么共同的做法？

paras.en: Question 11: What is the woman always talking about to her elder daughter?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士总跟她大女儿说什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Welcome to Books in Review.
paras.zh: 欢迎收看《书评》节目。

paras.en: Our guest today is John Banks, the author of the best-selling new book, Rewarding Success.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是约翰·班克斯，他是畅销新书《奖励成功》的作者。

paras.en: Glad to be here, Jane.
paras.zh: 很高兴来这儿，简。

paras.en: Your book has sold two million copies, but before we discuss why it’s getting so much attention, let’s talk about your background.
paras.zh: 您的书已经卖了两百万册，不过在讨论它为什么这么受关注之前，我们先聊聊您的背景吧。

paras.en: You’re an economist and spent two decades teaching at universities?
paras.zh: 您是经济学家，在大学里教了二十年书？

paras.en: I spent twenty-five years as a professor actually, and then for the last ten years I’ve worked as a political consultant, advising politicians at the national level about problems in our country.
paras.zh: 其实我当了二十五年教授，后来这十年当政治顾问，给国家层面的政界人士出主意，解决我们国家的一些问题。

paras.en: You discuss three of those problems in the book: improving public education, reducing our nation’s health care burden, and increasing personal savings.
paras.zh: 您在书里讨论了其中三个问题：改善公共教育、减轻我们国家的医疗负担、增加个人储蓄。

paras.en: But your ideas about education are the most controversial.
paras.zh: 不过您关于教育的观点争议最大。

paras.en: Absolutely.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: A lot of people think I’m trying to punish students who aren’t doing well, when actually my goal is to give all students more incentive to succeed.
paras.zh: 很多人以为我是想惩罚学习不好的学生，其实我的目的是让所有学生都更有动力去取得成功。

paras.en: I’m not sure I agree with you.
paras.zh: 我不太确定我同意您的看法。

paras.en: Your proposal to pay cash rewards to students who get good grades is a particular problem.
paras.zh: 您提议给成绩好的学生发现金奖励，这一点问题尤其大。

paras.en: What about students who don’t get good grades?
paras.zh: 那成绩不好的学生怎么办呢？

paras.en: It seems like you’re blaming them for not succeeding, when poor performance in school isn’t a child’s fault.
paras.zh: 这好像是在怪他们没学好，可在学校表现差并不是孩子的错。

paras.en: But my proposal is not just to reward students with good grades, but also students who show improvement.
paras.zh: 可我的提议不光是奖励成绩好的学生，也奖励有进步的学生。

paras.en: Okay, another criticism of the plan is the cash rewards themselves.
paras.zh: 好，对这个计划的另一个批评就是现金奖励本身。

paras.en: Where will the money come from?
paras.zh: 钱从哪儿来呢？

paras.en: If students do better, we’ll spend less on schooling, so in the end the rewards will pay for themselves.
paras.zh: 如果学生学得更好，我们花在学校教育上的钱就会少一些，所以到头来这些奖励等于自己给自己买了单。

paras.en: What about now?
paras.zh: 那现在呢？

paras.en: How will we fund the rewards in the meantime?
paras.zh: 在这段时间里，我们拿什么来支付这些奖励？

paras.en: Well, by increasing taxes or moving money from other areas of the budget into education.
paras.zh: 嗯，可以加税，或者把预算里其他方面的钱挪到教育上来。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What do we learn about the man?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于这位男士，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the woman say is the most controversial?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士说什么争议最大？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the man say is his real goal?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士说他真正的目标是什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What will be one option for funding the proposed rewards, according to the man?
paras.zh: 第十五题：据男士说，为提议中的奖励筹钱的一个办法是什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: I met three different people today, and each time when I asked, “How are you?”
paras.zh: 我今天遇到了三个不同的人，每次我问“你好吗？”，

paras.en: the reply was exactly the same: I’m busy.
paras.zh: 得到的回答都一模一样：“我很忙。”

paras.en: Honestly, I hear the same answer from the vast majority of people I meet.
paras.zh: 说实话，我遇到的绝大多数人都是这么回答的。

paras.en: So I started to think, guess what?
paras.zh: 于是我开始想，你猜怎么着？

paras.en: Everybody’s busy.
paras.zh: 每个人都很忙。

paras.en: I’m busy.
paras.zh: 我很忙。

paras.en: You’re busy.
paras.zh: 你很忙。

paras.en: Everybody’s busy.
paras.zh: 每个人都很忙。

paras.en: So you being busy doesn’t make me sympathetic at all because busy is the state of the world.
paras.zh: 所以你忙一点也不会让我同情你，因为忙就是这个世界的常态。

paras.en: So I’m launching a campaign to stop people complaining about being busy.
paras.zh: 所以我要发起一场运动，让大家别再抱怨自己忙。

paras.en: It may sound harsh, but the truth is nobody cares.
paras.zh: 这话听起来可能有点刺耳，可事实是，没人在乎。

paras.en: In a busy world, being busy doesn’t stand out, nor does it mean productive, creative, accomplished, or professional.
paras.zh: 在一个人人都忙的世界里，忙并不显得突出，也不代表高效、有创造力、有成就或者专业。

w.m: adj. 有成就的；有才艺的

paras.en: Steve Maraboli once said, When someone tells you they are too busy, it’s not a reflection of their schedule, it’s a reflection of your spot on their schedule.
paras.zh: 史蒂夫·马拉博利说过：“当有人告诉你他们太忙时，这反映的不是他们的日程，而是你在他们日程里的位置。”

paras.en: Donna Lynne Hope has also remarked, Busy doesn’t mean better.
paras.zh: 唐娜·琳恩·霍普也说过：“忙不代表更好。”

paras.en: I have never envied a busy person, the one who likes to point out their busy lives to others.
paras.zh: 我从来没羡慕过忙碌的人，也就是那种喜欢跟别人显摆自己有多忙的人。

paras.en: The reality is, nobody’s too busy.
paras.zh: 实际上，没有人真的忙到那个地步。

paras.en: It’s just about priorities.
paras.zh: 这只是优先次序的问题。

paras.en: So the next time someone asks you how you are, maybe respond differently.
paras.zh: 所以下次有人问你过得怎么样，也许可以换个说法回答。

paras.en: In my experience, the I’m busy response is really covering up the fact that they’re not actually accomplishing their real purpose, and being busy is the lie they tell themselves about why they can’t achieve it.
paras.zh: 依我的经验，回答“我很忙”，其实是在掩盖一个事实：他们并没有真正去完成自己真正的目标，而“忙”只是他们给自己找的、解释为什么做不到的谎言。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: Why is the speaker launching a campaign?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人为什么要发起一场运动？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the speaker advise us to do next time someone asks us how we are?
paras.zh: 第十七题：下次有人问我们过得怎么样，说话人建议我们怎么做？

paras.en: Question 18: Why do many people make the I’m busy response, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十八题：据说话人说，很多人为什么会回答“我很忙”？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: More and more people are taking up extreme sports like snowboarding, skateboarding, mountain biking, and many more.
paras.zh: 越来越多的人开始玩极限运动，比如单板滑雪、滑板、山地自行车等等。

paras.en: Why are these sports becoming so popular?
paras.zh: 这些运动为什么越来越受欢迎呢？

paras.en: One thing that extreme sports do better than perhaps anything else is to help you stop being afraid.
paras.zh: 极限运动有一点也许比其他任何东西都做得好，那就是帮你不再害怕。

paras.en: It may sound strange to say that their main function is to induce fear, but after a time, your fear response to other things in life will be dramatically reduced.
paras.zh: 说极限运动的主要作用是让人害怕，这听起来可能有点奇怪，但过一段时间，你对生活中其他事情的恐惧反应会大大减轻。

paras.en: After all, if you can jump out of a plane or off a bridge, then you can face anything else easily.
paras.zh: 毕竟，如果你敢从飞机上或桥上跳下去，那别的事你都能轻松面对。

paras.en: When doing extreme sports, you have to become more focused.
paras.zh: 玩极限运动的时候，你必须更加专注。

paras.en: You’ll be pushed to your limits, and if you aren’t focused, you’ll make dangerous mistakes.
paras.zh: 你会被逼到自己的极限，要是不专注，就会犯危险的错误。

paras.en: Learning to be this focused when enjoying extreme sports will help you to be focused at work, keeping you more productive and ultimately more successful.
paras.zh: 玩极限运动时学会这样专注，能帮你在工作中也保持专注，让你更高效，最终也更成功。

paras.en: It’s great to stay fit and healthy, but standard exercise routines and sports only work the same muscles repeatedly.
paras.zh: 保持健康、身材好当然很棒，但常规的锻炼和运动只会反复练同样的肌肉。

paras.en: With extreme sports, you’ll be working entirely different muscles, and that means you get an all-over workout.
paras.zh: 玩极限运动，你练的是完全不同的肌肉，也就是说你得到的是全身锻炼。

paras.en: Extreme sports also burn a lot more calories than other sports.
paras.zh: 极限运动消耗的热量也比其他运动多得多。

paras.en: Skateboarding, for example, can burn as many as 500 calories per hour.
paras.zh: 比如滑板，每小时能消耗多达五百卡路里。

paras.en: Basketball burns around 300 in the same time.
paras.zh: 打篮球同样的时间大约消耗三百卡路里。

paras.en: When you find that you can overcome the physical or mental challenges involved in extreme sports, you’ll feel superhuman and your self-confidence will be at an all-time high.
paras.zh: 当你发现自己能战胜极限运动中身体上或心理上的挑战时，你会觉得自己像超人一样，自信心也会达到前所未有的高度。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What may sound strange to say about extreme sports?
paras.zh: 第十九题：说极限运动的哪一点听起来可能有点奇怪？

paras.en: Question 20: Why should one be highly focused when doing extreme sports?
paras.zh: 第二十题：玩极限运动时为什么要高度专注？

paras.en: Question 21: How can extreme sports benefit us more than standard exercise routines and sports?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：和常规的锻炼和运动相比，极限运动怎样让我们受益更多？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Most of us have been in teams or organizations where we’ve had conflict with the people that we’re working with around the ideas or decisions that we’re discussing.
paras.zh: 我们大多数人都待过这样的团队或组织：在讨论想法或决定时，我们和一起工作的人发生过冲突。

paras.en: Conflict is natural.
paras.zh: 冲突是很自然的。

paras.en: We all bring different life and work experiences to the table.
paras.zh: 我们每个人带来的生活和工作经历都不一样。

paras.en: We all have different personality preferences and tendencies.
paras.zh: 我们每个人的性格偏好和倾向都不一样。

paras.en: We’re not all going to have the same ideas on how to approach policies, programs, or problems.
paras.zh: 在怎样处理政策、项目或问题上，我们不会都有同样的想法。

paras.en: But too often we get caught in this place where conflict is perceived to be negative, something we want to avoid so that we can maintain the harmony of our workplace.
paras.zh: 可我们常常陷入这样的处境：冲突被看成坏事，是我们想避开的东西，好维持工作场所的和谐。

paras.en: This could be because some people want to avoid conflict at all costs.
paras.zh: 这可能是因为有些人想不惜一切代价避免冲突。

paras.en: After all, they still have to work together.
paras.zh: 毕竟，他们还得一起共事。

paras.en: But this kind of artificial harmony isn’t the answer.
paras.zh: 但这种人为的和谐并不是解决办法。

paras.en: Productive conflict is a vital part of teams and organizations that want to push forward and do more.
paras.zh: 对想要往前走、做更多事的团队和组织来说，有建设性的冲突是至关重要的一部分。

w.m: adj. 富有成效的；有建设性的

paras.en: Without conflict, we’re often stuck in this artificial harmony where people don’t express potentially innovative ideas for fear that they may start conflict with others.
paras.zh: 没有冲突，我们常常困在这种人为的和谐里，大家不敢说出可能有创新性的想法，怕跟别人起冲突。

paras.en: But if you’re in a place where you have a basis of trust, conflict can be extremely productive.
paras.zh: 但如果你所在的地方有信任作为基础，冲突就可能非常有成效。

paras.en: It can lead to increased innovation and greater trust on teams.
paras.zh: 它能带来更多创新，让团队成员之间更加信任。

paras.en: It may be an uncomfortable process, but good leaders and healthy teams recognize that productive and healthy conflict is an important part of how they function.
paras.zh: 这个过程可能让人不太舒服，但好的领导者和健康的团队都明白，有建设性的、健康的冲突是他们运作中很重要的一部分。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What does the passage say about conflict in organizations?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于组织中的冲突，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: Why do some people want to avoid conflict at all costs?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：有些人为什么想不惜一切代价避免冲突？

paras.en: Question 24: Why is productive conflict important for teams and organizations?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：有建设性的冲突为什么对团队和组织很重要？

paras.en: Question 25: What does productive conflict need as a basis?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：有建设性的冲突需要什么作为基础？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2024年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲诺沃克主街上一栋三层楼起火，四套公寓因烟熏和高温受损、没法再住，六名住户只好搬走，消防部门正在调查起火原因。第二篇新闻报道讲一项针对欧洲七万多名老年人的新研究，没有发现出生月份和抑郁、焦虑症状之间有明显关系。第三篇新闻报道讲中国科研人员克隆了一只明星警犬，克隆犬表现出色，有望大大缩短警犬的训练时间。第一段长对话里，艾丽斯向忙着写论文的汤姆推荐科幻小说《三体》，建议他先读书、再看即将开播的电视剧。第二段长对话里，种有机蔬菜的女士打电话询问素食美食节招摊主的事，男士菲利普介绍了申请办法、截止日期和邮寄地址。第一篇短文讲英国野营热：原因、带来的垃圾问题，以及野营者应守的规矩。第二篇短文介绍亚马孙河的粉红海豚：体型大、雄性身上的粉色从何而来，以及它们的栖息地受到国际保护。第三篇短文讲一项调查：大多数刚成年的年轻人都接受父母的经济资助，他们认为经济独立才算真正成年，助学贷款是他们手头紧的一大原因。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet One with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Six people had to move away from their home to another place after a fire broke out in a building on Main Street Saturday, officials said.
paras.zh: 官员们说，周六主街上的一栋楼起火，六个人只好搬出家，住到别的地方去。

paras.en: Firefighters responded to the three-story building shortly after one PM for a reported structure fire, according to Norwalk deputy fire chief Adam Markowitz.
paras.zh: 据诺沃克消防局副局长亚当·马尔科维茨说，下午一点刚过，消防员接到报警说有建筑物起火，赶到了这栋三层楼。

paras.en: Markowitz said crews encountered heavy smoke coming from the second floor when they arrived.
paras.zh: 马尔科维茨说，消防队员赶到时，看到二楼冒出滚滚浓烟。

paras.en: A team of about twenty-five firefighters then spent about twenty-five minutes extinguishing the flames.
paras.zh: 随后，大约二十五名消防员花了二十五分钟左右把火扑灭。

paras.en: Officials described the structure as a mixed-use building that features commercial businesses on the first floor and residential on the second and third floors.
paras.zh: 官员们说，这是一栋商住两用楼，一楼是商铺，二楼和三楼是住宅。

paras.en: Town records list four apartments in the building.
paras.zh: 镇上的记录显示这栋楼里有四套公寓。

paras.en: Due to smoke and heat damage, the four apartments were declared uninhabitable and the six residents had to move to another place, officials said.
paras.zh: 官员们说，由于烟熏和高温造成的损坏，这四套公寓被认定不适合居住，六名住户只好搬到别处。

paras.en: No injuries were reported in connection with the fire.
paras.zh: 据报道，这场火灾没有造成人员受伤。

paras.en: The Norwalk Fire Marshal is investigating the cause and origin of the fire.
paras.zh: 诺沃克消防监察官正在调查这场火灾的起因和起火点。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: Why did the six residents have to find another place to stay?
paras.zh: 第一题：这六名住户为什么只好另找地方住？

paras.en: Question 2: What does the news report say the Norwalk Fire Marshal is doing?
paras.zh: 第二题：新闻报道说诺沃克消防监察官正在做什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A new study has cast doubt on historic research suggesting that the season or month of someone’s birth is associated with an increased risk of certain mental health conditions.
paras.zh: 以前有研究认为，一个人出生的季节或月份与某些心理健康问题的风险升高有关，现在一项新研究让人对这一点产生了怀疑。

paras.en: The study looks at symptoms of anxiety and depression among more than seventy thousand older adults in Europe.
paras.zh: 这项研究调查了欧洲七万多名老年人的焦虑和抑郁症状。

paras.en: A number of past studies have found the link between season of birth and mental health diagnoses.
paras.zh: 过去的许多研究发现，出生季节和心理健康诊断之间有关联。

paras.en: Researchers have suggested that such links could arise from various things.
paras.zh: 研究人员提出，这种关联可能来自各种因素。

paras.en: These include nutrient intake, sun exposure, climate and disease exposure varying across the course of the year.
paras.zh: 这些因素包括营养摄入、日晒、气候和接触疾病的情况，它们在一年中会不断变化。

paras.en: However, evidence has been mixed.
paras.zh: 不过，证据并不一致。

w.m: adj. 混杂的；好坏不一的

paras.en: More recent studies have suggested that factors such as social class or economic background have more to do with these diagnoses than month of birth.
paras.zh: 近期更多的研究认为，社会阶层或经济背景之类的因素，跟这些诊断的关系比出生月份更大。

paras.en: Overall, the new study found no significant relationship between participants’ month of birth and symptoms of depression or anxiety.
paras.zh: 总的来说，新研究没有发现参与者的出生月份与抑郁或焦虑症状之间有明显的关系。

paras.en: There was some variability in some countries.
paras.zh: 有些国家存在一些差异。

paras.en: In Poland, depressive symptoms fluctuated a little depending on birth month.
paras.zh: 在波兰，抑郁症状随出生月份略有波动。

paras.en: In the Czech Republic the same was true of anxiety symptoms, but on the whole there was no systematic pattern.
paras.zh: 在捷克，焦虑症状也是这样，但总的来看，并没有系统的规律。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What have a number of past studies found about season of birth?
paras.zh: 第三题：过去的许多研究在出生季节方面有什么发现？

paras.en: Question four: What did the new study find about the relationship between participants’ month of birth and symptoms of depression?
paras.zh: 第四题：新研究对参与者的出生月份与抑郁症状之间的关系有什么发现？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Genetic researchers in China have made a clone of a star police dog.
paras.zh: 中国的遗传学研究人员克隆了一只明星警犬。

paras.en: The clone was born in a laboratory in Beijing in December.
paras.zh: 这只克隆犬十二月在北京的一个实验室出生。

paras.en: Tests show that the clone and her mother are almost identical genetically.
paras.zh: 检测显示，克隆犬和它的“母亲”在基因上几乎一模一样。

paras.en: The mother dog helped solve multiple murders and many other crimes.
paras.zh: 这只“母亲”警犬曾帮助破获多起凶杀案和许多其他案件。

paras.en: The clone has already performed better than traditionally bred dogs on several tests.
paras.zh: 在好几项测试中，这只克隆犬的表现已经比用传统方法繁育的狗要好。

paras.en: If the clone continues to perform as well as expected, it could mean a huge reduction in the training time for police dogs, which usually takes about five years.
paras.zh: 如果克隆犬能像预期那样一直表现出色，警犬的训练时间就可能大大缩短，而通常训练要花五年左右。

paras.en: The ultimate goal of scientists is to produce clones of talented police dogs that can be trained in months instead of years.
paras.zh: 科学家的最终目标是克隆出有天赋的警犬，只要几个月而不是几年就能训练好。

paras.en: However, this goal is not yet possible due to the current costs of the technology.
paras.zh: 不过，由于眼下这项技术成本太高，这个目标还没法实现。

paras.en: This is not the first time a clone has been made of a star police dog.
paras.zh: 这已经不是第一次克隆明星警犬了。

paras.en: In South Korea six clones began working with the police in two thousand eight.
paras.zh: 在韩国，六只克隆犬在二〇〇八年就开始跟警方一起工作了。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do the researchers’ tests show about the cloned dog?
paras.zh: 第五题：研究人员的检测显示了这只克隆犬的什么情况？

paras.en: Question six: What is the scientist’s purpose in cloning police dogs?
paras.zh: 第六题：科学家克隆警犬的目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 7: Why does the news report say the scientist’s goal is not yet possible?
paras.zh: 第七题：新闻报道为什么说科学家的目标还没法实现？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet One, with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Tom, did you see the article online about the new TV series based on the book The Three-Body Problem?
paras.zh: 汤姆，你看到网上那篇文章了吗？讲的是根据《三体》这本书改编的新电视剧。

paras.en: A colleague mentioned the book, but I’ve been so busy writing my thesis that I haven’t been able to read for pleasure in months.
paras.zh: 有个同事提过这本书，可我一直忙着写论文，好几个月都没空看闲书了。

paras.en: Well, sounds like if you’re going to read anything for fun, this is the book.
paras.zh: 嗯，听起来你要是想读点书消遣，就该读这本。

paras.en: It’s written by a Chinese science fiction writer.
paras.zh: 它是一位中国科幻作家写的。

paras.en: I can’t remember his name, but he’s written three books in all, and The Three-Body Problem is the first in the series.
paras.zh: 我记不起他的名字了，不过他一共写了三本，《三体》是这个系列的第一本。

paras.en: I don’t want to say too much and spoil it for you, but it’s definitely got some amazing technological and sociological concepts in it.
paras.zh: 我不想说太多，免得给你剧透，不过书里确实有一些很了不起的科技和社会学概念。

w.m: v. 破坏；（提前透露情节）扫兴

paras.en: It does sound like it would suit my taste, but if they are making a TV series based on it now, I don’t know if I should read the book or watch the show first.
paras.zh: 听起来确实合我的口味，不过既然现在要根据它拍电视剧，我不知道该先看书还是先看剧。

paras.en: I think it’s better to read the book first.
paras.zh: 我觉得最好先看书。

paras.en: It’s rare for the show or movie to be better than the book, and then you just end up ruining the book for yourself if the show isn’t very good.
paras.zh: 电视剧或电影比原著好看的情况很少，要是剧拍得不怎么样，你最后就把这本书给毁了。

paras.en: When is the show supposed to start?
paras.zh: 这部剧什么时候开播？

paras.en: I’m a bit overwhelmed with the amount of data I still need to collect to finish my thesis.
paras.zh: 我还有一大堆数据要收集才能写完论文，有点忙不过来。

paras.en: But I still need to relax sometimes.
paras.zh: 不过我有时候还是得放松一下。

paras.en: I can’t remember exactly.
paras.zh: 我记不太清了。

paras.en: It’s pretty soon, and it’s going to be quite long.
paras.zh: 很快就播了，而且会挺长的。

paras.en: There are twenty-four episodes.
paras.zh: 一共有二十四集。

paras.en: Well, maybe you could download an electronic copy of the book and try to read it before the show starts.
paras.zh: 嗯，也许你可以下载这本书的电子版，争取在开播前读完。

paras.en: That’s a good idea, and then maybe we can watch the series together.
paras.zh: 好主意，然后也许我们可以一起看这部剧。

paras.en: Thanks for the tip, Alice.
paras.zh: 谢谢你的建议，艾丽斯。

paras.en: No problem.
paras.zh: 不客气。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: How did the man get to know about the book The Three-Body Problem?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士是怎么知道《三体》这本书的？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman say she can’t remember about the book’s author?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士说她记不起这本书作者的什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the man have to do to finish his thesis?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士要写完论文得做什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What will the man most probably do first after the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十一题：对话结束后，男士最有可能先做什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hello, good afternoon.
paras.zh: 喂，下午好。

paras.en: I have an inquiry to make.
paras.zh: 我想打听点事。

paras.en: It’s about the Vegetarian Food Festival you are holding on the nineteenth of August at the Newcastle City Hall.
paras.zh: 是关于你们八月十九日在纽卡斯尔市政厅举办的素食美食节。

paras.en: Yes, of course.
paras.zh: 是的，当然可以。

paras.en: My name’s Philip.
paras.zh: 我叫菲利普。

paras.en: How can I help you?
paras.zh: 有什么可以帮您的？

paras.en: It says on your website that you are still looking for vendors, and I grow organic vegetables on my farm, as well as doing my own home baking.
paras.zh: 你们网站上说，你们还在招摊主，我在自己的农场里种有机蔬菜，还自己在家烤面包点心。

paras.en: Would I be able to sell both the vegetables and items baked from them at the festival?
paras.zh: 我能在美食节上既卖蔬菜，又卖用这些蔬菜烤的点心吗？

paras.en: That’s exactly the type of thing we are looking for.
paras.zh: 这正是我们要找的那类东西。

paras.en: We are getting close to the deadline, however.
paras.zh: 不过，截止日期快到了。

paras.en: Do you prefer to fill out an application on the web or to print it out and fill it in by hand and then post it back to us?
paras.zh: 您是想在网上填申请表，还是打印出来手写填好，再寄回给我们？

paras.en: Remember that you will have to have all your certificates to hand when you are filling out the forms as the standards are high and they will be carefully checked before anyone will be able to sell their produce at the event.
paras.zh: 记住，填表的时候您得把所有证书都准备好，因为标准很高，任何人要在活动上卖农产品，证书都会被仔细检查。

paras.en: I should be fine with doing it on your website, and I already have all my certificates, as we run a small farm shop, too.
paras.zh: 我在你们网站上填应该没问题，所有证书我都有，因为我们也开了一家农场小店。

paras.en: But can you give me your details anyway?
paras.zh: 不过您还是能把你们的详细联系方式给我吗？

paras.en: Sure.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: Please address it to The Organic Organization Vendor Applications, one hundred and twelve Queens Road, Newcastle, Northumbria.
paras.zh: 请寄到诺森伯兰郡纽卡斯尔皇后路一百一十二号，有机组织摊主申请处收。

paras.en: The postcode is NU twenty nine three L J. Remember that the closing date is next Tuesday, the twenty eighth of June.
paras.zh: 邮编是NU二九三LJ。记住，截止日期是下周二，六月二十八日。

paras.en: That’s absolutely wonderful.
paras.zh: 那太好了。

paras.en: Thank you so much for your help.
paras.zh: 太谢谢您的帮助了。

paras.en: Goodbye.
paras.zh: 再见。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: Why does the woman call the man?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士为什么给男士打电话？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What is the man still looking for?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士还在找什么？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the man say they are getting close to?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士说什么快到了？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the man finally ask the woman to remember?
paras.zh: 第十五题：男士最后让女士记住什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Supporters call it wild camping; opponents call it illegal camping.
paras.zh: 支持的人管它叫野外露营，反对的人管它叫非法露营。

paras.en: What both sides accept is that there has been a boom in the past few months, with increasing numbers of visitors pitching their tents on any bit of land they fancy in the UK.
paras.zh: 双方都承认的是，过去几个月野营突然火了起来，越来越多的游客在英国随便找块看中的地就搭起帐篷。

paras.en: In part, this reflects the fact that official campsites have been wholly or partially closed or are overflowing in a summer when fewer people are going abroad.
paras.zh: 这在一定程度上是因为，正规营地有的全部关闭、有的部分关闭，有的又人满为患，而这个夏天出国的人又比较少。

paras.en: It is also cheap at a time when many are worried about what the economic future holds.
paras.zh: 而且在很多人担心经济前景的时候，野营也很便宜。

paras.en: But it may also be an expression of a desire for going outdoors, a response to the months of lockdown.
paras.zh: 不过，这也可能表明人们渴望走到户外，是对几个月封控的一种反应。

paras.en: Most of the coverage of the boom in wild camping has been negative.
paras.zh: 媒体对野营热的报道大多是负面的。

paras.en: Camping in public parks has now been banned for August and the early part of September because campers dump litter, human waste and even their tents on the grassland.
paras.zh: 现在八月和九月上旬已经禁止在公园里露营，因为露营的人把垃圾、人的排泄物甚至帐篷都扔在草地上。

paras.en: Similar action has been taken even in Scotland, where camping is usually permitted on most of its open land.
paras.zh: 就连苏格兰也采取了类似的措施，而苏格兰的大部分开阔地通常是允许露营的。

paras.en: Clearly there have to be rules.
paras.zh: 显然，必须有规矩。

paras.en: It would make sense that wild campers need to ask for permission to camp from land owners, especially outside Scotland where the law is far more restrictive.
paras.zh: 野营的人应该先征得土地主人的同意再露营，这是合情合理的，尤其是在苏格兰以外的地方，那里的法律要严格得多。

paras.en: It would be common sense for people to use small tents and leave no trace of their visit.
paras.zh: 人们用小帐篷、走的时候不留下任何痕迹，这本来就是常识。

paras.en: They have been attracted by a patch of land that is close to wilderness, and it is their responsibility to keep it that way.
paras.zh: 吸引他们的是一块接近荒野的土地，他们有责任让它一直保持原样。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: Why has wild camping become popular in the UK?
paras.zh: 第十六题：野外露营为什么在英国火了起来？

paras.en: Question 17: Why is camping banned for part of the summer in public parks?
paras.zh: 第十七题：夏天的一段时间里，公园为什么禁止露营？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker suggest campers do?
paras.zh: 第十八题：说话人建议露营的人怎么做？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Imagine boating down the Amazon River, minding your own business, calmly keeping an eye out for alarmingly large snakes, and a curious pink dolphin appears to swim alongside.
paras.zh: 想象一下，你正乘船顺着亚马孙河往下游走，不去管别的事，只是平静地留意着大得吓人的蛇，这时，一只好奇的粉红海豚出现了，游在船边。

paras.en: While this may seem like a mythical creature, pink dolphins do exist in the Amazon region.
paras.zh: 这听起来也许像神话里的动物，但亚马孙地区真的有粉红海豚。

paras.en: The Amazon river dolphin is a giant among its species.
paras.zh: 亚马孙河豚是同类中的大块头。

paras.en: It can measure up to two meters long and weigh around two hundred and four kilograms.
paras.zh: 它身长可达两米，体重大约两百零四千克。

paras.en: Size isn’t the only thing that sets the Amazon River Dolphin apart.
paras.zh: 让亚马孙河豚与众不同的，不只是它的体型。

paras.en: Thriving in South American rivers and temporary lakes caused by seasonal flooding, this freshwater dolphin is sometimes shockingly pink.
paras.zh: 这种淡水海豚生活在南美洲的河流和季节性洪水形成的临时湖泊里，有时粉得让人吃惊。

paras.en: Although born gray, males of the species are easily identified as they enter adulthood by a decisive pink shade.
paras.zh: 这种海豚生下来是灰色的，但雄性长大成年后，身上会有一种明显的粉色，很容易认出来。

paras.en: Their unusual colouring is believed to be the result of scar tissue from dolphin fights, whether play fighting or a serious bid for a mate.
paras.zh: 人们认为，它们这种不寻常的颜色是海豚打斗留下的伤疤组织造成的，不管是闹着玩的打斗，还是为争夺配偶而认真打的架。

paras.en: The deeper the pink, the more attractive the males are believed to be, and the older the male, the more pink he will have.
paras.zh: 人们认为，粉色越深，雄性就越有吸引力，而且雄性年纪越大，身上的粉色也越多。

paras.en: There is also a theory that this colour helps the dolphins more readily blend in with their surroundings.
paras.zh: 还有一种说法是，这种颜色能帮海豚更容易地融入周围的环境。

paras.en: During heavy rains, rivers along the Amazon rainforest turn a pink shade, and with their pink coloring, male dolphins are harder to detect.
paras.zh: 下大雨的时候，亚马孙雨林里的河流会变成粉色，雄性海豚有了一身粉色，就更难被发现。

paras.en: The Amazon wetlands system, fed by the Amazon River, is a crucial place for pink dolphins to breed, and since 2018 has been granted internationally protected status.
paras.zh: 亚马孙湿地系统由亚马孙河供水，是粉红海豚繁殖的关键地方，二〇一八年起已获得国际保护地位。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the passage say about pink dolphins?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于粉红海豚，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What is the unusual colouring of pink dolphins believed to originate in?
paras.zh: 第二十题：人们认为粉红海豚不寻常的颜色是从哪儿来的？

paras.en: Question 21: What has become of the Amazon wetland system since 2018?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：二〇一八年以来，亚马孙湿地系统怎么样了？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: In a new Merrill Lynch Age Wave survey, a full seventy per cent of the early adults said they’ve received financial support from their parents in the past year, and fifty-eight per cent said they couldn’t afford their current lifestyles without it.
paras.zh: 在美林证券和老龄浪潮公司的一项新调查中，足足百分之七十刚成年的年轻人说，过去一年里他们从父母那儿得到过经济资助，百分之五十八的人说，没有这些资助，他们负担不起现在的生活方式。

paras.en: The most common types of financial support include cell phone plans, food, school costs and car expenses.
paras.zh: 最常见的经济资助包括手机套餐、伙食、上学费用和用车开销。

paras.en: Parental financial support of early adults, said Ken Dychtwald, CEO of Age Wave, is the new normal.
paras.zh: 老龄浪潮公司首席执行官肯·迪赫特瓦尔德说，父母在经济上资助刚成年的孩子，已经成了新常态。

paras.en: But sixty-four per cent of the young adults surveyed said parents’ financial support to children aged twenty five to thirty four is a bad thing because it makes those kids dependent.
paras.zh: 但在接受调查的年轻人里，百分之六十四的人说，父母在经济上资助二十五到三十四岁的子女是坏事，因为这会让孩子产生依赖。

paras.en: By contrast, only twenty nine per cent thought supporting men and women aged eighteen to twenty-four is bad; the remaining seventy-one per cent thought that assistance helps the adult children get ahead.
paras.zh: 相比之下，只有百分之二十九的人认为资助十八到二十四岁的年轻人是坏事，其余百分之七十一的人认为这种帮助能让成年子女取得成功。

paras.en: Dychtwald believes the young women and men surveyed were saying that by twenty five young adults ought to be financially independent.
paras.zh: 迪赫特瓦尔德认为，接受调查的年轻人的意思是，到了二十五岁，年轻人就应该在经济上独立。

paras.en: In fact, the respondents said financial independence defines adulthood.
paras.zh: 事实上，受访者说，经济独立才算真正成年。

paras.en: Financial independence is something they were struggling with and challenged by, and it scared them a bit, Dychtwald said.
paras.zh: 迪赫特瓦尔德说：“经济独立是他们正在努力争取、觉得很有挑战的事，这让他们有点害怕。”

paras.en: One big reason they are struggling is attributed to college loans, of which the average amounts to thirty seven thousand dollars.
paras.zh: 他们手头紧的一大原因在于助学贷款，平均每人欠三万七千美元。

paras.en: Many of the parents have taken on college loans for the kids too, sometimes at the expense of their own finances.
paras.zh: 很多父母也替孩子背上了助学贷款，有时甚至牺牲了自己的财务状况。

paras.en: In the survey, sixty per cent of early adults define financial success as being debt-free.
paras.zh: 在这项调查中，百分之六十刚成年的年轻人把经济上的成功定义为没有债务。

paras.en: Whether that’s likely or even possible any time soon is anyone’s guess.
paras.zh: 这在近期能不能实现，甚至有没有可能，谁也说不准。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do we learn from a new survey by Merrill Lynch Age Wave?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：从美林证券和老龄浪潮公司的一项新调查中，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty three: Why did most young adults in the survey say financial support to children aged 25 to 34 is a bad thing?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：调查中的大多数年轻人为什么说，在经济上资助二十五到三十四岁的子女是坏事？

paras.en: Question 24: What did the respondents in the survey say regarding financial independence?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于经济独立，调查中的受访者是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 25: What is one big reason young adults are struggling?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：年轻人手头紧的一大原因是什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
