passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲费耶特维尔市在新设立的公交司机感谢日前夕表彰本市服务时间最长的公交司机雪莉·克里斯蒂安，她开了二十五年校车。第二篇新闻报道讲威尔顿学校董事会提出把预算增加百分之五点九九，教师工资是预算的大头，而学生人数减少意味着联邦和州的拨款也会减少。第三篇新闻报道讲苏格兰出现罕见的雷雪天气，当地居民以为听到了爆炸声纷纷报警，恶劣天气还影响了道路和铁路。第一段长对话里，男士打算刷信用卡再买一部新手机，女士劝他别这样，以免养成借钱消费的坏习惯。第二段长对话里，节目主持人玛丽采访博主鲍勃·琼斯，聊微型住宅运动怎样帮人们买得起房、保护环境。第一篇短文讲每天的体育活动对孩子的好处：增强自信、锻炼运动技能、改善情绪，并养成终身运动的习惯。第二篇短文讲一项研究：招聘信息里公布公司的多元化情况，求职者甚至愿意考虑工资较低的工作。第三篇短文讲俄勒冈州立大学的研究发现，狗会配合家里孩子的行为，但狗和孩子的关系还有很多需要了解。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news reports and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The city of Fayetteville is making a special effort to recognize its bus drivers ahead of the newly proclaimed Transit Driver Appreciation Day happening Saturday.
paras.zh: 费耶特维尔市正在专门表彰本市的公交司机，因为新设立的公交司机感谢日就在这个星期六。

paras.en: As part of the event, the city is celebrating its longest serving driver on the Force.
paras.zh: 作为活动的一部分，市里正在表彰司机队伍里服务时间最长的一位司机。

paras.en: That driver is Sherry Christian.
paras.zh: 这位司机就是雪莉·克里斯蒂安。

paras.en: Christian has been a driver for twenty-five years.
paras.zh: 克里斯蒂安已经当了二十五年司机。

paras.en: The Fayetteville native believes driving a school bus allows her to give back to her community.
paras.zh: 这位土生土长的费耶特维尔人认为，开校车让她能够回报自己的社区。

w.m: n. 本地人；土生土长的人

paras.en: She says that the best part of the job is watching the children who ride her bus grow up.
paras.zh: 她说，这份工作最棒的地方是看着坐她车的孩子们一天天长大。

paras.en: Transit Driver Appreciation Day has been celebrated across the country as far back as two thousand nine.
paras.zh: 早在二〇〇九年，全国各地就开始庆祝公交司机感谢日了。

paras.en: However, this week the city of Fayetteville issued a proclamation for the day to take place March 18th.
paras.zh: 不过，这个星期费耶特维尔市发布公告，把这一天定在三月十八日。

paras.en: Officials said they want bus drivers to know how important they are to Fayetteville, serving almost 1.6 million riders a year.
paras.zh: 官员们说，他们想让公交司机知道自己对费耶特维尔有多重要，他们每年为将近一百六十万人次的乘客服务。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn about Sherry Christian?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于雪莉·克里斯蒂安，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question two: What did city officials of Fayetteville want bus drivers to be aware of?
paras.zh: 第二题：费耶特维尔市的官员想让公交司机意识到什么？

paras.en: News report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The Wilton School Board has proposed a 5.99% spending increase.
paras.zh: 威尔顿学校董事会提议把开支增加百分之五点九九。

paras.en: If approved, it would be the largest jump in at least eight budget cycles.
paras.zh: 如果获得批准，这将是至少八个预算周期以来最大的一次增幅。

paras.en: The 5.99% request more than doubles the highest previous year over year increase in the last eight years, which was 2.99% for the twenty twenty-one to twenty twenty-two school year.
paras.zh: 百分之五点九九的申请比过去八年里最高的同比增幅高出一倍多，那次是二〇二一至二〇二二学年的百分之二点九九。

paras.en: The biggest driver of the 91.8 million dollar proposed budget remains teachers’ salaries.
paras.zh: 这份九千一百八十万美元的预算提案里，最主要的开支仍然是教师工资。

w.m: n. 驱动因素；主要因素

paras.en: These account for sixty-four percent of the total request at fifty-nine million dollars.
paras.zh: 教师工资占总申请金额的百分之六十四，共五千九百万美元。

paras.en: The fifty-nine million dollars is up from the 56.7 million dollars budgeted for the current school year.
paras.zh: 这五千九百万美元比本学年预算的五千六百七十万美元有所增加。

paras.en: There are some factors that could affect the budget moving forward.
paras.zh: 今后有一些因素可能会影响预算。

paras.en: One of those is total enrolment.
paras.zh: 其中之一是学生总人数。

w.m: n. 入学人数；注册人数

paras.en: The district will have a total enrolment of 3,742 students.
paras.zh: 这个学区的学生总数将达到三千七百四十二人。

w.m: n. 入学人数；注册人数

paras.en: Almost all of these students will be in kindergarten through high school, but 66 will be in pre-kindergarten and other programs.
paras.zh: 这些学生几乎都在幼儿园到高中阶段，但有六十六人会在学前班和其他项目里。

paras.en: This represents forty-seven fewer students than the current year.
paras.zh: 这比本学年少了四十七名学生。

paras.en: Fewer students mean less federal and state funding.
paras.zh: 学生少了，联邦和州的拨款也就少了。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What does the news report say the Wilton School Board has done?
paras.zh: 第三题：新闻报道说威尔顿学校董事会做了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What will a decline in the total enrollment lead to?
paras.zh: 第四题：学生总人数减少会导致什么？

w.m: n. 入学人数；注册人数

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A rare thunder snow event has taken place in Scotland, and alarmed locals contacted police thinking they had heard bombs going off.
paras.zh: 苏格兰出现了罕见的雷雪天气，受惊的当地人以为听到了炸弹爆炸，纷纷报警。

paras.en: The phenomenon happens when thunder and lightning mix with a heavy snowstorm, sometimes causing loud claps that can be confused with explosions.
paras.zh: 雷电和暴风雪交织在一起时就会出现这种现象，有时会发出很响的炸裂声，容易被误认为是爆炸。

paras.en: One person described it as a loud boom, similar to a plane crash.
paras.zh: 有人形容那是一声巨响，就像飞机坠毁一样。

paras.en: Another person was woken up in the middle of the night by what he thought was early construction work starting.
paras.zh: 还有人半夜被吵醒，以为是一大早就开工的施工。

paras.en: The noise was powerful enough to shake buildings and set off car alarms.
paras.zh: 这声音大得能震动楼房，还让汽车警报器响了起来。

paras.en: The police were flooded with many calls from the public, and they sent out a message asking people to remain calm.
paras.zh: 警方接到了公众打来的大量电话，随后发布消息，请大家保持冷静。

paras.en: The police assured everyone that it was just thunder and lightning rather than some military exercise.
paras.zh: 警方向大家保证，那只是打雷闪电，而不是什么军事演习。

paras.en: The weather was the coldest it had been for the season, so people were warned to be careful when traveling outside.
paras.zh: 这是本季以来最冷的天气，所以有关部门提醒大家外出时要小心。

paras.en: In particular, dangerous conditions such as icy roads or wet ground could cause difficulty for drivers.
paras.zh: 尤其是结冰的道路、湿滑的地面等危险路况，可能会给司机带来麻烦。

paras.en: The rail service also announced potential disruptions to trains due to the deep snow.
paras.zh: 铁路部门也宣布，由于积雪很深，火车可能会受到影响。

paras.en: Some roads were also closed because of the severe weather.
paras.zh: 由于天气恶劣，一些道路也已封闭。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about thunder snows from the report?
paras.zh: 第五题：从报道中，我们对雷雪了解到什么？

paras.en: Question six: What did the police do when they received the local residents’ phone calls?
paras.zh: 第六题：警方接到当地居民的电话后做了什么？

paras.en: Question 7: What were people advised to do when traveling outside?
paras.zh: 第七题：有关部门建议人们外出时要怎么做？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I’m going to the city center to buy a new phone today.
paras.zh: 我今天要去市中心买部新手机。

paras.en: Didn’t you buy a new phone just two months ago?
paras.zh: 你不是两个月前才买了新手机吗？

paras.en: It was three months ago, and I already know what you’re going to say.
paras.zh: 是三个月前，我也知道你要说什么。

paras.en: You’re thinking I shouldn’t replace my phone this soon.
paras.zh: 你是觉得我不该这么快就换手机。

paras.en: No, actually I was wondering how you could possibly afford a new phone.
paras.zh: 不是，其实我是在想，你怎么买得起新手机。

w.m: adv. （与 can 连用）到底；究竟

paras.en: But now that you mention it, I do think getting another phone so soon is wasteful, regardless of the cost.
paras.zh: 不过既然你提到了，我确实觉得这么快又买一部手机太浪费了，不管花多少钱。

paras.en: Maybe you’re right.
paras.zh: 也许你说得对。

paras.en: But the thing is, everyone at the office has a nice expensive phone and I’m a little embarrassed by mine.
paras.zh: 可问题是，办公室里每个人都有一部又好又贵的手机，我觉得我的手机有点拿不出手。

paras.en: I just got a credit card, so I thought I might as well buy a new phone.
paras.zh: 我刚办了张信用卡，所以想着不如买部新手机。

paras.en: I don’t think buying a phone on credit is a good idea.
paras.zh: 我觉得刷信用卡买手机不是什么好主意。

paras.en: Look, you’ve only been working for five months now.
paras.zh: 你看，你现在才工作了五个月。

paras.en: People understand that you are a recent graduate, and I doubt anyone cares about your phone other than yourself.
paras.zh: 大家都知道你刚毕业，而且我觉得除了你自己，没人会在意你的手机。

paras.en: Maybe you’re right.
paras.zh: 也许你说得对。

paras.en: But the credit card has a very good special offer where I don’t pay any interest for six months.
paras.zh: 可这张信用卡有个很好的优惠，六个月不用付利息。

paras.en: I’ll be able to pay for the phone well before that period is over.
paras.zh: 早在那之前我就能把手机钱还上。

paras.en: I still think it’s a bad idea to use a credit card for something you don’t need.
paras.zh: 我还是觉得，用信用卡买自己不需要的东西不是什么好主意。

paras.en: One of my colleagues bought a lot of things on credit during her first year of work, and it became a bad habit, and she accumulated a lot of debt.
paras.zh: 我有个同事工作第一年刷信用卡买了很多东西，结果成了坏习惯，欠了一大笔债。

paras.en: Well, I can see how that might happen to someone, and I’m sure she regrets it, but I know it won’t happen to me.
paras.zh: 嗯，我能理解有人会这样，我也相信她很后悔，可我知道这种事不会发生在我身上。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What does the woman say she was actually wondering about?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士说她其实是在想什么？

paras.en: Question 9: Why is the man a little embarrassed by the phone he’s using now?
paras.zh: 第九题：男士为什么觉得自己现在用的手机有点拿不出手？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the man say about the credit card he just got?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于刚办的信用卡，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What do we learn about one of the woman’s colleagues?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于女士的一位同事，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Welcome to The Morning Show.
paras.zh: 欢迎收看《晨间节目》。

paras.en: Our guest today is a popular blog writer and a major figure in the tiny home community.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是一位很受欢迎的博主，也是微型住宅圈里的重要人物。

paras.en: Welcome, Bob Jones.
paras.zh: 欢迎鲍勃·琼斯。

paras.en: Hi, Mary.
paras.zh: 你好，玛丽。

paras.en: Hi, Bob.
paras.zh: 你好，鲍勃。

paras.en: You’re an advocate of the tiny home movement.
paras.zh: 你是微型住宅运动的倡导者。

paras.en: A lot of people don’t know about this movement.
paras.zh: 很多人不了解这个运动。

paras.en: Can you tell our audience what it’s about?
paras.zh: 你能给我们的观众讲讲它是怎么回事吗？

paras.en: Well, it’s mainly about increasing home ownership and protecting the environment.
paras.zh: 嗯，主要是为了让更多人拥有自己的房子，同时保护环境。

paras.en: Of course, those are great goals.
paras.zh: 当然，这些目标都很好。

paras.en: But I’ve seen your blog and you write about houses that are as small as twenty square meters.
paras.zh: 可我看过你的博客，你写的房子有的只有二十平方米。

paras.en: That’s not a realistic size for families.
paras.zh: 对一家人来说，这个面积不现实。

paras.en: I do talk about very small homes, but there’s no set definition of a tiny home, and other people include homes that are much larger, say sixty square meters.
paras.zh: 我确实会谈到很小的房子，但微型住宅并没有固定的定义，有人把大得多的房子也算进去，比如说六十平方米的。

paras.en: And you’d be surprised.
paras.zh: 而且你会感到意外的。

paras.en: Many families of four are happy living in houses that are under thirty square meters.
paras.zh: 很多四口之家住在不到三十平方米的房子里，过得很开心。

paras.en: But I think most of us want spacious homes.
paras.zh: 可我觉得我们大多数人都想要宽敞的房子。

paras.en: The average new house in this area is one hundred fifty square meters, and that’s what people dream of owning.
paras.zh: 这个地区的新房平均一百五十平方米，那才是人们梦想拥有的房子。

paras.en: Yes.
paras.zh: 是的。

paras.en: But I think that dream needs to change, considering the cost of housing.
paras.zh: 可我觉得，考虑到住房成本，这个梦想得改一改了。

paras.en: Housing costs are high, but do people really save that much by having a smaller home?
paras.zh: 房价是很高，可人们住小一点的房子真能省那么多钱吗？

paras.en: Absolutely.
paras.zh: 当然能。

paras.en: Many people who can only afford to rent a larger home are able to buy a tiny home.
paras.zh: 很多只租得起大房子的人，都能买得起一套微型住宅。

paras.en: In this city the average home costs two hundred thousand dollars, and a tiny home costs just fifty thousand dollars.
paras.zh: 在这个城市，一套普通住房要二十万美元，而一套微型住宅只要五万美元。

paras.en: Those are huge savings.
paras.zh: 这可省了一大笔钱。

paras.en: So tiny homes might not be for everyone, but they’re a good option for many.
paras.zh: 所以，微型住宅也许不是人人都合适，但对很多人来说是个不错的选择。

paras.en: You mentioned the environment earlier.
paras.zh: 你刚才提到了环境。

paras.en: How does this benefit the planet?
paras.zh: 这对地球有什么好处？

paras.en: Well, if people have smaller homes they use less land and fewer resources to build them.
paras.zh: 嗯，如果人们的房子小一些，建房用的土地和资源就会少一些。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What does the Tiny Home movement mainly advocate?
paras.zh: 第十二题：微型住宅运动主要倡导什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the woman say about houses as small as twenty square meters?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于只有二十平方米的房子，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the man think about the dream of owning a 150 square meter house?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士怎么看待拥有一套一百五十平方米房子的梦想？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the man say about tiny homes?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于微型住宅，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Kids need time every day to run, jump, stretch and play.
paras.zh: 孩子们每天都需要时间跑跑、跳跳、伸展身体、玩一玩。

paras.en: These experiences have been shown to build children’s confidence and pleasure in physical activities, develop their motor skills and even improve emotional well-being.
paras.zh: 研究表明，这些经历能增强孩子们对体育活动的信心和兴趣，锻炼他们的运动技能，甚至改善情绪健康。

paras.en: To begin with, children seem to have a natural desire to overcome challenges and take risks.
paras.zh: 首先，孩子们似乎天生就想克服困难、敢于冒险。

paras.en: Taking healthy risks through physical movement builds children’s confidence and ability to solve problems and persist through frustration.
paras.zh: 在身体活动中适度冒险，能增强孩子们的自信和解决问题的能力，让他们受挫时也能坚持下去。

paras.en: Secondly, movement activities build children’s big body skills such as coordination and balance, as well as the fine motor skills they need for tasks like writing, tying their shoes, or throwing and catching a ball.
paras.zh: 其次，运动类活动能锻炼孩子们大肌肉的技能，比如协调和平衡，还有写字、系鞋带、扔球接球这类事情需要的精细动作技能。

paras.en: Thirdly, according to the American Psychological Association, regular physical activity, and especially outdoor activity, reduces children’s stress and depression and improves their ability to focus and learn.
paras.zh: 第三，据美国心理学会说，经常参加体育活动，尤其是户外活动，能减轻孩子们的压力和抑郁，提高他们集中注意力和学习的能力。

paras.en: Regular exercise can significantly improve self-regulation and decrease disciplinary consequences for negative behavior.
paras.zh: 经常锻炼能大大提高自我调节能力，减少因不良行为受到的处分。

paras.en: Physical activity provides a positive outlet for frustration, anxiety or anger and can become a healthy coping skill throughout life.
paras.zh: 体育活动能让孩子以积极的方式发泄挫败感、焦虑或愤怒，还能成为伴随一生的健康的应对方式。

paras.en: Finally, we know that physical activity is important for our physical and mental health, and cultivating the habit of physical activity starts early.
paras.zh: 最后，我们知道体育活动对身心健康很重要，而养成运动的习惯要从小开始。

paras.en: Children are more likely to develop a lifelong love of physical activity from frequent positive early experiences.
paras.zh: 小时候经常有积极的运动体验，孩子们就更有可能一辈子热爱体育活动。

paras.en: Not every child enjoys competitive sports or playing with balls, and that’s okay.
paras.zh: 并不是每个孩子都喜欢竞技体育或者玩球，这也没关系。

paras.en: There are plenty of other options, such as imaginative play, non-competitive games, and gardening or nature experiences.
paras.zh: 还有很多别的选择，比如想象类游戏、非竞技类游戏，还有园艺或者亲近大自然的体验。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What do children seem to have a natural desire to do?
paras.zh: 第十六题：孩子们似乎天生就想做什么？

paras.en: Question 17: According to the American Psychological Association, what does regular physical activity do to children?
paras.zh: 第十七题：据美国心理学会说，经常参加体育活动对孩子们有什么作用？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the passage say about cultivating the habit of physical activity?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于养成运动的习惯，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: A new study finds that job seekers are even willing to explore jobs with lower salaries when companies are more diverse.
paras.zh: 一项新研究发现，求职者甚至愿意考虑工资较低的工作，只要公司的员工更加多元。

paras.en: It finds that sharing information about diversity makes job postings more attractive to job seekers, even when pay is lower.
paras.zh: 研究发现，在招聘信息中公布多元化情况，能让求职者觉得这份工作更有吸引力，即使工资更低也是如此。

paras.en: To conduct the study, the team partnered with an online job listings platform, which emails postings relevant to individuals and their job search criteria.
paras.zh: 为了开展这项研究，研究团队与一家在线招聘平台合作，这家平台会根据个人情况和求职条件，给用户发送相关的招聘信息邮件。

w.m: n. 标准；条件（criterion 的复数）

paras.en: For the course of the eleven week study, the platform emailed job listings to some one hundred eighty thousand users, placed in one of two conditions.
paras.zh: 在为期十一周的研究中，这家平台给大约十八万名用户发送了招聘信息邮件，这些用户被分到两种条件中的一种。

paras.en: In the baseline condition, participants saw emails in the normal format, with no information on diversity.
paras.zh: 在基准条件下，参与者看到的是普通格式的邮件，没有任何多元化信息。

paras.en: In the diversity condition, participants saw a diversity score for each listing, information about the race, gender, education, and language skills of a company’s workforce, compared to others in the same sector and location.
paras.zh: 在多元化条件下，参与者会看到每条招聘信息的多元化评分，也就是这家公司员工的种族、性别、学历和语言能力等信息，与同一行业、同一地区的其他公司相比是什么情况。

paras.en: Information was then gathered on whether the email was opened and which job listings were clicked on by each user.
paras.zh: 然后研究人员收集了信息，看每位用户有没有打开邮件，点开了哪些招聘信息。

paras.en: Participants in the diversity condition tended to click on job listings from companies with slightly higher diversity scores than those in the baseline condition.
paras.zh: 和基准条件下的参与者相比，多元化条件下的参与者往往会点开多元化评分稍高的公司发布的招聘信息。

paras.en: That is, participants seemed to be paying attention to information about diversity, and using this when deciding whether to click on the listing.
paras.zh: 也就是说，参与者似乎很关注多元化方面的信息，并在决定要不要点开招聘信息时参考这些信息。

paras.en: And the team also found that participants were willing to look at listings with lower salaries if they came from companies with a higher diversity score.
paras.zh: 研究团队还发现，如果招聘信息来自多元化评分较高的公司，参与者愿意看看工资较低的职位。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: When are job seekers willing to explore jobs with lower salaries, according to a new study?
paras.zh: 第十九题：据一项新研究，求职者在什么情况下愿意考虑工资较低的工作？

paras.en: Question 20: What did participants see in the baseline condition of the study?
paras.zh: 第二十题：在这项研究的基准条件下，参与者看到了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the passage say participants seem to be paying attention to?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：短文说参与者似乎在关注什么？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: A new study from Oregon State University found that dogs tend to match their behavior with the children in their family.
paras.zh: 俄勒冈州立大学的一项新研究发现，狗往往会配合家里孩子的行为。

paras.en: The findings are important because there is a growing body of evidence that dogs can help children in many ways.
paras.zh: 这些发现很重要，因为越来越多的证据表明，狗能在很多方面帮助孩子。

paras.en: These include helping with social development, increasing physical activity, managing anxiety or serving as a source of attachment in the face of changing family structures.
paras.zh: 比如帮助孩子的社交发展、增加身体活动、缓解焦虑，或者在家庭结构发生变化时成为孩子情感依恋的对象。

paras.en: Yet very little research has focused on how dogs perceive and socially engage with children.
paras.zh: 可是，很少有研究关注狗是怎样看待孩子、怎样和孩子互动的。

paras.en: The great news is that this study suggests dogs are paying a lot of attention to the kids that they live with, said Monique Udell, the lead author of the study.
paras.zh: 这项研究的第一作者莫妮克·乌德尔说：“好消息是，这项研究表明，狗非常关注和它们一起生活的孩子。”

paras.en: One interesting thing we have observed is that dogs are matching children’s behavior, but less frequently than what we have seen between dogs and adults.
paras.zh: 我们观察到一件有意思的事：狗会配合孩子的行为，但次数没有我们在狗和成年人之间看到的那么多。

paras.en: This suggests that while dogs may view children as social companions, there are also some differences that we need to understand better.
paras.zh: 这说明，狗虽然可能把孩子当作社交伙伴，但其中也有一些差别，我们需要更好地了解。

paras.en: While research has found dogs can have a lot of positive impacts on a child’s life, there are also risks associated with a dog-child relationship.
paras.zh: 虽然研究发现，狗能给孩子的生活带来很多积极影响，但狗和孩子的关系也存在一些风险。

paras.en: For example, other studies have found dogs are more likely to bite children versus adults.
paras.zh: 比如，其他研究发现，狗咬孩子的可能性比咬成年人更大。

paras.en: We still have a lot to learn about the dog-child relationship, Udell said, but research does show that kids are very capable of training dogs.
paras.zh: 乌德尔说，关于狗和孩子的关系，我们还有很多要了解，不过研究确实表明，孩子们完全有能力训练狗。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What does the passage say about the findings of a new study from Oregon State University?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于俄勒冈州立大学一项新研究的发现，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does a growing body of evidence show according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：据短文说，越来越多的证据表明了什么？

paras.en: Question twenty-four: What did Monique Udell say their study suggests?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：莫妮克·乌德尔说他们的研究表明了什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What does research show kids are very capable of doing?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：研究表明孩子们非常擅长做什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.name: 2024年12月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲美国能源价格飞涨，今年冬天取暖费用大幅上涨，而政府的能源援助总额却比去年少。第二篇新闻报道讲美国农业部的一项研究：很多美国人以为自己吃得健康，其实大多高估了自己饮食的健康程度。第三篇新闻报道讲印度几十名救援人员用吊车把一头掉进深井的大象救了上来，检查后放归野外。第一段长对话里，男士说网上付款太方便、容易乱花钱，所以改用现金并记账，现在已经成了习惯。第二段长对话里，一对父母商量让儿子参加什么运动，从足球、羽毛球、篮球说到排球。第一篇短文讲航天发射对环境的危害，以及可持续燃料和可重复使用火箭如何让太空旅行更环保。第二篇短文讲照顾宠物对孩子情感、认知和身体发展的种种好处。第三篇短文讲俄亥俄州一项新议案，要求公立大学直接把学费、奖助学金、贷款和毕业后预期工资等信息寄给准新生。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news reports and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Across the US families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar.
paras.zh: 能源价格飞涨，美国各地的家庭都对即将到来的冬天忧心忡忡。

paras.en: A number of factors are creating a bad situation.
paras.zh: 多种因素正在造成糟糕的局面。

paras.en: Global energy consumption is up, but supplies have been reduced.
paras.zh: 全球能源消耗增加了，供应却减少了。

paras.en: The Energy Department projects heating bills will jump twenty-eight per cent this winter for those who rely on natural gas.
paras.zh: 美国能源部预计，今年冬天，靠天然气取暖的家庭取暖费将猛涨百分之二十八。

paras.en: Natural gas is used by nearly half of US households for heat.
paras.zh: 美国将近一半的家庭靠天然气取暖。

paras.en: Heating oil is projected to be twenty-seven per cent higher and electricity ten percent higher.
paras.zh: 取暖用油预计会贵百分之二十七，电价会高百分之十。

paras.en: That comes against inflation rates that accelerated last month, with consumer prices growing 6.6%.
paras.zh: 与此同时，上个月通胀率加快，消费价格上涨了百分之六点六。

paras.en: That’s the fastest pace in four decades.
paras.zh: 这是四十年来最快的涨幅。

paras.en: The pain will be especially acute in parts of the country that heavily rely on heating oil to keep homes warm.
paras.zh: 在家里主要靠取暖用油保暖的地区，人们的日子会尤其难熬。

w.m: adv. 严重地；在很大程度上

paras.en: It’s projected to cost more than two thousand three hundred dollars to heat a typical home with heating oil this winter.
paras.zh: 预计今年冬天，一户普通人家用取暖油取暖要花两千三百多美元。

paras.en: Last month the Federal Government added one billion dollars in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to 4.8 billion dollars.
paras.zh: 上个月，联邦政府给低收入家庭能源援助计划追加了十亿美元资金，总额达到四十八亿美元。

paras.en: But that represents a reduction from last year’s energy assistance package of over eight billion dollars.
paras.zh: 但这比去年八十多亿美元的能源援助方案少了。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: Why are families across the US looking to this winter with fear?
paras.zh: 第一题：美国各地的家庭为什么对今年冬天忧心忡忡？

paras.en: Question two: What did the federal government do last month?
paras.zh: 第二题：联邦政府上个月做了什么？

paras.en: News report two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Many Americans think they make healthy food choices, but they may be viewing their diet too optimistically.
paras.zh: 很多美国人认为自己在饮食上选得很健康，但他们对自己饮食的看法可能过于乐观了。

paras.en: That’s the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.
paras.zh: 这是密西西比州斯通维尔的美国农业部研究人员一项新研究的主要发现。

paras.en: The study aimed to identify disconnects between how healthily Americans think they eat and how they actually do.
paras.zh: 这项研究旨在找出美国人自以为吃得多健康与实际吃得多健康之间的差距。

paras.en: For the study, the researchers asked participants to rate their diet as excellent, very good, good, fair, or poor.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员请参与者给自己的饮食打分：优秀、很好、好、一般或差。

paras.en: Folks also completed twenty-four-hour food questionnaires.
paras.zh: 大家还填写了二十四小时饮食问卷。

paras.en: Then the researchers compared answers to see how well responses to the two exercises matched up.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员比较了答案，看两项调查的回答吻合程度如何。

paras.en: Of more than nine thousand seven hundred people, roughly eighty-five per cent were off base when asked to rate the quality of their diet, and almost all overestimated how healthy it was.
paras.zh: 在九千七百多人中，大约百分之八十五的人在给自己的饮食质量打分时都打偏了，而且几乎所有人都高估了自己饮食的健康程度。

paras.en: Those who rated their diet as poor tended to be far more accurate.
paras.zh: 那些给自己饮食打“差”的人往往准确得多。

paras.en: Their rating matched that of the researchers more than nine times out of ten.
paras.zh: 十次里有九次以上，他们的评分和研究人员的评分一致。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What is the main finding of a new study about many Americans?
paras.zh: 第三题：一项关于很多美国人的新研究，主要发现是什么？

paras.en: Question four: Who tended to rate their diet more accurately in the survey?
paras.zh: 第四题：调查中哪些人给自己饮食的评分往往更准确？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: It was a heartwarming moment that dozens of Indian rescuers rallied together to use a crane in order to save an elephant trapped at the bottom of a twenty-foot well.
paras.zh: 这是暖心的一刻：几十名印度救援人员齐心协力，用吊车救出一头被困在二十英尺深井底的大象。

paras.en: The massive rescue effort took place last week close to an army camp.
paras.zh: 这次大规模救援上周在一个军营附近进行。

paras.en: The elephant wandered out of the jungle and fell into the well.
paras.zh: 这头大象从丛林里走出来，掉进了井里。

paras.en: The army officers heard a noise coming from the well and realized an elephant was trapped deep inside.
paras.zh: 部队的军官听到井里传来声音，意识到有一头大象被困在井底深处。

paras.en: The officers then threw in some food for the creature and called the local Forest Department for help.
paras.zh: 军官们随后给这头动物扔了些食物下去，并打电话请当地林业部门帮忙。

paras.en: Video of the rescue operation shows how the team used a crane to lift up the huge animal out of the well and on to the back of a truck.
paras.zh: 救援行动的视频显示，救援队用吊车把这头庞然大物吊出井口，放到一辆卡车的后车厢上。

paras.en: It was then taken to an examining room for evaluation of any injuries.
paras.zh: 然后它被送到一间检查室，检查有没有受伤。

paras.en: The elephant was kept under close supervision for a few days before it was successfully released back into the wild.
paras.zh: 这头大象被密切观察了几天，然后成功放归野外。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the report say dozens of Indians did last week?
paras.zh: 第五题：报道说上周几十名印度人做了什么？

paras.en: Question six: Why did the army officers call the local forest department?
paras.zh: 第六题：部队的军官为什么给当地林业部门打电话？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the news report say happened finally?
paras.zh: 第七题：新闻报道说最后发生了什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you’ll hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I need to stop at the bank to withdraw some cash.
paras.zh: 我得去趟银行取点现金。

paras.en: Why not just pay with your phone?
paras.zh: 为什么不直接用手机付呢？

paras.en: Well, actually I’ve stopped using online payments for the past three months now.
paras.zh: 嗯，其实我已经有三个月不用网上支付了。

paras.en: Stopped paying online?
paras.zh: 不在网上付钱了？

paras.en: Oh, you must be worried that online payments aren’t secure.
paras.zh: 哦，你肯定是担心网上支付不安全吧。

paras.en: No, they are safe.
paras.zh: 不是，网上支付挺安全的。

paras.en: But paying online is too convenient and I spent too much money on things I didn’t need.
paras.zh: 可网上付钱太方便了，我花了太多钱买不需要的东西。

paras.en: Oh, impulse purchases can be an issue for me too.
paras.zh: 哦，冲动消费也是我的一个问题。

paras.en: I’ve definitely bought clothes and shoes I didn’t need because they were on sale, and paying with my phone was so easy.
paras.zh: 我确实买过不需要的衣服和鞋子，因为它们在打折，用手机付钱又那么方便。

paras.en: But I’ve found that if I review my spending every night, that keeps me from spending too much.
paras.zh: 不过我发现，如果每天晚上看一遍自己的开销，就不会花太多钱。

paras.en: I tried that strategy, but it just didn’t work, because I’d be busy studying all day, then, when I was tired and hungry, I’d use my phone to order food, like burgers and other junk, instead of going to the canteen, where I could get a healthier meal for half the price.
paras.zh: 这个办法我试过，可就是不管用，因为我一整天都忙着学习，等到又累又饿的时候，就会用手机点外卖，比如汉堡之类的垃圾食品，而不去食堂，其实在食堂花一半的钱就能吃上一顿更健康的饭。

paras.en: Well, what do you do now, then?
paras.zh: 那你现在怎么办呢？

paras.en: It seems like you’d have the same problems with cash.
paras.zh: 用现金好像也会有同样的问题吧。

paras.en: I go to the bank once a week, and the rest of the time I keep my bank card at home, so I can’t get more cash out.
paras.zh: 我一周去一次银行，其他时间都把银行卡放在家里，这样就没法取更多现金了。

paras.en: And I also have a notebook where I record my expenses.
paras.zh: 我还有个本子，用来记录自己的开销。

paras.en: But what prevents you from just going to the bank and getting more money if you want to buy something.
paras.zh: 可要是你想买什么东西，有什么能拦着你直接去银行多取点钱呢？

paras.en: The first month I did withdraw extra cash twice, but I felt guilty about it, and after that I refused to spend more than what I had budgeted, and by now it’s just a habit.
paras.zh: 第一个月我确实多取过两次现金，但事后很内疚，从那以后，我就坚决不花超出预算的钱，到现在已经成了习惯。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: Why has the man stopped paying online for the last three months?
paras.zh: 第八题：过去三个月男士为什么不在网上付钱了？

paras.en: Question nine: What problem does the woman say she may also have?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士说她可能也有什么问题？

paras.en: Question ten: What does the man say he could do at the canteen?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士说他在食堂可以做什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What is now just a habit for the man?
paras.zh: 第十一题：对男士来说，现在什么已经成了习惯？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Please hear me out.
paras.zh: 请听我把话说完。

paras.en: I don’t want our son to spend his afternoons doing something he hates, even if it might prepare him for the future.
paras.zh: 我不想让儿子下午都在做他讨厌的事，哪怕这能为他的将来做准备。

paras.en: What about getting him to join a sport like soccer?
paras.zh: 让他参加足球这类运动怎么样？

paras.en: From all the running and training he could become quite athletic, not to mention the great physical benefits from exercising outside every day.
paras.zh: 经过那么多跑步和训练，他会变得很健壮，更别说每天在户外锻炼对身体有很大好处了。

paras.en: Hmm, I don’t think he should be doing something so challenging with all his breathing issues.
paras.zh: 嗯，他呼吸方面老有毛病，我觉得不该让他做这么吃力的运动。

w.m: adj. 吃力的；有挑战性的

paras.en: What about playing an indoor sport, like badminton?
paras.zh: 做点室内运动怎么样，比如打羽毛球？

paras.en: The environment is easier to control and he can still get a good workout, in addition to improving his hand-eye coordination.
paras.zh: 室内环境更容易控制，他照样能好好锻炼，还能提高手眼协调能力。

paras.en: Besides, I could teach him some of the basics from my time as a badminton player.
paras.zh: 再说，我还能教他一些基本功，我以前就打过羽毛球。

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

paras.en: I’m thinking team sports should be the way to go.
paras.zh: 我在想，还是团体运动最合适。

paras.en: There’s nothing like playing as part of a unit to accomplish a goal like winning a game or even a championship.
paras.zh: 作为团队的一员去完成一个目标，比如赢一场比赛甚至拿冠军，没有什么比这更棒的了。

paras.en: He could try basketball, since many of the courts are indoors now, and it’s a sport that could help him understand team spirit while cooperating with others.
paras.zh: 他可以试试篮球，现在很多球场都在室内，而且这项运动能让他和别人配合的时候懂得团队精神。

paras.en: Maybe he could even join the school basketball team when he’s ready.
paras.zh: 也许等他准备好了，还能加入学校的篮球队呢。

paras.en: Oh, oh, what about volleyball?
paras.zh: 哦哦，排球怎么样？

paras.en: It’s a team sport, and they often have mixed-gender teams, so he could socialize with both girls and boys.
paras.zh: 排球是团体运动，还经常是男女混合队，这样他就能和男孩女孩都交往。

paras.en: It’s not as popular as some sports, which means he has better odds of possibly getting an athletic scholarship in the future.
paras.zh: 它不像有些运动那么热门，这就意味着他将来拿到体育奖学金的机会可能更大。

paras.en: I also believe you were a beach volleyball athlete yourself not so long ago.
paras.zh: 而且我记得，你自己不久前还是沙滩排球运动员呢。

paras.en: As I’ve said many times before, beach volleyball and indoor volleyball are completely different.
paras.zh: 我说过好多次了，沙滩排球和室内排球完全是两回事。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: Why is the woman opposed to their son joining a sport like soccer?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士为什么反对儿子参加足球这类运动？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the man suggest their son try in order to understand team spirit?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士建议儿子尝试什么来懂得团队精神？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What is one of the woman’s considerations in choosing a sport for her son?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士给儿子选运动时考虑的一点是什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the man say about beach volleyball?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于沙滩排球，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Liftoff is usually the most environmentally harmful stage of any space mission, with vast quantities of fuel burnt up in a matter of minutes.
paras.zh: 发射升空通常是所有太空任务中对环境危害最大的阶段，几分钟之内就要烧掉大量燃料。

paras.en: For instance, SpaceX’s Falcon nine gets through one hundred and twelve tons of refined fuel, emitting about three hundred and thirty-six tons of CO two.
paras.zh: 比如，太空探索技术公司的猎鹰九号火箭要消耗一百一十二吨精炼燃料，排放大约三百三十六吨二氧化碳。

paras.en: This is the equivalent produced by your average car driving almost seventy times around the world.
paras.zh: 这相当于一辆普通汽车绕地球开将近七十圈产生的排放量。

paras.en: As well as greenhouse gases, rocket engines emit particles that destroy ozone.
paras.zh: 除了温室气体，火箭发动机还会排放破坏臭氧的微粒。

paras.en: These issues are growing more pressing with the emergence of commercial space flight.
paras.zh: 随着商业航天的兴起，这些问题变得越来越紧迫。

paras.en: There were one hundred fourteen space launches in twenty twenty, but there may be up to one thousand per year in future.
paras.zh: 二〇二〇年全球共进行了一百一十四次航天发射，但将来每年可能多达一千次。

paras.en: Sustainable fuels are the top priority to enable greener space travel.
paras.zh: 要让太空旅行更环保，可持续燃料是重中之重。

paras.en: Current spacecraft use a variety of fuels, but most are based on fossil fuels.
paras.zh: 现在的航天器使用多种燃料，但大多以化石燃料为基础。

paras.en: One potentially greener option is liquid hydrogen and oxygen.
paras.zh: 一种可能更环保的选择是液氢和液氧。

paras.en: Hydrogen can be obtained sustainably by using solar power to break water down into oxygen and hydrogen.
paras.zh: 利用太阳能把水分解成氧和氢，就能以可持续的方式获得氢。

paras.en: Reusable rockets can cut down on some of the waste associated with space flight.
paras.zh: 可重复使用的火箭能减少航天带来的一部分浪费。

paras.en: Traditionally, boosters, fuel tanks and other components are treated as expendable, but guiding them back to earth in a controlled manner opens new possibilities.
paras.zh: 按照传统做法，助推器、燃料箱和其他部件都被当作一次性用品，但如果以可控的方式把它们引导回地球，就能开辟新的可能。

w.m: adj. 一次性的；消耗性的

paras.en: Most components from the Falcon nine can be reused up to one hundred times.
paras.zh: 猎鹰九号的大部分部件最多可以重复使用一百次。

paras.en: Truly environmentally friendly space travel is still some way off, but we already have many of the technologies needed to start limiting its impact on our planet.
paras.zh: 真正环保的太空旅行还有一段路要走，不过我们已经拥有了很多需要的技术，可以开始减轻它对地球的影响了。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What do we learn from the passage about the lift-off of spacecraft?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于航天器的发射升空，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What happens traditionally to boosters, fuel tanks and other components in space flight?
paras.zh: 第十七题：按照传统做法，航天中的助推器、燃料箱和其他部件会被怎样处理？

paras.en: Question eighteen: What does the passage say we already have regarding spaceflight?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于航天，短文说我们已经拥有什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Helping to look after a pet can facilitate numerous aspects of a child’s emotional development.
paras.zh: 帮着照顾宠物，能在很多方面促进孩子的情感发展。

paras.en: Research shows that reading to a loyal and non-judgmental companion, such as a dog or cat, can encourage reluctant readers to read aloud, which will in turn boost their self-confidence.
paras.zh: 研究表明，给忠诚、不会评判人的伙伴读书，比如给狗或猫读书，能鼓励不爱读书的孩子大声朗读，这又会增强他们的自信心。

paras.en: Having a companion to talk to about their feelings can also help children feel secure and develop communication skills.
paras.zh: 有个伙伴可以倾诉自己的感受，也能帮孩子获得安全感，培养沟通能力。

paras.en: A household pet can also cultivate a child’s sense of responsibility, as their parent explains the necessary processes of keeping their pet happy and healthy.
paras.zh: 家里养宠物还能培养孩子的责任感，因为父母会给孩子讲清楚，要让宠物开心健康，必须做哪些事。

paras.en: As a child matures they can then take on more of the daily responsibilities, boosting their sense of independence.
paras.zh: 孩子长大一些后，就能承担更多日常的责任，从而增强独立意识。

paras.en: Pets also provide a fantastic subject for research and learning.
paras.zh: 宠物还是研究和学习的绝佳题材。

paras.en: Parents can encourage their child to research their favorite pets at the library or during a supervised Internet search.
paras.zh: 父母可以鼓励孩子去图书馆，或者在大人的看护下上网，查一查自己最喜欢的宠物。

paras.en: Taking children along to the pet shop to buy food and supplies will support their cognitive development as their passion for learning flourishes.
paras.zh: 带孩子去宠物店买食物和用品，能促进他们的认知发展，他们对学习的热情也会越来越高。

paras.en: A child’s physical development can benefit greatly from taking pets for walks in the fresh air.
paras.zh: 带宠物去呼吸新鲜空气、散散步，对孩子的身体发育大有好处。

paras.en: Even their fine motor skills can be utilized in taking care of a beloved animal.
paras.zh: 照顾心爱的动物，甚至还能锻炼他们的精细动作技能。

paras.en: When responsibilities are well-paced and communicated, a child can benefit greatly from involvement in bringing up a happy and healthy pet.
paras.zh: 只要责任安排得循序渐进、讲得清清楚楚，孩子参与养育一只快乐健康的宠物，就能从中受益匪浅。

w.m: adj. 安排得循序渐进的

paras.en: And of course, if a child doesn’t have a pet in their own household, they can still benefit from all of the above when visiting a friend who does.
paras.zh: 当然，就算孩子自己家里没有宠物，去养宠物的朋友家做客时，照样能得到上面说的这些好处。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What does research show about reading to a loyal and non-judgmental companion?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于给忠诚、不会评判人的伙伴读书，研究表明了什么？

paras.en: Question twenty: How can parents make pets a fantastic subject for their children’s research and learning?
paras.zh: 第二十题：父母怎样让宠物成为孩子研究和学习的绝佳题材？

paras.en: Question twenty one: How can children still benefit even when their family doesn’t have a pet?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：家里没有宠物的时候，孩子怎样照样能受益？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: A new bill in the Ohio legislature would require state public colleges and universities to send prospective students a packet of information.
paras.zh: 俄亥俄州议会的一项新议案要求本州的公立大学和学院给准新生寄一份资料。

paras.en: This would include costs of college, grants and scholarships.
paras.zh: 资料里会有上大学的费用、助学金和奖学金。

paras.en: It would also include expected monthly loan payments and projected salary after college.
paras.zh: 还会有预计每月要还的贷款和毕业后的预期工资。

paras.en: State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill.
paras.zh: 州众议员亚当·马修斯是提出这项议案的两位议员之一。

paras.en: He said it would give prospective students more information about what to expect once they graduate.
paras.zh: 他说，这项议案能让准新生更清楚毕业以后会是什么情况。

paras.en: Putting that information in front of them will give them the best opportunity to match their skills and their dreams to what our schools can provide, said Mathews.
paras.zh: 马修斯说，把这些信息摆在他们面前，就能给他们最好的机会，让自己的能力和梦想与我们学校能提供的东西对上号。

paras.en: He notes that the state can only regulate public institutions in this way, but he hopes private institutions in Ohio follow the lead of the state and post similar information.
paras.zh: 他指出，州政府只能用这种方式管理公立院校，但他希望俄亥俄州的私立院校也跟着州里的做法，公布类似的信息。

paras.en: He believes giving out this information will help Ohio’s colleges and universities to be more competitive.
paras.zh: 他认为，公布这些信息能让俄亥俄州的大学和学院更有竞争力。

paras.en: The information will highlight what a great value they have for their very reasonable cost.
paras.zh: 这些信息能突出这些学校有多划算：收费很合理，得到的却很多。

paras.en: Ohio’s schools are already competitive.
paras.zh: 俄亥俄州的学校已经很有竞争力了。

paras.en: The state attracts more undergraduate students than it sends to colleges out of state.
paras.zh: 来这个州读书的本科生，比从这个州去外州上大学的还多。

w.m: adj. 本科生的；大学生的

paras.en: Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites.
paras.zh: 很多大学和学院目前都在自己的网站上提供类似的信息。

paras.en: This includes tuition, fees, graduation rates and more.
paras.zh: 包括学费、杂费、毕业率等等。

paras.en: But students need to search for the information.
paras.zh: 但学生得自己去找这些信息。

paras.en: This bill would require the universities and colleges to send a packet directly to students.
paras.zh: 这项议案则要求大学和学院把资料直接寄给学生。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What would the new bill in the Ohio Legislature require public colleges and universities to do?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：俄亥俄州议会的这项新议案会要求公立大学和学院做什么？

paras.en: Question twenty three: What can the state only do, according to Adam Mathews?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：据亚当·马修斯说，州政府只能做什么？

paras.en: Question twenty four: What do we learn about Ohio’s schools from the passage?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于俄亥俄州的学校，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question twenty five: What is the problem with schools providing information on their websites?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：学校在网站上提供信息，问题在哪里？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.name: 2025年6月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲七岁的塔里克因为一段爱吃玉米的采访走红，被称为“玉米小子”，还当上了南达科他州的玉米形象大使，受邀参观玉米宫。第二篇新闻报道讲两名男子用邮政钥匙多次从邮筒里偷邮件，已被逮捕，面临联邦监狱的刑罚。第三篇新闻报道讲快时尚造成大量服装浪费，研究人员提出政策建议，认为要先找出问题在供应链上的源头。第一段长对话里，女士抱怨早高峰太难熬，希望政府给地铁装空调，男士坐公交上班比较方便，还给她推荐了一位房产中介。第二段长对话里，两人谈到约翰尼为了女朋友做整容手术去掉脸上的疤，都觉得他女朋友太肤浅、太自私。第一篇短文介绍语言起源的两种主要理论：一种认为语言来自模仿声音，另一种认为来自手势。第二篇短文讲炫耀财富和地位的利弊：这样做显得有能力，却让人不愿与之合作。第三篇短文讲动物园的历史，从古埃及的王室收藏到中国周文王的灵囿，再到英国亨利一世的动物收藏。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D, then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案，然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Everything changed for seven-year-old Tariq when he slapped some butter on an ear of corn.
paras.zh: 七岁的塔里克在一根玉米棒上抹了些黄油，从那以后，一切都变了。

paras.en: He knew it tasted good, but butter made it better.
paras.zh: 他知道玉米本来就好吃，但抹上黄油更好吃。

paras.en: His passion for produce got him a position as South Dakota’s official corn ambassador.
paras.zh: 他对农产品的热爱让他当上了南达科他州的官方玉米形象大使。

paras.en: Tariq’s profession of love for his favorite vegetable earned him the name the Corn Kid.
paras.zh: 塔里克大声说出自己有多爱吃最喜欢的蔬菜，因此得了个“玉米小子”的名号。

paras.en: This was after his online interview attracted millions of views and was made into a song.
paras.zh: 那是在他的网络采访获得了几百万次观看、还被改编成一首歌之后。

paras.en: South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America.
paras.zh: 南达科他州是美国最大的玉米产地之一。

paras.en: The corn provides nourishment across the globe.
paras.zh: 这里的玉米为全世界提供食物。

paras.en: Tariq said not everyone has to like corn, but everyone should definitely try it, especially with butter.
paras.zh: 塔里克说，不是每个人都非得喜欢玉米，但每个人都一定要尝一尝，最好抹上黄油。

paras.en: Tariq and his family were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony at the State’s Corn Palace.
paras.zh: 塔里克一家受邀来到南达科他州，到州里的玉米宫参加授予荣誉的仪式。

paras.en: Officials wanted to highlight South Dakota’s two largest industries: tourism and agriculture.
paras.zh: 官员们想借此突出南达科他州的两大产业：旅游业和农业。

paras.en: Tariq couldn’t believe his eyes when he saw the palace made of corn.
paras.zh: 塔里克看到这座用玉米建成的宫殿时，简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: How did Tariq make corn taste better?
paras.zh: 第一题：塔里克是怎样让玉米更好吃的？

paras.en: Question two: Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota?
paras.zh: 第二题：塔里克一家为什么受邀去南达科他州？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Two arrests were announced Thursday.
paras.zh: 周四，警方宣布逮捕了两个人。

paras.en: The arrests were in connection with a string of mail thefts from U.S. Post Service’s collection boxes in Marion County and for the possession of a stolen postal key, according to the Department of Justice.
paras.zh: 据美国司法部称，这两人被捕，是因为在马里恩县从美国邮政署的邮筒里接连偷了好多邮件，而且持有一把偷来的邮政钥匙。

paras.en: Jordan Jacks and Tarad Goodman, both twenty-three, were arrested after evidence gathered in an investigation showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according to a news release.
paras.zh: 据一份新闻稿称，乔丹·杰克斯和塔拉德·古德曼都是二十三岁，调查中收集到的证据显示，两人多次用邮政钥匙偷邮件，随后被逮捕。

paras.en: Jacks and Goodman stole mail for around four months.
paras.zh: 杰克斯和古德曼偷了大约四个月的邮件。

paras.en: Investigators reviewed videos of the collection boxes.
paras.zh: 调查人员查看了邮筒的监控录像。

paras.en: The video showed the two men loading the stolen mail into Jacks’ vehicle.
paras.zh: 录像显示，这两名男子把偷来的邮件装进了杰克斯的车里。

paras.en: Investigators were also able to recover the key that was used to open the collection boxes.
paras.zh: 调查人员还找回了用来打开邮筒的那把钥匙。

paras.en: Jacks and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten years for possession of the postal key.
paras.zh: 杰克斯和古德曼因为偷邮件，每人都可能在联邦监狱服刑最多五年，因为持有邮政钥匙，还可能被判最多十年。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What did Jordan Jacks and Tara Goodman do according to a news release?
paras.zh: 第三题：据新闻稿称，乔丹·杰克斯和塔拉德·古德曼做了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What do Jordan Jacks and Territ Goodman face?
paras.zh: 第四题：乔丹·杰克斯和塔拉德·古德曼面临什么？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Can fast fashion be sustainable?
paras.zh: 快时尚能做到可持续吗？

paras.en: Researchers think yes.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为能。

paras.en: Identifying why the fast fashion business model creates waste and determining whether regulators can establish incentives for consumers and manufacturers are steps to reduce waste.
paras.zh: 找出快时尚商业模式产生浪费的原因，确定监管部门能否给消费者和生产商制定激励措施，这些都是减少浪费的步骤。

paras.en: Recently the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with serious environmental consequences.
paras.zh: 最近，服装业受到抨击，因为它造成了浪费问题，给环境带来了严重后果。

paras.en: In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options, fast fashion manufacturers pump out low quality clothes produced in high volumes that are worn only a few times and then discarded.
paras.zh: 由于没有既环保又经济可行的回收办法，快时尚生产商大批量生产低质量的衣服，这些衣服只穿几次就被扔掉了。

paras.en: The researchers put forth policy contributions ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious.
paras.zh: 研究人员提出了一些政策建议，从可持续地处理库存剩货到征收生产税，目的是激励生产商和消费者都更有减少浪费的意识。

paras.en: In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry, it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain.
paras.zh: 要制定有效的政策来遏制服装业对环境的影响，就必须在供应链上找出问题的源头。

paras.en: Manufacturers, consumers and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach to recognize the environmental impact of fast fashion and to design an ecosystem to reduce waste, incentivize innovation and create new business models to manage waste.
paras.zh: 这样，生产商、消费者和监管机构就能在充分了解情况的基础上，认识快时尚对环境的影响，并设计一个生态系统来减少浪费、激励创新、创造新的商业模式来管理废物。

w.m: adj. 有根据的；了解情况的

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: Why has the clothing industry come under attack?
paras.zh: 第五题：服装业为什么受到抨击？

paras.en: Question six: Why do the researchers put forth such policies as production tax?
paras.zh: 第六题：研究人员为什么提出征收生产税这样的政策？

paras.en: Question 7: What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry?
paras.zh: 第七题：要消除服装业造成的危害，首先应该做什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hey, Mary, you seem to be very much annoyed.
paras.zh: 嘿，玛丽，你看起来很烦啊。

paras.en: What happened?
paras.zh: 怎么了？

paras.en: Rush hour in this city is killing me.
paras.zh: 这座城市的早晚高峰快把我折磨死了。

paras.en: Ah, yes, rush hour is terrible, especially in the morning between eight and nine.
paras.zh: 啊，是啊，高峰期太糟糕了，尤其是早上八九点。

paras.en: But what else can you expect in a city this big?
paras.zh: 可这么大的城市，你还能指望怎么样呢？

paras.en: Well, I think the local government could help improve things.
paras.zh: 嗯，我觉得当地政府可以帮着改善一下。

paras.en: I mean, getting rid of rush hour may be impossible, but it could be made more tolerable, don’t you think?
paras.zh: 我是说，要消除高峰期也许不可能，但可以让它不那么难熬，你不觉得吗？

paras.en: Um, but I’m not sure how.
paras.zh: 嗯，可我不知道该怎么做。

paras.en: Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning.
paras.zh: 嗯，比如说，地铁可以装上空调。

paras.en: I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can’t we?
paras.zh: 我知道世界上很多城市的地铁都有空调，那我们为什么不能有？

paras.en: It gets so hot in the summer.
paras.zh: 夏天地铁里热得要命。

paras.en: I can hardly breathe down there.
paras.zh: 我在下面都快喘不过气了。

paras.en: And add to that the rush hour crowds, with strangers packed close together in the subway carriages.
paras.zh: 再加上高峰期的人潮，陌生人在地铁车厢里挤得紧紧的。

paras.en: The whole thing is just horrible.
paras.zh: 整个情况简直太可怕了。

paras.en: Ah, yes, you are completely right.
paras.zh: 啊，是啊，你说得完全对。

paras.en: The trains here are too old.
paras.zh: 这里的列车太旧了。

paras.en: The government should definitely invest in new ones with air conditioning.
paras.zh: 政府真应该投资买些带空调的新车。

paras.en: I guess I’m fortunate I take the bus instead.
paras.zh: 看来我挺幸运，我是坐公交的。

paras.en: Oh, that’s much better.
paras.zh: 哦，那好多了。

paras.en: Yeah, it’s more convenient.
paras.zh: 是啊，更方便。

paras.en: Bus number thirty six goes straight from my house to the office.
paras.zh: 三十六路公交车从我家直达公司。

paras.en: It’s a thirty-minute ride and I don’t have to make any changes.
paras.zh: 坐车三十分钟，而且不用换乘。

paras.en: That sounds nice.
paras.zh: 听起来不错。

paras.en: I tell you, my current commute is killing me.
paras.zh: 跟你说，我现在上下班通勤快把我折磨死了。

paras.en: Maybe I should move closer to the office.
paras.zh: 也许我该搬到离公司近一点的地方。

paras.en: Well, I know a great housing agent.
paras.zh: 嗯，我认识一个很棒的房产中介。

paras.en: I found the flat I’m living in now through him, and I love it.
paras.zh: 我现在住的这套公寓就是通过他找到的，我很喜欢。

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

paras.en: Could you send me his number, please?
paras.zh: 你能把他的电话号码发给我吗？

paras.en: Sure thing.
paras.zh: 没问题。

paras.en: Just tell him exactly what you are looking for, and I’m sure he will find something good.
paras.zh: 你就跟他说清楚你想找什么样的，我相信他会帮你找到好房子的。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: Why is the woman complaining?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士为什么抱怨？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman suggest doing?
paras.zh: 第九题：女士建议做什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十题：从对话中，我们对男士了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十一题：对话最后，女士请男士做什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Did you hear about Johnny?
paras.zh: 你听说约翰尼的事了吗？

paras.en: No, why?
paras.zh: 没有，怎么了？

paras.en: Is he okay?
paras.zh: 他没事吧？

paras.en: He had some plastic surgery done.
paras.zh: 他去做了整容手术。

paras.en: What?
paras.zh: 什么？

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么呢？

paras.en: Do you remember he had a scar on his face?
paras.zh: 你还记得他脸上有一道疤吗？

paras.en: Yes, of course.
paras.zh: 记得，当然记得。

paras.en: He always had that.
paras.zh: 他一直都有那道疤。

paras.en: I’ve known him since primary school, and I always remember him having that on his cheek.
paras.zh: 我从小学就认识他了，一直记得他脸颊上有那道疤。

paras.en: Well, he had it fixed.
paras.zh: 嗯，他把它弄掉了。

paras.en: Fixed?
paras.zh: 弄掉了？

paras.en: What do you mean?
paras.zh: 你这话什么意思？

paras.en: You can’t fix a scar.
paras.zh: 疤又不是能修好的东西。

paras.en: You know what I mean.
paras.zh: 你知道我的意思。

paras.en: He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery, in order to cover it and make it less noticeable.
paras.zh: 他做了手术，就是整容手术，把疤遮住，让它不那么显眼。

paras.en: Oh, well, that’s ridiculous, isn’t it?
paras.zh: 哦，那也太荒唐了，不是吗？

paras.en: It was noticeable, sure, but it wasn’t an ugly scar.
paras.zh: 那道疤确实挺显眼，可并不难看啊。

paras.en: It never occurred to me that he should have it taken care of like that.
paras.zh: 我从来没想过他应该那样去处理它。

paras.en: I agree.
paras.zh: 我同意。

paras.en: I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but not Johnny’s.
paras.zh: 我能理解，有些伤疤和身体缺陷可能很难看、很让人分心，但约翰尼的不是。

paras.en: In fact, I thought it added character, like it gave him a certain uniqueness.
paras.zh: 其实，我觉得它让他更有个性，好像让他显得与众不同。

paras.en: He must have felt differently, though.
paras.zh: 不过他自己的感觉肯定不一样。

paras.en: He must have felt self-conscious and insecure, perhaps.
paras.zh: 也许他一直很在意，觉得没有安全感。

w.m: adj. 没有安全感的；不自信的

paras.en: No, no, that’s not the reason.
paras.zh: 不，不，不是这个原因。

paras.en: He was totally fine with his scar.
paras.zh: 他对那道疤完全不在乎。

paras.en: As you said, he had had it for most of his life.
paras.zh: 就像你说的，他这辈子大部分时间都带着它。

paras.en: Then why did he have the operation?
paras.zh: 那他为什么还要做手术？

paras.en: Because his girlfriend wanted him to.
paras.zh: 因为他女朋友想让他做。

paras.en: What?
paras.zh: 什么？

paras.en: That’s so superficial and selfish of her.
paras.zh: 她也太肤浅、太自私了吧。

paras.en: If Johnny’s girlfriend doesn’t like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend.
paras.zh: 约翰尼的女朋友要是不喜欢他本来的样子，那她就不配做他的女朋友。

paras.en: You’re right.
paras.zh: 你说得对。

paras.en: So he is insane to give in to her like that.
paras.zh: 所以他那样向她让步，简直是疯了。

paras.en: But when I told him, he said he loves her and would just do what she wants him to.
paras.zh: 可我跟他说了以后，他说他爱她，她想让他做什么他就做什么。

paras.en: What a fool he is!
paras.zh: 他真是个傻瓜！

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What does the man say about Johnny?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士说约翰尼怎么了？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the woman find puzzling?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士对什么感到不解？

paras.en: Question fourteen: What did the man think of Johnny’s scar?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士觉得约翰尼的疤怎么样？

paras.en: Question fifteen: How could we describe the speakers’ attitude towards Johnny’s girlfriend?
paras.zh: 第十五题：说话人对约翰尼的女朋友是什么态度？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Talking is unique to humans.
paras.zh: 说话是人类独有的。

paras.en: An animal might make ten different sounds, but an adult human knows more than twenty thousand words.
paras.zh: 一种动物也许能发出十种不同的声音，而一个成年人认识两万多个单词。

paras.en: Additionally, we’re the only animal that expresses thoughts in full sentences.
paras.zh: 另外，人类是唯一能用完整的句子表达想法的动物。

paras.en: Researchers don’t think language was invented.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为语言不是发明出来的。

paras.en: Instead, they think it evolved.
paras.zh: 他们认为语言是逐渐进化来的。

paras.en: How did talking evolve?
paras.zh: 说话是怎样进化来的呢？

paras.en: There are two main theories.
paras.zh: 主要有两种理论。

paras.en: The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools.
paras.zh: 第一种理论认为，语言起源于人们发出各种声音，主要是模仿身边的东西，比如动物的叫声、大自然的声音和工具的声音。

paras.en: Perhaps they made the sound of wind to comment on the weather, or imitated the sound of a bird to tell a friend that there was a bird nearby.
paras.zh: 也许他们模仿风声来说天气，或者模仿鸟叫来告诉朋友附近有只鸟。

paras.en: Then, over hundreds of thousands of years, those sounds turned into words that people began to learn as part of their language.
paras.zh: 后来，经过几十万年，这些声音变成了单词，人们开始把它们作为语言的一部分来学。

w.h: over hundreds of thousands of years

paras.en: At some point people started stringing the words together to form sentences.
paras.zh: 到了某个时候，人们开始把单词串在一起组成句子。

paras.en: The other main theory, which is more recent, is that people started off by gesturing, pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies.
paras.zh: 另一种主要理论出现得比较晚，它认为人们一开始是打手势，用手指东西、用身体模仿动作。

paras.en: Eventually these gestures turned into full sign language.
paras.zh: 后来，这些手势变成了完整的手语。

paras.en: This theory guesses that after developing sign languages people eventually started making sounds along with their gestures.
paras.zh: 这种理论推测，人们在发展出手语之后，最终开始一边打手势一边发出声音。

paras.en: At some point they switched to mostly making sounds that became words instead of just using their bodies.
paras.zh: 到了某个时候，他们转而主要靠发出声音来交流，这些声音变成了单词，而不再只用身体。

paras.en: The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can’t see them.
paras.zh: 按照这种理论的说法，人们之所以改成发出声音，是因为大声说话能让你在看不见对方的时候也能和他交流。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: How did language come into being, according to researchers?
paras.zh: 第十六题：据研究人员说，语言是怎样产生的？

paras.en: Question seventeen: How did language start according to the first theory?
paras.zh: 第十七题：按照第一种理论，语言是怎样开始的？

paras.en: Question 18: Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds, according to the more recent theory?
paras.zh: 第十八题：按照较新的那种理论，人们为什么从打手势改成发出声音？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Is it a good idea to display luxury brands and other signals of status?
paras.zh: 展示奢侈品牌和其他身份地位的象征，是个好主意吗？

paras.en: It depends on the situation.
paras.zh: 这要看情况。

paras.en: Studies have shown that people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined, and competent than those who do not.
paras.zh: 研究表明，看起来有钱的人往往被认为比看起来没钱的人更聪明、更自律、更能干。

paras.en: But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others.
paras.zh: 但一项新研究发现，人们认为炫耀自己社会地位的人更在乎让自己得好处，而不是帮助别人。

paras.en: This means people are less willing to collaborate with them.
paras.zh: 这意味着人们不太愿意和他们合作。

paras.en: Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential, but the researchers also found that in some cases status signaling has advantages.
paras.zh: 需要合作的时候，谦虚可能是关键，但研究人员也发现，在有些情况下，显示身份地位也有好处。

w.m: adj. 必不可少的；非常重要的

paras.en: Experiments showed that participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to join a group seeking cooperative members, but participants were more likely to choose that person when they were looking for a competitive team member.
paras.zh: 实验显示，组建一个寻找合作型成员的小组时，参与者不太会选显示自己财富或地位的人加入；但在找有竞争力的队员时，参与者更可能选这样的人。

w.m: adj. 有竞争力的；好胜的

paras.en: These findings suggest that people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal.
paras.zh: 这些发现表明，人们应该根据自己的社交目标，改变展示自己的方式。

paras.en: This is the era of social media.
paras.zh: 现在是社交媒体的时代。

paras.en: People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider the consequences.
paras.zh: 人们可以轻松地向大量受众分享自己的财富和地位，但需要考虑后果。

paras.en: Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to persuade others and frighten competitors, but it could also signal to potential friends or future employers that you are unlikely to think about the needs of others.
paras.zh: 在网上晒奢侈品购物和昂贵的度假，也许能帮你说服别人、吓住竞争对手，但也可能向潜在的朋友或未来的雇主传递一个信号：你不太会考虑别人的需要。

paras.en: This makes things tricky for people who may want to impress others while also demonstrating that they are a team player.
paras.zh: 有的人既想给别人留下好印象，又想表现出自己有团队精神，这样一来事情就难办了。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?
paras.zh: 第十九题：根据新研究，人们会怎样描述炫耀自己社会地位的人？

paras.en: Question 20: When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?
paras.zh: 第二十题：参与者在什么时候更可能选显示自己财富或地位的人？

paras.en: Question 21: What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：人们在网上分享自己的财富和地位时应该怎么做？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do.
paras.zh: 人类对动物的着迷，和人类本身一样古老。

paras.en: Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to forty thousand years old, and there are more images of animals than humans.
paras.zh: 在已发现的最古老的洞穴壁画中，有些距今四万年，画里的动物比人还多。

paras.en: At some point, humans began to capture and hold animals.
paras.zh: 到了某个时候，人类开始捕捉并饲养动物。

paras.en: The first known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public.
paras.zh: 已知最早的动物收藏归王室所有，不对公众开放。

paras.en: In Egypt, researchers have found buildings from around 3500 BC containing the remains of animals, including elephants, which were not native to Egypt.
paras.zh: 在埃及，研究人员发现了大约公元前三五〇〇年的建筑，里面有动物的遗骸，其中包括大象，而大象并不是埃及本土的动物。

paras.en: But life wasn’t easy for these animals.
paras.zh: 可这些动物的日子并不好过。

paras.en: They probably had short lives, and the remains show evidence of severe injuries.
paras.zh: 它们的寿命可能很短，遗骸上还有受过重伤的痕迹。

paras.en: The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt’s queen Hatshepsut around 1480 BC.
paras.zh: 最早公开展示动物的场所，可能是埃及女王哈特谢普苏特在大约公元前一四八〇年建的。

paras.en: Researchers think the zoo was started with animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，这座动物园一开始养的是从一个叫蓬特的遥远国度带回来的动物。

paras.en: It’s unclear why the queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power.
paras.zh: 女王为什么建这座动物园还不清楚，但可能是为了炫耀自己的财富和权力。

paras.en: Early zoos are found all over the world.
paras.zh: 早期的动物园世界各地都有。

paras.en: In China Emperor Wen Wang is said to have built a garden of intelligence around ten sixty BC.
paras.zh: 在中国，据说周文王在大约公元前一〇六〇年建了一座灵囿。

paras.en: It included deer, birds, and many fish.
paras.zh: 里面有鹿、鸟和许多鱼。

paras.en: In England King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about eleven ten as part of the royal estate.
paras.zh: 在英国，国王亨利一世在大约一一一〇年建了一处动物收藏，作为王室庄园的一部分。

paras.en: His collection included tigers and lions.
paras.zh: 他收藏的动物里有老虎和狮子。

paras.en: This collection eventually moved to the Tower of London in 1235.
paras.zh: 这些动物最终在一二三五年搬到了伦敦塔。

paras.en: The collection stayed at that location for six hundred years.
paras.zh: 它们在那里待了六百年。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What can we see in the oldest cave paintings?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：在最古老的洞穴壁画中，我们能看到什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What do we learn about the first known collections of animals?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于已知最早的动物收藏，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What might be the reason the Egyptian queen created the zoo?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：这位埃及女王建动物园的原因可能是什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What do we learn about King Henry I’s collection of animals in England?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于英国国王亨利一世的动物收藏，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2025年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2025年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一年一度的七英里大桥长跑赛：佛罗里达州一名十五岁少年和一名亚特兰大女子分获男子组和女子组冠军，比赛吸引了全美四十一个州和多个国家的选手。第二篇新闻报道讲英国宇航员蒂姆·皮克永久卸任欧洲宇航员，改为全职担任科学与太空大使，并回顾了他的太空经历。第三篇新闻报道讲威尔士一家阿斯达超市成了五只猫的家，店员只好贴出告示，请顾客不要喂它们。第一段长对话里，女儿想下学期搬出校园和朋友合租，父亲担心安全、花费和通勤，答应和她母亲商量。第二段长对话里，女士给十岁的侄子挑礼物，店员推荐了动作人偶、益智拼图，最后她买了经典游戏“海战棋”。第一篇短文讲“选择悖论”：选择太多，人们反而更不愿意买。第二篇短文讲公司把员工志愿服务纳入工作，对员工和雇主都有好处。第三篇短文讲法国创业者索菲·安德烈在伦敦用高端食品供应商剩下的优质食材，为商务活动制作早餐和点心。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet One with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A Florida teenager and an Atlanta woman won the overall men’s and women’s divisions Saturday at the annual Seven Mile Bridge Run.
paras.zh: 周六，在一年一度的七英里大桥长跑赛上，一名佛罗里达少年和一名亚特兰大女子分别获得男子组和女子组的总冠军。

paras.en: Vaclav Bursa, fifteen, of Big Pine Key, Florida, finished first overall.
paras.zh: 来自佛罗里达州大派恩岛的十五岁少年瓦茨拉夫·布尔沙获得了总成绩第一。

paras.en: He completed the race in forty-one minutes and one second and claimed the top spot in the men’s division.
paras.zh: 他用四十一分零一秒跑完全程，夺得男子组第一名。

paras.en: Bursa won third place in the twenty twenty two race.
paras.zh: 布尔沙在二〇二二年的比赛中获得了第三名。

paras.en: He is a student at Marathon High School.
paras.zh: 他是马拉松高中的学生。

paras.en: Joanna Stevens, twenty-eight, of Atlanta, completed the course in forty-one minutes and twelve seconds.
paras.zh: 来自亚特兰大的二十八岁女子乔安娜·史蒂文斯用四十一分十二秒跑完全程。

paras.en: She won the Women’s Division title and placed second overall.
paras.zh: 她获得了女子组冠军，总成绩排名第二。

paras.en: The race drew competitors from forty-one US states.
paras.zh: 这场比赛吸引了来自美国四十一个州的选手。

paras.en: There were also runners from other countries, including Canada, the UK and Switzerland.
paras.zh: 还有来自其他国家的选手，包括加拿大、英国和瑞士。

paras.en: The run closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for three hours Saturday.
paras.zh: 周六，因为这场长跑，中礁群岛和下礁群岛之间的路段封闭了三个小时，禁止车辆通行。

paras.en: The April contest is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States.
paras.zh: 这场四月份的比赛是美国东南部最受欢迎的跑步赛事之一。

paras.en: The race field filled within minutes after online registration opened in January.
paras.zh: 一月份网上报名一开放，几分钟内名额就满了。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the news report say about Vaclav Bursa and Joanna Stevens?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于瓦茨拉夫·布尔沙和乔安娜·史蒂文斯，这篇新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question two: What do we learn about the April contest?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于这场四月份的比赛，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: British astronaut Tim Peake is stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut.
paras.zh: 英国宇航员蒂姆·皮克将永久卸任欧洲宇航员一职。

paras.en: He’s going to take up a full-time position as Ambassador for Science and Space instead, work he’s been doing since twenty nineteen.
paras.zh: 他将改为全职担任科学与太空大使，这份工作他从二〇一九年起就一直在做。

paras.en: The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in two thousand nine.
paras.zh: 这位英国陆军航空兵前直升机飞行员在二〇〇九年被选为欧洲航天局宇航员。

paras.en: He flew to the space station for a six-month tour in twenty fifteen.
paras.zh: 二〇一五年，他飞往空间站，执行了为期六个月的任务。

paras.en: The tour saw him control a robot on Earth remotely from orbit.
paras.zh: 执行任务期间，他在轨道上远程操控了地面上的一台机器人。

paras.en: He also helped dock two spacecraft.
paras.zh: 他还协助两艘航天器完成了对接。

paras.en: Tim said, being an astronaut has been the most extraordinary experience.
paras.zh: 蒂姆说，当宇航员是他最不平凡的经历。

paras.en: I’ve had the privilege of working with an exceptional team of individuals during the past thirteen years with the agency.
paras.zh: 在航天局的这十三年里，我有幸和一支优秀的团队共事。

paras.en: It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding.
paras.zh: 这段经历非常激动人心，也很有收获。

paras.en: By assuming the role of an ambassador for human flights to space, I’ll continue to support the European and the UK space agencies.
paras.zh: 担任载人航天飞行大使以后，我将继续支持欧洲航天局和英国航天局。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What do we learn from the news report about Tim Peake?
paras.zh: 第三题：从这篇新闻报道中，我们对蒂姆·皮克了解到什么？

paras.en: Question four: What does Tim Peake say about his work with the European Space Agency?
paras.zh: 第四题：蒂姆·皮克是怎样评价他在欧洲航天局的工作的？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: An Asda store in Wales is now home to five cats, after they wandered in and made themselves comfortable.
paras.zh: 威尔士的一家阿斯达超市现在成了五只猫的家，它们溜达进来后就在这里住得舒舒服服。

paras.en: The supermarket is known for its loyal customers, but now has a different kind of visitor that has appeared over the last year.
paras.zh: 这家超市以顾客忠诚出名，可在过去一年里，这里出现了另一种访客。

paras.en: Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats settling down in the shop aisles.
paras.zh: 超市的常客都见惯了几只猫在店里的过道上安顿下来的情景。

paras.en: The unusual situation started about twelve months ago, when one cat routinely started visiting the store.
paras.zh: 这种不寻常的情况大约从十二个月前开始，当时有一只猫开始经常来店里。

paras.en: Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost.
paras.zh: 据当地报纸报道，不解的顾客在脸书群组里发帖，想弄清楚这只猫是不是走丢了。

paras.en: But its owner assured the concerned customers it was very much loved and fed at home.
paras.zh: 但猫的主人向担心的顾客保证，猫在家里很受宠爱，也吃得很好。

paras.en: It just enjoyed visiting the shop.
paras.zh: 它只是喜欢来店里逛逛。

paras.en: Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around, but instead of leaving and never coming back, it invited its friends round.
paras.zh: 店员想尽办法不让这只猫在店里转悠，可它不但没有离开、再也不来，反而把朋友们都叫来了。

paras.en: There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.
paras.zh: 现在至少有五只不同的猫几乎天天都来。

paras.en: They visit the store so much that staff have been forced to put up signs asking their customers not to feed them.
paras.zh: 它们来店里的次数太多，店员只好贴出告示，请顾客不要喂它们。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about the five cats seen in the Asda store?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于阿斯达超市里的五只猫，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 6: What did some customers think when they saw the first cat routinely appear in the store?
paras.zh: 第六题：有些顾客看到第一只猫经常出现在店里时是怎么想的？

paras.en: Question seven: What are customers asked not to do?
paras.zh: 第七题：顾客被要求不要做什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I’ve been thinking about moving off campus next semester.
paras.zh: 我一直在考虑下学期搬到校外去住。

paras.en: Hmm, I don’t know if that’s a good idea, as your mother and I would worry about you living all by yourself in an apartment so far from home.
paras.zh: 嗯，我不知道这是不是个好主意，你离家这么远，一个人住公寓，你妈妈和我都会担心你。

paras.en: And then there’s the expense, too.
paras.zh: 还有，花费也是个问题。

paras.en: I’m not sure we can afford it.
paras.zh: 我不确定我们负担得起。

paras.en: Well, I wouldn’t be alone, actually.
paras.zh: 其实，我不会一个人住。

paras.en: Three of my friends from the dormitory would share the place with me.
paras.zh: 宿舍里的三个朋友会跟我合租。

paras.en: And, with four of us, it wouldn’t cost any more than living in the dorm.
paras.zh: 而且四个人一起住，花的钱不会比住宿舍多。

paras.en: Are you sure about that?
paras.zh: 你确定吗？

paras.en: Rents in big cities are high, and then there’s the cost of electricity and gas.
paras.zh: 大城市房租很贵，还有电费和燃气费。

paras.en: Have you factored those in?
paras.zh: 这些你都算进去了吗？

paras.en: We’ve budgeted for those, and for Internet and transportation.
paras.zh: 这些我们都做了预算，还有网费和交通费。

paras.en: And if we move far enough from the city center, the rent is low enough for us to afford all of it.
paras.zh: 而且如果我们搬到离市中心足够远的地方，房租就够低，这些我们都负担得起。

paras.en: What about the commute to and from campus?
paras.zh: 那往返学校的通勤呢？

w.m: n. 通勤；上下班（学）路程

paras.en: It sounds like you’ll be wasting several hours every day on the road instead of studying.
paras.zh: 听起来你每天要在路上浪费好几个小时，而不是用来学习。

paras.en: It’s about an hour to campus, but there’s no reason I can’t study on the bus.
paras.zh: 到学校大约一个小时，不过我完全可以在公交车上学习啊。

paras.en: After all, I did that during high school, and my commute was even longer then.
paras.zh: 毕竟我上高中时就这么做过，那时通勤时间还更长。

w.m: n. 通勤；上下班（学）路程

paras.en: That’s true.
paras.zh: 那倒是。

paras.en: But I’m not sure why you want to leave campus and go through all that trouble when the cost is the same.
paras.zh: 可我不明白，花费既然一样，你为什么要离开学校，费那么大劲。

paras.en: For a lot of reasons.
paras.zh: 原因有很多。

paras.en: We’d have a kitchen so we could cook ourselves.
paras.zh: 我们会有厨房，可以自己做饭。

paras.en: And we’d each have our own bedroom where we could study instead of going to the library.
paras.zh: 而且我们每个人都会有自己的卧室，可以在卧室学习，不用去图书馆。

paras.en: We’d just have more space and privacy.
paras.zh: 我们会有更多的空间和隐私。

paras.en: I’m not convinced that the benefits are greater than the disadvantages, but I’ll discuss this with your mother.
paras.zh: 我不相信好处比坏处多，不过我会和你妈妈商量一下。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What has the woman been thinking of doing next semester?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士一直在考虑下学期做什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the man suggest the woman take into consideration?
paras.zh: 第九题：男士建议女士考虑什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the woman say she did during high school?
paras.zh: 第十题：女士说她上高中时做过什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the man say he’ll do at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十一题：对话最后，男士说他会做什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Good morning.
paras.zh: 早上好。

paras.en: I’m looking for a present for my nephew, Lawrence.
paras.zh: 我想给我侄子劳伦斯买个礼物。

paras.en: Hi.
paras.zh: 你好。

paras.en: Do you have anything in mind?
paras.zh: 您心里有想好的吗？

paras.en: I’m not sure.
paras.zh: 我不确定。

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 没有。
