paras.en: Do you know what boys aged around ten typically like?
paras.zh: 你知道十岁左右的男孩一般喜欢什么吗？

paras.en: For that age group, our biggest seller this year has been this action figure.
paras.zh: 这个年龄段的话，我们今年卖得最好的就是这个动作人偶。

paras.en: It’s called Bobo Man, and it’s incredibly popular.
paras.zh: 它叫“波波人”，特别受欢迎。

paras.en: Does it do anything?
paras.zh: 它会动吗？

paras.en: Not by itself.
paras.zh: 自己不会动。

paras.en: It has no batteries, if that’s what you mean.
paras.zh: 它不用电池，如果您是这个意思的话。

paras.en: There’s a Bobo Man cartoon popular amongst young children, you see, and this toy is the lead character from the show.
paras.zh: 您知道，有一部《波波人》动画片在小孩子里很流行，这个玩具就是片里的主角。

paras.en: Oh, I understand now.
paras.zh: 哦，我现在明白了。

paras.en: I’ve never heard of it, but I do know little Lawrence loves cartoons.
paras.zh: 我从没听说过这部动画片，不过我知道小劳伦斯确实很喜欢动画片。

paras.en: Do you have any other popular toys?
paras.zh: 你们还有别的受欢迎的玩具吗？

paras.en: Perhaps something educational?
paras.zh: 有没有益智一点的？

w.m: adj. 有教育意义的；益智的

paras.en: Yes, of course.
paras.zh: 有，当然有。

paras.en: Right over here we have dozens of puzzles for children of all ages.
paras.zh: 这边就有几十种拼图，各个年龄的孩子都适合。

paras.en: They are fun, great for exercising the mind, and can be played either alone or in groups.
paras.zh: 这些拼图很好玩，很能锻炼脑子，一个人玩、几个人一起玩都行。

paras.en: I like this sort of idea.
paras.zh: 我喜欢这种想法。

paras.en: Lawrence has a sister, who is slightly older, so maybe a game that they can play together would be good.
paras.zh: 劳伦斯有个姐姐，比他大一点，所以也许买个他们俩能一起玩的游戏比较好。

paras.en: What do you think of battleships, then?
paras.zh: 那您觉得“海战棋”怎么样？

paras.en: It’s a total classic.
paras.zh: 这可是经典中的经典。

paras.en: It has been around since the 1930s.
paras.zh: 它从二十世纪三十年代就有了。

paras.en: Oh yeah, we had one of those when growing up.
paras.zh: 哦，对，我们小时候就有一副。

paras.en: Of course you did.
paras.zh: 您当然有。

paras.en: Everyone did.
paras.zh: 人人都有。

paras.en: And kids enjoy it just as much today as you and I did when we were young.
paras.zh: 现在的孩子玩起来，还是像您和我小时候一样开心。

paras.en: Some games just never get old.
paras.zh: 有些游戏就是永远不过时。

paras.en: I suppose you are right.
paras.zh: 我想你说得对。

paras.en: I have fond memories playing battleships when it was raining outside and we had to stay indoors.
paras.zh: 我还清楚地记得，外面下雨、我们只能待在屋里的时候，就玩海战棋，那些回忆很美好。

paras.en: That’s decided, then.
paras.zh: 那就定了。

paras.en: How much?
paras.zh: 多少钱？

paras.en: Nineteen pounds and 90 pence, please.
paras.zh: 一共十九英镑九十便士。

paras.en: There you are.
paras.zh: 给您。

paras.en: Have a nice day.
paras.zh: 祝您愉快。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。

paras.en: You too.
paras.zh: 你也是。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What is the woman doing?
paras.zh: 第十二题：女士在做什么？

paras.en: Question thirteen: How does the man describe Bobo Man, the action figure?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士是怎样描述动作人偶“波波人”的？

paras.en: Question 14: What kind of game does the woman think would be good for Lawrence?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士认为什么样的游戏适合劳伦斯？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What do we learn from the conversation about the game Battleships?
paras.zh: 第十五题：从对话中，我们对“海战棋”这款游戏了解到什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: We assume that if we offer our customers more choices, then they’ll be more likely to buy our products.
paras.zh: 我们以为，给顾客提供的选择越多，他们就越可能买我们的产品。

paras.en: But here’s the paradox of choice.
paras.zh: 可这里有个“选择悖论”。

paras.en: If a person is presented with too many choices, they are actually less likely to buy.
paras.zh: 一个人面对的选择太多，反而更不愿意买。

paras.en: In twenty twelve, psychologists published a study about jams.
paras.zh: 二〇一二年，心理学家发表了一项关于果酱的研究。

paras.en: On a regular day at a local food market, people would find a display table with twenty-four different kinds of jams.
paras.zh: 在当地一个食品市场，平常的某一天，人们会看到一张摆着二十四种果酱的展示桌。

paras.en: Then, on another day, at that same food market, people were given only six different types of jam choices.
paras.zh: 然后，换一天，还是在这个食品市场，只给人们提供六种果酱。

paras.en: Guess which display table led to more sales?
paras.zh: 猜猜哪张展示桌卖得更多？

paras.en: The study found that, while the bigger display table created more interest, people were almost ten times less likely to purchase a jar of jam than in the case of the smaller display.
paras.zh: 研究发现，虽然大展示桌引起的兴趣更大，但和小展示桌相比，人们买一罐果酱的可能性几乎低了十倍。

paras.en: Customer satisfaction takes a hit as well.
paras.zh: 顾客满意度也会下降。

paras.en: In the study, the bigger display of jams leads to lower customer satisfaction than the smaller display.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，果酱展示得多，顾客满意度反而比展示得少时更低。

paras.en: In an extensive study published in twenty fifteen, researchers analyzed a total of ninety-nine choice studies and specifically looked at those cases in which reducing choices helped to boost sales.
paras.zh: 二〇一五年发表的一项大规模研究中，研究人员总共分析了九十九项关于选择的研究，专门研究了那些减少选择反而促进销售的案例。

paras.en: They found four rules that motivate consumers to buy.
paras.zh: 他们发现了促使消费者购买的四条规律。

paras.en: When people want to make a quick and easy choice, when the product is complex, when it’s difficult to compare alternatives, and when consumers don’t have clear preferences.
paras.zh: 那就是：人们想快速、轻松地做出选择时，产品比较复杂时，各种选项难以比较时，以及消费者没有明确的偏好时。

paras.en: So as you can see, when it comes to choices, less is more.
paras.zh: 所以你看，说到选择，少就是多。

paras.en: Questions sixteen to eighteen are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question sixteen: What do we learn from the passage about the paradox of choice?
paras.zh: 第十六题：从短文中，我们对“选择悖论”了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What did the psychologists want to find out in their 2012 study about jams?
paras.zh: 第十七题：心理学家在二〇一二年关于果酱的研究中想弄清楚什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What is the finding of an extensive study published in 2015?
paras.zh: 第十八题：二〇一五年发表的那项大规模研究有什么发现？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: The New Year has come and gone, and many may have already forgotten what they had resolved to do on January first.
paras.zh: 新年来了又过去了，很多人可能已经忘了自己一月一日下定决心要做的事。

paras.en: But if that resolution was to volunteer more, now is the best time to start.
paras.zh: 不过，如果你的新年决心是多做志愿服务，那现在就是开始的最好时机。

paras.en: Volunteering can drop after the holiday season, and by February some organizations lack the volunteers they had in surplus just a month ago.
paras.zh: 假期一过，志愿服务往往会减少，到了二月，一些机构就缺志愿者了，而一个月前他们的志愿者还多得用不完。

paras.en: According to one survey, only twenty-six per cent of Americans volunteer, despite reports that many Americans view volunteering as worthwhile.
paras.zh: 一项调查显示，只有百分之二十六的美国人做志愿服务，尽管有报告称很多美国人认为志愿服务很有意义。

w.m: adj. 值得做的；有意义的

paras.en: Why such a disconnect?
paras.zh: 为什么会脱节呢？

paras.en: Most people cite time and conflicting work schedules as major barriers.
paras.zh: 大多数人说主要障碍是没时间、工作安排有冲突。

paras.en: But employees and employers would actually benefit if companies made employee volunteering part of the job.
paras.zh: 但如果公司把员工的志愿服务作为工作的一部分，员工和雇主其实都会受益。

paras.en: Researchers have found donating our time and talent to others can lower blood pressure, boost happiness, and improve mental and physical health.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，把自己的时间和才能献给别人，可以降低血压、增加幸福感、改善身心健康。

paras.en: Studies have also linked employee volunteer programs with more productive employees.
paras.zh: 研究还发现，员工志愿服务项目和员工工作效率更高有关系。

paras.en: With so much emphasis on employee wellness these days, company volunteer programs could be the perfect twenty twenty five resolution.
paras.zh: 如今大家这么重视员工的身心健康，公司志愿服务项目也许正是二〇二五年最好的新年计划。

paras.en: But for volunteering to benefit employees and the workplace, the entire organization needs to be involved.
paras.zh: 但要让志愿服务真正对员工和工作场所有好处，整个机构都得参与进来。

paras.en: By allowing employees to donate their time during work hours, the workplace becomes an outlet for personal fulfillment without affecting personal time.
paras.zh: 允许员工在上班时间奉献时间，工作场所就成了实现个人价值的地方，又不占用个人时间。

paras.en: In one survey, eighty nine per cent of employees perceived companies that sponsored volunteer activities as creating a better working environment, and seventy-five per cent said volunteering was critical to their well-being.
paras.zh: 在一项调查中，百分之八十九的员工认为，资助志愿活动的公司能营造更好的工作环境，还有百分之七十五的员工说，志愿服务对他们的身心健康非常重要。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What do many Americans think of volunteering?
paras.zh: 第十九题：很多美国人对志愿服务有什么看法？

paras.en: Question twenty: How could companies ensure both employees and employers benefit from volunteering?
paras.zh: 第二十题：公司怎样才能保证员工和雇主都从志愿服务中受益？

paras.en: Question 21: What did seventy five per cent of employees say about volunteering in a survey?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：在一项调查中，百分之七十五的员工对志愿服务有什么说法？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: The vast majority of the UK’s two hundred thousand tons of retail sector’s annual food waste comes from supermarkets, but it’s a problem that impacts independent luxury food suppliers too.
paras.zh: 英国零售业每年有二十万吨食物浪费，其中绝大部分来自超市，但这个问题也影响到独立的高端食品供应商。

paras.en: The scale is small.
paras.zh: 规模不大。

paras.en: It’s estimated at less than one per cent of the UK’s food waste total, but the quality from these suppliers is high.
paras.zh: 据估计，它占英国食物浪费总量不到百分之一，但这些供应商的东西质量很高。

paras.en: Everything from specialist cheeses to sought-after coffee beans gets thrown away every day in the current food system.
paras.zh: 在现在的食品体系里，从特色奶酪到抢手的咖啡豆，什么都会被扔掉，天天如此。

paras.en: This is where French entrepreneur Sophie Andre comes in.
paras.zh: 这正是法国创业者索菲·安德烈出场的地方。

paras.en: In twenty sixteen she moved to London and began by setting up a business delivering luxury handmade food across the city.
paras.zh: 二〇一六年她搬到伦敦，一开始创办了一家企业，在全市配送高端手工食品。

paras.en: Food delivery seems to be a big thing here, she says.
paras.zh: 她说，外卖配送在这里好像很火。

paras.en: So I started delivering products by bicycle.
paras.zh: 所以我开始骑自行车送货。

paras.en: Talking with local producers I learned that a small part of the production is sometimes wasted due to problems with size or shape, but the quality of the products remains unchanged.
paras.zh: 和当地生产商聊天时，我了解到，有时候因为大小或形状有问题，一小部分产品会被浪费掉，但产品的质量并没有变。

paras.en: Unlike many food waste projects that have sprung up in recent years, the idea is not simply to redistribute waste food, but to provide a high-quality product.
paras.zh: 近几年冒出了不少减少食物浪费的项目，但和它们中的很多不一样，她的想法不只是把剩余的食物重新分配出去，而是要提供高质量的产品。

paras.en: Andre’s company, Elysia, offers breakfasts and snacks specifically aimed at business meetings and events.
paras.zh: 安德烈的公司叫“伊莉西亚”，专门为商务会议和活动提供早餐和点心。

paras.en: Once sourced, Elysia uses waste products to create simple, natural, straightforward meals and snacks.
paras.zh: 食材一采购到位，伊莉西亚就用这些剩余产品做出简单、天然、朴实的餐点和小吃。

paras.en: Perhaps unlike other waste food, the supply is regular.
paras.zh: 也许和别的剩余食物不同，这里的供应是稳定的。

paras.en: Suppliers will always have a certain amount of surplus.
paras.zh: 供应商总会有一定数量的剩余。

paras.en: So the menus remain regular too.
paras.zh: 所以菜单也能保持固定。

paras.en: Andre believes this benefits both her business and her customers.
paras.zh: 安德烈认为，这对她的公司和顾客都有好处。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What do we learn about the UK’s retail sector food waste?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于英国零售业的食物浪费，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does Sophie Andre’s business do in London?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：索菲·安德烈的公司在伦敦做什么？

paras.en: Question 24: In what way does Sophie Andre’s business differ from many food waste projects?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：索菲·安德烈的公司和很多减少食物浪费的项目有什么不同？

paras.en: Question 25: Why will suppliers always have a certain amount of surplus?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：供应商为什么总会有一定数量的剩余？

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2025年12月大学英语四级 第1套
passages.name: 2025年12月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲英国肯特郡一只受惊的猫躲在汽车引擎盖下，跟着车跑了五英里，被救出后回到了主人身边。第二篇新闻报道讲特殊奥林匹克春季运动会时隔五年重回费耶特维尔，组织者欢迎大家报名当志愿者。第三篇新闻报道讲一家德国超市输掉官司，被判销毁仿冒瑞士品牌的巧克力兔子。第一段长对话里，女士要给姐姐素食的男朋友做菜，两人聊到吃素的原因和动物园该不该存在。第二段长对话里，两人聊起一期讲坐飞机出行的电视节目：怎样克服时差反应，以及很多人怕坐飞机。第一篇短文里，作者认为入行用户体验设计，什么都代替不了实际工作经验。第二篇短文讲一所学校把传统的成排课桌换成灵活座位，学生更投入、违纪也少了。第三篇短文讲英国一所中学因为新的校服规定，开学第一天把约三十名学生送回了家，在生活成本高涨的情况下，一些家长觉得负担太重。

paras.en: College English Test.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Band 4.
paras.zh: 四级。

paras.en: Part 2.
paras.zh: 第二部分。

paras.en: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the centre.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案，然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A terrified cat has survived a five mile round trip under the engine cover of a car on a school run.
paras.zh: 一只吓坏了的猫躲在汽车的引擎盖下，跟着送孩子上学的车跑了五英里的来回，竟然活了下来。

w.m: adj. 吓坏了的；非常害怕的

paras.en: The black cat was found curled up under the engine cover of David King’s car when he decided to do an oil check after dropping his grandson off at school in Kent.
paras.zh: 戴维·金在肯特郡把孙子送到学校后，决定检查一下机油，这才发现这只黑猫蜷缩在他汽车的引擎盖下。

paras.en: Mr. King’s wife said her husband had come running in and was shouting for me to come have a look.
paras.zh: 金先生的妻子说，她丈夫跑进屋，大声喊我过去看看。

paras.en: We weren’t even sure it was alive, so I gently pushed it with a stick to check it was breathing, and saw it was a terrified little cat.
paras.zh: 我们连它是不是还活着都不确定，所以我用一根棍子轻轻捅了捅它，看它还有没有呼吸，结果发现是一只吓坏了的小猫。

w.m: adj. 吓坏了的；非常害怕的

paras.en: It reversed even further into the engine and was stuck.
paras.zh: 它往发动机里面退得更深了，卡在了里面。

paras.en: I tried to reach it, but it was too far down, and there wasn’t any way I could get it out.
paras.zh: 我想够到它，可它躲得太深了，我怎么也没办法把它弄出来。

paras.en: Following a rescue by UK charity Cats Protection, the four-year-old cat was later reunited with its owner, Mr. King’s neighbor.
paras.zh: 英国慈善机构“猫咪保护”把它救了出来，之后这只四岁的猫回到了主人身边——它的主人正是金先生的邻居。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: Where was the black cat found?
paras.zh: 第一题：这只黑猫是在哪里被发现的？

w.m: v. 发现（find 的过去分词）

paras.en: Question two: What do we learn about the cat at the end of the news report?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于这只猫，新闻报道最后告诉了我们什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: In less than a month, the Special Olympic Spring Games will make a return to Fayetteville.
paras.zh: 不到一个月后，特殊奥林匹克春季运动会将重回费耶特维尔。

paras.en: The Games are coming back for the first time in five years.
paras.zh: 这是运动会五年来第一次回到这里。

paras.en: The event will take place at Methodist University.
paras.zh: 比赛将在卫理公会大学举行。

paras.en: Event organizer Benjamin Kowalzik says he’s excited that athletes will get a chance to come back and demonstrate their abilities.
paras.zh: 赛事组织者本杰明·科瓦尔齐克说，运动员们有机会回来展示自己的能力，他感到很兴奋。

paras.en: Organizers expect about 100 athletes will come out to compete in Fayetteville.
paras.zh: 组织者预计将有大约一百名运动员来费耶特维尔参赛。

paras.en: They will have a variety of events to choose from, including running, throwing, and jumping.
paras.zh: 他们有各种项目可以选，包括跑步、投掷和跳跃。

paras.en: There will also be a fun tent for children.
paras.zh: 现场还会有一个儿童游乐帐篷。

paras.en: Kowalzik said it’s rewarding to see athletes with special needs triumph in the Games.
paras.zh: 科瓦尔齐克说，看到有特殊需要的运动员在运动会上取得胜利，让人很有成就感。

w.m: adj. 有成就感的；值得做的

paras.en: For anyone who wants to help make this year’s Games a massive success, there are still opportunities to volunteer for Fayetteville’s Special Olympics.
paras.zh: 谁想帮忙让今年的运动会大获成功，现在还有机会报名当费耶特维尔特殊奥运会的志愿者。

paras.en: Organizers encourage them to visit the Games website to sign up.
paras.zh: 组织者鼓励他们登录运动会的网站报名。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What will Fayetteville witness in less than a month?
paras.zh: 第三题：不到一个月后，费耶特维尔将迎来什么？

paras.en: Question four: What did Benjamin Kowalczyk say is rewarding to see?
paras.zh: 第四题：本杰明·科瓦尔齐克说，看到什么让人很有成就感？

w.m: adj. 有成就感的；值得做的

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A German supermarket has been ordered to destroy its chocolate rabbits after it lost a court battle with a Swiss chocolate manufacturer.
paras.zh: 一家德国超市输掉了和一家瑞士巧克力生产商的官司，被勒令销毁它的巧克力兔子。

paras.en: The Swiss firm had argued its gold-wrapped chocolate rabbit deserved copyright protection from a similar product sold by the budget supermarket.
paras.zh: 这家瑞士公司此前提出，它那款金色包装的巧克力兔子应该受到版权保护，不能让这家廉价超市卖的类似产品仿冒。

paras.en: Switzerland’s highest court agreed and overturned a ruling last year by the country’s commercial court that had sided with the supermarket.
paras.zh: 瑞士最高法院认同这一点，推翻了该国商事法院去年作出的一项支持超市的裁决。

paras.en: It ordered that all the imitation rabbits be destroyed, but suggested the chocolate needn’t be wasted, it could be melted for use in other products.
paras.zh: 法院下令销毁所有仿冒的兔子，但也提出巧克力不必浪费，可以融化后用来做别的产品。

paras.en: It said even though there are some differences between the two products, there was still the possibility of confusion for consumers.
paras.zh: 法院说，虽然两种产品有些不同，但消费者还是可能把它们弄混。

paras.en: The Swiss manufacturer’s rabbit has a red bow and bell, while the German supermarket’s has a green bow and bell.
paras.zh: 瑞士生产商的兔子系着红色的蝴蝶结和铃铛，而德国超市的兔子系的是绿色的蝴蝶结和铃铛。

paras.en: The color of the wrapper is similar, as are the illustrations of the features.
paras.zh: 包装纸的颜色很像，兔子五官的图案也很像。

paras.en: The chocolate company has been to court before to protect its popular chocolate treat.
paras.zh: 为了保护这款很受欢迎的巧克力，这家巧克力公司以前就打过官司。

paras.en: Last year a German federal court said the shade of the gold wrapping was also protected.
paras.zh: 去年，德国一家联邦法院裁定，这种金色包装的色调也受到保护。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What has the German supermarket been ordered to do?
paras.zh: 第五题：这家德国超市被勒令做什么？

paras.en: Question six: What did Switzerland’s highest court suggest about the chocolate in question?
paras.zh: 第六题：对于涉事的巧克力，瑞士最高法院提出了什么建议？

paras.en: Question seven: Why did Switzerland’s highest court overturn the Commercial Court’s ruling?
paras.zh: 第七题：瑞士最高法院为什么推翻商事法院的裁决？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Can you please hand me that book over there?
paras.zh: 你能把那边那本书递给我吗？

paras.en: It has instructions for making a winter bean salad.
paras.zh: 书里有做冬季豆子沙拉的方法。

paras.en: My sister’s boyfriend is coming over for dinner.
paras.zh: 我姐姐的男朋友要来家里吃晚饭。

paras.en: He’s vegetarian, so I need to make a lot of vegetable dishes.
paras.zh: 他吃素，所以我得做很多素菜。

paras.en: He only eats vegetables?
paras.zh: 他只吃蔬菜？

paras.en: No meat?
paras.zh: 一点肉都不吃？

paras.en: That doesn’t sound like a very balanced diet.
paras.zh: 这样饮食听起来不太均衡啊。

paras.en: How can he get enough protein?
paras.zh: 他怎么能摄入足够的蛋白质呢？

paras.en: What does he do to strengthen his muscles and all that?
paras.zh: 他怎么增强肌肉之类的？

paras.en: Apparently that’s no problem.
paras.zh: 看来这完全没问题。

paras.en: He’s explained this to me when we first met.
paras.zh: 我们第一次见面时，他就给我解释过这个。

paras.en: He eats a variety of different vegetables and nuts, especially those with high amounts of protein.
paras.zh: 他吃各种各样的蔬菜和坚果，尤其是蛋白质含量高的那些。

paras.en: It sounds a bit difficult, but he’s done his research, I suppose.
paras.zh: 听起来有点难，不过我想他应该做过一番研究。

paras.en: What’s his reasoning for being vegetarian?
paras.zh: 他吃素的理由是什么？

paras.en: Is it his religion, health condition, or lifestyle?
paras.zh: 是因为宗教信仰、身体状况，还是生活方式？

paras.en: He’s an animal activist.
paras.zh: 他是个动物保护活动人士。

w.m: n. 活动人士；积极分子

paras.en: He’s always been very sensitive and sympathizes with animals.
paras.zh: 他一直很敏感，很同情动物。

paras.en: He’s even written to his state senator about the torture of dolphins in sea parks.
paras.zh: 他甚至给本州的参议员写过信，说海洋公园里的海豚受到了虐待。

paras.en: He says that keeping animals in zoos and parks causes them great distress.
paras.zh: 他说，把动物关在动物园和公园里会让它们非常痛苦。

paras.en: That’s a little gloomy, but I can understand that to a point.
paras.zh: 这有点悲观，不过在一定程度上我能理解。

w.m: adj. 悲观的；令人沮丧的

paras.en: Not all zoos and animal parks have the most favorable conditions.
paras.zh: 不是所有动物园和动物公园的条件都那么好。

paras.en: But without them, it just wouldn’t be feasible to learn about animals and their environments.
paras.zh: 可是没有它们，就根本没法去了解动物和它们的生存环境。

paras.en: Besides, I don’t think I could ever give up a good hot dog at a baseball game.
paras.zh: 再说了，我觉得我怎么也戒不掉在棒球赛上吃个热乎乎的热狗。

paras.en: Honestly, I agree.
paras.zh: 说实话，我也这么觉得。

paras.en: But just don’t let him hear you say that.
paras.zh: 不过千万别让他听到你这么说。

paras.en: He’s the spokesperson for his local animal rights group.
paras.zh: 他是当地一个动物权益组织的发言人。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: What does the man request the woman to do?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士请女士做什么？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman say about eating vegetables only?
paras.zh: 第九题：对于只吃蔬菜，女士怎么说？

paras.en: Question 10: Why does the boyfriend of the man’s sister choose to be a vegetarian?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士姐姐的男朋友为什么选择吃素？

paras.en: Question eleven: On what point does the man agree with the woman at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十一题：对话最后，男士在哪一点上同意女士的看法？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Did you see that television program on air travel last night?
paras.zh: 昨晚那个讲坐飞机出行的电视节目你看了吗？

paras.en: Yes.
paras.zh: 看了。

paras.en: The part about overcoming jet lag was interesting.
paras.zh: 讲怎么克服时差反应的那部分很有意思。

paras.en: I was surprised that the expert recommended not eating for the entire journey and avoiding sleeping on the plane.
paras.zh: 让我吃惊的是，那位专家建议整个旅途都不吃东西，也别在飞机上睡觉。

paras.en: I was, too, as I read an article on the subject in the past that suggested the opposite.
paras.zh: 我也很吃惊，因为我以前读过一篇这方面的文章，说法正好相反。

paras.en: It claimed that it was important not to miss meals and that taking a nap on the plane was the best way to adjust to a new time zone.
paras.zh: 文章说，重要的是不能错过饭点，在飞机上小睡一会儿是适应新时区的最好办法。

paras.en: Well, the expert on the show did cite research supporting her recommendations, so I guess I’ll give it a try next time I fly a long distance.
paras.zh: 嗯，节目里的专家确实引用了支持她建议的研究，所以我想下次坐飞机出远门的时候试一试。

paras.en: Jet lag is a big problem for me, and has been for the last few years, even though I never suffered from it before.
paras.zh: 时差反应对我来说是个大问题，这几年一直这样，可我以前从来没受过这个罪。

paras.en: Well, she did say that jet lag often becomes more of a problem after 40.
paras.zh: 嗯，她确实说过，四十岁以后时差反应往往会更严重。

paras.en: So I guess I’m lucky that I can still adjust to different time zones well.
paras.zh: 这么说我还挺幸运的，还能很好地适应不同时区。

paras.en: My problem is I’m afraid to fly.
paras.zh: 我的问题是我怕坐飞机。

paras.en: Oh, I didn’t know that.
paras.zh: 哦，我都不知道。

paras.en: Actually, my mother is terrified of airplanes to the point where she can’t even fly, so our family vacations were always by car or train.
paras.zh: 其实我妈妈特别怕坐飞机，怕到根本没法坐，所以我们全家度假一直都是开车或坐火车。

paras.en: I’m not as bad as that.
paras.zh: 我没她那么严重。

paras.en: I just get anxious before I fly and feel nervous the whole time we’re in the air.
paras.zh: 我只是上飞机前会焦虑，飞在天上的整个过程都很紧张。

paras.en: Which is why I was hoping the television program would cover that topic more than it did.
paras.zh: 所以我本来希望那个电视节目能多讲讲这方面的内容。

paras.en: Yeah, that segment was too brief, especially as so many people have that problem.
paras.zh: 是啊，那部分太短了，何况有这个问题的人那么多。

paras.en: She said 20% of people are afraid to fly.
paras.zh: 她说有百分之二十的人怕坐飞机。

paras.en: Actually, it was a quarter of people, so the problem really is widespread and deserves attention.
paras.zh: 其实是四分之一的人，所以这个问题真的很普遍，值得重视。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What part of the TV program does the man say was interesting?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士说电视节目的哪一部分很有意思？

paras.en: Question thirteen: What does the man say he will do next time he flies a long distance?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士说下次坐飞机出远门时他会怎么做？

paras.en: Question 14: Why does the woman think she is lucky?
paras.zh: 第十四题：女士为什么觉得自己很幸运？

paras.en: Question 15: Why does the woman think the problem of being afraid to fly deserves attention?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士为什么认为怕坐飞机这个问题值得重视？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: The most common question I’m asked always centers around how to get started in user experience design, to which my response is always that nothing can substitute real world experience.
paras.zh: 别人问我最多的问题，总是围绕怎样入行用户体验设计，我的回答永远是：什么都代替不了实际工作经验。

paras.en: Building the skills required of a user experience designer takes time, patience and commitment.
paras.zh: 要练就用户体验设计师需要的技能，得花时间，要有耐心，还得全身心投入。

paras.en: Higher education is a great way to equip yourself with some core skills but it will not prepare you for actual challenges you’ll face with client work.
paras.zh: 高等教育是让自己掌握一些核心技能的好途径，但它没法让你为给客户做项目时会遇到的实际挑战做好准备。

paras.en: In other words, being proficient with a design tool and a few methods doesn’t make you a user experience designer.
paras.zh: 换句话说，会用一种设计工具、懂几种方法，并不能让你成为用户体验设计师。

paras.en: There simply isn’t a one-size-fits-all process.
paras.zh: 根本就没有一套适用于所有情况的流程。

w.m: adj. 一刀切的；适用于所有情况的

paras.en: Being effective requires adaptability, something you don’t really learn in school, much less in a six-month training camp.
paras.zh: 想做得出色，就要有适应能力，这在学校里学不到，在六个月的培训营里就更学不到了。

paras.en: It’s gained through experience on the job and learning what’s appropriate given the needs of the project.
paras.zh: 这种能力要靠在工作中积累经验，根据项目的需要，学会判断怎样做才合适。

paras.en: I found my way to user experience through graphic design and slowly over many different roles and experiences, that led me to become a user experience designer.
paras.zh: 我是从平面设计起步走进用户体验这一行的，慢慢地，经过很多不同的岗位和经历，我成了一名用户体验设计师。

paras.en: It took time and commitment to continue to pursue roles within teams that I knew could teach and challenge me.
paras.zh: 我花了时间，也全身心投入，一直去争取那些我知道能让我学到东西、给我挑战的团队岗位。

paras.en: That’s not to say that I think my path is the only one.
paras.zh: 这并不是说我认为只有我这条路才走得通。

paras.en: But once again, nothing can substitute real world experience.
paras.zh: 不过还是那句话，什么都代替不了实际工作经验。

paras.en: You can start anywhere, as long as you know your end goal, and you commit to actively pursuing opportunities to learn and grow along the way.
paras.zh: 你从哪里起步都可以，只要你清楚自己的最终目标，并且下决心一路上主动去争取学习和成长的机会。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker think is the best way to get started in user experience design?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人认为入行用户体验设计的最好办法是什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What does the speaker say being effective requires?
paras.zh: 第十七题：说话人说，想做得出色需要什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What can people do as long as they know their end goal and strive for it?
paras.zh: 第十八题：只要人们清楚自己的最终目标，并为之努力，就能做什么？

paras.en: Passage 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: When planning for this year, our principal asked what needed to change to engage students more in their learning.
paras.zh: 规划今年的工作时，我们校长问，需要做出哪些改变，才能让学生更投入地学习。

paras.en: I responded in a whisper, “Flexible seating,” thinking about our then current classroom.
paras.zh: 我小声回答：“灵活座位。”心里想着我们当时的教室。

paras.en: It had rows of desks with blue chairs and name plates, reminding each student where they should be sitting.
paras.zh: 教室里是一排排的课桌，配着蓝色椅子和名牌，提醒每个学生该坐在哪里。

paras.en: This began a journey to transform our practice and challenge the ways of learning for a group of Year Six students used to sitting in desks and rows for years.
paras.zh: 就这样，我们开始了一段历程：改变我们的教学做法，挑战一群六年级学生的学习方式——他们多年来已经习惯了坐在一排排的课桌前。

paras.en: Flexible seating has been defined as movable furniture to create an engaging learning environment.
paras.zh: 灵活座位的定义是：用可移动的家具营造一个吸引人投入学习的环境。

w.m: adj. 吸引人的；令人投入的

paras.en: It is a shift in practice from being teacher focused to student focused learning.
paras.zh: 这是教学做法上的转变：从以教师为中心转向以学生为中心的学习。

w.m: adj. 以……为中心的；专注的

paras.en: For us, flexible seating has meant removing most of the traditional chairs and desks, and introducing a variety of different seating options to promote student engagement.
paras.zh: 对我们来说，灵活座位就是撤掉大部分传统的桌椅，换上各种不同的座位，让学生更投入。

paras.en: The use of rows and their minimal adaptations to U-shape were traditionally intended to maximize on-task behavior and reduce distraction from the teacher.
paras.zh: 成排的座位，以及把它稍加调整成的U形，原本是为了尽量让学生专心做该做的事，减少学生分心，让他们专心听老师讲。

w.m: adj. 极小的；最低限度的

paras.en: Teachers tend to still use this format because of either the need to control students or the belief that the teacher is the most important person in the room.
paras.zh: 老师们之所以还爱用这种排法，要么是因为需要管住学生，要么是因为觉得老师是教室里最重要的人。

paras.en: Now our students have a range of different seating options, including a floor desk, couches, stools, bean bags, and the traditional desk and chair.
paras.zh: 现在，我们的学生有各种不同的座位可以选，有矮桌、沙发、凳子、豆袋椅，还有传统的桌椅。

paras.en: From our experience so far, flexible seating enhances student ownership of space and engagement in learning, while reducing rates of student disengagement and disciplinary actions.
paras.zh: 从我们目前的经验来看，灵活座位能增强学生对空间的主人翁意识，让他们更投入学习，同时也让学生不投入和违纪受处分的情况变少了。

w.m: n. 主人翁意识；所有权

paras.en: It is a win for all concerned.
paras.zh: 这对各方都是好事。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: Why did the school principal ask what needed to change?
paras.zh: 第十九题：校长为什么问需要做出哪些改变？

paras.en: Question twenty: What has flexible seating meant at the speaker’s school?
paras.zh: 第二十题：在说话人的学校，灵活座位意味着什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What has flexible seating brought about at the speaker’s school?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：灵活座位给说话人的学校带来了什么？

paras.en: Passage Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Dozens of British students arriving for their first day of school on Tuesday were sent home over their shoes.
paras.zh: 周二开学第一天，几十名英国学生到校后因为鞋子不合规定被送回了家。

paras.en: About thirty students were turned away from Taverham High School in Norfolk, England.
paras.zh: 英格兰诺福克郡的塔弗汉姆中学拒收了大约三十名学生。

paras.en: Headteacher Dr. Roger Harris confirmed that this was due to a change in the school’s uniform policy.
paras.zh: 校长罗杰·哈里斯博士证实，这是因为学校的校服规定改了。

paras.en: Harris, who became headteacher this year, said he notified parents of the updated rules in an email in June.
paras.zh: 哈里斯今年刚当上校长，他说六月份就已经发邮件把更新后的规定通知了家长。

paras.en: The price of school uniforms can spark panic among families struggling with the high cost of living.
paras.zh: 在生活成本高、日子过得紧巴巴的家庭里，校服的价格可能会引起恐慌。

paras.en: Nearly all British schools have uniforms.
paras.zh: 几乎所有英国学校都有校服。

paras.en: They cost parents an average of three hundred and thirty seven pounds per year for each secondary school child.
paras.zh: 家长每年为每个上中学的孩子在校服上平均要花三百三十七英镑。

paras.en: According to the new rules, students of Taverham are required to wear smart black shoes appropriate for the workplace.
paras.zh: 按照新规定，塔弗汉姆中学的学生必须穿适合工作场合的正式黑色皮鞋。

paras.en: Harris held that strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behaviour.
paras.zh: 哈里斯认为，校服规定加强以后，学生的学习成绩和行为表现都会变好。

paras.en: But for some parents, the school’s restrictions are an unnecessary burden.
paras.zh: 可对一些家长来说，学校的这些限制是不必要的负担。

paras.en: As annual inflation climbs over ten per cent, many households are on tight budgets.
paras.zh: 年通胀率涨到百分之十以上，很多家庭的预算都很紧。

paras.en: Private rental prices in Britain rose 3.2 percent over the twelve months to July twenty twenty two, the largest jump since twenty sixteen.
paras.zh: 截至二〇二二年七月的十二个月里，英国私人租房价格上涨了百分之三点二，是二〇一六年以来涨幅最大的一次。

paras.en: Soaring energy bills have made things worse.
paras.zh: 能源账单飞涨，让情况雪上加霜。

paras.en: Lucinda May, mum of a Taverham student, said that she had to ask her parents for sixty five pounds to buy her child the correct pair of shoes.
paras.zh: 一名塔弗汉姆中学学生的妈妈露辛达·梅说，她只好找自己的父母要了六十五英镑，才给孩子买了一双合规定的鞋。

w.m: adj. 正确的；合乎要求的

paras.en: May said that the school’s uniform policy showed a lack of regard for parents dealing with the high cost of living.
paras.zh: 梅说，学校的校服规定表明，学校根本不体谅那些在应对高昂生活成本的家长。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: Why were dozens of British students sent home on Tuesday?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：周二为什么有几十名英国学生被送回家？

paras.en: Question 23: What can the price of school uniforms spark among families in financial difficulty?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：校服的价格可能在经济困难的家庭里引起什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What did the head teacher think of the school’s new uniform rules?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：校长对学校新的校服规定有什么看法？

paras.en: Question 25: What did Lucinda May have to do to buy her child the correct pair of shoes?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：露辛达·梅为了给孩子买一双合规定的鞋，不得不做什么？

w.m: adj. 正确的；合乎要求的

paras.en: That’s the end of Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2025年12月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2025年12月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲美国鸡蛋涨价，越来越多的人从墨西哥非法带鸡蛋入境，海关一般会没收销毁并罚款。第二篇新闻报道讲美国一家餐厅宣布不再接待十岁以下的儿童，有人批评，也有人支持。第三篇新闻报道讲澳大利亚一处工地发现一张刚蜕下的巨大蛇皮，安保人员在附近搜寻这条大蛇。第一段长对话里，汉娜上电视答题节目赢了几百万欧元，却很快把钱花光了，丈夫还不肯卖掉新买的跑车。第二段长对话里，一对夫妻商量明年送儿子杰克去哪所学校，寄宿学校、新开的学校和家门口的学校都各有顾虑。第一篇短文讲分析型决策的缺点和长处：费时间、不够灵活，但能减少犯错。第二篇短文讲世界上最年长的人布拉尼亚斯·莫雷拉的长寿秘诀：弹钢琴、生活积极、每天吃酸奶，还要懂得该忘掉什么。第三篇短文讲教室里的座位会影响学习成绩和老师对你的看法，坐在前排中间的学生成绩更好，但也可能更常被老师点名。

paras.en: College English Test, Band 4.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part 2: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Customs and Border Protection officials are seeing a rise in people illegally bringing eggs from Mexico into border states such as Texas.
paras.zh: 美国海关与边境保护局的官员发现，从墨西哥非法把鸡蛋带进得克萨斯等边境州的人越来越多。

paras.en: The U.S. average price for a dozen large eggs last month hit $4.25.
paras.zh: 上个月，美国一打大号鸡蛋的平均价格达到了四点二五美元。

paras.en: That’s more than double their $1.78 price in December 2023.
paras.zh: 这比二〇二三年十二月一点七八美元的价格翻了一倍还多。

paras.en: Meanwhile, 30 eggs in Mexico sell for just $3.40.
paras.zh: 而在墨西哥，三十个鸡蛋只卖三点四美元。

paras.en: Those bringing eggs into the U.S. risk fines of up to $10,000.
paras.zh: 把鸡蛋带进美国的人可能被罚款，最高一万美元。

paras.en: But officials say they usually seize and destroy the eggs.
paras.zh: 不过官员们说，他们通常会没收并销毁这些鸡蛋。

paras.en: They also impose a $300 penalty.
paras.zh: 他们还会罚款三百美元。

paras.en: The Department of Agriculture banned eggs from Mexico in 2012.
paras.zh: 美国农业部二〇一二年就禁止从墨西哥进口鸡蛋了。

paras.en: This was due to the risk of bird flu.
paras.zh: 这是因为有禽流感的风险。

paras.en: Officials said most people arriving at international borders with eggs are truthful about their purchases.
paras.zh: 官员们说，带着鸡蛋到达国际边境的人，大多会如实说明自己买了鸡蛋。

paras.en: They simply don’t know bringing eggs is not allowed.
paras.zh: 他们只是不知道不能带鸡蛋。

paras.en: Generally, the items are declared during the first inspection.
paras.zh: 一般来说，这些物品在第一次检查时就申报了。

paras.en: Then the person can abandon the eggs without consequence, a customs and border protection spokesperson said.
paras.zh: 一位海关与边境保护局的发言人说，这样当事人就可以把鸡蛋扔掉，不会有什么后果。

paras.en: Even so, there have been a very small number of cases recently when authorities discovered eggs during further inspections.
paras.zh: 即便如此，最近也有极少数案例，是有关部门在进一步检查时才发现鸡蛋的。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news reports you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn from the news report about the egg price in the U.S.?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于美国的鸡蛋价格，我们从新闻报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 2: What does the news report say about most people arriving at American borders with eggs?
paras.zh: 第二题：对于大多数带着鸡蛋到达美国边境的人，新闻报道是怎么说的？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Nettie’s House, a restaurant in America, has been hit with criticism after announcing on their website that children under the age of 10 are no longer welcome.
paras.zh: 美国一家叫“内蒂之家”的餐厅在网站上宣布不再欢迎十岁以下的儿童，随后招来一片批评。

paras.en: Among the reasons given for the decision, the restaurant cited noise levels, lack of space for high chairs, cleaning up crazy messes, and the liability of kids running around the restaurant.
paras.zh: 餐厅给出的理由包括噪音大、没地方放儿童高脚椅、要收拾乱七八糟的残局，还有孩子在店里乱跑出了事要担责任。

paras.en: They decided that it was time to take control.
paras.zh: 他们认为是时候管一管了。

paras.en: The decision wasn’t made lightly, but some recent events pushed them to implement this new policy.
paras.zh: 这个决定不是轻易做出的，但最近发生的一些事促使他们实行了这项新规定。

paras.en: Responding to the post, one person commented that it is messed up beyond another level.
paras.zh: 有人回复这条帖子说，这简直离谱到家了。

paras.en: Children are children.
paras.zh: 孩子就是孩子。

paras.en: Moms are tired and don’t have time to cook.
paras.zh: 妈妈们很累，没时间做饭。

paras.en: Not welcoming children under 10 is a complete slap in the face to families.
paras.zh: 不欢迎十岁以下的孩子，简直是在打有孩子的家庭的脸。

paras.en: He felt so disappointed in the establishment.
paras.zh: 他对这家店非常失望。

paras.en: There are others, however, who showed support for the restaurant’s decision.
paras.zh: 不过，也有人支持这家餐厅的决定。

paras.en: They said it has the right to implement any rules it wants.
paras.zh: 他们说，餐厅有权实行它想定的任何规定。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What do we learn from the news report about the restaurant Nettie’s House?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于“内蒂之家”这家餐厅，我们从新闻报道中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question four: What do supporters say in response to the restaurant’s new policy?
paras.zh: 第四题：对餐厅的新规定，支持者怎么说？

paras.en: News Report 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Security officers were searching a suburb in Australia where an adult snake was believed to be wandering after the discovery of a huge, freshly shed snake skin.
paras.zh: 澳大利亚一处郊区发现了一张刚蜕下的巨大蛇皮，人们认为有一条成年大蛇正在附近游荡，安保人员随即展开了搜寻。

paras.en: The skin was found at a construction site and the government wrote to residents to warn them.
paras.zh: 蛇皮是在一处建筑工地上发现的，政府写信提醒了附近的居民。

paras.en: They were told to observe and, if possible, photograph the animal.
paras.zh: 居民们被告知要注意观察，可能的话，把这条蛇拍下来。

paras.en: If it was moving, watch where it went.
paras.zh: 如果它在移动，就留意它往哪儿去了。

paras.en: It was recommended not to make contact with the animal.
paras.zh: 政府建议居民不要接触这条蛇。

paras.en: The type of snake was determined to be one of the world’s largest snake species.
paras.zh: 经过确认，这条蛇属于世界上最大的蛇类之一。

paras.en: It is not poisonous, but can still attack and kill its victims.
paras.zh: 它没有毒，但仍然会攻击猎物，把猎物杀死。

paras.en: This type of snake is classified as a threat to humans, especially small children, as well as pets.
paras.zh: 这种蛇被列为会对人类，尤其是小孩，还有宠物构成威胁的物种。

paras.en: They may carry viruses that are fatal to native snakes, which do not have resistance.
paras.zh: 它们可能携带对本地蛇类致命的病毒，本地蛇对这些病毒没有抵抗力。

paras.en: If officers found the snake, they would employ a licensed snake catcher to catch it and transport it to a specialist animal doctor, the government said.
paras.zh: 政府说，安保人员如果找到这条蛇，会请一位持证捕蛇人把它抓住，送到专门的动物医生那里。

w.m: adj. 持证的；获得许可的

paras.en: If caught, the snake would be examined to determine where it came from, how long it had been in the area, what it had been eating, whether it was carrying any diseases of concern, and whether it had produced babies.
paras.zh: 蛇一旦被抓住，就要接受检查，查明它是从哪里来的、在这一带待了多久、一直在吃什么、有没有携带让人担心的疾病，以及有没有生下小蛇。

paras.en: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news reports you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 5: What does the report say security officers were searching for?
paras.zh: 第五题：报道说安保人员在搜寻什么？

paras.en: Question 6: Where does the report say the discovery was made?
paras.zh: 第六题：报道说是在哪里发现的？

paras.en: Question 7: What did the government say would be done if security officers found what they were searching for?
paras.zh: 第七题：政府说，如果安保人员找到了他们要找的东西，会怎么处理？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Poor Hannah.
paras.zh: 汉娜真可怜。

paras.en: Why, what happened?
paras.zh: 怎么了，出什么事了？

paras.en: Didn’t you hear?
paras.zh: 你没听说吗？

paras.en: She won a TV competition and became a millionaire overnight.
paras.zh: 她在一个电视比赛里赢了，一夜之间成了百万富翁。

paras.en: No way.
paras.zh: 不会吧。

paras.en: That’s incredible.
paras.zh: 太不可思议了。

w.m: adj. 难以置信的；不可思议的

paras.en: Are you kidding?
paras.zh: 你开玩笑吧？

paras.en: No, I’m serious.
paras.zh: 没有，我是认真的。

paras.en: I swear it.
paras.zh: 我发誓。

paras.en: She went on a TV show where they quiz on general knowledge and she won first prize.
paras.zh: 她上了一个考常识的电视节目，拿了一等奖。

paras.en: Wow, that’s so lucky of her.
paras.zh: 哇，她运气真好。

paras.en: How much did she win?
paras.zh: 她赢了多少钱？

paras.en: I’m not sure of the exact figure, but it’s a few million euros.
paras.zh: 具体数目我不太清楚，不过有好几百万欧元。

paras.en: Maybe five million euros after tax.
paras.zh: 税后大概五百万欧元吧。

paras.en: I can’t believe it.
paras.zh: 真不敢相信。

paras.en: You are really not joking, are you?
paras.zh: 你真不是在开玩笑吧？

paras.en: Honestly, look at my face.
paras.zh: 说真的，你看我的脸。

paras.en: Our friend Hannah won a ton of money.
paras.zh: 咱们的朋友汉娜赢了一大笔钱。

paras.en: Unbelievable.
paras.zh: 真不敢相信。

paras.en: Then why were you saying poor Hannah?
paras.zh: 那你干吗说汉娜可怜呢？

paras.en: Well, it turns out that she’s spent it all already.
paras.zh: 唉，结果她已经把钱全花光了。

paras.en: Five million euros.
paras.zh: 五百万欧元啊。

paras.en: How is that even possible?
paras.zh: 这怎么可能呢？

paras.en: She bought a house for herself and her husband, a house for her parents, and then a house for each of her four brothers and sisters.
paras.zh: 她给自己和丈夫买了一套房子，给父母买了一套，又给她的四个兄弟姐妹每人买了一套。

paras.en: And then she bought her husband a ridiculously expensive sports car.
paras.zh: 然后她又给丈夫买了一辆贵得离谱的跑车。

paras.en: Wow.
paras.zh: 哇。

paras.en: Are they all happy?
paras.zh: 那他们都开心吗？

paras.en: Because that’s what matters, isn’t it?
paras.zh: 因为这才是最重要的，对吧？

paras.en: I know for a fact Hannah isn’t.
paras.zh: 我很清楚，汉娜并不开心。

paras.en: You see, she was planning to quit the job she hates and retire early.
paras.zh: 你知道，她本来打算辞掉那份她讨厌的工作，早点退休。

paras.en: But now that she ran out of money, she can’t.
paras.zh: 可现在钱花光了，她就退不成了。

paras.en: Basically, she miscalculated how fast she was burning through the money.
paras.zh: 说白了，她没算好自己花钱花得有多快。

paras.en: And she’s now full of regret.
paras.zh: 她现在后悔得不得了。

paras.en: Why don’t they sell that flashy new car?
paras.zh: 他们为什么不把那辆扎眼的新车卖掉呢？

w.m: adj. 扎眼的；华而不实的

paras.en: She wants to, but her husband refuses to get rid of it.
paras.zh: 她想卖，可她丈夫不肯把车处理掉。

paras.en: He says the car is the best thing that has ever happened to him, and if she sells it, he will divorce her.
paras.zh: 他说这辆车是他这辈子遇到的最好的东西，要是她卖了车，他就跟她离婚。

paras.en: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 8: Why does the woman say she swears it?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士为什么说她发誓？

paras.en: Question nine: What do we learn about Hannah from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于汉娜，我们从对话中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the man think really matters to people?
paras.zh: 第十题：男士认为对人们来说真正重要的是什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does Hannah’s husband say he’ll do if she sells the new car?
paras.zh: 第十一题：汉娜的丈夫说，如果她把新车卖了，他会怎么做？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: If you have time right now, I think we need to sit down and discuss what exactly we are going to do for Jake’s education next year.
paras.zh: 你现在要是有空，我觉得咱们得坐下来商量一下，明年杰克上学的事到底怎么安排。

paras.en: I’ve been thinking it over, and I’d like to send him to Westwood Elementary.
paras.zh: 我一直在考虑这件事，我想送他去韦斯特伍德小学。

paras.en: You mean that boarding school?
paras.zh: 你是说那所寄宿学校？

paras.en: I thought we agreed that we would not be sending him away at such a young age.
paras.zh: 我记得咱们说好了，不在他这么小的时候把他送走。

paras.en: I admit that their academic record is very strong, with many outstanding awards for achievements in science and math, but he is just not mature enough to live on his own at this point.
paras.zh: 我承认他们的学业成绩非常好，在科学和数学方面得过很多了不起的奖，可他现在还不够成熟，没法自己一个人生活。

paras.en: What about enrolling him in Lakeview School?
paras.zh: 让他上莱克维尤学校怎么样？

paras.en: They do have a great outdoor campus, where he could finally learn all those outdoor sports you have been wanting him to try.
paras.zh: 他们的户外校园特别好，他终于可以去学那些你一直想让他试试的户外运动了。

paras.en: With so much greenery and fresh air, I think his current breathing problems would probably disappear.
paras.zh: 那里绿树成荫、空气新鲜，我觉得他现在的呼吸问题说不定就没了。

paras.en: They did just open, though, so I don’t think I feel comfortable having our son in the first class of a brand-new school.
paras.zh: 不过这所学校才刚开办，让咱们儿子当一所全新学校的第一届学生，我心里不太踏实。

paras.en: Yeah.
paras.zh: 是啊。

paras.en: The classrooms would probably smell like paint, making the air in the school all stuffy.
paras.zh: 教室里很可能还有油漆味，学校里的空气都会很闷。

paras.en: What about our local school, then?
paras.zh: 那咱们这儿本地的学校呢？

paras.en: They have a wonderful arts program that would really challenge Jake in terms of creativity and imagination.
paras.zh: 他们的艺术课程非常好，在创造力和想象力方面真的能让杰克得到锻炼。

paras.en: Being practically next door, one of us could take him to school every day before going to work.
paras.zh: 那所学校差不多就在隔壁，咱们俩谁都可以每天上班前送他去学校。

paras.en: I don’t know.
paras.zh: 我说不好。

paras.en: They have a reputation of being overly strict with the students, not to mention the overwhelming amount of homework they assign, which would lead to a lot of pressure for Jake and me.
paras.zh: 那所学校出了名地对学生管得太严，更别说布置的作业多得吓人，这会给杰克和我都带来很大压力。

w.m: adj. 压倒性的；多得吓人的

paras.en: What if we send him to the place near your mother’s house?
paras.zh: 要不咱们送他去你妈妈家附近的那所学校吧？

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the man say about Jake?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于杰克，男士是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 13: Why does the woman feel uncomfortable about sending Jake to Lakeview School?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士为什么对送杰克去莱克维尤学校感到不放心？

w.m: adj. 不放心的；不自在的

paras.en: Question fourteen: What does the man say about their local school?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于他们本地的学校，男士是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question fifteen: What does the woman suggest at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第十五题：对话最后，女士提出了什么建议？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Analytical decision-making is a decision-making approach where a manager makes important business decisions only with solid data.
paras.zh: 分析型决策是一种决策方式：管理者只有掌握了可靠的数据，才做出重要的商业决定。

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: This style contrasts with more instinctive leadership styles, where managers make many decisions using instinct or opinion.
paras.zh: 这种风格和更凭直觉的领导风格形成对比，后者的管理者很多决定都是凭直觉或个人看法做出的。

paras.en: While analytical decision-makers benefit from a deliberate, thoughtful approach, this style also has some shortcomings.
paras.zh: 分析型决策者得益于审慎、周到的处事方式，但这种风格也有一些缺点。

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的
adj. 审慎的；深思熟虑的

paras.en: A key flaw with analytical decision-making is that it takes time.
paras.zh: 分析型决策的一个主要缺陷是费时间。

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: While this approach is beneficial when you have the time and the decision is important, it is problematic when time is crucial.
paras.zh: 时间充裕、决定又很重要的时候，这种方式很有好处；可时间紧迫的时候，它就成问题了。

w.m: adj. 至关重要的；紧要的

paras.en: Analytical decision-makers struggle with deadlines and a sense of urgency with decisions.
paras.zh: 分析型决策者很难应对截止期限，做决定时也很难有紧迫感。

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: In situations where you need more timely action, decisions based on some information and instinct may work better.
paras.zh: 在需要更及时采取行动的情况下，根据部分信息加上直觉做决定，效果可能更好。

paras.en: The desire to be right is a major driver of analytical decision-making.
paras.zh: 想要做对，是分析型决策的一大驱动力。

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: Leaders who use this style don’t want to make mistakes.
paras.zh: 采用这种风格的领导者不想犯错。

paras.en: This commitment to one right way of thinking or doing things hinders the manager’s flexibility.
paras.zh: 这种执着于唯一正确的思考或做事方式的态度，妨碍了管理者的灵活性。

paras.en: Inflexibility causes you to ignore or avoid listening to the thoughts and ideas of others.
paras.zh: 缺乏灵活性会让你忽视或不愿去听别人的想法和意见。

paras.en: You only want to utilize hard data or facts.
paras.zh: 你只想用确凿的数据或事实。

paras.en: Despite its restrictions, analytical decision-making does have several key strengths.
paras.zh: 尽管有局限，分析型决策确实也有几个主要的长处。

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: By relying on facts and data, you minimize your potential for a wrong decision.
paras.zh: 依靠事实和数据，你就能把做错决定的可能性降到最低。

paras.en: You also get away from the habit of making guesses or following instincts.
paras.zh: 你还能改掉靠猜测或凭直觉做事的习惯。

paras.en: Database technology enables business leaders to look to hard evidence in analyzing target markets and promotional strategies rather than making assumptions or guesses on what works.
paras.zh: 有了数据库技术，企业领导者在分析目标市场和促销策略时，就能依靠确凿的证据，而不是对什么管用去做假设或猜测。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the passage say is a major flaw of analytical decision-making?
paras.zh: 第十六题：短文说分析型决策的一个主要缺陷是什么？

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: Question 17: What does a leader tend to do when they are committed to analytical decision-making?
paras.zh: 第十七题：一个坚持分析型决策的领导者往往会怎么做？

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: Question 18: What is a key strength of analytical decision-making?
paras.zh: 第十八题：分析型决策的一个主要长处是什么？

w.m: adj. 分析的；善于分析的

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: What is the secret to living past 100?
paras.zh: 活过一百岁的秘诀是什么？

paras.en: Playing the piano is among the things the world’s oldest person believes has contributed to her long life.
paras.zh: 世界上最年长的人认为，弹钢琴是让她长寿的原因之一。

paras.en: Branyas Morera is now 115 years and 320 days old.
paras.zh: 布拉尼亚斯·莫雷拉现在一百一十五岁零三百二十天了。

paras.en: That means she’s been alive longer than any other living individual.
paras.zh: 也就是说，她比现在活着的任何人活得都长。

paras.en: Branyas was born in the United States on April 4, 1907.
paras.zh: 布拉尼亚斯一九〇七年四月四日出生在美国。

paras.en: But her family moved to Spain, where they were originally from, when she was a young child.
paras.zh: 不过在她很小的时候，全家就搬回了西班牙，那里是她家的老家。

paras.en: She has lived there ever since.
paras.zh: 从那以后她就一直住在那里。

paras.en: The 115-year-old is active on social media, regularly sharing aspects of her life.
paras.zh: 这位一百一十五岁的老人很活跃，经常在社交媒体上分享她生活的方方面面。

paras.en: She also shares some of her secrets to living so long.
paras.zh: 她还分享了自己长寿的一些秘诀。

paras.en: These include playing the piano from a young age.
paras.zh: 其中包括从小就弹钢琴。

paras.en: Unfortunately, she had to give up the practice seven years ago, at 108.
paras.zh: 可惜七年前，一百零八岁的时候，她不得不放弃了弹琴。

paras.en: Her other secrets for living a long life?
paras.zh: 她长寿的其他秘诀呢？

paras.en: She led an active lifestyle until her later years, but has never followed a specific diet.
paras.zh: 她直到晚年都过着积极活跃的生活，但从来没有遵循过什么特定的饮食。

paras.en: Many people ask me what diet I follow to live so many years, Branyas wrote.
paras.zh: 布拉尼亚斯写道，很多人问我，我吃什么才活了这么多年。

paras.en: I have always eaten little, but everything, and I have never followed any plan.
paras.zh: 我一直吃得很少，但什么都吃，也从来没按什么计划吃过。

paras.en: But she does eat yogurt every day, which, she said, has an infinite number of positive properties for the body.
paras.zh: 不过她确实每天都吃酸奶，她说酸奶对身体有数不清的好处。

paras.en: She has also said that the secret to a long life is knowing how to choose what to forget.
paras.zh: 她还说过，长寿的秘诀是懂得选择忘掉什么。

paras.en: Life would be impossible if we remembered everything, she said.
paras.zh: 她说，如果我们什么都记得，日子就没法过了。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn about Branyas Morera?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于布拉尼亚斯·莫雷拉，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What is one of Branyas Morera’s secrets to living a long life?
paras.zh: 第二十题：布拉尼亚斯·莫雷拉的长寿秘诀之一是什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does Branyas Morera think also contributes to a long life?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：布拉尼亚斯·莫雷拉认为还有什么有助于长寿？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: It’s the first day of school and your teacher tells you to find a seat in the classroom.
paras.zh: 开学第一天，老师让你在教室里找个座位。

paras.en: Where do you sit?
paras.zh: 你坐哪儿？

paras.en: Does it matter?
paras.zh: 这重要吗？

paras.en: Yes, it does matter where you sit in your classroom.
paras.zh: 重要，你坐在教室的哪个位置真的很重要。

paras.en: So choose and choose carefully.
paras.zh: 所以要选，而且要仔细地选。

paras.en: Studies report that where you sit in the classroom can impact your ability to learn and the way your teacher perceives you.
paras.zh: 研究表明，你在教室里坐在哪儿，会影响你的学习能力，也会影响老师对你的看法。

paras.en: Guess what else?
paras.zh: 你猜还会影响什么？

paras.en: Your grade.
paras.zh: 你的成绩。

paras.en: Then what is the best seat in the classroom?
paras.zh: 那教室里最好的座位是哪儿呢？

paras.en: In one study, students who sat in the front and center of the classroom received a higher grade average and scored higher on tests than those sitting towards the back of the classroom.
paras.zh: 一项研究发现，坐在教室前排中间的学生，平均成绩比坐在后面的学生高，考试分数也更高。

paras.en: Get this.
paras.zh: 听好了。

paras.en: Students sitting in the middle of the classroom also outscored students sitting behind them.
paras.zh: 坐在教室中间的学生，成绩也比坐在他们后面的学生好。

paras.en: This study gathered that students had a clearer vision of the blackboard and were able to focus more attention on the instructor.
paras.zh: 这项研究得出的结论是，这些学生能更清楚地看到黑板，也更能把注意力集中在老师身上。

paras.en: By sitting front and center, students were able to hear better too.
paras.zh: 坐在前排中间，学生也能听得更清楚。

paras.en: The instructors said that they also formed a better connection with the students who sat in front.
paras.zh: 老师们说，他们和坐在前排的学生关系也更好。

paras.en: Perhaps the connection is made because of eye contact and visibility and more interaction.
paras.zh: 这种关系之所以能建立起来，或许是因为有眼神交流、看得见，互动也更多。

paras.en: But when you sit in the front row, you may be called on more by your teacher, mainly due to the fact that you are easier to see.
paras.zh: 不过坐在前排的话，老师可能更常点你回答问题，主要是因为你更容易被看到。

paras.en: So for students who are not prepared and for those who are extremely shy, the attention could cause some unwanted stress.
paras.zh: 所以对没有准备好的学生，还有特别害羞的学生来说，这种关注可能会带来一些不必要的压力。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What is of great importance to students according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人认为，什么对学生非常重要？

paras.en: Question 23: What did one study find about students seated in the middle of the classroom?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：一项研究发现，坐在教室中间的学生怎么样？

paras.en: Question 24: What can eye contact, visibility, and more interaction probably bring about?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：眼神交流、看得见和更多的互动，很可能带来什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What do we learn about extremely shy students sitting in the front row of the classroom?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于坐在教室前排的特别害羞的学生，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
