passages.name: 2026年6月大学英语四级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲一个六岁男孩用爸爸的手机在网上从好几家餐馆点了一大堆外卖，爸爸收到一千美元的账单，外卖平台送了这家人一千美元的礼品卡，还考虑请他们拍广告。第二篇新闻报道讲动物行为专家分析一百多篇论文，发现游客会影响动物园里动物的行为，比如大象在公开喂食时更爱互动、更少无聊地重复动作。第三篇新闻报道讲丹佛暂停了很受欢迎的电动自行车补贴项目，因为六个月就花完了三年的经费，打算明年年初调整后重新启动。第一段长对话里，迈克和苏聊各自的游览：迈克最喜欢博物馆的钱币收藏，苏逛了老城区，两人约好第二天一起去西班牙台阶广场。第二段长对话里，女士给即将入职的男士出主意：重视头几天、从多个角度了解自己的角色、了解公司业务，并认识有决策权的人。第一篇短文讲消费者并不像自己以为的那么理性，购买行为主要受情感驱动，营销要卖生活方式和感受。第二篇短文讲美国人每年吃进、吸进大量微塑料，主要来自空气、瓶装水和海鲜，实际数量可能更高。第三篇短文讲一项调查发现，养宠物对老年人的身心健康有很多好处，也有一些麻烦。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I, with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A man was left with a one thousand dollar bill after his six-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend.
paras.zh: 上周末，一个六岁男孩在几家餐馆点了一大堆网上外卖，他爸爸因此收到一张一千美元的账单。

w.m: n. 自助餐；一大堆食物

paras.en: This led to a string of unexpected deliveries, and maybe a starring role in an advertisement campaign.
paras.zh: 这引来了一连串意想不到的外卖，说不定还能让他们当上广告活动的主角。

w.m: adj. 意想不到的；出乎意料的
adj. 主演的；担任主角的

paras.en: Keith Stonehouse said the food piled up quickly at his home Saturday night after he let his son use his cell phone to play a game before bed.
paras.zh: 基思·斯通豪斯说，星期六晚上，他让儿子睡前用他的手机玩游戏，结果家里的食物很快就堆成了山。

paras.en: He said the youngster instead used his father’s online food ordering account to order food from one restaurant after another.
paras.zh: 他说，这孩子没玩游戏，而是用爸爸的网上订餐账户，一家接一家地从餐馆点菜。

paras.en: The boy’s mother, Kristen Stonehouse, said that the online food app has reached out to the family and offered them a one thousand dollar gift card.
paras.zh: 男孩的妈妈克里斯汀·斯通豪斯说，那个网上订餐应用已经联系了他们家，送给他们一张一千美元的礼品卡。

paras.en: The company also is considering using the family in an online promotional campaign.
paras.zh: 这家公司还在考虑请这家人参加一次网上推广活动。

paras.en: Most of the food went into the family’s refrigerators.
paras.zh: 大部分食物都放进了家里的冰箱。

paras.en: They also invited some neighbors over to eat some of it.
paras.zh: 他们还请了几个邻居过来一起吃。

paras.en: The father is planning to change his password.
paras.zh: 爸爸打算改掉自己的密码。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: Why was Keith Stonehouse left with a one thousand dollar bill?
paras.zh: 第一题：基思·斯通豪斯为什么收到一张一千美元的账单？

paras.en: Question 2: What does the news report say Keith Stonehouse is planning to do?
paras.zh: 第二题：新闻报道说基思·斯通豪斯打算做什么？

paras.en: News Report 2.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Animal behavior experts looked at more than 100 research papers.
paras.zh: 动物行为专家研究了一百多篇论文。

paras.en: They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than two hundred and fifty species in zoos.
paras.zh: 他们研究了游客如何影响动物园里二百五十多个物种的行为。

paras.en: They found that elephants socialized more with each other during public feeding times.
paras.zh: 他们发现，在公开喂食的时间里，大象彼此之间的互动更多。

paras.en: After public feeding times they were more likely to search for food and less likely to be inactive.
paras.zh: 公开喂食之后，它们更可能去找食物，也更不容易待着不动。

paras.en: In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom.
paras.zh: 游客多的时候，大象就更少做那些重复的动作，这类动作往往说明它们觉得无聊。

paras.en: Visitors had a similar effect on some other species, too, including polar bears, certain jungle cats, and black-tailed prairie dogs.
paras.zh: 游客对其他一些物种也有类似的影响，包括北极熊、某些丛林猫科动物和黑尾草原犬鼠。

paras.en: Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans.
paras.zh: 有些动物物种是在动物园里出生长大的，所以很可能已经习惯了有人在身边。

paras.en: Zoo visitors are often aspects of zoo animals’ environment that animals cannot control and as such can be stressful, although some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors.
paras.zh: 动物园的游客往往是动物环境里动物自己控制不了的因素，因此可能让它们感到紧张，不过有些物种似乎能很好地适应游客带来的变化。

paras.en: Questions three and four are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question three: What did animal behavior experts do according to the news report?
paras.zh: 第三题：根据这篇新闻报道，动物行为专家做了什么？

paras.en: Question four: Why have some animal species likely become used to the presence of humans?
paras.zh: 第四题：为什么有些动物物种很可能已经习惯了有人在身边？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.
paras.zh: 丹佛正在暂停很受欢迎的电动自行车补贴项目。

paras.en: The program was launched in April.
paras.zh: 这个项目是四月份推出的。

paras.en: It allowed Denver residents to apply for four hundred dollars in government funds before buying an electric bike from a participating shop.
paras.zh: 丹佛居民在参与项目的商店买电动自行车之前，可以申请四百美元的政府资金。

paras.en: Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for one thousand two hundred dollars.
paras.zh: 符合一定收入条件的居民可以领到一千二百美元。

paras.en: More than three thousand Denver residents applied for incentives within the first three weeks.
paras.zh: 头三个星期里，就有三千多名丹佛居民申请了补贴。

paras.en: The city then changed the program to limit the number of applications each month.
paras.zh: 于是市政府调整了项目，限制每个月的申请数量。

paras.en: On Monday, the city announced the pause.
paras.zh: 星期一，市政府宣布暂停项目。

paras.en: We’re honored to be a part of transforming the way Denver wants to move around, said Grace Rink, Denver’s chief climate officer.
paras.zh: 丹佛的首席气候官格雷丝·林克说，我们很荣幸能为改变丹佛人的出行方式出一份力。

paras.en: We exhausted three years’ worth of funding in six months.
paras.zh: 我们六个月就用完了三年的经费。

w.m: n. 价值；（一定时间的）量

paras.en: The city said the program has put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver and invested $8.6 million into the local economy.
paras.zh: 市政府说，这个项目已经让四千四百辆电动自行车上了丹佛的街道，给当地经济投入了八百六十万美元。

paras.en: The city has provided 2,200 incentives to lower-income residents.
paras.zh: 市政府给低收入居民发放了二千二百份补贴。

paras.en: That represents 68% of the program funding.
paras.zh: 这占了项目经费的百分之六十八。

paras.en: The city expects to resume the programme early next year.
paras.zh: 市政府希望明年年初重新启动这个项目。

paras.en: It also plans design changes to make participation easier and increase access to the programme.
paras.zh: 市政府还打算修改项目设计，让大家更容易参加，也让更多人能用上这个项目。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is Denver doing with its popular electric bike incentive program?
paras.zh: 第五题：丹佛要怎么处理它那个很受欢迎的电动自行车补贴项目？

paras.en: Question six: How did the Electric Bike Incentive Program benefit residents?
paras.zh: 第六题：电动自行车补贴项目让居民得到了什么好处？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the city of Denver expect to do early next year?
paras.zh: 第七题：丹佛市预计明年年初会做什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hey, Mike, what do you think of the museum you visited today?
paras.zh: 嘿，迈克，你觉得今天参观的那个博物馆怎么样？

paras.en: Hey Sue, the museum is great, very interesting.
paras.zh: 嘿，苏，博物馆很棒，特别有意思。

paras.en: They have loads of stuff there on display.
paras.zh: 那里展出了好多东西。

paras.en: The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life.
paras.zh: 早期人类用过的那些原始工具，能让人了解他们的很多生活情况。

paras.en: But my favorite is the coin collection.
paras.zh: 不过我最喜欢的是钱币收藏。

paras.en: They have some coins that are over two thousand years old.
paras.zh: 他们有些钱币有两千多年的历史了。

paras.en: That sounds cool.
paras.zh: 听起来真不错。

paras.en: Yeah.
paras.zh: 是啊。

paras.en: What did you do today?
paras.zh: 你今天干什么了？

paras.en: Kathy and I just wandered through the old city center.
paras.zh: 我和凯茜就在老城区随便逛了逛。

paras.en: The streets are narrow but beautiful, with plenty of charm.
paras.zh: 街道很窄，但很漂亮，特别有味道。

paras.en: We saw the Trevi Fountain, which is in all the guidebooks.
paras.zh: 我们看了特雷维喷泉，所有的旅游指南上都有它。

paras.en: How do you like it?
paras.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

paras.en: It’s very pretty, but it was overcrowded with tourists.
paras.zh: 很漂亮，可是游客太多，挤得要命。

paras.en: Yeah, well, it’s crowded everywhere.
paras.zh: 是啊，嗯，哪儿都挤。

paras.en: It is August, after all, the busiest month of the year.
paras.zh: 毕竟现在是八月，一年里最忙的月份。

paras.en: Yes, it’s like the whole world is here on holiday, including us.
paras.zh: 是啊，好像全世界的人都来这儿度假了，包括我们。

paras.en: What will you do tomorrow?
paras.zh: 你明天打算干什么？

paras.en: I haven’t decided yet.
paras.zh: 我还没定呢。

paras.en: I was thinking of doing what you did today: wandering the old streets and taking pictures.
paras.zh: 我在想要不要做你今天做的事：在老街上逛逛，拍拍照。

paras.en: I was also thinking of visiting the square with the Spanish steps.
paras.zh: 我还想去那个有西班牙台阶的广场看看。

paras.en: What is that?
paras.zh: 那是什么地方？

paras.en: I haven’t heard of it.
paras.zh: 我没听说过。

paras.en: It’s a square where, on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a church.
paras.zh: 那是一个广场，一边有很宽的台阶，上面摆着花，一直通到一座教堂。

paras.en: It’s also in all the tourist guidebooks.
paras.zh: 所有的旅游指南上也都有它。

paras.en: It’s very famous and pretty.
paras.zh: 它很有名，也很漂亮。

paras.en: I was also thinking of seeing that tomorrow.
paras.zh: 我明天也想去看看那儿。

paras.en: It sounds very nice.
paras.zh: 听起来很不错。

paras.en: Do you mind if Kathy and I join you tomorrow?
paras.zh: 明天我和凯茜跟你一起去，你介意吗？

paras.en: Not at all.
paras.zh: 一点也不介意。

paras.en: I spent the whole day today pretty much alone.
paras.zh: 我今天差不多一整天都是一个人过的。

paras.en: Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change.
paras.zh: 能跟别人一起逛逛景点，换换口味，挺好的。

w.m: adj. 受欢迎的；令人高兴的

paras.en: Let me ask her first, but I’m sure she’ll be up for it.
paras.zh: 我先问问她，不过我肯定她会乐意的。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: What exhibits does the man like best in the museum he visited?
paras.zh: 第八题：在他参观的博物馆里，男士最喜欢哪些展品？

paras.en: Question nine: What does the woman say about the old city centre?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于老城区，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the man say about the square with the Spanish steps?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于有西班牙台阶的广场，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question eleven: What does the woman say she is going to do first?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士说她要先做什么？

paras.en: Conversation Two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Can you give me advice about being successful at a new job?
paras.zh: 你能给我出出主意，怎样才能在新工作上干得好吗？

paras.en: I start mine next week.
paras.zh: 我下周就开始上班了。

paras.en: Sure.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: It’s important not to undermine the significance of the first few days of your job, since this is the best time to create a solid first impression.
paras.zh: 千万别小看上班头几天的重要性，因为这是给人留下良好第一印象的最佳时机。

paras.en: That’s a good point.
paras.zh: 说得好。

paras.en: I’ll need to collaborate with my co-workers, and I’m very aware of just how important others are for my success at work.
paras.zh: 我得跟同事合作，我也很清楚别人对我工作成功有多重要。

paras.en: It’s also important to understand your role thoroughly to gain a comprehensive picture of your job.
paras.zh: 还有一点很重要，就是要彻底了解自己的角色，全面认识自己的工作。

paras.en: The most important thing for you to do at first is to understand your role from multiple perspectives.
paras.zh: 刚开始，你最重要的是从多个角度了解自己的角色。

paras.en: Why is that?
paras.zh: 为什么呢？

paras.en: Well, what you do at work is not just limited to your job description.
paras.zh: 嗯，你在工作中做的事，不只是职位说明里写的那些。

paras.en: You need to consider how your work relates to other people within the organization.
paras.zh: 你要考虑自己的工作跟单位里其他人有什么关系。

paras.en: Oh, right.
paras.zh: 哦，对。

paras.en: So, for example, certain reports that I create at the end of the month may be used by a team in another department.
paras.zh: 比如说，我月底做的某些报告，可能会被另一个部门的团队用到。

paras.en: That’s right.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: And in that respect, it’s also important to learn about the business to see the big picture.
paras.zh: 在这一点上，了解公司业务、看清全局也很重要。

paras.en: You mean like knowing about the history of the company?
paras.zh: 你是说，比如了解公司的历史？

paras.en: Kind of, but more like knowing the details of the products and services that the company exists to deliver.
paras.zh: 有点儿吧，不过更像是了解公司提供的产品和服务的细节。

paras.en: Learning about the business will give you a chance to understand how your role fits into the bigger picture.
paras.zh: 了解公司业务，你就能明白自己的角色在全局中处于什么位置。

paras.en: Okay.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: I’m feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss as well.
paras.zh: 跟老板见面，我也有点儿不安。

paras.en: That’s to be expected.
paras.zh: 这很正常。

paras.en: However, it’s crucial that you get to know the people who have decision-making authority to gain insight regarding how the business is run and decisions are made.
paras.zh: 不过，你一定要认识那些有决策权的人，这样才能深入了解公司是怎么经营、怎么做决定的。

paras.en: Great advice.
paras.zh: 好主意。

paras.en: Thanks.
paras.zh: 谢谢。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question twelve: What advice does the man want to get from the woman?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士想从女士那里得到什么建议？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the woman say is the most important thing for the man to do at first?
paras.zh: 第十三题：女士说，男士刚开始最重要的是做什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the man say he is feeling a bit uneasy about?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士说他对什么有点儿不安？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the woman suggest the man do to gain insight about the running of the business?
paras.zh: 第十五题：为了深入了解公司的经营，女士建议男士做什么？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage 1.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Contrary to popular belief, consumers aren’t as smart as they like to believe.
paras.zh: 跟大家普遍以为的相反，消费者并没有他们自以为的那么精明。

paras.en: Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a purchase.
paras.zh: 很多消费者说，他们在考虑买东西时，会比较多个互相竞争的品牌和价格。

paras.en: However, research indicates that this is not actually the case.
paras.zh: 然而，研究表明，实际情况并不是这样。

paras.en: What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say.
paras.zh: 消费者真实的想法或感受往往跟他们说的相矛盾。

paras.en: A big reason is that they are driven by unconscious urges, the biggest of which is emotion.
paras.zh: 一个重要原因是，他们受无意识的冲动驱使，其中最大的冲动就是情感。

paras.en: Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also decision making in general.
paras.zh: 真正推动购买行为的是情感，总的来说，做决定也是这样。

paras.en: Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time.
paras.zh: 优秀的营销人员时时刻刻都记着这个重要事实。

paras.en: And examples of emotion-based campaigns are everywhere.
paras.zh: 以情感为基础的营销活动随处可见。

paras.en: Think for a moment what is actually being sold in most marketing campaigns.
paras.zh: 想一想，大多数营销活动实际上卖的是什么。

paras.en: Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world.
paras.zh: 奢侈品瞄准的是我们的自我价值感、被认可的感觉和在世上的地位。

paras.en: Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family, and a broader network of people.
paras.zh: 通信设备让我们和朋友、家人以及更广的人际网络联系在一起，所以让我们兴奋。

paras.en: And many other products, such as rings, target emotions related to love and relationships.
paras.zh: 还有很多其他产品，比如戒指，瞄准的是跟爱情和感情关系有关的情感。

paras.en: As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the lifestyle and the feeling.
paras.zh: 作为营销人员，我们应该重视产品的特点，但也必须卖生活方式和感受。

paras.en: The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product.
paras.zh: 关键是突出消费者使用产品时会产生的情感反应。

paras.en: To achieve the highest emotional response, we should target our consumer through many different senses.
paras.zh: 为了让情感反应最强烈，我们应该通过多种不同的感官来打动消费者。

paras.en: A lot of what drives consumers is subconscious behavior.
paras.zh: 推动消费者的很多东西，都是潜意识里的行为。

paras.en: But this isn’t a bad thing.
paras.zh: 不过这并不是坏事。

paras.en: There’s nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of emotion.
paras.zh: 帮消费者达到他们想要的情感状态，这里面没有什么操纵的成分。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does research indicate about many consumers when they evaluate a purchase?
paras.zh: 第十六题：研究表明，很多消费者在考虑买东西时是怎样的？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What do good marketers keep in mind all the time?
paras.zh: 第十七题：优秀的营销人员一直记着什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What should marketers do besides stressing the features of a product?
paras.zh: 第十八题：除了强调产品的特点，营销人员还应该做什么？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us, but along the way they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment, the food we eat, and the air we breathe.
paras.zh: 多年来，塑料被用来制造我们身边几乎所有的东西，可是一路下来，它们跑出了包装和物品的范围，进入了环境，进入了我们吃的食物和呼吸的空气。

paras.en: Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic.
paras.zh: 美国人正在吃进、吸进大量塑料。

paras.en: Based on available data, Americans take in an estimated 74,000 to 121,000 microplastic particles every year.
paras.zh: 根据现有数据，美国人每年估计会摄入七万四千到十二万一千个微塑料颗粒。

paras.en: However, scientists believe the true number is probably much higher because for some likely sources of microplastics there was no strong data available.
paras.zh: 不过，科学家认为，真实数字很可能要高得多，因为对于微塑料的一些可能来源，没有可靠的数据。

paras.en: Microplastics get into food and air in several ways.
paras.zh: 微塑料进入食物和空气的途径有好几种。

paras.en: Many start off as part of larger plastic objects which over time fragment into smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny, five millimeters or less in diameter.
paras.zh: 很多微塑料原本是较大塑料物品的一部分，随着时间推移，碎成越来越小的碎片，直到变得很小，直径不超过五毫米。

paras.en: They are breathed in or consumed by animals that then become our food.
paras.zh: 它们被动物吸进去或吃进去，而这些动物后来又成了我们的食物。

paras.en: The particles float through the air until people breathe them in.
paras.zh: 这些颗粒在空气中飘浮，直到被人吸进去。

paras.en: They also settle on the food that people eat.
paras.zh: 它们还会落在人们吃的食物上。

paras.en: Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed in or consumed microplastics.
paras.zh: 数据显示，对美国人来说，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或吃进的微塑料最大的来源。

paras.en: Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts.
paras.zh: 添加糖占得少一些，而盐、自来水和啤酒的贡献量很小。

paras.en: These estimates are conservative.
paras.zh: 这些估计都是保守的。

paras.en: The included foods only make up about 15% of the average American diet.
paras.zh: 研究里算进去的食物只占美国人平均饮食的大约百分之十五。

paras.en: It’s not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet.
paras.zh: 在一般饮食里剩下的百分之八十五中，含有多少塑料，现在还不知道。

paras.en: Questions nineteen to twenty one are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nineteen: What does the passage say about Americans?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于美国人，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What counted as the biggest sources for Americans breathing in or consuming microplastics?
paras.zh: 第二十题：美国人吸入或吃进微塑料，最大的来源是什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the passage say is still unknown?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：短文说什么还不知道？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: People looking to stay well as they age may want to adopt a pet animal, according to new data from the University of Michigan National Poll on Healthy Aging.
paras.zh: 密歇根大学全国健康老龄化民意调查的新数据显示，想在上了年纪以后依然保持健康的人，也许可以考虑养一只宠物。

paras.en: For the survey, researchers polled about 2,000 U.S. adults from ages fifty to eighty.
paras.zh: 在这次调查中，研究人员调查了大约两千名五十到八十岁的美国成年人。

paras.en: Fifty five percent said they owned at least one pet.
paras.zh: 百分之五十五的人说他们至少养了一只宠物。

paras.en: Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats.
paras.zh: 狗是最常见的宠物，其次是猫。

paras.en: But whatever the type of animal, the vast majority of owners said their pets boosted their mental and physical health.
paras.zh: 但不管养的是什么动物，绝大多数主人都说，宠物让他们的身心更健康了。

paras.en: Nearly 90% of older pet owners said their animals helped them enjoy life and feel loved.
paras.zh: 将近百分之九十的老年宠物主人说，宠物让他们更享受生活，也让他们感到被爱。

paras.en: Roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress.
paras.zh: 大约百分之八十的人说，宠物减轻了他们的压力。

paras.en: And almost three quarters said their pets provided a sense of purpose.
paras.zh: 将近四分之三的人说，宠物让他们有了目标感。

paras.en: However, people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership.
paras.zh: 不过，大家也说了养宠物的一些坏处。

paras.en: These included difficulty traveling and financial strains.
paras.zh: 比如出门旅行不方便、经济上有压力。

paras.en: 6% of pet owners said they’d fallen or injured themselves as a result of having a pet.
paras.zh: 百分之六的宠物主人说，他们因为养宠物摔倒过或受过伤。

paras.en: Still, plenty of research has shown that just about anyone can benefit from their pet, since animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety, and encourage physical activity.
paras.zh: 不过，大量研究表明，几乎人人都能从宠物身上受益，因为动物能减轻压力，缓解抑郁和焦虑的症状，还能鼓励人多活动身体。

paras.en: The new poll suggests that pet ownership may be especially beneficial for older adults, given how common loneliness and social isolation are within this age group.
paras.zh: 这次新的调查说明，养宠物可能对老年人特别有好处，因为这个年龄段的人孤独和与社会隔绝的情况很普遍。

paras.en: Human social support comes with a host of health benefits: less stress, lower rates of long-term disease, and more.
paras.zh: 来自他人的社会支持会给健康带来一大堆好处：压力更小、长期疾病的发病率更低，等等。

paras.en: And research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits.
paras.zh: 研究表明，和宠物互动也能带来很多同样的好处。

paras.en: Questions twenty two to twenty five are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question twenty two: What did over half of the respondents say in the survey?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：在这次调查中，一半以上的受访者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What did most older pet owners in the survey say their pets provided?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：调查中大多数老年宠物主人说，宠物给他们带来了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What does the passage say people did report in the survey?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：短文说人们在调查中确实提到了什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What does research show interacting with pets can do?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：研究表明，和宠物互动能起到什么作用？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2026年6月大学英语四级 第2套
passages.name: 2026年6月大学英语四级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 长对话 · 短文
passages.summary: 第一篇新闻报道讲英国一位一百零四岁的老太太南希·吉福德要卖掉她从两岁起就住着的房子，因为身体原因要搬进养老院。第二篇新闻报道讲一名男子被洋流冲到海上，靠番茄酱和蔬菜粉在船上撑了二十四天，船上写的“救命”一词帮他获救，被救时身体还好，只是瘦了。第三篇新闻报道讲丹佛公立学校因为入学人数下降、预算减少，准备关掉几所学生少的小学和初中，以免学区负债。第一段长对话里，海伦在网上订不了音乐剧《猫》的票，菲利普在电话里帮她订了两张楼上中间的票。第二段长对话里，约翰发现自己每天用手机八个小时，就关了手机，改去实体店买东西、跟朋友见面吃饭，女士却因为亲友不在本地离不开手机。第一篇短文讲美国跳槽者的涨薪幅度曾远高于留在原岗位的人，现在差距正在缩小，劳动力市场可能在降温。第二篇短文讲一项研究发现，人们吃高度加工食品时每天多摄入约五百卡路里，吃得也更快，可能因此长胖。第三篇短文讲女性比男性花更多时间做家务、带孩子，新研究认为这可能跟男女各自的喜好有关。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Four.
paras.zh: 大学英语四级考试。

paras.en: Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 第二部分：听力理解。

paras.en: Section A. Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three news reports.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: At the end of each news report, you will hear two or three questions.
paras.zh: 每篇新闻报道结束时，你会听到两到三个问题。

paras.en: Both the news report and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 新闻报道和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet I, with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: News Report One.
paras.zh: 第一篇新闻报道。

paras.en: A one hundred and four year old woman is selling the house she has lived in since she was two years old.
paras.zh: 一位一百零四岁的老太太要卖掉她从两岁起就一直住着的房子。

paras.en: Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset village of Street.
paras.zh: 南希·吉福德出生在第一次世界大战结束几个月后，在萨默塞特郡斯特里特村那座有三间卧室的房子里住了一百零二年。

paras.en: She is now putting it on the market, having lived in it through the Second World War and the invention of television.
paras.zh: 她在这座房子里经历了第二次世界大战，也见证了电视的发明，现在她要把房子挂牌出售了。

paras.en: Her family bought the house for two hundred pounds in nineteen twenty one, and it is now priced at some one hundred and seventy thousand pounds.
paras.zh: 一九二一年，她家花两百英镑买下了这座房子，现在它的标价大约是十七万英镑。

paras.en: According to the Bank of England’s inflation calculator, two hundred pounds in nineteen twenty one would be worth seven thousand seven hundred and fifty pounds today.
paras.zh: 按照英格兰银行的通胀计算器，一九二一年的两百英镑相当于今天的七千七百五十英镑。

paras.en: According to the estate agent, the house was built in eighteen eighty two and originally featured a well for the entire road.
paras.zh: 据房产中介说，这座房子建于一八八二年，原来有一口井，供整条路的人用。

paras.en: Except for some changes in the toilet and wash area, much of the house remains the same.
paras.zh: 除了厕所和洗漱区有些改动，房子的大部分地方都还是老样子。

paras.en: Mrs Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.
paras.zh: 吉福德太太因为身体原因，要卖掉房子，搬进附近格拉斯顿伯里的一家养老院。

paras.en: Questions one and two are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一、二题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the news report say about Nancy Gifford?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于南希·吉福德，新闻报道说了什么？

paras.en: Question two: Why is Mrs. Gifford selling the house?
paras.zh: 第二题：吉福德太太为什么要卖房子？

paras.en: News Report Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The Navy rescued a man who survived twenty four days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce and vegetable powder.
paras.zh: 海军救起了一名男子，他靠吃番茄酱和蔬菜粉，在海上漂着的一条船上活了二十四天。

paras.en: The man, forty seven, wrote the word help in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue.
paras.zh: 这名男子四十七岁，他在船上用英文写了 help（救命）这个词，这是他获救的关键。

paras.en: The man told authorities that his experience began in December, when currents swept the sailboat out to sea while he was making repairs.
paras.zh: 他告诉有关部门，事情发生在十二月，他正在修船，洋流把帆船冲到了海上。

paras.en: To survive, the man collected rain water with a cloth.
paras.zh: 为了活下来，他用一块布收集雨水。

paras.en: He had to constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking.
paras.zh: 他得不停地把水从船里舀出去，免得船沉下去。

paras.en: He also tried to light a fire to send a distress signal without success.
paras.zh: 他还试过生火发出求救信号，但没成功。

paras.en: Finally a plane passed by and he signalled with a mirror.
paras.zh: 最后，一架飞机从上空飞过，他用一面镜子发信号。

paras.en: He said the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again.
paras.zh: 他说，海军告诉他，那架飞机再次飞过时发现了他。

paras.en: The sailboat was abandoned at sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship.
paras.zh: 附近一艘商船把他救上来以后，那条帆船就被弃在了海上。

paras.en: He was found in good health, but had lost weight.
paras.zh: 他被发现时身体还不错，只是瘦了。

paras.en: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第三、四题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question 3: What does the news report say was key to the man’s rescue?
paras.zh: 第三题：新闻报道说这名男子获救的关键是什么？

paras.en: Question four: What do we learn about the man when he was rescued?
paras.zh: 第四题：这名男子获救时情况怎么样？

paras.en: News Report Three.
paras.zh: 第三篇新闻报道。

paras.en: The Board of Denver Public Schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment.
paras.zh: 丹佛公立学校董事会准备关掉几所小学和初中，因为入学人数下降，预算减少了，要靠这个来弥补。

paras.en: The specific schools will be announced in the coming days, a district spokesperson said.
paras.zh: 学区的一位发言人说，具体是哪几所学校，会在接下来几天公布。

paras.en: The school board approved criteria to close schools with fewer than 215 students, as well as schools with fewer than 275 students and a projected decline in enrollment.
paras.zh: 学校董事会批准了关闭学校的标准：学生少于二百一十五人的学校，以及学生少于二百七十五人、预计入学人数还会下降的学校。

paras.en: In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said.
paras.zh: 学区说，预计未来三年，小学和初中的入学人数会减少三千人。

paras.en: 3,000 students may not seem like that many students, but to a budget where you’re receiving per-pupil funding, that’s about $36 million, district spokesperson Scott Pribble said.
paras.zh: 学区发言人斯科特·普里布尔说，三千个学生看上去可能不算多，可对按学生人数拨款的预算来说，这就差不多是三千六百万美元。

paras.en: We know that there are impacts and it’s heartbreaking and difficult work, but in order for the district to stay out of debt, it’s a step that needs to be taken, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，我们知道这会带来影响，这件工作让人心痛，也很难，但学区要想不欠债，就必须走这一步。

paras.en: The district said the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services or specialized programming to schools with lower enrollment.
paras.zh: 学区说，预算减少意味着，对入学人数较少的学校，学区没法再提供同样的心理健康支持、社交和情感服务，也没法提供专门的课程项目。

paras.en: Questions five to seven are based on the news report you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第七题根据你刚才听到的新闻报道提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about the elementary and middle schools to be closed in Denver?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于丹佛要关闭的那些小学和初中，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 6: What does the Denver District expect to do in the next three years?
paras.zh: 第六题：丹佛学区预计未来三年会出现什么情况？

paras.en: Question 7: Why are some schools in Denver to be closed, according to the district spokesperson?
paras.zh: 第七题：根据学区发言人的说法，丹佛为什么要关闭一些学校？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation One.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Good afternoon.
paras.zh: 下午好。

paras.en: Theatre Bookings International.
paras.zh: 这里是国际剧院订票公司。

paras.en: My name’s Philip.
paras.zh: 我叫菲利普。

paras.en: How may I help you today?
paras.zh: 今天有什么可以帮您的吗？

paras.en: Oh, good afternoon.
paras.zh: 哦，下午好。

paras.en: My name’s Helen.
paras.zh: 我叫海伦。

paras.en: I’ve been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the 28th.
paras.zh: 我一直想订五月二十八号晚上在伦敦演出的音乐剧《猫》的票。

paras.en: But I can’t get the computer to accept my card payment.
paras.zh: 可电脑就是不接受我的银行卡付款。

paras.en: I’ve tried three times, but it just doesn’t want to take it.
paras.zh: 我试了三次，可它就是不收。

paras.en: That’s okay, madam.
paras.zh: 没关系，女士。

paras.en: I can book it and take the payment over the phone if that’s not a problem for you.
paras.zh: 如果您方便的话，我可以在电话里帮您订票、收款。

paras.en: That would be wonderful.
paras.zh: 那太好了。

paras.en: I’m not very good with computers.
paras.zh: 我不太会用电脑。

paras.en: My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next Thursday.
paras.zh: 这些事一般都是我丈夫做，可他到意大利出差了，下星期四才回来。

paras.en: And I know how quickly these things can sell out.
paras.zh: 我也知道这种票很快就会卖光。

paras.en: They do indeed, madam.
paras.zh: 确实是这样，女士。

paras.en: Cats on May the 28th at the Lion Theatre in London at 7:30 P.M.?
paras.zh: 五月二十八号晚上七点半，伦敦狮子剧院的《猫》，对吗？

paras.en: Yes, that’s the one.
paras.zh: 对，就是这场。

paras.en: And I will need two tickets, please.
paras.zh: 我要两张票，谢谢。

paras.en: Not too close to the front.
paras.zh: 别离前面太近。

paras.en: Actually, all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway, but I can offer you two upstairs near the middle.
paras.zh: 其实，前面的票反正已经全卖光了，不过我可以给您楼上靠中间的两张。

paras.en: I assume that you don’t want to be too high up.
paras.zh: 我想您不会想坐得太高吧。

paras.en: Oh my goodness, no.
paras.zh: 哎呀，可不要。

paras.en: I’m scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway.
paras.zh: 我恐高，再说坐得太高，反正什么也看不见。

paras.en: No problem, madam.
paras.zh: 没问题，女士。

paras.en: I’ll reserve those for you now, and all we need after that is the details of your card number and your full name, and then we are done.
paras.zh: 我现在就给您把这两张票留下，然后只需要您的卡号和全名，就办好了。

paras.en: Questions eight to eleven are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第八到第十一题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question eight: Why does the woman call the man?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士为什么给男士打电话？

paras.en: Question nine: What do we learn about the woman’s husband?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于女士的丈夫，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the man say about the tickets at the front?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于前面的票，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question eleven: What does the woman say she is scared of?
paras.zh: 第十一题：女士说她害怕什么？

paras.en: Conversation 2.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi, John.
paras.zh: 你好，约翰。

paras.en: Why haven’t you answered my text messages lately?
paras.zh: 你最近怎么不回我的短信？

paras.en: Oh, I didn’t know you had sent any.
paras.zh: 哦，我都不知道你给我发过短信。

paras.en: I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven’t turned it back on since then.
paras.zh: 我差不多一个星期前就把手机关了，从那以后一直没开。

paras.en: Why would you do something like that when our phones make our lives so much more convenient?
paras.zh: 手机让我们的生活方便了那么多，你干吗要这么做？

paras.en: Well, I downloaded an app that recorded how much time I spent on my phone, and I was shocked to realize I was using my phone an average of eight hours a day, and, on my worst day, I used it for twelve hours.
paras.zh: 嗯，我下载了一个应用，记录我每天花多少时间用手机，结果吃惊地发现，我平均每天要用八个小时，最厉害的一天用了十二个小时。

paras.en: Were you addicted to mobile phone games?
paras.zh: 你是玩手机游戏上瘾了吗？

paras.en: I had a friend who was, and he sometimes played them all day and into the night.
paras.zh: 我有个朋友就是这样，他有时候从白天一直玩到深夜。

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不是的。

paras.en: My problem was that I was spending too much time on social media, messaging friends, and commenting on other people’s posts.
paras.zh: 我的问题是在社交媒体上花的时间太多了，给朋友发消息，给别人的帖子写评论。

paras.en: I do all of that too, as well as shopping online, and paying for everything with my phone.
paras.zh: 这些我也都做，另外我还在网上购物，买什么都用手机付钱。

paras.en: That is really why I don’t see how anyone could live without a mobile phone.
paras.zh: 所以我真想不出谁能离得开手机。

paras.en: How do you buy things, or communicate with your friends?
paras.zh: 那你怎么买东西，怎么跟朋友联系呢？

paras.en: Since I’ve stopped using my phone, I go to physical stores and pay in cash.
paras.zh: 不用手机以后，我就去实体店买东西，付现金。

paras.en: I’ve actually met friends for meals at cafes and restaurants.
paras.zh: 我还真的跟朋友约在咖啡馆和餐馆吃过饭。

paras.en: That’s great for you.
paras.zh: 那对你来说挺好的。

paras.en: But my friends and family don’t live in this city, so we can’t see each other often, and I don’t have any choice but to chat with them online.
paras.zh: 可我的朋友和家人都不住在这座城市，我们没法常见面，我只能在网上跟他们聊天。

paras.en: Questions twelve to fifteen are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Why hasn’t the man answered the woman’s text messages lately?
paras.zh: 第十二题：男士最近为什么没回女士的短信？

paras.en: Question 13: What was the man shocked to realize after he downloaded the app?
paras.zh: 第十三题：男士下载那个应用以后，吃惊地发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What did the man spend much time doing with his phone?
paras.zh: 第十四题：男士用手机花很多时间做什么？

paras.en: Question fifteen: Why does the woman say she has to use her mobile phone?
paras.zh: 第十五题：女士为什么说她不得不用手机？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section you will hear three passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet 1 with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage One.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: If US workers want to switch jobs they’d better do it now.
paras.zh: 美国的上班族要是想跳槽，最好现在就跳。

paras.en: Last year job switchers earned far higher wage increases than those staying in their jobs, but the gap is now closing.
paras.zh: 去年，跳槽的人涨薪幅度比留在原岗位的人高得多，不过现在差距正在缩小。

paras.en: A three-month moving average of annual wage increases from the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank’s Wage Tracker shows that US job switchers got the highest wage increase last July when the measure touched 8.5 percent.
paras.zh: 亚特兰大联邦储备银行的“工资追踪器”显示，按三个月移动平均算，美国跳槽者的年涨薪幅度在去年七月最高，达到百分之八点五。

paras.en: Since then it has gone up and down, and has been going steadily down since November.
paras.zh: 从那以后，这个数字有升有降，从十一月起就一直在稳步下降。

paras.en: The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing.
paras.zh: 跳槽的人和留在原岗位的人在涨薪上的差距，现在正在缩小。

paras.en: On average, people who changed jobs have almost always gotten better pay raises than those who stayed, but in the past the difference was usually around one percentage point.
paras.zh: 总的来说，换工作的人涨薪几乎总是比留下来的人多，可过去两者的差距通常只有一个百分点左右。

paras.en: In July, though, the gap widened to two point six percentage points.
paras.zh: 不过在七月，差距扩大到了二点六个百分点。

paras.en: But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller wage bumps in their new jobs.
paras.zh: 可现在，所有人的工资增长都在放缓，跳槽的人在新工作上的涨薪也变小了。

paras.en: At the moment, those who change jobs get an average 7.3 percent raise every year, while those who stay get a 5.4 percent raise.
paras.zh: 眼下，换工作的人每年平均涨薪百分之七点三，而留下来的人涨百分之五点四。

paras.en: That suggests the demand for workers has reached, or is at least nearing, its peak.
paras.zh: 这说明，对劳动力的需求已经达到，或者至少接近顶峰了。

paras.en: The labor market is likely cooling because even a shortage of workers isn’t overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the US.
paras.zh: 劳动力市场很可能在降温，因为就算劳动力短缺，也没能扭转美国雇主和雇员之间由来已久的不平衡。

w.m: adj. 历史上的；由来已久的

paras.en: The volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the US economy produces is still falling.
paras.zh: 工人拿回家的收入占美国经济产出的比例，仍然在下降。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the passage say about the gap in wage gains between job switchers and those who stay in their jobs?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于跳槽的人和留在原岗位的人在涨薪上的差距，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question seventeen: What do we learn about wage growth now?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于现在的工资增长，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What is the labor market likely doing according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第十八题：根据短文，劳动力市场很可能在发生什么变化？

paras.en: Passage Two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Highly processed foods, the kinds made with lots of sugar, fat, and salt, make up as much as sixty per cent of the average American diet.
paras.zh: 高度加工食品，就是那种用大量的糖、脂肪和盐做的食品，最多能占到美国人平均饮食的百分之六十。

paras.en: But a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health.
paras.zh: 但一项新研究表明，它们价格低、吃着方便，代价却是损害健康。

paras.en: The study found that, when people ate a highly processed diet, they consumed about five hundred more calories per day than they did when they ate a less processed diet.
paras.zh: 研究发现，人们吃高度加工食品时，每天摄入的热量比吃加工程度低的食品时多出大约五百卡路里。

paras.en: They also gained two pounds over two weeks, even though both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber, and salt.
paras.zh: 尽管两种饮食里糖、脂肪、纤维和盐这些营养成分的量都一样，他们还在两周里长了两磅。

paras.en: It wasn’t a shock to find highly processed foods weren’t healthy.
paras.zh: 发现高度加工食品不健康，这并不让人意外。

w.m: n. 震惊；令人意外的事

paras.en: Other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity.
paras.zh: 别的研究已经发现，它们跟更高的癌症和肥胖风险有关。

paras.en: What was unexpected was that sugar, fat, and salt didn’t seem to be what caused people to overeat.
paras.zh: 出乎意料的是，让人吃多的好像并不是糖、脂肪和盐。

w.m: adj. 意想不到的；出乎意料的

paras.en: This is the first trial that demonstrates that there is something about highly processed foods, independent of those nutrients, that causes people to overeat.
paras.zh: 这是第一个证明了下面这一点的试验：高度加工食品里有某种东西会让人吃多，而且跟那些营养成分无关。

paras.en: The study also found that, when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster.
paras.zh: 研究还发现，人们吃高度加工食品时，吃得更快。

paras.en: This could be one reason why they gained more weight.
paras.zh: 这可能就是他们体重长得更多的一个原因。

paras.en: Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow.
paras.zh: 高度加工食品往往更软，所以更容易嚼、更容易咽。

paras.en: One theory is that if you’re eating more quickly, you’re not giving your gut enough time to signal to your brain that you’ve had enough calories and that you’re full.
paras.zh: 有一种理论认为，要是你吃得太快，肠胃就来不及给大脑发信号，告诉它你摄入的热量已经够了、你已经饱了。

paras.en: By the time the brain gets that signal, you’ve already overeaten.
paras.zh: 等大脑收到这个信号，你已经吃多了。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does a new study show about highly processed foods?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于高度加工食品，一项新研究表明了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What are highly processed foods linked to, according to other research?
paras.zh: 第二十题：根据别的研究，高度加工食品跟什么有关？

paras.en: Question 21: What do people tend to do when eating highly processed foods?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：人们吃高度加工食品时往往会怎样？

paras.en: Passage 3.
paras.zh: 第三篇短文。

paras.en: Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house.
paras.zh: 女性花在照顾孩子和做家务上的时间仍然比男性多。

paras.en: This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values.
paras.zh: 人们一般把这归因于落后的思想和保守的价值观。

paras.en: But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females.
paras.zh: 可新的研究表明，这种差别可能跟男女的喜好不同有关。

paras.en: The new study looked at how men and women were dividing work at home, and why they divided it that way.
paras.zh: 这项新研究考察了男人和女人在家里怎样分工，以及为什么这样分工。

paras.en: In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked.
paras.zh: 总的来说，男人和女人都会多承担自己喜欢的那些事。

paras.en: For example, men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women.
paras.zh: 比如说，男人比女人更喜欢打理院子和维修房屋。

paras.en: They leaned toward wanting primary responsibility for such tasks.
paras.zh: 他们更倾向于主要负责这类事。

paras.en: The researchers stated that differences in enjoyment of household and child care tasks matched how men and women chose to split tasks.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，男女对家务和带孩子这些事喜欢的程度不同，这跟他们选择怎样分工正好吻合。

paras.en: The researchers added that there was not a single child care task that men liked more than women.
paras.zh: 研究人员还说，没有哪一件带孩子的事是男人比女人更喜欢的。

paras.en: Keep in mind, however, that, as with any research on group differences, there were large within-group differences.
paras.zh: 不过要记住，跟所有关于群体差异的研究一样，同一群体内部的差异也很大。

paras.en: The study’s authors concluded that differences in men’s and women’s time spent on child care and household tasks do not mean dissatisfaction.
paras.zh: 这项研究的作者得出结论：男人和女人花在带孩子和做家务上的时间不同，并不代表他们不满意。

paras.en: The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards family and career.
paras.zh: 作者指出，以前的研究揭示了男女在对待家庭和事业的态度上有差别。

paras.en: These differences appear as early as six years old.
paras.zh: 这些差别早在六岁时就会出现。

paras.en: Girls that age already show more interest in helping and caring for others than boys do, and they already exhibit a greater orientation toward family versus career.
paras.zh: 那个年纪的女孩就已经比男孩更愿意帮助和照顾别人，也已经表现出更看重家庭而不是事业。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 22: How do people generally account for differences between men and women in the amount of time spent on housework?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：对于男女花在家务上的时间不同，人们一般怎样解释？

paras.en: Question 23: What did men lean toward doing according to the new study?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：根据这项新研究，男人倾向于做什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What should we keep in mind as regards any research on group differences?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于任何群体差异的研究，我们应该记住什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What did previous research reveal about gender differences in attitudes toward family and career?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于男女对待家庭和事业的态度，以前的研究揭示了什么性别差异？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
